en: So, how long have you been a Market Research Consultant?
cn: 那么，你做市场研究顾问多长时间了？

en: Well, I started straight after finishing university.
cn: 嗯，我从大学一毕业就开始做了。

en: Did you study market research?
cn: 你学的是市场研究专业吗？

en: Yeah, and it really helped me to get into the industry, but I have to say that it's more important to get experience in different types of market research to find out exactly what you're interested in.
cn: 是的，这确实帮助我进入了这个行业，但我必须说，更重要的是在不同类型的市场研究中获取经验，从而弄清楚你真正感兴趣的是什么。

en: So what are you interested in?
cn: 那么你对什么感兴趣呢？

en: Well, at the moment, I specialize in quantitative advertising research, which means that I do two types of projects.
cn: 嗯，目前我专攻定量广告研究，这意味着我做两种类型的项目。

en: Trackers, which are ongoing projects that look at trends or customer satisfaction over a long period of time.
cn: 跟踪研究，是持续进行的项目，长期观察趋势或顾客满意度。

en: The only problem with trackers is that it takes up a lot of your time.
cn: 跟踪研究唯一的问题是它占用了你很多时间。

en: But you do build up a good relationship with the client.
cn: 但你确实能和客户建立良好的关系。

en: I also do a couple of ad-hoc jobs which are much shorter projects.
cn: 我也做一些专题研究，是时间短得多的项目。

en: What exactly do you mean by ad-hoc jobs?
cn: 你说的专题研究具体指什么？

en: It's basically when companies need quick answers to their questions about their consumers' habits.
cn: 基本上就是当公司需要对消费者习惯的问题快速得到答案时。

en: They just ask for one questionnaire to be sent out, for example, so the time you spend on an ad-hoc project tends to be fairly short.
cn: 他们只要求发放一份问卷，所以你花在专题研究上的时间往往相当短。

en: Which do you prefer, trackers or ad-hoc?
cn: 你更喜欢哪种，跟踪研究还是专题研究？

en: I like doing both and in fact I need to do both at the same time to keep me from going crazy.
cn: 两种我都喜欢，事实上我需要同时做两种来让自己不至于疯掉。

en: I need the variety.
cn: 我需要多样性。

en: Can you just explain what process you go through with a new client?
cn: 你能解释一下你和新客户合作时经历的过程吗？

en: Well, together we decide on the methodology and the objectives of the research.
cn: 嗯，我们一起确定研究的方法和目标。

en: I then design a questionnaire.
cn: 然后我设计问卷。

en: Once the interviewees have been briefed, I send the client a schedule and then they get back to me with deadlines.
cn: 一旦受访者了解了基本情况，我就发给客户一份时间表，然后他们给我回复截止日期。

en: Once the final charts and tables are ready, I have to check them and organize a presentation.
cn: 最终的图表准备好后，我必须检查它们并组织演示。

en: Hmm.
cn: 嗯。

en: One last question, what do you like and dislike about your job?
cn: 最后一个问题，你喜欢和不喜欢你工作的哪些方面？

en: As I said, variety is important and as for what I don't like, it has to be the checking of charts and tables.
cn: 正如我所说，多样性很重要，至于我不喜欢的方面，那一定是检查图表和表格。

en: Hello.
cn: 你好。

en: I'm here with Frederick.
cn: 我和弗雷德里克在一起。

en: Now Fred, you went to university in Canada?
cn: 弗雷德，你在加拿大上的大学？

en: Yeah, that's right.
cn: 是的，没错。

en: OK, and you have very strong views about universities in Canada.
cn: 好的，你对加拿大的大学有着非常鲜明的观点。

en: Could you please explain?
cn: 你能解释一下吗？

en: Well, we don't have private universities in Canada.
cn: 嗯，加拿大没有私立大学。

en: They're all public.
cn: 它们都是公立的。

en: All the universities are owned by the government, so there is the Ministry of Education in charge of creating the curriculum for the universities and so there's not much room for flexibility.
cn: 所有大学都归政府所有，所以由教育部负责制定大学的课程，因而没有太多灵活调整的余地。

en: Since it's a government-operated institution, things don't move very fast.
cn: 因为它是政府运营的机构，事情进展不那么快。

en: If you want something to be done, then their staff do not have so much incentive to help you because he's a worker for the government.
cn: 如果你想做某件事，他们的员工没有太多动力去帮助你，因为他是为政府工作的。

en: So I don't think it's very efficient.
cn: 所以我认为效率不高。

en: However, there are certain advantages of public universities, such as the fees being free.
cn: 然而，公立大学有某些优势，比如学费免费。

en: You don't have to pay for your education.
cn: 你不需要为教育付费。

en: But the system isn't efficient, and it does not work that well.
cn: 但这个体系效率不高，运行得也不是那么好。

en: Yeah, I can see your point.
cn: 是的，我明白你的观点。

en: But in the United States we have many private universities, and I think they're large bureaucracies also.
cn: 但在美国我们有很多私立大学，我认为它们也是庞大的官僚机构。

en: Maybe people don't act that much differently, because it's the same thing working for a private university.
cn: 也许人们的行为并没有太大不同，因为在私立大学工作也是一样的。

en: They get paid for their job.
cn: 他们为工作获得报酬。

en: I don't know if they're that much more motivated to help people.
cn: 我不知道他们是否更有动力去帮助别人。

en: Also, we have a problem in the United States that usually only wealthy kids go to the best schools and it's kind of a problem actually.
cn: 而且，在美国我们有一个问题，通常只有富裕家庭的孩子才能上最好的学校，这实际上是个问题。

en: I agree with you.
cn: 我同意你的观点。

en: I think it's a problem because you're not giving equal access to education to everybody.
cn: 我认为这是个问题，因为你没有给每个人平等的受教育机会。

en: It's not easy, but having only public universities also might not be the best solution.
cn: 这不容易，但只有公立大学也可能不是最好的解决方案。

en: Perhaps we can learn from Japan where they have a system of private and public universities.
cn: 也许我们可以向日本学习，他们有私立和公立大学并存的体系。

en: Now, in Japan, public universities are considered to be the best.
cn: 现在，在日本，公立大学被认为是最好的。

en: Right.
cn: 是的。

en: It's the exact opposite in the United States.
cn: 在美国则完全相反。

en: So, as you see, it's very hard to say which one is better.
cn: 所以，如你所见，很难说哪一个更好。

en: Right, a good point.
cn: 是的，说得好。

en: A recent International Labor Organization report says the deterioration of real wages around the world calls into question the true extent of an economic recovery, especially if government rescue packages are phased out too early.
cn: 最近的一项国际劳工组织报告称，全世界实际工资状况的恶化令人对经济复苏的真实程度产生质疑，特别是如果政府救助方案过早逐步取消的话。

en: The report warns the picture on wages is likely to get worse this year despite indications of an economic rebound.
cn: 该报告警告说，尽管有经济反弹的迹象，今年的工资状况可能会变得更糟。

en: Patrick Belser, an International Labor Organization specialist says declining wage rates are linked to the levels of unemployment.
cn: 国际劳工组织专家帕特里克·贝尔瑟表示，工资率下降与失业率水平有关。

en: The quite dramatic unemployment figures, which we now see in some of the countries strongly suggest that there will be greater pressure on wages in the future as more people will be unemployed, more people will be looking for jobs and the pressure on employers to raise wages to attract workers will decline.
cn: 我们现在在一些国家看到的相当惊人的失业数据强烈表明，未来工资将面临更大压力，因为会有更多人失业，更多人找工作，而雇主通过提高工资来吸引工人的压力将会下降。

en: So, we expect that the second part of the year will not be very good in terms of wage growth.
cn: 因此，我们预计今年下半年在工资增长方面不会很好。

en: The report finds more than a quarter of the countries experienced flat or falling monthly wages in real terms.
cn: 该报告发现，超过四分之一的国家经历了实际月工资持平或下降。

en: They include the United States, Austria, Costa Rica, South Africa and Germany.
cn: 这些国家包括美国、奥地利、哥斯达黎加、南非和德国。

en: International Labor Organization economists say some nations have come up with policies to lessen the impact of lower wages during the economic crisis.
cn: 国际劳工组织经济学家表示，一些国家已经出台了政策，以减轻经济危机期间工资下降的影响。

en: An example of these is Work Sharing with government subsidies.
cn: 其中一个例子是政府补贴的工作分享计划。

en: Under this scheme, the number of individual working hours is reduced in an effort to avoid layoffs.
cn: 根据这项计划，个人的工作时间会缩短，以避免裁员。

en: For this scheme to work, the government must provide wage subsidies to compensate for lost pay due to the shorter hours.
cn: 为了使该计划奏效，政府必须提供工资补贴，以补偿因工时缩短而损失的工资。

en: Is there really a magic memory pill or a herbal recall remedy?
cn: 是否真的有某种神奇记忆药丸或者某种草药记忆唤醒疗法？

en: I have been frequently asked if these memory supplements work.
cn: 我经常被问到这些记忆保健品是否有作用。

en: You know, one of these first things I like to tell people when they ask me about the supplements, is that a lot of them are promoted as a cure for your memory.
cn: 你知道，当人们问我关于这些保健品的问题时，我最先告诉他们的事情之一是，很多保健品被宣传为治疗记忆力的良药。

en: But your memory doesn't need a cure.
cn: 但你的记忆力不需要治疗。

en: What your memory needs is a good work-out.
cn: 你的记忆力需要的是良好的锻炼。

en: So really, those supplements aren't going to give you that perfect memory in the way that they promise.
cn: 所以实际上，那些保健品不会像它们承诺的那样给你完美的记忆力。

en: The other thing is that a lot of these supplements aren't necessarily what they claim to be, and you really have to be wary when you take any of them.
cn: 另一件事是，很多这些保健品不一定如它们所声称的那样，你在服用任何一种时都必须小心。

en: The science isn't there behind most of them.
cn: 大多数保健品背后没有科学依据。

en: They're not really well-regulated unless they adhere to some industry standard.
cn: 它们并没有得到很好的监管，除非它们遵守某些行业标准。

en: You don't really know that what they say is in there, isn't in there.
cn: 你并不真正知道他们所说的成分是否真的在里面。

en: What you must understand is that those supplements, especially in some eastern cultures, are part of a medical practice tradition.
cn: 你必须理解的是，这些保健品，尤其是在一些东方文化中，是医疗实践传统的一部分。

en: People don't just go in a local grocery store and buy these supplements.
cn: 人们不只是去当地的杂货店买这些保健品。

en: In fact, they are prescribed and they're given at a certain level, a dosage that is understood by a practitioner who's been trained.
cn: 事实上，它们是由医生开具处方的，并且有一定的剂量，这由受过训练的从业者掌握。

en: And that's not really the way they're used in this country.
cn: 而在这个国家，它们并非以这种方式被使用。

en: The other thing that people do forget is that these are medicines, so they do have an impact.
cn: 人们常忘记的另一件事是，这些是药品，所以它们确实有影响。

en: A lot of times people are not really aware of the impact they have, or the fact that taking them in combination with other medications might put you at increased risk for something that you wouldn't otherwise be countering or be at risk for.
cn: 很多时候人们并没有真正意识到它们的影响，或者与其他药物一起服用可能会增加你本不会对抗或面临的风险。

en: The negative impacts of natural disasters can be seen everywhere.
cn: 自然灾害的负面影响随处可见。

en: In just the past few weeks, the world has witnessed the destructive power of earthquakes in Indonesia, typhoons in the Philippines, and the destructive sea waves that struck Samoa and neighboring islands.
cn: 就在过去几周里，世界见证了印度尼西亚的地震、菲律宾的台风以及袭击萨摩亚及其邻近岛屿的破坏性海浪的威力。

en: A study by the Center for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters finds that, between 1980 and 2007, nearly 8,400 natural disasters killed more than two-million people.
cn: 灾害流行病学研究中心的一项研究发现，1980年至2007年间，近8400次自然灾害导致200多万人丧生。

en: These catastrophic events caused more than $1.5 trillion in economic losses.
cn: 这些灾难性事件造成了超过1.5万亿美元的经济损失。

en: U.N. weather expert Geoffrey Love says that is the bad news.
cn: 联合国天气专家杰弗里·洛夫说这是坏消息。

en: Over the last 50 years, economic losses have increased by a factor of 50.
cn: 在过去的50年里，经济损失增加了50倍。

en: That sounds pretty terrible, but the loss of life has decreased by a factor of 10 simply because we are getting better at warning people: We are making a difference.
cn: 这听起来相当可怕，但死亡人数减少了10倍，这仅仅是因为我们在预警方面做得更好了：我们正在发挥作用。

en: Extreme events, however, will continue to occur.
cn: 然而，极端事件将继续发生。

en: But the message is that they need not be disasters.
cn: 但关键信息是它们不必成为灾难。

en: Love, who is director of Weather and Disaster Risk Reduction at the World Meteorological Organization, says most of the deaths and economic losses were caused by weather, climate, or water-related extremes.
cn: 洛夫是世界气象组织天气与灾害风险降低部主任，他说大多数死亡和经济损失是由天气、气候或与水有关的极端事件造成的。

en: These include droughts, floods, windstorms, strong tropical winds and wildfires.
cn: 这些包括干旱、洪水、风暴、强热带风和野火。

en: He says extreme events will continue.
cn: 他说极端事件将继续发生。

en: But, he says extreme events become disasters only when people fail to prepare for them.
cn: 但是，他说极端事件只有在人们没能做好准备时才会成为灾难。

en: Many of the remedies are well-known.
cn: 许多补救措施是众所周知的。

en: From a planning perspective, it's pretty simple.
cn: 从规划的角度来看，这相当简单。

en: Build better buildings.
cn: 建造更好的建筑。

en: Don't build where the hazards will destroy them.
cn: 不要在危险会摧毁它们的地方建造。

en: From an early-warning perspective, make sure the warnings go right down to the community level.
cn: 从预警的角度来看，确保预警直接传达到社区层面。

en: Build community action plans.
cn: 建立社区行动计划。

en: As U.S. banks recovered with the help of the American government and the American taxpayer, president Obama held meetings with top bank executives, telling them it's time to return the favor.
cn: 在美国政府和美国纳税人的帮助下，美国银行逐渐复苏，奥巴马总统与银行高层管理者举行了会谈，告知他们是时候作出一些回报了。

en: The way I see it are banks now having a greater obligation to the goal of a wider recovery, he said.
cn: 他说，我所看到的情况是，当前银行应为取得更大范围复苏的目标承担更大的义务。

en: But the president may be giving the financial sector too much credit.
cn: 但总统可能对金融行业评价过高了。

en: It was in a free fall, and it was a very scary period, Economist Martin Neil Baily said.
cn: 当时处于自由落体状态，那是一个非常可怕的时期，经济学家马丁·尼尔·贝利说。

en: After the failure of Lehman Brothers, many of the world's largest banks feared the worst as the collapse of the housing bubble exposed investments in risky loans.
cn: 雷曼兄弟倒闭后，随着房地产泡沫的破灭暴露了风险贷款投资，世界上许多最大的银行都担心最坏的情况发生。

en: Although he says the worst is over, Bailey says the banking crisis is not.
cn: 尽管他说最坏的时期已经过去，但贝利说银行业危机还没有结束。

en: More than 130 U.S. banks failed in 2009.
cn: 2009年，130多家美国银行倒闭。

en: He predicts high failure rates for smaller, regional banks in 2010 as commercial real estate loans come due.
cn: 他预言，随着商业地产贷款到期，小型的地方性银行在2010年的倒闭风险较高。

en: So there may actually be a worsening of credit availability to small and medium-sized businesses in the next year or so.
cn: 所以在接下来的一年左右，中小企业的信贷可用性实际上可能会恶化。

en: Analysts say the biggest problem is high unemployment, which weakens demand and makes banks reluctant to lend.
cn: 分析人士说，最大的问题是高失业率，这削弱了需求，使银行不愿放贷。

en: But U.S. Bancorp chief Richard Davis sees the situation differently.
cn: 但美国合众银行首席执行官理查德·戴维斯对形势的看法不同。

en: We're probably more optimistic than the experts might be.
cn: 我们可能比专家更乐观。

en: With that in mind, we're putting in everything we can.
cn: 考虑到这一点，我们正在尽我们所能。

en: Lending is the coal to our engine, so we want to make more loans.
cn: 放贷是我们发展的动力，所以我们愿意多放贷。

en: We have to find a way to qualify more people and not put ourselves at risk.
cn: 我们必须设法使更多人获得贷款，同时又不使自己陷入风险之中。

en: While some economists predict continued recovery in the future, Baily says the only certainty is that banks are unlikely to make the same mistakes twice.
cn: 虽然一些经济学家预测未来将继续复苏，但贝利说，唯一确定的是银行不太可能再犯同样的错误。

en: You know, forecasting's become a very hazardous business so I don't want to commit myself too much.
cn: 你知道，预测已经变成一项非常危险的事情，所以我不想过多承诺。

en: I don't think we know exactly what's going to happen but it's certainly possible that we could get very slow growth over the next year or two.
cn: 我认为我们并不确切知道会发生什么，但在未来一两年内出现非常缓慢的增长肯定是可能的。

en: If the economy starts to shrink again, Baily says it would make a strong case for a second stimulus—something the Obama administration hopes will not be necessary.
cn: 贝利说，如果经济再次开始萎缩，将有充分理由出台第二轮刺激政策——这是奥巴马政府希望没有必要做的事情。

en: A new study has failed to find any conclusive evidence that lifestyle changes can prevent cognitive decline in older adults.
cn: 一项新的研究未能找到任何确凿证据表明生活方式的改变可以预防老年人的认知能力下降。

en: Still, there are good reasons to make positive changes in how we live and what we eat as we age.
cn: 尽管如此，随着我们年龄的增长，在我们的生活方式和饮食方面做出积极改变仍有充分的理由。

en: Cognitive decline is the loss of ability to learn new skills, or recall words, names, and faces that is most common as we age.
cn: 认知能力下降是指丧失学习新技能或回忆单词、名字和面孔的能力，这是随着年龄增长最常见的情况。

en: To reduce or avoid it, researchers have examined the effect of smoking, diet, brain-challenging games, exercise and other strategies.
cn: 为了减少或避免这种情况，研究人员研究了吸烟、饮食、挑战大脑的游戏、锻炼和其他策略的效果。

en: Researchers at Duke University scrutinized more than 160 published studies and found an absence of strong evidence that any of these approaches can make a big difference.
cn: 杜克大学的研究人员仔细审查了160多项已发表的研究，发现缺乏强有力的证据表明这些方法中的任何一种能产生重大影响。

en: Co-author James Burke helped design the study.
cn: 合著者詹姆斯·伯克帮助设计了这项研究。

en: In the observational studies we found that some of the B vitamins were beneficial.
cn: 在观察性研究中，我们发现一些B族维生素是有益的。

en: Exercise, diet, cognitive stimulation showed some positive effects, although the evidence was not so strong that we could actually consider these firmly established.
cn: 锻炼、饮食和认知刺激显示出一些积极效果，尽管证据并不强到足以让我们认为这些已得到充分证实。

en: Some previous studies have suggested that challenging your brain with mentally stimulating activities might help.
cn: 此前的一些研究表明，用激发智力的活动挑战你的大脑可能会有所帮助。

en: And Burke says that actually does seem to help, based on randomized studies—the researcher's gold standard.
cn: 伯克说，基于随机研究——研究者的黄金标准——这确实似乎有所帮助。

en: Cognitive stimulation is one of the areas where we did find some benefit.
cn: 认知刺激是我们确实发现一些益处的领域之一。

en: The exact type of stimulation that an individual uses is not as important as being intellectually engaged.
cn: 个人使用的刺激类型并不如保持智力参与重要。

en: The expert review also found insufficient evidence to recommend any drugs or dietary supplements that could prevent or slow cognitive decline.
cn: 专家审查还发现，没有足够的证据推荐任何可以预防或减缓认知能力下降的药物或膳食补充剂。

en: However, given that there is at least some evidence for positive effects from some of these lifestyle changes, plus other benefits apparently unrelated to cognitive decline, Burke was willing to offer some recommendations.
cn: 然而，鉴于至少有一些证据表明这些生活方式改变中的一些有积极作用，加上其他明显与认知能力下降无关的好处，伯克愿意提出一些建议。

en: I think that by having people adopt a healthy lifestyle, both from a medical standpoint as well as nutritional and cognitive stimulation standpoint, we can reduce the incidence of cognitive decline, which will be proof that these factors are, in fact, important.
cn: 我认为通过使人们采取健康的生活方式，无论是从医疗角度还是从营养和认知刺激角度，我们都能降低认知能力下降的发生率，这将证明这些因素事实上是重要的。

en: James Burke of Duke University is one of the authors of a study reviewing previous research on cognitive decline.
cn: 杜克大学的詹姆斯·伯克是一项回顾认知能力下降先前研究的研究的作者之一。

en: The paper is published online by the Annals of Internal Medicine.
cn: 该论文由《内科学年鉴》在线发表。

en: So, Mike, you managed the innovation project at CucinTech.
cn: 那么，迈克，你在CucinTech负责创新项目。

en: I did, indeed.
cn: 是的，确实。

en: Well, then.
cn: 嗯，那好。

en: First, congratulations!
cn: 首先，祝贺你！

en: It seems to have been very successful.
cn: 这个项目似乎非常成功。

en: Thanks.
cn: 谢谢。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: I really helped things turn around at CucinTech.
cn: 我确实帮助CucinTech扭转了局面。

en: Was the revival in their fortunes entirely due to strategic innovation?
cn: 他们命运的复兴完全归功于战略创新吗？

en: Yes, yes.
cn: 是的，是的。

en: I think it was.
cn: 我认为是的。

en: CucinTech was a company who were very much following the pack, doing what everyone else was doing, and getting rapidly left behind.
cn: CucinTech曾经是一家随大流的公司，做别人都在做的事，很快就被甩在了后面。

en: I could see there was a lot of talent there, and some great potential, particularly in their product development.
cn: 我可以看出那里有很多人才，还有一些巨大的潜力，尤其是在他们的产品开发方面。

en: I just had to harness that somehow.
cn: 我只是必须以某种方式加以利用。

en: Was innovation at the core of the project?
cn: 创新是项目的核心吗？

en: Absolutely.
cn: 绝对是。

en: If it doesn't sound like too much of a cliché, our world is constantly changing and it's changing quickly.
cn: 如果这听起来不太像老生常谈的话，我们的世界在不断变化，而且变化很快。

en: We need to be innovating constantly to keep up with this.
cn: 我们需要不断创新以跟上这一变化。

en: Stand still, and you're lost.
cn: 停滞不前，你就会迷失。

en: No stopping to sniff the roses?
cn: 不停下来闻闻玫瑰花香吗？

en: Well, I'll do that in my personal life.
cn: 嗯，我会在个人生活中那样做。

en: Sure.
cn: 当然。

en: But as a business strategy, I'm afraid there is no stopping.
cn: 但作为一种商业战略，恐怕没有止境。

en: What exactly is strategic innovation then?
cn: 那么战略创新到底是什么？

en: Strategic innovation is the process of managing innovation, of making sure it takes place at all levels of the company and that is related to the company's overall strategy.
cn: 战略创新是管理创新的过程，确保创新发生在公司的各个层面，并与公司的整体战略相关联。

en: I see.
cn: 我明白了。

en: So, instead of innovation for innovation's sake and new products being created simply because the technology is there, the company culture must switch from these point-in-time innovations to a continuous pipeline of innovations from everywhere and everyone.
cn: 所以，不是为创新而创新，不是仅仅因为技术存在就创造新产品，公司文化必须从这些一时的创新转变为来自各处、每个人的持续创新流。

en: How did you align strategies throughout the company?
cn: 你是如何在公司范围内协调战略的？

en: I soon became aware that campaigning is useless.
cn: 我很快就意识到宣传是没有用的。

en: People take no notice.
cn: 人们不会注意。

en: Simply, it came about through good practice trickling down.
cn: 简单来说，它是通过良好实践的逐渐渗透而实现的。

en: This built consent.
cn: 这建立了共识。

en: People could see it was the best way to work.
cn: 人们可以看出这是最好的工作方式。

en: Does innovation on this scale really give a competitive advantage?
cn: 这种规模的创新真的能带来竞争优势吗？

en: I'm certain of it, absolutely, especially if it's difficult for a competitor to copy.
cn: 我对此非常肯定，尤其是如果竞争对手难以模仿的话。

en: The risk is of course that innovation may frequently lead to imitation.
cn: 风险当然是创新可能经常导致模仿。

en: But not if it's strategic?
cn: 但如果是战略性的就不会吗？

en: Precisely.
cn: 正是。

en: Thanks for talking to us.
cn: 感谢你接受我们的采访。

en: Sure.
cn: 不客气。

en: Today my guest is Dana Ivanovich, who has worked for the last 20 years as an interpreter.
cn: 今天我请到的嘉宾是唐娜·伊万诺维奇，她从事口译工作已有20年。

en: Dana, welcome.
cn: 唐娜，欢迎。

en: Thank you.
cn: 谢谢。

en: Now, I'd like to begin by saying that I have on occasions used an interpreter myself as a foreign correspondent.
cn: 现在，我想首先说，我本人作为驻外记者也曾多次使用过口译员。

en: So I'm full of admiration for what you do.
cn: 所以我对您所做的工作充满钦佩。

en: But I think your profession is sometimes underrated and many people think anyone who speaks more than one language can do it.
cn: 但我认为您的职业有时被低估了，很多人认为任何会说超过一种语言的人都能做。

en: There aren't any interpreters I know who don't have professional qualifications and training.
cn: 我认识的口译员都有专业资质并接受过培训。

en: You only really get profession after many years in the job.
cn: 只有在这个行业工作多年后你才能真正专业。

en: And am I right in saying you can divide what you do into two distinct methods: simultaneous and consecutive?
cn: 我说的对吗，你可以将你的工作分为两种不同的方法：同声传译和交替传译？

en: That's right.
cn: 没错。

en: The techniques you use are different.
cn: 你使用的技巧是不同的。

en: And a lot of interpreters will say one is easier than the other, less stressful.
cn: 很多口译员会说一种比另一种容易，压力较小。

en: Simultaneous interpreting, putting someone's words into another language more or less as they speak, sounds to me like the more difficult.
cn: 同声传译，也就是在别人说话时基本上同时将其话语翻译成另一种语言，在我看来似乎更难。

en: Well, actually no.
cn: 嗯，实际上不是。

en: Most people in the business would agree that consecutive interpreting is the more stressful.
cn: 业内大多数人都同意交替传译压力更大。

en: You have to wait for the speaker to deliver quite a chunk of language before you then put it into the second language, which puts your short-term memory under intense stress.
cn: 你必须等待讲话者说出一大段话，然后再将其翻译成第二种语言，这会给你的短期记忆带来巨大压力。

en: You make notes, I presume?
cn: 我想你会做笔记吧？

en: Absolutely.
cn: 当然。

en: Anything like numbers, names, places have to be noted down, but the rest is never translated word for word.
cn: 像数字、名字、地点之类的东西必须记下来，但其余部分从不逐字翻译。

en: You have to find a way of summarizing it, so that the message is there.
cn: 你必须找到一种方法来概括它，以便传达信息。

en: Turning every single word into the target language would put too much strain on the interpreter and slow down the whole process too much.
cn: 把每一个词都翻译成目标语言会给口译员带来太大压力，也会使整个过程过于缓慢。

en: But with simultaneous interpreting, you start translating almost as soon as the other person starts speaking.
cn: 但是在同声传译中，你几乎在对方开始说话的同时就开始翻译。

en: You must have some preparation beforehand.
cn: 你肯定事先做了一些准备。

en: Well, hopefully, the speakers will let you have an outline of the topic a day or two in advance.
cn: 嗯，希望讲话者能提前一两天给你一个主题提纲。

en: You have a little time to do research, prepare technical expressions and so on.
cn: 你有一点时间做研究，准备技术术语等等。

en: Mothers have been warned for years that sleeping with their newborn infant is a bad idea, because it increases the risk that the baby might die unexpectedly during the night.
cn: 多年来，妈妈们都被提醒与新生儿同睡不是一个好主意，因为这可能会增加婴儿在夜间意外死亡的风险。

en: But now Israeli researchers are reporting that even sleeping in the same room can have negative consequences, not for the child, but for the mother.
cn: 但现在以色列研究人员报告说，即使睡在同一个房间也可能产生负面后果，不是对孩子，而是对母亲。

en: Mothers who slept in the same room as their infants, whether in the same bed or just the same room, had poorer sleep than mothers whose baby slept elsewhere in the house.
cn: 与婴儿睡在同一个房间的母亲，无论是同床还是只是同房，其睡眠质量都比婴儿睡在房子其他地方的母亲差。

en: They woke up more frequently, were awake approximately 20 minutes longer per night, and had shorter periods of uninterrupted sleep.
cn: 她们更频繁地醒来，每晚大约多醒20分钟，并且不间断睡眠的时间更短。

en: These results held true even taking into account that many of the women in the study were breast-feeding their babies.
cn: 即使考虑到研究中的许多妇女正在母乳喂养，这些结果仍然成立。

en: Infants, on the other hand, didn't appear to have worse sleep whether they slept in the same or different room from their mothers.
cn: 另一方面，无论婴儿是与母亲同房还是分房睡，他们的睡眠似乎没有变差。

en: The researchers acknowledge that since the families they studied were all middle-class Israelis, it's possible the results would be different in different cultures.
cn: 研究人员承认，由于他们研究的家庭都是以色列中产阶级，结果在不同文化中可能会有所不同。

en: Lead author Lyati Sotski wrote in an email that the research team also didn't measure fathers' sleep, so it's possible that their sleep patterns could also be causing the sleep disruptions for mums.
cn: 主要作者利亚蒂·索茨基在一封电子邮件中写道，研究团队也没有测量父亲的睡眠，所以他们的睡眠模式也可能导致母亲的睡眠中断。

en: Right now, to reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome, the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that mothers not sleep in the same bed as their babies, but sleep in the same room.
cn: 目前，为了降低婴儿猝死综合征的风险，美国儿科学会建议母亲不要和婴儿同床睡，但要睡在同一个房间。

en: The Israeli study suggests that doing so may be best for the baby, but may take a toll on mum.
cn: 以色列的研究表明，这样做可能对婴儿最好，但可能会对母亲造成伤害。

en: The US has already lost more than a third of the native languages that existed before European colonization and the remaining 192 are classed by UNESCO as ranging between unsafe and extinct.
cn: 美国已经失去了欧洲殖民之前存在的超过三分之一的本土语言，剩下的192种被联合国教科文组织列为从危险到灭绝不等。

en: We need more funding and more effort to return these languages to everyday use, says Fred Nawusky of the National Museum of the American Indian.
cn: 美国印第安人国家博物馆的弗雷德·努瓦斯基说，我们需要更多的资金和更多的努力来让这些语言恢复日常使用。

en: We are making progress, but money needs to be spent on revitalizing languages, not just documenting them.
cn: 我们正在取得进展，但资金需要用于振兴语言，而不仅仅是记录它们。

en: Some 40 languages mainly in California and Oklahoma where thousands of Indians were forced to relocate in the 19th century have fewer than 10 native speakers.
cn: 大约40种语言，主要分布在加利福尼亚州和俄克拉荷马州，19世纪那里有成千上万的印第安人被强制迁移，这些语言如今只有不到10名母语使用者。

en: Part of the issue is that tribal groups themselves don't always believe their languages are endangered until they are down to the last handful of speakers.
cn: 部分问题在于，部落群体自己往往不认为自己的语言濒危，直到只剩下最后几个使用者。

en: But progress is being made through emerging schools, because if you teach children when they are young, it will stay with them as adults and that's the future, says Mr. Nawusky, a Comanche Indian.
cn: 但通过新兴学校的努力正在取得进展，因为如果你在孩子年幼时教他们，语言会伴随他们成年，这就是未来，科曼奇印第安人努瓦斯基先生说。

en: Such schools have become a model in Hawaii, but the islanders' local language is still classed by UNESCO as critically endangered because only 1,000 people speak it.
cn: 这类学校在夏威夷已成为典范，但岛民的本地语言仍被联合国教科文组织列为极度濒危，因为只有1000人使用它。

en: The decline in American Indian languages has its historical roots.
cn: 美国印第安语言的衰落有其历史根源。

en: In the mid-19th century, the US government adopted a policy of Americanizing Indian children by removing them from their homes and culture.
cn: 在19世纪中期，美国政府采取了一项政策，通过将印第安儿童从他们的家园和文化中带走，使他们美国化。

en: Within a few generations, most had forgotten their native tongues.
cn: 几代之内，大多数人忘记了自己的母语。

en: Another challenge to language survival is television.
cn: 语言生存的另一个挑战是电视。

en: It has brought English into homes, and pushed out traditional storytelling and family time together, accelerating the extinction of native languages.
cn: 它将英语带入家庭，排挤掉了传统的讲故事和家庭团聚时间，加速了本土语言的灭绝。

en: Greg Rosen lost his job as a sales manager nearly three years ago and is still unemployed.
cn: 格雷格·罗森近三年前失去了销售经理的工作，至今仍失业。

en: It literally is like something in a dream to remember what it's like to actually be able to go out and put in a day's work and receive a day's pay.
cn: 回想能够真正外出工作一天并拿到一天工资的感觉，简直就像梦中的事情一样。

en: At first Rosen bought groceries and made house payments with the help from unemployment insurance.
cn: 起初，罗森在失业保险的帮助下购买食品杂货并支付房款。

en: It pays laid-off workers up to half of their previous wages while they look for work.
cn: 它在失业者找工作期间支付给他们以前工资的一半。

en: But now, that insurance has run out for him and he has to make tough choices.
cn: 但现在，他的保险金已经用完了，他必须做出艰难的选择。

en: He's cut back on medications and he no longer helps support his disabled mother.
cn: 他减少了药物开支，也不再帮助供养他残疾的母亲。

en: It is a devastating experience.
cn: 这是一次毁灭性的经历。

en: New research says the US recession is now over.
cn: 新的研究称美国经济衰退现在已经结束。

en: But many people remain unemployed and unemployed workers face difficult odds.
cn: 但许多人仍然失业，失业工人面临困难。

en: There is literally only one job opening for every five unemployed workers, so four out of five unemployed workers have actually no chance of finding a new job.
cn: 实际上每五个失业工人只有一个职位空缺，所以五分之四的失业工人实际上没有机会找到新工作。

en: Businesses have downsized or shut down across America, leading fewer job opportunities for those in search of work.
cn: 全美各地的企业都在裁员或关闭，导致找工作的人机会更少。

en: Experts who monitor unemployment statistics here in Bucks County, Pennsylvania say about 28,000 people are unemployed and many of them are jobless due to no fault of their own.
cn: 在宾夕法尼亚州巴克斯县监测失业统计数据的专家说，约有28000人失业，其中许多人的失业并非自身过错所致。

en: That's where the Bucks County Careerlink comes in.
cn: 这就是巴克斯县职业链接发挥作用的地方。

en: Local director Elizabeth Walsh says they provide training and guidance to help unemployed workers find local job opportunities.
cn: 当地主管伊丽莎白·沃尔什说，他们提供培训和指导，帮助失业工人找到当地的就业机会。

en: So here's the job opening.
cn: 这里是职位空缺。

en: Here's the job seeker.
cn: 这里是求职者。

en: Match them together under one roof, she says.
cn: 她说，在同一个屋檐下将他们匹配起来。

en: But the lack of work opportunities in Bucks County limits how much she can help.
cn: 但巴克斯县缺乏工作机会限制了她能提供的帮助。

en: Rosen says he hopes Congress will take action.
cn: 罗森说他希望国会采取行动。

en: This month, he launched the Ninety-Niners Union, an umbrella organization of eighteen Internet-based grass roots groups of Ninety-Niners.
cn: 本月，他发起了99人联盟，这是一个由18个基于互联网的99人草根团体组成的伞式组织。

en: Their goal is to convince lawmakers to extend unemployment benefits.
cn: 他们的目标是说服立法者延长失业救济金。

en: But Pennsylvania State representative Scott Petri says governments simply do not have enough money to extend unemployment insurance.
cn: 但宾夕法尼亚州众议员斯科特·佩特里表示，政府根本没有足够的资金来延长失业保险。

en: He thinks the best way to help the long-term unemployed is to allow private citizens to invest in local companies that can create more jobs.
cn: 他认为帮助长期失业者的最好办法是允许普通公民投资于能够创造更多就业机会的当地公司。

en: But the boost in investor confidence needed for the plan to work will take time—time that Rosen says still requires him to buy food and make monthly mortgage payments.
cn: 但该计划所需的投资者信心提振需要时间——罗森说，这段时间他仍然需要购买食物并支付每月的抵押贷款。

en: Rosen says he'll use the last of his savings to try to hang onto the home he worked for more than twenty years to buy.
cn: 罗森说他将用最后的积蓄努力保住他工作了二十多年才买下的房子。

en: But once that money is gone, he says he doesn't know what he'll do.
cn: 但一旦那笔钱用完，他说他不知道该怎么办。

en: Earlier this year, British explorer Pen Hadow and his team trekked for three months across the frozen Arctic Ocean, taking measurements and recording observations about the ice.
cn: 今年早些时候，英国探险家佩恩·哈多和他的团队在北冰洋的冰面上跋涉了三个月，进行测量并记录关于冰的观测数据。

en: Well, we've been led to believe that we would encounter a good proportion of this older, thicker, technically multi-year ice that's been around for a few years and just get thicker and thicker.
cn: 我们一直相信会遇到相当大比例的更古老、更厚、技术上多年形成的冰，这种冰已经存在了几年，而且会越来越厚。

en: We actually found there wasn't any multi-year ice at all.
cn: 我们实际上发现根本没有多年冰。

en: Satellite observations and submarine service over the past few years had shown less ice in the polar region.
cn: 过去几年的卫星观测和潜艇服务显示极地地区的冰减少了。

en: But the recent measurements show the loss is more pronounced than previously thought.
cn: 但最近的测量显示，冰的减少比之前想象的更为显著。

en: We are looking at roughly 80 percent loss of ice cover on the Arctic ocean in ten years, roughly ten years and 100 percent loss in nearly twenty years.
cn: 我们预计大约十年内北冰洋冰盖将减少约80%，大约十年，而近二十年内将完全消失。

en: Cambridge scientist Peter Wadhams, who's been measuring and monitoring the Arctic since 1971, says the decline is irreversible.
cn: 自1971年以来一直在测量和监测北极的剑桥科学家彼得·沃德姆斯说，这种下降是不可逆转的。

en: The more you lose, the more open water is created, the more warming goes on in that open water during the summer, the less ice forms in the winter, the more melt there is the following summer.
cn: 冰越少，形成的开放水域越多，夏季开放水域的变暖越多，冬季形成的冰越少，次年夏季的融化就越多。

en: It becomes a breakdown process where everything ends up accelerating until it's all gone.
cn: 这变成一个崩溃过程，一切都加速进行，直到完全消失。

en: Martin Summercorn runs the Arctic program for the environmental charity the World Wildlife Fund.
cn: 马丁·萨默康负责世界野生动物基金会环境慈善机构的北极项目。

en: The Arctic sea ice holds a central position in the earth's climate system and it's deteriorating faster than expected.
cn: 北极海冰在地球气候系统中占据核心地位，而且它的恶化速度比预期的要快。

en: Actually, it has to translate into more urgency to deal with the climate change problem and reduce emissions.
cn: 实际上，这必须转化为更大的紧迫性来应对气候变化问题并减少排放。

en: Summercorn says a plan to reduce greenhouse gas emissions blamed for global warming needs to come out of the Copenhagen Climate Change Summit in December.
cn: 萨默康说，一项减少被认为是导致全球变暖的温室气体排放的计划需要在12月的哥本哈根气候变化峰会上出台。

en: We have to basically achieve there—the commitment to deal with the problem now.
cn: 我们基本上必须在那里实现——现在应对问题的承诺。

en: That's the minimum.
cn: 这是最低要求。

en: We have to do that equitably, and we have to find a commitment that is quick.
cn: 我们必须公平地做到这一点，而且我们必须找到一个快速的承诺。

en: Wadhams echoes the need for urgency.
cn: 沃德姆斯呼应了紧迫性的需要。

en: The carbon that we've put into the atmosphere keeps having a warming effect for 100 years.
cn: 我们排放到大气中的碳会持续产生100年的变暖效应。

en: So we have to cut back rapidly now.
cn: 所以我们现在必须迅速削减。

en: Because it would take a long time to work its way through into our response by the atmosphere.
cn: 因为需要很长时间才能通过大气对我们的应对产生影响。

en: We can't switch off global warming just by being good in future.
cn: 我们不能仅仅通过在未来表现良好来关闭全球变暖。

en: We have to start being good now.
cn: 我们现在就必须开始表现良好。

en: Wadhams says there is no easy technological fix to climate change.
cn: 沃德姆斯说，气候变化没有简单的技术解决方案。

en: He and other scientists say there are basically two options to replacing fossil fuels, generating energy with renewables or embracing nuclear power.
cn: 他和其他科学家说，取代化石燃料基本上有两种选择，用可再生能源发电或采用核能。

en: From a very early age, some children exhibit better self-control than others.
cn: 从很小的时候起，一些孩子就表现出比其他人更好的自控力。

en: Now, a new study that began with about 1,000 children in New Zealand has tracked how a child's low self-control can predict poor health, money troubles and even a criminal record in their adult years.
cn: 现在，一项以新西兰约1000名儿童为起点的新的研究追踪了儿童低自控力如何预示他们在成年后的健康不佳、经济问题甚至犯罪记录。

en: Researchers have been studying this group of children for decades now.
cn: 研究人员研究这组儿童已有几十年了。

en: Some of their earliest observations have to do with the level of self-control the youngsters displayed.
cn: 他们最早的一些观察与年轻人表现出的自控力水平有关。

en: Parents, teachers, even the kids themselves, scored the youngsters on measures like "acting before thinking" and "persistence in reaching goals".
cn: 家长、老师，甚至孩子们自己，都在“行动前思考”和“坚持达成目标”等方面给年轻人打分。

en: The children of the study are now adults in their thirties.
cn: 研究中的孩子们现在已是三十多岁的成年人。

en: Terrie Moffitt of Duke University and her research colleagues found that kids with self-control issues tended to grow up to become adults with a far more troubling set of issues to deal with.
cn: 杜克大学的特里·莫菲特和她的研究同事发现，有自控力问题的孩子长大后往往会成为面临更麻烦问题的成年人。

en: The children who had the lowest self-control when they were age 3 to 10, later on had the most health problems in their thirties, and they had the worst financial situation.
cn: 3到10岁时自控力最低的孩子，在三十多岁时健康问题最多，经济状况也最差。

en: And they were more likely to have a criminal record and to be raising a child as a single parent on a very low income.
cn: 而且他们更可能有犯罪记录，并且更可能作为单亲父母以很低的收入抚养孩子。

en: Speaking from New Zealand via Skype, Moffitt explained that self-control problems were widely observed and weren't just a feature of a small group of misbehaving kids.
cn: 莫菲特通过Skype从新西兰发言解释说，自控力问题被广泛观察到，不仅仅是一小部分行为不端的孩子的特征。

en: Even the children who had above-average self-control as pre-schoolers, could have benefited from more self-control training.
cn: 即使是学龄前自控力高于平均水平的孩子，也能从更多的自控力训练中受益。

en: They could have improved their financial situation and their physical and mental health situation 30 years later.
cn: 他们本可以在30年后改善他们的经济状况和身心健康状况。

en: So, children with minor self-control problems were likely as adults to have minor health problems, and so on.
cn: 所以，有轻微自控力问题的孩子在成年后可能有轻微的健康问题，以此类推。

en: Moffitt said it's still unclear why some children have better self-control than others, though she says other researchers have found that it's mostly a learned behavior, with relatively little genetic influence.
cn: 莫菲特说，目前还不清楚为什么有些孩子的自控力比其他人好，尽管她说其他研究人员发现这主要是一种后天习得的行为，遗传影响相对较小。

en: But good self-control can be set to run in families in that children who have good self-control are more likely to grow up to be healthy and prosperous parents.
cn: 但良好的自控力可以在家庭中传承，因为自控力好的孩子更有可能成长为健康、富有的父母。

en: Whereas some of the low self-control study members are more likely to be single parents with a very low income and the parent is in poor health and likely to be a heavy substance abuser.
cn: 而自控力低的研究对象更可能成为收入极低的单亲父母，且健康状况不佳，很可能是重度药物滥用者。

en: So that's not a good atmosphere for a child.
cn: 所以这对孩子来说不是一个好的环境。

en: So it looks as though self-control is something that in one generation can disadvantage the next generation.
cn: 所以看起来自控力是一代人对下一代不利的因素。

en: But the good news is that Moffitt says self-control can be taught by parents, and through school curricula that have proved to be effective.
cn: 但好消息是，莫菲特说自控力可以由父母教导，也可以通过已被证明有效的学校课程来培养。

en: Terrie Moffitt's paper "On the Link Between Childhood Self-control and Adults' Status Decades Later" is published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
cn: 特里·莫菲特的论文《论童年自控力与数十年后成年人状况之间的联系》发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

en: Professor Henderson, could you give us a brief overview of what you do, where you work and your main area of research?
cn: 亨德森教授，您能否简要概述一下您做何工作、就职于何处以及您的主要研究领域？

en: Well, the Center for Climate Research where I work links the science of climate change to issues around economics and policy.
cn: 唔，我所就职的气候研究中心将气候变化科学与经济学相关问题、政策相关问题联系起来。

en: Some of our research is to do with the likely impacts of climate change and all of the associated risks.
cn: 我们的一些研究涉及气候变化的影响及各种相关风险。

en: And how strong is the evidence that climate change is happening?
cn: 那气候变化正在发生的证据有多可靠？

en: That is really something we need to be worried about.
cn: 这确是我们需要担心的。

en: Well most of the science of climate change, particularly that to do with global warming, is simply fact.
cn: 嗯，气候变化科学的大部分内容，特别是与全球变暖相关的内容，的确都是确凿事实。

en: But other aspects of the science are less certain or at least more disputed.
cn: 不过，其它方面的（气候变化）研究并没那么确定，或至少更具争议。

en: And so we're really talking about risk.
cn: 因此，我们实际是在讨论风险。

en: What the economics tells us is that it's probably cheaper to avoid climate change to avoid the risk than it is to deal with the likely consequences.
cn: 经济学告诉我们，避免气候变化——规避其风险——比应付其可能后果似乎更划算。

en: So what are we doing?
cn: 那我们在做什么？

en: What can we do about it?
cn: 我们对此又能做什么？

en: Well, I would argue that we need to develop the science specifically to understand the likely impacts of climate change in different contexts.
cn: 我认为，我们要着重发展这门科学、认识不同环境下气候变化的影响。

en: As I said, we need to understand the best ways of avoiding climate change.
cn: 像我说过的，我们要了解避免气候变化的最佳方式。

en: And this will involve a huge transition to low-carbon energy systems.
cn: 这涉及迈向低碳能源体系的大转型。

en: And the transition is a tremendous priority.
cn: 这项转型是头等大事。

en: And for this to happen, we may need action on a global scale.
cn: 要做到这点，我们也许要在全球范围采取行动。

en: From a political perspective, We need to understand the terms on which major countries like China and the USA might sign up to a global agreement because at the moment we don't have that consensus.
cn: 从政治的角度看，我们要了解中国、美国这样的主要国家可能就哪些条款签署全球性协议，因为目前我们尚未达成共识。

en: Right.
cn: 是这样。

en: And we also need to plan ahead so that we are in a position to deal with the likely levels of climate change which are already inevitable, and even more so, too, for the levels that are likely if we don't get those global agreements.
cn: 而且，我们还要提早计划，这样我们就可以应对现已无可避免的气候可能变化水平，更可应对全球协议无法达成所可能带来的气候变化水平。

en: I have many business English students.
cn: 我有许多商务英语专业的学生。

en: When I teach in the classroom, we often end up talking about things like success and what leads to success.
cn: 当我在教室上课时，我们常常以讨论成功以及什么会带来成功之类的话题来结束。

en: And it's interesting that many of them mention the element of luck.
cn: 他们中的许多人都提及运气的因素，这很有意思。

en: Right.
cn: 是的。

en: Luck is important to success.
cn: 运气对于成功来说很重要。

en: But since you've seen that fantastic video on the TED Talks website by Richard St. John, he doesn't mention luck at all.
cn: 但是你们也看到了理查德·圣约翰在TED演讲网站上的精彩视频，他就根本没有提到运气。

en: Well, I'm a firm believer that people can make their own luck.
cn: 嗯，我坚信人们可以创造自己的运气。

en: I mean what people regard as luck, you can actually create, to a degree.
cn: 我的意思是人们视为运气的东西，在某种程度上，你实际上可以去创造。

en: Sure.
cn: 当然。

en: I think a lot of what people consider "luck is attributed to how you respond to the opportunities that come your way.
cn: 我认为人们觉得是运气的东西都归因于你如何回应出现在你身边的机遇。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: Very good point.
cn: 说得非常好。

en: Seizing the opportunities.
cn: 抓住机遇。

en: But was there any point in the video that you thought was particularly interesting?
cn: 但是视频里有没有哪一点你觉得特别有意思呢？

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: Actually there was.
cn: 实际上确实有。

en: Something very impressive to me is many people think that luck is important and that natural talent is something you must have in order to be successful.
cn: 令我印象非常深刻的是许多人认为运气很重要，而且要想成功的话，你必须拥有天赋。

en: And in the video we saw, the point about getting good at something is not about having some natural talent.
cn: 在视频中，我们看到变得擅长某种东西的关键并不是说要有一些天赋。

en: It's all about practice, practice, practice.
cn: 而是指要练习、练习、再练习。

en: Definitely yeah.
cn: 肯定是这样的。

en: Natural talent helps in some way but at the end of the day you really do need to work hard and get really, really good at what you do.
cn: 天赋在某种程度上会起作用，但最后你真正需要做的是努力工作，对自己的职业变得真正精通。

en: Sure.
cn: 当然。

en: I thought one interesting thing in the video was the idea of passion being so important.
cn: 我觉得视频里有意思的是热情很重要这一观点。

en: And there're people who really love what they do — of course, you're going to want to work harder and put the time and effort into it.
cn: 有些人真的热爱他们所做的事——自然而然，会想要更努力地工作，投入时间和精力。

en: And the funny thing is that if you love what you do and are really passionate about it and work really hard, the money kind of comes automatically.
cn: 有意思的是如果你热爱你所做的事，并且真的对于它充满热情，真的努力，钱什么的自然而然就会来。

en: Devils Tower, the first national monument in America, could almost be mistaken for the stump of an enormous tree.
cn: 魔鬼塔是美国第一座国家纪念碑，它很容易被误认为是一个巨大的树桩。

en: Its sheer rock sides sweep up from a broad base until they cut off abruptly at the flat summit.
cn: 其陡峭的岩石边从宽阔的基底上拔地而起，直到平坦的峰顶突然被切断。

en: Rising more than 1,000 feet in the middle of the gently rolling plains of Wyoming, the massive column of rock looks as though it was dropped down into this location from a different time and place.
cn: 超过1000多英尺的巨大岩石柱耸立在怀俄明州平缓的平原中央，看起来就像是从另外一个时空坠入此处。

en: In a sense it was.
cn: 从某种意义上来说，它的确如此。

en: Devils Tower is a relic of the past, when the molten rock of the earth's core forced its way to the surface to form the throat of a volcano.
cn: 魔鬼塔是历史的遗迹，当时正值地球核心的熔融岩石被挤压到地表形成火山口。

en: As the centuries passed, the rock cooled and hardened, shrinking and cracking into long columns.
cn: 几个世纪过去了，岩石冷却变硬，并收缩开裂成长柱。

en: Born in fire and fury, Devils Tower was then shaped by the slow, gentle work of wind and water.
cn: 诞生于烈火与怒焰的魔鬼塔，随后又被和风静水加以塑造。

en: The outer layers of the volcano were worn away, until the hard core stood completely exposed.
cn: 火山外层被侵蚀，直到坚硬的核心完全暴露出来。

en: Small wonder that an Indian legend described Devils Tower as being formed by supernatural powers.
cn: 难怪一个印第安传说称魔鬼塔是由超自然力量形成的。

en: The legend says that when seven girls were attacked by bears, they took refuge on top of a small rock, and they appealed to the Rock God for help.
cn: 传说中，七个女孩被熊袭击后，躲避在一块小岩石上，并向岩神寻求帮助。

en: The god caused the rock to grow and to lift the girls far above the ground, while its sides were scored by the claws of the angry bears.
cn: 岩神让岩石生长，把女孩们举到远离地面的地方，而岩石的四周则被愤怒的熊用熊掌抓伤了。

en: Even today, says the legend, the girls can be seen above the towering rock, as seven shining stars in the night sky.
cn: 据传说，即便到了今天，在高耸的岩石上还能看到女孩们，她们就像夜空中七颗闪亮的星星。

en: It's no accident that most gas stations have a convenience stores attached.
cn: 大多数加油站都附带便利店，这并非偶然。

en: Few of us can fill up the tank without buying a few snacks, cigarettes, soft drinks or other items we can live without.
cn: 几乎没有人不在加油的时候买点零食、香烟、软饮或其他可有可无的物件。

en: "I deserve it."
cn: “我应得的。”

en: That's what hard-working men and women say to justify their lavish vacations, big stereo systems or regular restaurant meals.
cn: 这是辛苦工作的男男女女证明自己理应享受豪华假期、大型音响系统或者定期下馆子的说辞。

en: They do deserve such indulgences.
cn: 这些享受确实是他们应得的。

en: However, they also deserve a home of their own, a secure retirement and freedom from worrying about unpaid bills.
cn: 但是，他们也理应拥有属于自己的家，有保障的退休生活，以及不必忧心欠账的自在。

en: No one should have to live with what a Texas mother described as constant stress, tension, even fear about money.
cn: 没有人理应忍受一位德克萨斯母亲称之为因金钱而产生的长期压力、紧张、甚至忧虑。

en: Sadly, the pleasure that comes from extravagances often disappears long before the bills do.
cn: 很遗憾，因奢侈消费而来的愉悦往往早在账单付清之前就会消失不见。

en: The video camera that one single mother bought for a special occasion, for example, is not much fun now.
cn: 例如，一位单亲妈妈为某种特殊场合而购买的摄影机，现在就不怎么好玩了。

en: She's figured out that it will take her another three years to pay it off at $30 a month.
cn: 她已经算清楚，每月还付30美元，还需三年才能还清全款。

en: And the New Yorkers who spent a bundle on an outdoor hot tub now admit they rarely use it, "because we can't afford to heat it in winter."
cn: 而且那些花一大笔钱购置户外热水浴缸的纽约人现在承认，他们很少用它，“因为我们无力负担冬季加热浴缸的费用。”

en: The solution - set priorities, add up the annual cost of each item, then consider what else she could buy with the same money.
cn: 解决措施是，分清主次，合计各项物品的全年花费，然后思考花同样的钱可以买点什么别的东西。

en: That will help you decide which items are really worth it.
cn: 这能帮助你确定哪些物品真的物有所值。

en: One Chicago woman, for example, discovered that daily lunches with coworkers cost her $2000 a year; she decided to take lunch to work instead.
cn: 例如，芝加哥一位女士发现，每天和同事共用午餐一年花费2000美元；她决定带午餐上班。

en: "I now put $20 a week into my vacation fund and another 20 into retirement savings," she says.
cn: “现在，我每周往假日基金存20美元，再往退休储蓄存20美元，”她说。

en: "Those mean more to me than lunch."
cn: “比起午餐，这些对我更重要。”

en: Let's say you start to brainstorm a list of all the emotions you've ever experienced.
cn: 假设你开始一场头脑风暴，列出你所体验过的所有情绪。

en: Just for fun, try it now.
cn: 就是图个乐子，现在试试吧。

en: What's on your list?
cn: 你的列表上有什么呢？

en: Chances are, you included things like happy, sad, excited, angry, afraid, grateful, proud, scared, confused, stressed, relaxed and amazed.
cn: 有可能你列出的情绪包括：欢喜、悲伤、兴奋、愤怒、害怕、感激、自豪、恐慌、困惑、压抑、轻松和惊奇。

en: Now sort your list into two categories—positive emotions and negative emotions.
cn: 现在把你列表上的情绪分成两类：积极情绪和消极情绪。

en: Feeling both positive and negative emotions is a natural part of being human.
cn: 既感觉到积极情绪、也感觉到消极情绪，这是人之为人的自然一部分。

en: We might use the word "negative" to describe more difficult emotions, but it doesn't mean those emotions are bad or we shouldn't have them.
cn: 我们可能会用“负面”一词来描述那些更为麻烦的情绪，但这并不意味着这些情绪是坏的，或我们不该有这些情绪。

en: Still, most people would probably rather feel a positive emotion than a negative one.
cn: 然而，大多数人可能更愿意感受积极情绪而非消极情绪。

en: It's likely you'd prefer to feel happy instead of sad, or confident instead of insecure.
cn: 你可能会更喜欢感到欢乐而非难过，更喜欢感到自信而非没有把握。

en: What matters is how our emotions are balanced—how much of each type of emotion, positive or negative, we experience.
cn: 重要的是我们如何平衡情绪——每一种情绪，积极情绪也好、消极情绪也罢，我们经历多少。

en: Negative emotions warn us of threats or challenges that we may need to deal with.
cn: 消极的情绪提醒我们可能有需要处理的威胁或挑战。

en: For example, fear can alert us to possible danger.
cn: 比如，恐惧使我们警觉可能存在的危险。

en: It's a signal that we might need to protect ourselves.
cn: 这是我们可能需要自我保护的信号。

en: Angry feelings warn us that someone is stepping on our toes, crossing a boundary, or violating our trust.
cn: 愤怒的感觉提醒我们，有人在踩我们的脚趾、在越界或在违背我们的信任。

en: Anger can be a signal that we might need to act on our own behalf.
cn: 愤怒是我们或许需为自己出头的信号。

en: Negative emotions focus our awareness.
cn: 消极情绪集中我们的意识。

en: They help us to zero in on a problem so we can deal with it.
cn: 它们帮助我们将精力集中在一个问题上以便将其解决。

en: But too many negative emotions can make us feel overwhelmed, anxious, exhausted or stressed out.
cn: 但太多的消极情绪可能会使我们感到难以承受、焦虑不安、精疲力尽或极度紧张。

en: When negative emotions are out of balance, problems might seem too big to handle.
cn: 当负面情绪失衡时，可能问题似乎太大而无法处理。

en: The more we dwell on negative emotions, the more negative we begin to feel.
cn: 我们越是老想着消极情绪，我们越是会开始感到消极。

en: Focusing on negativity just keeps it going.
cn: 将注意力集中在消极情绪上只会让这样的情绪持续下去。

en: Positive emotions balance out negative ones, but they have other powerful benefits, too.
cn: 积极情绪平衡了消极情绪，但积极情绪也有其他巨大的好处。

en: Instead of narrowing our focus like negative emotions do, positive emotions affect our brains in ways that increase our awareness, attention and memory.
cn: 积极情绪会通过增强我们的感悟力、注意力和记忆力的方式影响我们的大脑，而非像消极情绪那样缩小我们注意力的集中点。

en: They help us take in more information, hold several ideas in mind at once, and understand how different ideas relate to each other.
cn: 这些积极情绪帮助我们接收更多的信息，即刻记住几个概念，并理解不同想法如何相互关联。

en: When positive emotions open us up to new possibilities, we are more able to learn and build on our skills.
cn: 当积极情绪为我们开启崭新的可能性时，我们便能够更好地学习并拓展我们的技能。

en: That leads to doing better on tasks and tests.
cn: 这使得我们在任务和测试中表现得更为出色。

en: People who have plenty of positive emotions in their everyday lives tend to be happier, healthier, learn better, and get along well with others.
cn: 在日常生活中，那些充满积极情绪的人往往更快乐，更健康，学得更好，并能与别人融洽相处。

en: In the past few months, I've been traveling for weeks at a time with only one suitcase of clothes.
cn: 过去几个月里，我一直在旅行，每趟旅行都接连好几个星期，随身只带一手提箱衣服。

en: One day, I was invited to an important event, and I wanted to wear something special for it.
cn: 有一天，我被邀请参加一个重要的活动，我想为这个场合穿得特别一点。

en: I looked through my suitcase but couldn't find anything to wear.
cn: 我翻遍手提箱，却找不到任何可以穿的。

en: I was lucky to be at the technology conference then, and I had access to 3D printers.
cn: 当时，我有幸正在参加技术会议，可以使用3D打印机。

en: So I quickly designed a skirt on my computer, and I loaded the file on the printer.
cn: 所以我很快在电脑上设计了一条裙子，然后把文件载入打印机。

en: It just printed the pieces overnight.
cn: 连夜打印出裙子的各个部件。

en: The next morning, I just took all the pieces, assembled them together in my hotel room, and this is actually the skirt that I'm wearing right now.
cn: 第二天早上，我就拿着所有部件，在我的酒店房间里把它们组装起来，实际上就是我现在穿的裙子。

en: So it wasn't the first time that I printed clothes.
cn: 这不是我第一次打印衣服。

en: For my senior collection at fashion design school, I decided to try and 3D print an entire fashion collection from my home.
cn: 为了时装设计学院的毕业时装展，我决定在家中尝试3D打印整个时装系列。

en: The problem was that I barely knew anything about 3D printing, and I had only nine months to figure out how to print five fashionable looks.
cn: 问题是我对3D打印几乎一无所知，而且只有9个月的时间来弄清楚如何打印五种时尚款式。

en: I always felt most creative when I worked from home.
cn: 我一直觉得我在家工作时极富创意。

en: I loved experimenting with new materials, and I always tried to develop new techniques to make the most unique textiles for my fashion projects.
cn: 我喜欢尝试新材料，并一直在努力开发新技术，为我的时尚项目制作最独特的纺织物。

en: One summer break, I came here to New York for an internship at a fashion house in Chinatown.
cn: 有一年暑假，我来到了纽约，在唐人街的一家时装店实习。

en: We worked on two incredible dresses that were 3D printed.
cn: 我们制作了两件3D打印的惊艳服装。

en: They were amazing—like you can see here.
cn: 它们非常棒——你可以从这里看到。

en: But I had a few problems with them.
cn: 但是我在这些服装上遇到一些问题。

en: They were made from hard plastics and that's why they were very breakable.
cn: 它们是由硬塑料制成的，所以非常易碎。

en: The models couldn't sit in them, and they even got scratched from the plastics under their arms.
cn: 模特不能穿着它们坐下，他们甚至被手臂下的塑料刮伤。

en: So now, the main challenge was to find the right material for printing clothes with, I mean the material you feed the printer with.
cn: 因此现在，主要的挑战是找到适用于打印衣服的材料，我指的是你放入打印机的材料。

en: The breakthrough came when I was introduced to Filaflex, which is a new kind of printing material.
cn: 突破性进展出现在我初次了解新型打印材料Filaflex之后。

en: It's strong, yet very flexible.
cn: 它非常结实，却很有弹性。

en: And with it, I was able to print the first garment, a red jacket that had the word "freedom" embedded into it.
cn: 有了它，我成功打印出第一件衣服，一件镶有“自由”字样的红色外套。

en: And actually, you can easily download this jacket, and change the word to something else.
cn: 实际上，你可以轻松地下载这件夹克，并将这个词语改成别的内容。

en: For example, your name or your sweetheart's name.
cn: 例如你的名字或你爱人的名字。

en: So I think in the future, materials will evolve, and they will look and feel like fabrics we know today, like cotton or silk.
cn: 所以我认为在未来，材料将会进一步发展，它们的外观和质感将像我们今天所知道的面料——比如棉布或丝绸一样。

en: Welcome to the third lecture in our series on the future of small businesses in Europe.
cn: 欢迎来到“欧洲小企业未来”系列讲座的第三讲。

en: The purpose of today's lecture, as you have seen from the title and the abstract, is to examine in more detail the problems facing small- and medium-sized enterprises which arise at least in part from having to adapt to rapid advances in technology.
cn: 正如你从标题和简介中看到的，今天讲座的目的是更细致地探讨中小型企业面临的问题，这些问题出现，至少有一部分原因是我们不得不适应科技的迅速发展。

en: And I want to look at these both from a financial and from a personnel point of view and to offer a few hopefully effective solutions.
cn: 我想从财务和人事的角度考虑这些问题，并提供一些有望奏效的解决方案。

en: Here we have three of the most important problems facing small businesses that I want to look at today.
cn: 今天我想谈谈小企业面临的三个最重要的问题。

en: First, keeping up with the pace of technological change, recruiting high quality staff in a time of skills shortages in IT as a whole and in a highly competitive market, and the issue of retaining staff once they've been recruited and trained.
cn: 首先是紧跟科技变革的步伐，（其次是）在IT业整体面临高技能人才短缺及市场竞争激烈的条件下招聘高质量员工，（最后是）在聘用和培训结束后留住这些员工的问题。

en: Now, all of these problems involve significant costs for all businesses.
cn: 现在，对各企业而言，所有这些问题都涉及相当高的成本。

en: But they are particularly challenging issues for small- and medium-sized enterprises.
cn: 但对中小企业而言，这些问题尤其具有挑战性。

en: And those costs would vary depending on the size and scale of the businesses.
cn: 这些成本会因企业的大小和规模而各异。

en: So let's come to the first issue on our list which is keeping pace with developments in technology.
cn: 那么我们来看看列表上的第一个问题：紧跟科技发展的步伐。

en: Now we all know that the technology industry is intensely competitive with new products being launched all year round as the various companies strive to compete with each other, rather than, say, once a year or every couple of years.
cn: 现在我们都知道，由于各家公司都在卖力比拼，科技行业竞争激烈，一年到头都会有新产品投放，而不是，比方说，一年一次或几年一次。

en: And this is a real headache for smaller businesses.
cn: 这对较小的企业来说真的很头疼。

en: So, let's imagine we have a small company which is doing OK.
cn: 那么想象一下，我们有一家经营得还行的小公司。

en: It's just about making a profit and it spends most of its income on the overheads.
cn: 这家公司一心想盈利，大部分收入都花在日常管理费用上。

en: So for a company in this situation, keeping up to date with the latest technology, even if it's only for the benefit of key staff, this can be hugely expensive.
cn: 因此，对于一家处于这种情况下的公司来说，跟上最新技术的步伐都可能极为昂贵，即使这只是为了核心员工的利益。

en: So in my view, some creative thinking needs to come in here to find ways to help companies in this situation to stay ahead in the game, but at the same time, to remain technologically competitive.
cn: 所以在我看来，需要引入一些创造性思维，来寻找一些方法帮助处于这种情形下的公司保持领先地位，但同时又保持技术上的竞争力。

en: Well, there's a possibility that small groups of companies with similar requirements but not directly competing with each other—they could share the cost of upgrading in much the same way as, let's say, an intranet operates within large organizations.
cn: 有一种可能，就是那些有类似要求、但不构成直接竞争的一小群公司——它们可以共同承担升级成本，所用的方法，打个比方，就跟大企业中运行的内联网差不多。

en: In fact, cost-sharing could be a very practical solution, especially in times of financial difficulty.
cn: 事实上，分摊成本可能是相当切实有效的解决方案，特别是在财务困难时期。

en: If there's downward pressure on costs, because of a need for investment in other areas, I would argue that this is a perfectly feasible solution.
cn: 如果因为需要向其他领域投资而面临成本下行压力，我认为这个解决方案是完全可行的。

en: Guess what?
cn: 你猜怎么着？

en: The worst food I've ever had was in France.
cn: 最难吃的东西我是在法国碰上的。

en: Really?
cn: 真的吗？

en: That's odd.
cn: 这倒怪了。

en: I thought the French were all good cooks.
cn: 我还以为法国人个个都很会烧菜。

en: Yes.
cn: 是啊。

en: That's right.
cn: 我也这么想。

en: I suppose it's really like anywhere else, though.
cn: 不过我觉得它真的和任何其他地方一样。

en: You know, some places are good.
cn: 你懂的，有些地方好。

en: Some bad.
cn: 有些地方差。

en: But it's really all our own fault.
cn: 但这确实是我们自己的错。

en: What do you mean?
cn: 这话怎么说？

en: Well, it was the first time I'd been to France.
cn: 那是我第一次去法国。

en: This was years ago when I was at school.
cn: 过去好些年了，那时我还在上学。

en: I went there with my parents' friends, from my father's school.
cn: 我和父母的朋友一起去那儿，从我父亲的学校出发。

en: They'd hired a coach to take them to Switzerland.
cn: 他们租了一辆大巴带他们去瑞士。

en: A school trip?
cn: 学校旅行？

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: Most of them had never been abroad before.
cn: 他们大多数人以前从没去过国外。

en: We'd crossed the English Channel at night, and we set off through France, and breakfast time arrived, and the coach driver had arranged for us to stop at this little café.
cn: 我们在夜里穿过英吉利海峡，启程穿过法国；早餐时间到了，司机之前已安排我们停在一家小餐馆。

en: There we all were, tired and hungry, and then we made the great discovery.
cn: 于是我们就都到了那儿，又累又饿，然后我们有了一个伟大的发现。

en: What was that?
cn: 是什么呢？

en: Bacon and eggs.
cn: 培根煎蛋。

en: Fantastic!
cn: 太棒了！

en: The real English breakfast.
cn: 正宗的英式早餐。

en: Yes.
cn: 是啊。

en: Anyway, we didn't know any better—so we had it, and ugh...!
cn: 反正我们不知道还有什么更好的，于是就点了，然后，呃！

en: What was it like?
cn: 什么味道？

en: Disgusting?
cn: 很恶心吗？

en: Oh, it was incredible!
cn: 呵，你想都想不到！

en: They just got a bowl and put some fat in it.
cn: 他们就拿了个碗，往里面倒了点油。

en: And then they put some bacon in the fat, broke an egg over the top and put the whole lot in the oven for about ten minutes.
cn: 再放些培根进去，上面打了个蛋，然后一股脑塞烤箱里热了大概十分钟。

en: In the oven!
cn: 烤箱！

en: You're joking.
cn: 你在开玩笑吧。

en: You can't cook bacon and eggs in the oven!
cn: 烤箱怎么做培根煎蛋！

en: Well, they must have done it that way.
cn: 对啊，反正他们肯定是这么弄的。

en: It was hot, but it wasn't cooked.
cn: 菜是热的，但没有烹煮。

en: There was just this egg floating about in gallons of fat and raw bacon.
cn: 就这么个鸡蛋浮在一大堆油里头，再加上生的培根。

en: Did you actually eat it?
cn: 你们不会真的吃了吧？

en: No!
cn: 怎么可能！

en: Nobody did.
cn: 谁都没吃。

en: They all wanted to turn round and go home.
cn: 他们都想掉头回家。

en: You know, back to teabags and fish and chips.
cn: 你也知道，回来有茶包还有炸鱼薯条。

en: You can't blame them really.
cn: 你真的没法怪他们。

en: Anyway, the next night we were all given another foreign speciality.
cn: 反正第二天晚上又给我们上了一道外国特色菜。

en: What was that?
cn: 是什么啊？

en: Snails.
cn: 蜗牛。

en: That really finished them off.
cn: 那可真让他们熬不下去了。

en: "Lovely holiday that was!
cn: 真是个美好的假期！

en: You say your shop has been doing well.
cn: 你说你的店铺做得不错。

en: Could you give me some idea of what "doing well" means in facts and figures?
cn: 你能不能拿出一些事实和数据，让我了解一下什么叫“做得不错”？

en: Well, "doing well" means averaging £1,200 or more a week for about 7 years, making almost a quarter of a million pounds.
cn: 嗯，“做得不错”意味着过去大概7年时间里，平均每周1200英镑或更多，这样几乎就是25万英镑。

en: And "doing well" means your earnings are rising.
cn: “做得不错”还意味着收入在上升。

en: Last year, we did slightly over 50,000 and this year, we hope to do more than 60,000.
cn: 去年，我们做到了5万多，今年我们希望做到6万以上。

en: So, that's good if we continue to rise.
cn: 嗯，如果我们能保持上升势头的话就还不错。

en: Now, that's gross earnings, I assume.
cn: 我想这是总收入吧。

en: What about your expenses?
cn: 你的开支呢？

en: Yes, that's gross.
cn: 对，是总收入。

en: The expenses, of course, go up steadily.
cn: 开支当然在持续增加。

en: And since we've moved to this new shop, the expenses have increased greatly, because it's a much bigger shop.
cn: 而且自从我们搬到了这家新店，开支大大增加了，因为这边的店面要大得多。

en: So I couldn't say exactly what our expenses are.
cn: 我也说不清有哪些开支。

en: They are something in the region of six or seven thousand pounds a year, which is not high.
cn: 每年的开支大概在六、七千英镑，不算高。

en: Commercially speaking, it's fairly low, and we try to keep our expenses as low as we can.
cn: 从商业角度来说，这其实相当低了，我们还会努力使开支保持在尽可能低的水平。

en: And your prices are much lower than the same goods in shops round about.
cn: 同样的商品，你店里的售价要比周围店铺的售价低得多。

en: How do the local shopkeepers feel about having a shop doing so well in their midst?
cn: 当地的店主怎么看他们中间有一家做得这么好的店？

en: Perhaps a lot of them don't realize how well we are doing, because we don't make a point of publicizing.
cn: 也许他们很多人都不知道我们做得有多好吧，因为我们不会特意去宣传。

en: That was a lesson we learned very early on.
cn: 这是我们很早就学到的一个教训。

en: We were very friendly with all local shopkeepers and we happened to mention to a local shopkeeper how much we had made that week.
cn: 我们本来和当地所有的店主关系都很好，但有一次碰巧跟当地一位店主提起我们那个星期的收入。

en: He was very unhappy and never as friendly again.
cn: 他非常不高兴，再也不给我们好脸色看了。

en: So we make a point of never publicizing the amount of money we make.
cn: 所以我们特意不公开自己的收入。

en: But we are on very good terms with all the shops.
cn: 但是我们与所有店铺的关系都很好。

en: None of them have ever complained that we are putting them out of business or anything like that.
cn: 他们从没抱怨我们把他们的生意抢光了或者其他什么。

en: I think it's a nice friendly relationship.
cn: 我认为这种友好的关系还是挺好的。

en: Maybe if they did know what we made, perhaps they wouldn't be so friendly.
cn: 如果他们知道我们赚了多少，或许就不会那么友善了。

en: Birds are famous for carrying things around.
cn: 鸟类以携带东西而闻名。

en: Some, like homing pigeons, can be trained to deliver messages and packages.
cn: 有些鸟，比如信鸽，经过训练后可以传递信息和包裹。

en: Other birds unknowingly carry seeds that cling to them for the ride.
cn: 其他鸟在不知不觉中携带附着在它们身上搭顺风车的种子。

en: Canadian scientists have found a worrisome, new example of the power that birds have to spread stuff around.
cn: 关于鸟类传播物体的能力，加拿大科学家们发现了一个令人担忧的新例子。

en: Way up north in the Canadian Arctic, seabirds are picking up dangerous chemicals in the ocean and delivering them to ponds near where the birds live.
cn: 在加拿大北极地区的北部，海鸟在海洋中拾取危险的化学物品，并将它们运送到自己栖居的池塘附近。

en: Some 10,000 pairs of the birds, called fulmars, a kind of Arctic seabird, make their nests on Devon Island, north of the Arctic Circle.
cn: 大约有一万对被称为管鼻藿的北极海鸟在北极圈以北的德文岛上筑巢。

en: The fulmars travel some 400 kilometers over the sea to find food.
cn: 这些管鼻藿在海上长途跋涉400多公里寻找食物。

en: When they return home, their droppings end up all around their nesting sites, including in nearby ponds.
cn: 当它们回巢时，它们的粪便会遍布筑巢地的周围，包括附近的池塘。

en: Previously, scientists noticed pollutants arriving in the Arctic with the wind.
cn: 此前，科学家注意到有污染物随风来到北极。

en: Salmon also carry dangerous chemicals as the fish migrate between rivers and the sea.
cn: 鲑鱼在河流和海洋间迁徙时也携带着危险的化学物质。

en: The bodies of fish and other meat-eaters can build up high levels of the chemicals.
cn: 鱼和其他食肉动物的体内会积累大量的化学物质。

en: To test the polluting power of fulmars, researchers collected samples of deposit from 11 ponds on Devon Island.
cn: 为了测试管鼻藿的污染力，研究人员从德文岛的11个池塘采集了沉积物样本。

en: In ponds closest to the colony, the results showed there were far more pollutants than in ponds less affected by the birds.
cn: 结果显示，在最靠近管鼻藿栖息地的池塘中，污染物质远远多于受其影响较小的池塘。

en: The pollutants in the ponds appear to come from fish that fulmars eat when they're out on the ocean.
cn: 池塘里的污染物似乎来自于管鼻藿在海中吃的鱼。

en: People who live, hunt, or fish near bird colonies need to be careful, the researchers say.
cn: 研究人员称，在鸟类栖息地附近生活、狩猎或捕鱼的人需要小心。

en: The birds don't mean to cause harm, but the chemicals they carry can cause major problems.
cn: 鸟类并非有意造成伤害，但它们携带的化学物质可能会导致重大问题。

en: In recent years, the death rate among American centenarians—people who have lived to age 100 or older—has decreased, dropping 14 percent for women and 20 percent for men from 2008 to 2014.
cn: 近年来，美国百岁老人（年龄在100岁或者以上的人）的死亡率下降了，从2008年到2014年，女性（的死亡率）下降了14%，男性（的死亡率）下降了20%。

en: The leading causes of death in this age group are also changing.
cn: 这一年龄段人群的主要死亡原因也在变化。

en: In 2000, the top five causes of death for centenarians were heart disease, stroke, flu, cancer and Alzheimer's disease.
cn: 2000年时，百岁老人死亡的前五大原因分别是心脏病、中风、流感、癌症以及老年痴呆症。

en: But by 2014, the death rate from Alzheimer's disease for this age group had more than doubled—increasing from 3.8 percent to 8.5 percent—making the progressive brain disease the second leading cause of death for centenarians.
cn: 但是到了2014年，这一年龄段人群因老年痴呆症而死亡的比例已经增加了一倍不止——从3.8%增加到了8.5%——这使得渐进性的大脑疾病成为百岁老人的第二大死亡原因。

en: One reason for the rise in deaths from Alzheimer's disease in this group may be that developing this condition remains possible even after people beat the odds of dying from other diseases such as cancer.
cn: 这一群体中死于老年痴呆症的人数量增加的一个原因可能是，即使人们从诸如癌症这样的疾病中奇迹般地活了下来，却仍然有可能患这种病。

en: People physically fit enough to survive over 100 years ultimately give in to diseases such as Alzheimer's which affects the mind and cognitive function.
cn: 那些身体健康，足以活到100多岁的人最终会屈服于诸如老年痴呆症这种影响大脑和认知功能的疾病。

en: In other words, it appears that their minds give out before their bodies do.
cn: 换句话说，他们的大脑似乎比他们的身体先失灵。

en: On the other hand, the death rate from flu dropped from 7.4 percent in 2000 to 4.1 percent in 2014.
cn: 另一方面，流感死亡率从2000年的7.4%下降到了2014年的4.1%。

en: That pushed flu from the third leading cause of death to the fifth.
cn: 这使流感从第三大死亡原因变成第五大死亡原因。

en: Overall, the total number of centenarians is going up.
cn: 总的来说，百岁老人的总数在上升。

en: In 2014, there were 72,197 centenarians, compared to 50,281 in 2000.
But because this population is getting larger, the number of deaths in this group is also increasing—18,434 centenarians died in 2000, whereas 25,914 died in 2014.
cn: 但是由于这一群体日益壮大，其死亡数量也在增加——2000年有18434位百岁老人死亡，而在2014年有25914位百岁老人死亡。

en: Okay.
cn: 好。

en: So let's get started.
cn: 那我们开始吧。

en: And to start things off I think what we need to do is consider a definition.
cn: 首先，我想我们需要做的是思考一个定义。

en: I'm going to define what love is but then most of the experiments I'm going to talk about are really focused more on attraction than love.
cn: 我接下来要定义爱情是什么，但是我将谈到的多数实验实际上都更关注爱慕、而非爱情。

en: And I'm going to pick a definition from a former colleague, Robert Sternberg, who is now the dean at Tufts University but was here on our faculty at Yale for nearly thirty years.
cn: 所以，我要从我的前同事罗伯特·斯腾伯格那里借个定义，他现在是塔夫茨大学的系主任，但曾在耶鲁大学我系任职近30年。

en: And he has a theory of love that argues that it's made up of three components: intimacy, passion, and commitment, or what is sometimes called decision/commitment.
cn: 他有一套爱情理论，认为爱情由三部分构成：亲密、激情和承诺（有时被称作承诺/决定）。

en: And these are relatively straightforward.
cn: 这些都还比较容易懂。

en: He argued that you don't have love if you don't have all three of these elements.
cn: 他认为，如果你并未拥有全部这三项要素，你就没有拥有爱情。

en: Intimacy is the feeling of closeness, of connectedness with someone, of bonding.
cn: 亲密即与某人相近相通、彼此联结的感觉。

en: Operationally, you could think of intimacy as you share secrets, you share information with this person that you don't share with anybody else.
cn: 实践上，你可以把亲密视作“你与这个人分享你不与其他任何人分享的秘密、讯息”。

en: Okay.
cn: 好。

en: That's really what intimacy is, the bond that comes from sharing information that isn't shared with other people.
cn: 这正是亲密的本质——一种纽带，它源于分享那些不会分享给他人的信息。

en: The second element is passion.
cn: 第二项要素是激情。

en: Passion is the drive that leads to romance.
cn: 激情是带来爱情的动力。

en: You can think of it as physical attraction.
cn: 你可以把它看作身体吸引。

en: And Sternberg argues that this is a required component of a love relationship.
cn: 斯腾伯格认为，这是爱情关系的必需要素。

en: The third element of love in Sternberg's theory is what he calls decision/commitment, the decision that one is in a love relationship, the willingness to label it as such, and a commitment to maintain that relationship at least for some period of time.
cn: 斯腾伯格理论中的第三项爱情要素是他所谓的承诺/决定，即一个人对自己拥有爱情关系的认定、把它归于这种关系的意愿、以及至少在一段时间内维持这种关系的承诺。

en: Sternberg would argue it's not love if you don't call it love and if you don't have some desire to maintain the relationship.
cn: 斯腾伯格主张，如果你不称其为爱情、没有维持这段关系的愿望，它就不是爱情。

en: So if you have all three of these, intimacy, passion and commitment, in Sternberg's theory, you have love.
cn: 所以，如果你拥有所有这三项，亲密、激情和承诺，按照斯腾伯格的理论，你就拥有爱情。

en: Now what's interesting about the theory is what do you have if you only have one out of three or two out of three?
cn: 这一来，这个理论的有趣之处就在于如果你只拥有三项要素中的一项或者两项，你拥有的是什么？

en: What do you have and how is it different if you have a different two out of three?
cn: 如果你拥有三项要素中不同的两项，你拥有的是什么、又有何不同？

en: What's interesting about this kind of theorizing is it gives rise to many different combinations that can be quite interesting when you break them down and start to look them carefully.
cn: 这种理论探讨的有趣之处在于它产生了许多不同的组合，你若将它们分类并仔细审视它们就会发现这很有意思。

en: So what I've done is I've taken Sternberg's three elements of love, intimacy, passion and commitment, and I've listed out the different kinds of relationships you would have if you had zero, one, two or three out of the three elements.
cn: 所以，我所做的就是选取了斯腾伯格的爱情三要素“亲密、激情和承诺”，列出了你拥有三项要素中的零项、一项、两项或三项时所得到的各种关系。

en: Hi!
cn: 大家好！

en: I am Elizabeth Hoffler, Master of Social Work.
cn: 我是伊丽莎白·霍福乐，社会工作专业硕士。

en: I am a social worker, a lobbyist, and a special assistant to the executive director at the National Association of Social Workers.
cn: 我是一名社会福利工作者、说客，也是全国社会工作者协会执行理事的特别助理。

en: Today we are going to be talking about becoming a social worker.
cn: 今天，我们来谈谈做一名社会工作者（意味着什么）。

en: Social work is the helping profession.
cn: 社会工作是一项助人的职业。

en: Its primary mission is to enhance human well-being and help meet the basic needs of all people, with a particular focus on those who are vulnerable, oppressed, and living in poverty.
cn: 它的主要任务是提高人类福祉，帮助所有人满足基本需求，特别关注那些易受伤害、受到压迫以及生活贫困的人们。

en: We often deal with complex human needs.
cn: 我们常常处理复杂的人类需求。

en: Social work is different from other professions, because we focus on the person and environment.
cn: 社会工作不同于其他职业，因为我们关注人和环境。

en: We deal with the external factors that impact a person's situation and outlook.
cn: 我们处理影响一个人处境和前景的外部因素。

en: And we create opportunity for assessment and intervention, to help clients and communities cope effectively with their reality and change that reality when necessary.
cn: 我们还创造了评估和干预的机会，从而帮助客户和社会有效应对现实，并在必要时改变现实。

en: In thousands of ways social workers help other people, people from every age, every background, across the country.
cn: 社会工作者通过无数种方式帮助全国各地不同年龄、不同背景的人。

en: Wherever needed, social workers come to help.
cn: 不管哪里有需要，社会工作者都会前往帮忙。

en: The most well-known aspect of the profession is that of a social safety net.
cn: 这个职业最为人所知的一方面是社会安全网。

en: We help guide people to critical resources and counsel them on life-changing decisions.
cn: 我们引导人们获取关键资源，并就改变人生的决定向他们提出建议。

en: There are more than 600,000 professional social workers in the country, and we all either have a bachelor's degree, a master's degree, or a PhD in Social Work.
cn: 这个国家有超过60万职业社会工作者，我们要么拥有社会工作学士学位或硕士学位，要么拥有博士学位。

en: There are more clinically trained social workers than clinically trained psychiatrists, psychologists, and psychiatric nurses combined.
cn: 受过临床培训的社会工作者比受过临床培训的精神病医生、心理医生和精神科护士加起来还多。

en: Throughout this series you will learn more about the profession, the necessary steps to get a social work degree, the rich history of social work, and the many ways that social workers help others.
cn: 在本系列节目当中，你将对这个职业、获取社会工作学位的必要步骤、社会工作的丰富历史以及社会工作者帮助他人的众多方式有更多的了解。

en: Later in this series, you will hear from Stacy Collins and Mel Wilson, fellow social workers at the National Association of Social Workers.
cn: 在本系列的稍后部分，你将会听到来自史黛西·柯林斯和梅尔·威尔逊的演讲，他们是我在全国社会工作者协会的同事。

en: Stacy is going to walk you through the step-by-step process of becoming a social worker, and Mel will tell you about the range of options you have once you get your social work degree, as well as the high standards of responsibility the social workers must adhere to.
cn: 史黛西将会为你介绍逐步成为一名社会工作者的过程，而梅尔将会告诉你取得社会工作学位后你所拥有的选择范围，以及社会工作者必须坚守的高标准责任感。

en: The National Association of Social Workers represents nearly 145,000 social workers across the country.
cn: 全国社会工作者协会代表着全国145000名社会工作者。

en: Our mission is to promote, protect, and advance the social work profession.
cn: 我们的任务是促进、保护和发展社会工作职业。

en: We hope you enjoy this series about how you can make a difference by becoming a social worker.
cn: 我们希望你们喜欢这个关于“如何通过成为一名社会工作者来有所作为”的系列节目。

en: Next, we are going to talk about choosing social work.
cn: 接下来，我们来谈谈如何选择社会工作。

en: Today, I'd like to talk about what happens when celebrity role models get behind healthy habits but at the same time, promote junk food.
cn: 今天，我想谈谈名人榜样支持健康习惯、但同时又宣传垃圾食品时会发生什么。

en: Currently, there's mounting criticism of Michelle Obama's "Let's Move!" campaign, which fights childhood obesity by encouraging youngsters to become more physically active, and has signed on singer Beyoncé, and basketball player Shaquille O'Neal, both of whom also endorse sodas, which are a major contributor to the obesity epidemic.
cn: 当前，对米歇尔·奥巴马发起的运动“让我们动起来！”的批评日益增多，该运动通过鼓励儿童多锻炼身体来对抗儿童期肥胖，而且该运动已与歌手碧昂丝和篮球运动员沙奎尔·奥尼尔签约，（可）两人也代言苏打水——造成肥胖流行的主要因素。

en: Now there's a lot more evidence of how powerful a celebrity—especially a professional athlete—can be in influencing children's behavior.
cn: 现如今，有了更多的证据证明名人——尤其是职业运动员——在影响儿童的行为方面可以有多强大。

en: In a report published by the Rudd Center for Food Policy & Obesity at Yale University, researchers studied 100 professional athletes and their endorsement contracts.
cn: 耶鲁大学路德食品政策与肥胖研究中心发布的一项报告中，研究人员研究了100名职业运动员和他们的代言合同。

en: The team focused on athletes since they are theoretically the best role models for active, healthy lifestyles for children.
cn: 研究团队聚焦运动员，因为对孩子们而言，他们理论上是积极健康生活方式的最佳榜样。

en: After sorting the deals by category, they determined that among the 512 brands associated with the athletes, most involved sporting goods, followed closely by food and beverage brands.
cn: 按类别整理协议后，他们确定，512个与运动员有关系的品牌中，大多涉及运动产品，食品及饮料品牌紧随其后。

en: Sports drinks, which are often high in sugar and calories, made up most of the food and drink deals, with soft drinks and fast food filling out the remainder.
cn: 食品和饮料代言中大多数是通常高糖、高卡路里的运动饮料，软饮和快餐则填补了剩余部分。

en: Of the 46 beverages endorsed by professional athletes, 93% relied exclusively on sugar for all of their calories.
cn: 职业运动员代言的46种饮料中，93%纯粹靠糖来提供所有的卡路里。

en: It's no surprise that high-profile athletes can influence children's eating behaviors, but the scientists were able to quantify how prevalent these endorsements are in the children's environment.
cn: 名人运动员能影响儿童饮食行为，这不足为奇，但科学家可以量化“这些代言在儿童所处的环境中有多普遍”。

en: Advertisements featuring professional athletes and their endorsed products tend to get impressive exposure, on TV, radio, in print and online.
cn: 有职业运动员及其代言产品的广告往往会在电视上、广播中、报纸上、网络上得到令人印象深刻的曝光。

en: And in 2010, the researchers reported that children ages 12 to 17 saw more athlete-endorsed food and beverage brand commercials than adults.
cn: 2010年，研究人员称，12到17岁的儿童比成年人看过更多运动员代言的食品和饮料品牌商业广告。

en: One reason any campaign wants a popular celebrity spokesperson is because kids are attracted to them no matter what they are doing.
cn: 任何运动都想要一位受欢迎的名人倡导者，原因之一就是无论他们做什么，孩子们都会被他们吸引。

en: We can't expect kids to turn off that admiration when the same person is selling sugar.
cn: 我们不能指望同样是这位名人，如果他售卖糖果孩子们就不再倾慕他。

en: At best, kids might be confused.
cn: 最好的情况是，孩子们也许困惑不解。

en: At worst, they'll think the messages about soda are the same as the messages about water, but those two beverages aren't the same.
cn: 最坏的情况是，他们会以为有关苏打水的信息与有关饮用水的信息是一样的，但这两种饮料完全不同。

en: If children are turning to athletes as role models, it's in their best interest if their idols are consistent.
cn: 如果孩子们正把目光转向运动员，将其视作榜样，那么对他们最有利的情况是他们的偶像始终如一。

en: Consistent messaging of positive behaviors will show healthier lifestyles for kids to follow.
cn: 一如既往传递关于积极行为的信息会展现出更健康的生活方式让孩子们效仿。

en: Welcome to Work Place, and in today's program we are looking at the results of two recently published surveys, which both deal with the same topic—happiness at work.
cn: 欢迎来到《职场》，在今天的节目中，我们要关注的是最近发布的两项调查的结果，这两项调查都讨论了同一话题——工作中的幸福感。

en: John, tell us about the first survey.
cn: 约翰，给我们讲讲第一个调查。

en: Well, this was done by a human resources consultancy who interviewed more than 1,000 workers and established a top 10 of the factors which make people happy at work.
cn: 好，这项调查是由一个人力资源咨询公司完成的，它采访了1000多名员工，并确定了让人们在工作中感到幸福的前十项因素。

en: The most important factor, for the majority of the people interviewed, was having friendly, supportive colleagues.
cn: 对于大多数受访者来说，最重要的因素是拥有友善的、给人支持帮助的同事。

en: In fact, 73% people interviewed put their relationship with colleagues as the key factor contributing to happiness at work, which is a very high percentage.
cn: 事实上，73%的受访者将他们与同事的关系作为提升工作幸福感的关键因素，这个比例非常高。

en: The second most important factor was having work that is enjoyable.
cn: 第二重要的因素是拥有令人愉悦的工作。

en: The two least important factors were having one's achievements recognized and rather surprisingly, earning a competitive salary.
cn: 两个最不重要的因素是让自己的成就获得认可，以及——相当出乎意料——获得有竞争力的薪水。

en: So, we are not mainly motivated by money?
cn: 这么说，我们的主要动机不是金钱？

en: Apparently not.
cn: 显然不是。

en: Any other interesting information in the survey?
cn: 调查中还有其他有趣信息吗？

en: Yes.
cn: 有。

en: For example, 25% of the working people interviewed described themselves as very happy at work.
cn: 例如，受访的职场人员中有25%表示自己在工作中非常幸福。

en: However, 20% of employees described themselves as being unhappy.
cn: 但是，有20%的员工认为自己不幸福。

en: That's quite a lot of unhappy people at work every day.
cn: 每天在工作中感到不幸福的人真不少啊。

en: It is, isn't it?
cn: 确实不少，不是吗？

en: And there were several more interesting conclusions revealed by the survey.
cn: 而且调查还披露了几个有趣的结论。

en: First of all, small is beautiful.
cn: 第一个是，小的即是美的。

en: People definitely prefer working for smaller organizations or companies with less than 100 staff.
cn: 毫无疑问人们更喜欢为员工少于100人的小机构或小公司工作。

en: We also find out that, generally speaking, women were happier in their work than men.
cn: 我们还发现，总体来说，女性在工作中比男性更有幸福感。

en: Yes, we are, aren't we?
cn: 对，我们确实是这样，不是吗？

en: And workers on part-time contracts who only work 4 or 5 hours a day are happier than those who work full time.
cn: 那些只工作四五个小时的兼职合同工比那些全职工作的人更幸福。

en: The researchers concluded that this is probably due to a better work-life balance.
cn: 研究者得出的结论是，这可能是由于（前者）在工作和生活之间平衡得更好。

en: Are bosses happier than their employees?
cn: 老板会比他们的员工更幸福吗？

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: Perhaps not surprisingly, the higher people go in a company, the happier they are.
cn: 也许这并不奇怪，人们在公司的职位越高，他们越感到幸福。

en: So senior managers enjoy their jobs more than people working under them.
cn: 所以高级管理人员比在他们手下工作的人更喜欢自己的工作。

en: Mr. De Keyzer, I am a great lover of your book, Moments Before the Flood.
cn: 德·凯瑟尔先生，我非常喜欢您的作品《洪水袭来前》。

en: Can you tell us how you first became interested in this subject matter?
cn: 能告诉我们您一开始是怎么对这个主题感兴趣的吗？

en: In 2006, when the concert hall of the city of Bruges asked me to take some pictures for a catalogue for a new concert season around the theme of water, I found myself working along the Belgian coastline.
cn: 2006年，布鲁日市音乐厅让我以水为主题给新的音乐季的节目单拍一些照片，那时我发现自己沿着比利时海岸工作。

en: As there had been numerous alarming articles in the press about a climate catastrophe waiting to happen, I started looking at the sea and the beach very differently, a place where I spent so many perfect days as a child.
cn: 当时媒体上铺天盖地、满是气候灾害即将到来的骇人报道，我便开始以截然不同的方式审视这片大海和沙滩，在这里，我度过了那么多美好的童年时光。

en: This fear of a looming danger became the subject of a large-scale photo project.
cn: 这种对步步逼近的危险的恐惧成为了一个大型摄影项目的主题。

en: You wrote in the book "I don't want to photograph the disaster; I want to photograph the disaster waiting to happen."
cn: 您在作品中写道：“我不想拍摄灾难本身，我想拍摄灾难即将到来的样子。”

en: Can you talk a bit about that?
cn: 您能就此谈一谈吗？

en: It is clear now that it's a matter of time before the entire European coastline disappears under water.
cn: 如今显而易见的是，整个欧洲海岸线消失在水中只是时间问题。

en: The same goes for numerous big cities around the world.
cn: 世界上许许多多的大城市也会如此。

en: My idea was to photograph this beautiful and very unique coastline, rich in history, before it's too late - as a last witness.
cn: 我想的就是在还来得及的时候拍下这美丽独特、历史底蕴深厚的海岸线，作为最后的见证。
