en: I think there's no limit to the amount of personal attention and personal care people would like if they could afford it.
cn: （但）我认为只要支付得起，人们对私人关怀和私人护理数量的要求是没有上限的。

en: But the real question in the future is how come people afford these things if they don't have money, because they can't get a job that pays enough.
cn: 不过，未来真正的问题在于，如果人们因找不到工资足够多的工作而挣不到钱，他们怎样支付得起这些服务。

en: That's why I wrote this book which is about how to reorganize the economy for the future when technology brings about destructive changes to what we used to consider high income work.
cn: 这就是我写这本书的原因，这本书主要讲的是，在技术给我们曾经视作高薪的工作带来毁灭性转变时，我们应如何面向未来、重组经济。

en: American researchers have discovered the world's oldest paved road, a 4,600-year-old highway.
cn: 美国研究人员发现了世界上最古老的人工铺就的道路，一条4600年前修建的公路。

en: It linked a stone pit in the Egyptian desert to waterways that carried blocks to monument sites along the Nile.
cn: 它将埃及沙漠中的一个采石场和沿尼罗河运送石块到纪念碑工地的航道连接了起来。

en: The 8-mile road is at least 500 years older than any previously discovered road.
cn: 这条八英里的路比先前发现的任意一条路都要古老至少五百年。

en: It is the only paved road discovered in ancient Egypt, said geologist Thomas Bowen of the United States Geological Survey.
cn: 它是古埃及已发现的唯一一条人工铺就的道路，美国地质调查局的地质学家托马斯·鲍恩说道。

en: He reported the discovery on Friday.
cn: 他于周五报告了这一发现。

en: "The road probably doesn't rank with the pyramids as a construction feat, but it is a major engineering achievement," said his colleague, geologist James Harrell of the University of Toledo.
cn: “这条道路也许无法和金字塔相媲美，算不上建筑成就，但它是一项重大的工程成就”，他的同事、托莱多大学的地质学家詹姆斯·哈勒尔说道。

en: "Not only is the road earlier than we thought possible, we didn't even think they built roads."
cn: “不仅仅是这条道路比我们所想象的要古老，我们甚至都没想到他们修建了道路”。

en: The researchers also made a discovery in the stone pit at the northern end of the road; the first evidence that the Egyptians used rock saws.
cn: 研究人员还在这条道路北部尽头的采石场有所发现；埃及人使用石锯的首个证据。

en: "This is the oldest example of saws being used for cutting stone," said Bowen's colleague James Hoffmeier of Wheaton College in Illinois.
cn: “这是人们使用锯来切割石头的最古老的例子”，鲍恩的同事、伊利诺伊州威顿学院的詹姆斯·霍夫梅尔说道。

en: "That's two technologies we didn't know they had," Harrell said.
cn: “这是两项我们不知道他们已拥有的技术”，哈勒尔说道。

en: "And we don't know why they were both abandoned."
cn: “并且我们不知道它们为何都被废弃”。

en: The road was discovered in the Faiyum Depression, about 45 miles southwest of Cairo.
cn: 这条道路是在法尤姆洼地中被发现的，位于开罗西南方向大约45英里。

en: Short segments of the road had been observed by earlier explorers, Bowen said, but they failed to realize its significance or follow up on their observations.
cn: 鲍恩说，早期探险家已观察到了这条路的一小部分，但是他们未能意识到其重要性，也未能跟进其观察。

en: Bowen and his colleagues stumbled across it while they were doing geological mapping in the region.
cn: 鲍恩和其同事在这片区域进行地质填图时无意中发现了这条道路。

en: The road was clearly built to provide services for the newly discovered stone pit.
cn: 这条路显然是为了给新近发现的采石场提供服务而修建的。

en: Bowen and Harrell have found the camp that housed workers at the stone pit.
cn: 鲍恩和哈勒尔在采石场发现了供工人居住的营地。

en: The road appears today to go nowhere, ending in the middle of the desert.
cn: 今天这条路似乎不知所终，止于沙漠的中间。

en: When it was built, its terminal was a dock on the shore of Lake Moeris, which had an elevation of about 66 feet above sea level, the same as the dock.
cn: 在其被修建时，它的终点是莫里斯湖岸边的一个码头，莫里斯湖高于海平面约66英尺，与码头高度一样。

en: Lake Moeris received its water from the annual floods of the Nile.
cn: 莫里斯湖中的水来自每年尼罗河的洪水。

en: At the time of the floods, the river and lake were at the same level and connected through a gap in the hills near the modern villages of el-Lahun and Hawara.
cn: 在洪水期，尼罗河和莫里斯湖处于同一水平面，通过靠近拉罕和哈瓦拉的现代村庄的山丘内的一个洞相连。

en: Harrell and Bowen believe that blocks were loaded onto barges during the dry season, then floated over to the Nile during the floods to be shipped off to the monument sites at Giza and Saqqara.
cn: 哈勒尔和鲍恩认为这些石块是在旱季被装入驳船，然后在洪水期漂到尼罗河上，并被运往吉萨和塞加拉的金字塔工地。

en: The thin, extremely sharp needles didn't hurt at all going in.
cn: 那一根根纤细而又极其尖锐的针扎进去时一点也不疼。

en: Dr. Gong pierced them into my left arm, around the elbow that had been bothering me.
cn: 龚医生将这些针刺入我的左臂，环绕在困扰我很久的手肘周围。

en: Other needles were slipped into my left wrist and, strangely, into my right arm, and then into both my closed eyelids.
cn: 其他一些针插入了我的左手腕，还有很不可思议的地方——我的右臂和我闭着的双眼眼睑。

en: There wasn't any discomfort, just a mild warming sensation.
cn: 没有任何的不适，只有轻微的温热感。

en: However, I did begin to wonder what had driven me here, to the office of Dr. James Gong in New York's Chinatown.
cn: 但是，我确实开始疑惑，是什么让我来到这里，来到医生詹姆斯·龚位于纽约唐人街的办公室。

en: Then I remembered the torturing pain in that left elbow.
cn: 随后我记起来了——是我左手肘难忍的疼痛（让我来到这里的）。

en: Several trips to a hospital and two expensive, uncomfortable medical tests had failed to produce even a diagnosis.
cn: 去了好几趟医院，做了两次价格昂贵又不舒服的医疗检查，甚至连个诊断都做不出来。

en: "Maybe you lean on your left arm too much," the doctor concluded, suggesting I see a bone doctor.
cn: “也许你靠左臂支撑得过多了，”医生总结道，并建议我去看骨科大夫。

en: During the hours spent waiting in vain to see a bone doctor, I decided to take another track and try acupuncture.
cn: 在徒然地等着看骨科医生的时间里，我决定试试另外一条路，中医针灸。

en: A Chinese-American friend recommended Dr. Gong.
cn: 一个美籍华人朋友推荐了龚医生。

en: I took the subway to Gong's second-floor office, marked with a hand-painted sign.
cn: 我坐地铁去了龚医生坐落在二楼、以手写指示牌标识的办公室。

en: Dr. Gong speaks English, but not often.
cn: 龚医生说英语，但不经常说。

en: Most of my questions to him were greeted with a friendly laugh, but I managed to let him know where my arm hurt.
cn: 对我的大多数问题他都报以友善的一笑，但我设法让他知道了我的胳膊哪里疼。

en: He asked me to go into a room, had me lie down on a bed, and went to work.
cn: 他让我走进一个房间，躺到床上，然后便开始了治疗。

en: In the next room, I learned, a woman dancer was also getting a treatment.
cn: 我得知，在隔壁的房间里，一个女舞者也在接受治疗。

en: As I lay there a while, I drifted into a dream-like state and fantasized about what she looked like.
cn: 我在床上躺了一会儿，就渐渐进入了一种做梦般的状态，幻想着那个女舞者长什么样子。

en: Acupuncturists today are as likely to be found on Park Avenue as on Mott Street.
cn: 现在，你在派克大街上找到针灸师的概率跟在唐人街的勿街上找到针灸师的概率没什么两样。

en: In all there are an estimated 10,000 acupuncturists in the country.
cn: 据估计，在美国总共有一万名针灸师。

en: Nowadays, a lot of medical doctors have learned acupuncture techniques; so have a number of dentists.
cn: 如今，许多医生都学了针灸技法，连许多牙医都学了针灸。

en: Reason?
cn: 原因呢？

en: Patient demand.
cn: 患者需求呗。

en: Few, though, can adequately explain how acupuncture works.
cn: 尽管几乎没人能充分解释针灸是如何奏效的。

en: Acupuncturists may say that the body has more than 800 acupuncture points.
cn: 针灸师可能会说，人体有不下800个穴位。

en: A life force called qi circulates through the body.
cn: 一种被称之为“气”的生命之力在体内循环流通。

en: Points on the skin are energetically connected to specific organs, body structures and systems.
cn: 肌肤上的穴位与特定器官、人体结构和系统强有力地连接着。

en: Acupuncture points are stimulated to balance the circulation of qi.
cn: 刺激针灸穴位是为了平衡“气”循环。

en: The truth is, though acupuncture is at least 2,200 years old, "nobody really knows what's happening," says Paul Zmiewski, a Ph.D. in Chinese studies who practices acupuncture in Philadelphia.
cn: 真实情况是，尽管针灸至少有2200年的历史，“没有人真正知道这到底是怎么一回事，”在费城练习针灸的汉学博士Paul Zmiewski说道。

en: After five treatments, there has been dramatic improvement in my arm, and the pain is a fraction of what it was.
cn: 经过了五次治疗之后，我的胳膊好多了，痛楚只是原来的一点点了。

en: The mainly silent Dr. Gong finally even offered a diagnosis for what troubled me.
cn: 大多沉默不语的龚医生最后甚至对这一令我烦恼的病症给出了诊断。

en: "Pinched nerve," he said.
cn: “是神经压迫，”他说。

en: Ronald and Lois, married for two decades, consider themselves a happy couple.
cn: 结婚二十年的罗纳德、罗伊斯夫妇认为自己是幸福的一对。

en: But in the early years of their marriage, both were distilled by persistent arguments that seem to fade away without ever being truly resolved.
cn: 但在早期婚姻生活中，两人都被持续反复的争执历练，这些争执虽从未真正得到解决却似乎已经慢慢消失。

en: They uncovered clues to what was going wrong by researching a fascinating subject: how birth order affects not only your personality, but also how compatible you are with your mate!
cn: 他们通过研究一个极具吸引力的课题发现了两人之间问题的线索，这个课题是：出生次序如何不但影响你的性格，还影响你与配偶的匹配程度！

en: Ronald and Lois are only children, and "onlies" grow up accustomed to being the apple of their parents' eyes.
cn: 罗纳德和罗伊斯都是独生子女，独生子女在成长过程中已经习惯被父母视为珍宝。

en: Match two "onlies" and you have partners who subconsciously expect each other to continue fulfilling this expectation, while neither has much experience in the "giving" end.
cn: 如果两个独生子女结婚，两人潜意识里都希望对方继续满足这一期待，而都没有多少作为“付出”一方的经验。

en: Here's a list of common birth-order characteristics — and some thoughts on the best and worst marital matches for each.
cn: 下面是不同出生次序对应的一些常见性格特征及其相应的最佳和最差婚配的一些想法。

en: The oldest tends to be self-assured, responsible, a high achiever and relatively serious and reserved.
cn: 长子女往往是拥有自信和责任感的成功人士，相对严谨和保守。

en: He may be slow to make friends, perhaps content with only one companion.
cn: 他可能不会轻易结交朋友，或许只需一个同伴就心满意足。

en: The best matches are with a youngest, an "only," or a mate raised in a large family.
cn: 最佳婚配对象是么子女、独生子女或在大家庭中长大的配偶。

en: The worst match is with another oldest, since the two will be too sovereign to share a household comfortably.
cn: 最差婚配对象是长子女，因为两人都过于强势，无法在同一屋檐下舒适共处。

en: The youngest child of the family thrives on attention and tends to be outgoing, adventurous, optimistic, creative and less ambitious than others in the family.
cn: 家中的么子女在关注中长大，往往是外向、有冒险精神、乐观、有创造力的，不如家中其他人那么雄心勃勃。

en: He may lack self-discipline and have difficulty making decisions on his own.
cn: 他可能缺乏自律精神，难以自主做决定。

en: A youngest brother of brothers, often unpredictable and romantic, will match best with an oldest sister of brothers.
cn: 兄弟中最小的一位往往善变且浪漫，与有若干弟弟的长姐最配。

en: The youngest sister of brothers is best matched with an oldest brother of sisters, who will happily indulge these traits.
cn: 有若干哥哥的么妹和有若干妹妹的长兄最配，后者会很乐意纵容前者的这些特点。

en: The middle child is influenced by many variables; however, middles are less likely to take initiative and more anxious and self-critical than others.
cn: 排行中间的孩子受许多变量的影响；但是，他们不会像其他人那样采取主动，但更为焦虑，更多地自我批判。

en: Middles often successfully marry other middles, since both are strong on tact, not so strong on the aggressiveness and tend to crave affection.
cn: 他们往往相互匹配成功结合，因为双方都机敏过人，攻击性不强，且倾向于渴求感情。

en: The only child is often most comfortable when alone.
cn: 独生子女通常在独处时最自在。

en: But since an "only" tends to be a well-adjusted individual, she'll eventually learn to relate to any chosen spouse.
cn: 但因为独生子女往往是一个个适应性强的个体，无论她选择了哪类配偶，最终都会学着与对方相处。

en: The male only child expects his wife to make life easier without getting much in return.
cn: 独子盼望妻子改善他的生活而不向他索取太多回报。

en: He is sometimes best matched with a younger sister of brothers.
cn: 他有时与有若干哥哥的妹妹最配。

en: The female only child, who tends to be slightly more flexible, is well matched with an older man, who will indulge her tendency to test his love.
cn: 独女往往稍微灵活一些，与较年长的男子相配，这样的男子会纵容她常常测试他的爱。

en: Her worst match?
cn: 她的最差婚配对象呢？

en: Another "only," of course.
cn: 当然就是另一个独生子女了。

en: Tonight we have a special guest from a local establishment, the Parisian Cafe.
cn: 今晚我们邀请到一位来自本地企业“巴黎人咖啡馆”的特别来宾。

en: Welcome!
cn: 欢迎！

en: Hi, thanks for having me on your show.
cn: 你好，谢谢你邀请我上节目。

en: Thank you for joining us.
cn: 感谢你的到来。

en: So please tell us, why did you decide to open a cafe?
cn: 那么请跟我们说说你为什么决定开一家咖啡馆呢？

en: Well, we saw the opportunity to offer something a little special and different from other establishments.
cn: 唔，我们发现了一个提供稍微有些特殊、有别于其他企业的东西的机会。

en: Cafes certainly are a very competitive market sector.
cn: 咖啡馆确实是个竞争特别激烈的行业。

en: There are more than plenty in our city, and we felt they are all rather similar to each other.
cn: 我们市里（咖啡馆）真是太多了，而且感觉它们都挺相似的。

en: Wouldn't you agree?
cn: 你不觉得吗？

en: Certainly yes.
cn: 确实是这样。

en: So how is your establishment any different?
cn: 那么你的咖啡馆是怎么个与众不同法呢？

en: Well, simply put, we have rabbits wandering freely around the place.
cn: 唔，简单来说，我们那儿有自由跑跳的兔子。

en: Our customers come in and enjoy their food and drinks while little rabbits play about and brush against their legs.
cn: 顾客进店享用食物和饮品，而小兔子们就在一旁玩耍，蹭着他们的腿。

en: There is no other place like it.
cn: 这可是个独一无二的地方。

en: That's amazing!
cn: 这真棒！

en: How did you come up with the idea?
cn: 你是怎么想出这个主意的？

en: We saw other cafes with cats in them.
cn: 我们看到其他一些咖啡馆里有小猫。

en: So we thought, why not rabbits?
cn: 所以我们就想，为什么不能是兔子呢？

en: People love rabbits.
cn: 人们非常喜欢兔子。

en: They are very cute animals.
cn: 它们特别可爱。

en: But is it safe?
cn: 但这安全吗？

en: Do the rabbits ever bite people?
cn: 这些兔子咬过人吗？

en: Or do any customers ever hurt the rabbits?
cn: 有顾客伤害过它们吗？

en: It's perfectly safe for both rabbits and our customers.
cn: 不管是兔子还是顾客都安全极了。

en: Rabbits are very peaceful and certainly do not bite.
cn: 兔子们都非常平和，当然不会咬人。

en: Furthermore, our rabbits are regularly cleaned and have all received the required shots.
cn: 另外，我们的兔子都会定期清洁，并且都按照要求打过疫苗。

en: So there is no health risk whatsoever.
cn: 所以是一丁点儿健康风险都没有。

en: As for our customers, they are all animal lovers, so they would never try to hurt the rabbits.
cn: 至于我们的顾客，他们都是爱动物的人，因此他们决不会试图伤害兔子。

en: Occasionally, a young child might get overexcited and a bit rough, but it's never a serious issue.
cn: 有时候，孩子可能会过于兴奋，动作不怎么温柔，但是这绝不是什么严重的问题。

en: On the contrary, the Parisian Cafe offers children a great experience, an opportunity to learn about rabbits and how to take care of them.
cn: 相反，巴黎人咖啡馆为孩子们提供了绝佳的体验，一个让他们能够了解兔子并学习如何照顾它们的机会。

en: Well, it's certainly the first time I've heard of a cafe like that.
cn: 好吧，这可确确实实是我第一次听说这样的咖啡馆。

en: Hey, there.
cn: 嗨。

en: How are you?
cn: 你好吗？

en: Oh, hi.
cn: 嗨。

en: I'm great!
cn: 我很好！

en: Thanks.
cn: 谢谢。

en: And you look great, too.
cn: 你看起来也很好。

en: Thank you.
cn: 谢谢关心。

en: It's good to see you shopping at the organic section.
cn: 很高兴看见你在有机食品货架这个区域买东西。

en: I see you've got lots of healthy stuff.
cn: 我看到你买了很多健康的东西。

en: I wish I could buy more organic produce from here, but I find the kids don't like it.
cn: 我好想能在这里购买更多有机产品，但我发现孩子们不喜欢。

en: I don't know about yours, but mine are all about junk food.
cn: 我不知道你的孩子怎么样，但我的孩子喜欢的都是垃圾食品。

en: Oh, trust me!
cn: 哦，相信我！

en: I know exactly how you feel.
cn: 我非常清楚你的感受。

en: My children are the same.
cn: 我的孩子也一样。

en: What is it with kids these days and all that junk food they eat?
cn: 现在的孩子都怎么了，怎么那么喜欢吃垃圾食品？

en: I think it's all that advertising on TV.
cn: 我认为这都是因为电视上的广告。

en: That's where they get it.
cn: 他们就从那儿知道的垃圾食品。

en: Yes, it must be.
cn: 是的，一定是。

en: My children see something on TV and they immediately want it.
cn: 我的孩子们在电视上看到了什么，他们立即就想要。

en: It's like they don't realize it's just an advertisement.
cn: 就像他们没有意识到这只是一个广告。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: And practically everything that's advertised for children is unhealthy processed foods.
cn: 几乎所有向儿童做广告的东西都是不健康的加工食品。

en: No surprise then it becomes a battle for us parents to feed our children ordinary food and vegetables.
cn: 毫不奇怪，对我们做父母的来说，给孩子提供普通食物和蔬菜成为一场战斗。

en: That's just the thing.
cn: 事情就是这样的。

en: One never sees ordinary ingredients being advertised on TV.
cn: 人们从未在电视上看到过普通食材的广告。

en: It's never a carrot or a peach.
cn: 广告里从来没有胡萝卜或桃子。

en: It's always some garbage, like chocolate-covered sweets.
cn: 总是一些垃圾食品，比如巧克力糖果。

en: So unhealthy.
cn: 太不健康了。

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: And these big food corporations have so much money to spend on clever tactics designed to make young children want to buy their products.
cn: 而且这些大型食品公司有很多钱花在巧妙的策略上，目的就是让年龄小一些的孩子想要购买他们的产品。

en: Children never stand a chance.
cn: 孩子们永远都不能抵抗住这种诱惑。

en: It's really not fair.
cn: 这真的不公平。

en: You are so right.
cn: 你是对的。

en: When we were children, we barely had any junk food available, and we turned out just fine.
cn: 我们还是孩子时，我们几乎吃不到任何垃圾食品，但也好好的。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: My parents don't understand any of it.
cn: 我的父母不明白这一点。

en: Both the TV commercials and the supermarkets are alien to them.
cn: 电视广告和超市对他们来说都是陌生的。

en: Their worlds were so different back when they were young.
cn: 在他们年轻的时候，他们的世界是如此不同。

en: I don't know what will happen to the next generation.
cn: 我不知道下一代会发生什么。

en: The world is going crazy.
cn: 世界正变得疯狂。

en: You bet.
cn: 你说的没错。

en: At some 2,300 miles in length, the Mississippi is the longest river in the United States.
cn: 密西西比河长约2300英里，是美国最长的河流。

en: At some 1,000 miles, the Mackenzie is the longest river in Canada.
cn: 马更些河长约1000英里，是加拿大最长的河流。

en: But these waterways seem minute in comparison to the world's two lengthiest rivers—the Nile and the Amazon.
cn: 但这两条水路与世界上最长的两条河——尼罗河和亚马逊河——相比就显得渺小了。

en: The Nile, which begins in central Africa and flows over 4,100 miles north into the Mediterranean, hosted one of the world's great ancient civilizations along its shores.
cn: 尼罗河（发源于非洲中部，跨越4100多英里向北注入地中海）沿岸孕育了世界上伟大的古代文明之一。

en: Calm and peaceful for most of the year, the Nile used to flood annually, thereby creating, irrigating and carrying new topsoil to the nearby farmland on which ancient Egypt depended for livelihood.
cn: 尼罗河在每年的大部分时间里都是平静温和的，过去它总是年年泛滥，从而创造、灌溉了附近的农田——古埃及赖以生存的田地，并为其运送去新鲜的表层土。

en: As a means of transportation, the river carried various vessels up and down its length.
cn: 作为一种交通方式，这条河运载着来往的各种船只。

en: A journey through the unobstructed part of this waterway today would pass by the splendid Valley of the Kings, where the tombs of many of these ancient monarchs have stood for over 3,000 years.
cn: 今天沿着这条水路中的畅通河段旅行时，会路过辉煌的帝王谷，众多古代帝王的陵墓在这里伫立了3000多年。

en: Great civilizations and intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon.
cn: 伟大的文明和密集的聚落几乎与亚马逊河沾不上边。

en: Yet this 4,000-mile-long south American river carries about 20% of the world's fresh water—more than the Mississippi, Nile, and Yangtze combined.
cn: 然而，这条4000英里长的南美洲河流承载了世界上约20%的淡水，比密西西比河、尼罗河和长江的总和还要多。

en: Other statistics are equally astonishing.
cn: 其他统计数据同样惊人。

en: The Amazon is so wide at some points that from its center neither shore can be seen.
cn: 亚马逊河的某些河段非常宽阔，以至于从河中心看不到两侧的岸边。

en: Each second, the Amazon pours some 55 million gallons of water into the Atlantic; there, at its mouth, stands one island larger than Switzerland.
cn: 亚马逊河每秒钟向大西洋注入约5500万加仑的水，其入海口处坐落着一个面积比瑞士还大的岛屿。

en: Most important of all, the Amazon irrigates the largest tropical rain forest on earth.
cn: 最重要的是，亚马逊河灌溉了地球上最大的热带雨林。

en: How often do you say to people "I'm busy" or "I haven't got time for that."
cn: 你多久对人说一次“我很忙”或者“我没时间弄这个”呢。

en: It's an inevitable truth that all of us live a life in the fast lane, even though we know that being busy is not always particularly healthy.
cn: 这是一个不可避免的事实：我们所有人都生活在快节奏中，即使我们知道忙碌并不总是特别健康。

en: Growing up in New Zealand, everything was always calm and slow.
cn: 我在新西兰长大，那里的一切总是平静而缓慢。

en: People enjoyed the tranquility of a slower pace of life.
cn: 人们享受着慢节奏生活的宁静。

en: But after I moved to Tokyo and lived there for a number of years, I got used to having a pile of to-do lists and my calendar always looked like a mess, with loads of things to do written across it.
cn: 但在我搬到东京并在那里住上几年后，我习惯了有一堆的待办事项清单，而且我的日历看起来总是一团糟，上面记满了要做的事情。

en: I found myself filling my time up with endless work meetings and social events, rushing along as busy as a bee.
cn: 我发现自己的时间填满了无休止的工作会议和社交活动，自己像蜜蜂一样忙碌。

en: Then, one day, I came across a book called In Praise of Slowness and realized that being busy is not only detrimental, but also has the danger of turning life into an endless race.
cn: 后来有一天，我无意中发现了一本名为《慢活》的书，意识到忙碌不仅有害，而且还有将生命变成一场没有尽头的赛跑的危险。

en: So I started practicing the various practical steps mentioned by the author in the book, and began to revolt against the very idea of being too busy.
cn: 所以我开始实践作者在书中提到的各种实用措施，对忙碌过头的想法变得反感。

en: It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist, but I've become more aware of the importance of slowing down and making sure that I enjoy the daily activities as I carry them out.
cn: 这不是说我就没有待办事项清单了，而是说我更清晰地意识到放慢生活节奏、确保自己处理日常事务时乐在其中的重要性。

en: From now on, when someone asks you how your life is, try responding with words like "exciting and fun" instead of the cultural norm that says "busy."
cn: 从现在开始，当有人问你过得怎么样的时候，尝试用“既刺激又有趣”这样的词来回应吧，而不是按照文化规范回答“很忙”。

en: See if you experience the tranquility that follows.
cn: 然后看看你是否感受到了宁静。

en: Governments, private groups and individuals spend billions of dollars a year trying to root out non-native organisms that are considered dangerous to ecosystems, and to prevent the introduction of new intruders.
cn: 政府、私人团体和个人每年花费数十亿美元试图彻底根除被认为对生态系统有危险的非本地生物体，并防止引进新的入侵者。

en: But a number of scientists question the assumption that the presence of alien species can never be acceptable in a natural ecosystem.
cn: 但是一些科学家对“在自然生态系统中，外来物种的存在永远不能被接受”这一假设提出了质疑。

en: They say that portraying introduced species as inherently bad is an unscientific approach.
cn: 他们指出，将引进的物种描绘成本质上不好的东西是不科学的。

en: Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial, said Dr. Michael Rosenzweig, a professor of evolutionary biology at the University of Arizona, because they depend on picking a date and calling the plants and animals that show up after that date exotic.
cn: 外来物种和本土物种的区别是人为（划分）的，亚利桑那大学进化生物学教授迈克尔·罗森茨威格博士指出，因为他们依靠的方法是选择一个日期，然后把那个日期之后出现的动植物叫作外来物种。

en: Ecosystems free of species defined as exotic are, by default, considered the most natural.
cn: 没有外来物种的生态系统，在默认情况下，被看作是最天然的。

en: "You can't roll back the clock and remove all exotics or fix habitats," Dr. Rosenzweig said.
cn: “你不能倒转时钟并驱除所有外来物种或修复栖息地”，罗森茨威格博士表示。

en: "Both native and exotic species can become invasive, and so they all have to be monitored and controlled when they begin to get out of hand."
cn: “本土物种和外来物种都能变成入侵物种，因此当它们开始失去控制时都必须被监控起来。”

en: At its core, the debate is about how to manage the world's remaining natural ecosystems and about how, and how much, to restore other habitats.
cn: 争论的核心是如何管理世界上现存的天然生态系统，以及如何恢复其他栖息地，恢复到何种程度。

en: Species that invade a territory can harm ecosystems, agriculture and human health.
cn: 侵入一个领地的物种可能会损害生态系统、农业和人类健康。

en: They can threaten some native species or even destroy and replace others.
cn: 它们可能会威胁一些本地物种，甚至毁灭和取代其他物种。

en: Next to habitat loss, these invasive species represent the greatest threat to biodiversity worldwide, many ecologists say.
cn: 许多生态学家指出，这些入侵物种，仅次于栖息地的减少，是全球生物多样性面临的最大威胁。

en: Ecologists generally define an alien species as one that people, accidentally or deliberately, carried to its new location.
cn: 生态学家通常将外来物种定义为人们偶然或故意带到新地区的物种。

en: Across the American continents, exotic species are those introduced after the first European contact.
cn: 在美洲大陆，外来物种是指欧洲人第一次进入美洲后引进的那些物种。

en: That date, rounded off to 1500 AD, represents what ecologists consider to have been a major shift in the spread of species, including crops and livestock, as they began to migrate with humans from continent to continent.
cn: 这一时期——大约在公元1500年——在生态学家看来，标志着农作物、牲畜等物种传播发生了重大转变，因为它们开始跟随人类从一个大陆迁移到另一个大陆。

en: Only a small percentage of alien species cause problems in their new habitats, said Don Smith, professor of ecology and evolutionary biology at the University of Tennessee.
cn: 只有一小部分外来物种会在它们的新栖息地引发问题，田纳西大学生态学和进化生物学教授唐·史密斯说道。

en: Of the 7,000 alien species in the United States — out of a total of 150,000 species — only about 10 percent are invasive, he pointed out.
cn: 他指出，美国15万个物种中，有7000个外来物种，其中只有大约10%是入侵物种。

en: The other 90 percent have fit into their environments and are considered naturalized.
cn: 其余90%已经融入到它们的环境中并被认定为归化物种。

en: Yet appearances can deceive, ecologists caution, and many of these exotics may be considered acceptable only because no one has documented their harmful effects.
cn: 然而，生态学家警告说，眼见不一定为实，这些外来物种中有很多可能只是因为没人记录它们的危害而被认定为可接受的物种。

en: What is more, non-native species can appear harmless for decades, then turn invasive.
cn: 更重要的是，非本土物种可能在几十年中看起来无害，然后才变成入侵物种。

en: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen.
cn: 女士们、先生们，早上好。

en: And welcome to the third in our series of business seminars in the program — Doing Business Abroad.
cn: 欢迎来到“境外经商”栏目第三期商务研讨会。

en: Today we are going to look at intercultural awareness, that is, the fact that not everyone is British, not everyone speaks English and not everyone does business in the British way.
cn: 今天，我们将着眼跨文化意识。也即：并非每个人都是英国人、并非每个人都说英语、并非每个人都以英国人的方式做生意。

en: And why should they?
cn: 他们又何必要那么做？

en: If overseas business people are selling to us and they will make every effort to speak English and to respect our traditions and methods.
cn: 如果外国商人要向我们销售商品，他们会尽一切努力说英语、尊重我们的传统和方式。

en: It is only polite for us to do the same when we visit them.
cn: 我们拜访他们时也这样做才是礼貌的。

en: It is not only polite.
cn: 这样做不仅关乎礼貌。

en: It is essential if we want to sell British products overseas.
cn: 如果我们想在国外销售英国产品，这样做也必不可少。

en: First, a short quiz.
cn: 首先，来个小测验。

en: Let's see how interculturally aware you are.
cn: 一起看看你们有多少跨文化意识？

en: Question 1: Where must you not drink alcohol on the first and seventh of every month?
cn: 问题一：在哪里每月的1日和7日不能喝酒？

en: Question 2: Where should you never admire your host's possessions?
cn: 问题二：在哪里绝不该称赞招待你的主人的财物？

en: Question 3: How should you attract the waiter during a business lunch in Bangkok?
cn: 问题三：在曼谷享用商业午餐时应如何招呼服务员？

en: And Question 4: Where should you try to make all your appointments either before 2:00 or after 5:30 p.m.?
cn: 以及问题四：在哪里应该将所有约见都安排在下午2点之前或5：30之后？

en: OK.
cn: 好。

en: Everyone had a chance to make some notes?
cn: 大家都做好笔记了吗？

en: Right.
cn: 好的。

en: Here are the answers — although I am sure that the information could equally well apply to countries other than those I have chosen.
cn: 答案揭晓——不过我敢确定除了我选取的国家，这些信息（这种文化差异）同样适用于其他国家。

en: So No. 1, you must not drink alcohol on the first and seventh of the month in India.
cn: 那么第一：在印度，不能在每月1日和7日喝酒。

en: In international hotels, you may find it served, but if you are having a meal with an Indian colleague, remember to avoid asking for a beer if your arrival coincides with one of those dates.
cn: 你可能会发现国际酒店里提供酒，但如果你刚好撞上这两天中的一天到印度，又正和印度同事一同用餐，记住不要点啤酒。

en: 2. In Arab countries, the politeness and generosity of the people is without parallel.
cn: 第二：在阿拉伯国家，人们的礼貌和慷慨无可比拟。

en: If you admire your colleague's beautiful golden bowls, you may well find yourself being presented with them as a present.
cn: 如果夸同事的金饭碗好看，很可能发现它们会被当作礼物送给你。

en: This is not a cheap way to do your shopping, however, as your host will, quite correctly, expect you to respond by presenting him with a gift of equal worth and beauty.
cn: 不过，这可不是一种省钱的购物方式，因为招待你的主人会理所当然地希望你回赠他同样价值、同样漂亮的礼物。

en: In Thailand, clicking the fingers, clapping your hands, or just shouting "Waiter!" will embarrass your hosts, fellow diners, the waiter himself and, most of all, you!
cn: 在泰国，打响指、拍手或者只是大喊“服务员！”都会令招待你的主人、同席的其他人、这位服务员、特别是你自己难堪。

en: Place your palm downward and make an inconspicuous waving gesture, which will produce instant and satisfying results.
cn: 将手掌朝下，做出一个不明显的挥手姿势会产生立竿见影、令人满意的效果。

en: And finally, in Spain, some businesses maintain the pattern of working until about 2 o'clock and then returning to the office from 5:30 to 8:00, 9:00 or 10:00 in the evening.
cn: 最后，在西班牙，一些企业保持着“工作到大约下午2点整、再于晚上5：30到8点、9点或10点接着办公”的模式。

en: Shortly after he took over the Reader's Digest Association in 1984, George Grune unlocked the company's boardroom and announced that the room was now open to the employees.
cn: 乔治·格鲁恩1984年接管读者文摘协会后不久就打开公司董事会议室的大门，宣布会议室现在向员工们开放。

en: It was a symbolic act, indicating that under Grune's leadership, Reader's Digest was going to be different.
cn: 这是一种象征性的举动，表明《读者文摘》在格鲁恩的领导下将会不同。

en: True to his word, Grune has shaken up the culture here.
cn: 确实如格鲁恩所说，他已重塑了这里的文化。

en: To get an idea of the culture we're talking about, consider the boardroom Grune opened up.
cn: 为了弄明白我们所说的这种文化，想想看格鲁恩开放的董事会议室。

en: It has artworks that any museum in the world would want to collect, paintings by many world famous artists like Monet and Picasso.
cn: 它拥有世界上任何一家博物馆都想要收藏的艺术品，拥有莫奈和毕加索等许多世界知名艺术家的画作。

en: Its headquarters houses some 3,000 works of art.
cn: 公司总部存放有3000多件艺术品。

en: The main building is topped with a Georgian Tower with four sculptures of the mythical winged horse, the magazine's corporate logo.
cn: 公司主楼顶部为乔治王朝时期的塔楼，塔楼上有四座雕塑，雕刻着神话中的飞马——该杂志公司的标志。

en: It sits on 127 acres of well-trimmed lawns.
cn: 主楼坐落在127英亩修剪整齐的草坪上。

en: The editor's office used to be occupied by founder DeWitt Wallace, who, along with his wife, Lila Acheson Wallace, launched Reader's Digest in 1922 with condensed articles from other publications.
cn: 编辑办公室过去被德威特·华莱士占用，他和他的妻子莉拉·埃奇森·华莱士将其他出版物中的文章缩编，于1922年创办了《读者文摘》。

en: It has become the world's most widely read magazine, selling 28 million copies each month in 17 languages and 41 different editions.
cn: 它每月以17种语言和41个版本发行2800万册，已成为世界上阅读量最大的杂志。

en: The Wallaces, both children of church ministers, had a clearly defined formula for their "little magazine" as Reader's Digest was originally subtitled.
cn: 华莱士夫妇均为教堂牧师的孩子，他们最初在给《读者文摘》写副标题时就给自己这本小杂志制定了明确的准则。

en: Articles were to be short, readable and uplifting.
cn: 文章要简短易读、鼓舞人心。

en: Subjects were picked to inspire or entertain.
cn: 文章主题经过挑选，意在鼓舞或取悦（读者）。

en: The Wallaces didn't accept advertising in the US edition until 1955 and even then they didn't allow any ads for cigarettes, liquor or drugs.
cn: 直到1955年，华莱士夫妇才接受在美国版杂志上刊登广告，即便如此，他们也不允许有任何烟酒或毒品的广告。

en: The Wallaces also had a clear sense of the kind of workplace they wanted.
cn: 华莱士夫妇也很清楚他们想要怎样的工作环境。

en: It started as a mom-and-pop operation and the childless Wallaces always considered employees to be part of their family.
cn: 公司最初以夫妻店的形式经营，华莱士夫妇没有孩子，他们总是把员工当作家庭的一份子。

en: Employees still tell stories of how the Wallaces would take care of their employees who had met with misfortunes and they showered their employees with unusual benefits, like a turkey on Thanksgiving and Fridays off in May.
cn: 员工现在仍会谈到夫妇二人如何照料遭遇不幸的员工，谈到他们给予员工许多罕见的福利，比如感恩节的火鸡、五月份周五不上班。

en: This cozy workplace no longer exists here.
cn: 这种舒适的工作环境已不复存在。

en: The Wallaces both died in their nineties in the early 1980s.
cn: 夫妇二人均于20世纪80年代初去世，享年九十余岁。

en: George Grune, a former ad salesman who joined Reader's Digest in 1960, has his eye focused on the bottom line.
cn: 乔治·格鲁恩于1960年加入《读者文摘》，此前是一名广告推销员，他将着眼点放在了净利润上。

en: In a few short years, he turned the magazine on its head.
cn: 短短几年里，他彻底改变了杂志社。

en: He laid off several hundred workers.
cn: 他解雇了数百名员工。

en: Especially hard hit were the blue- and pink-collar departments such as subscription fulfillment.
cn: 尤其受到重创的是订阅执行部等蓝领和粉领部门。

en: Hey, I just read a great book about physics.
cn: 嗨，我刚读了一本有关物理学的书。

en: I think you'd like it.
cn: 我想你会喜欢的。

en: It's called The Physics of the World.
cn: 书名叫《物理世界》。

en: It's written by a scientist named Sylvia Mundus.
cn: 作者是一名叫做西尔维亚·蒙德斯的科学家。

en: Oh I read that book.
cn: 噢，我读过这本书。

en: It was great.
cn: 特别棒。

en: The writer is a warm and competent guide to the mysteries of physics.
cn: 作者是一位热情而又称职的向导，引领读者开启物理学奥秘之旅。

en: I think it promises enrichment for any reader, from those who know little about science to the career physicist.
cn: 我想这本书会让每一位读者，从对科学知之甚少者到职业物理学家，都受益匪浅。

en: And it's refreshing to see a strong, curious, clever woman adding her voice to the scientific discourse in a field that has been traditionally dominated by men.
cn: 而且，看到一位坚强的、好求知的、聪慧的女性在传统上由男性主导的科学领域发出声音也让人耳目一新。

en: I think she is to be commended for making an effort to include anecdotes about little-known female scientists.
cn: 她努力把鲜为人知的女性科学家轶事著入书中，我认为这一点值得称赞。

en: You know, they were often victims of "a generation firmly convinced that the woman's place was in the home."
cn: 你知道的，她们通常是“坚信女性应该待在家里一代”的受害者。

en: I like how the book is clearly written with each chapter brought to life by pieces of fascinating knowledge.
cn: 我喜欢这本书的写作风格，清晰而又生动，包含许多有趣知识。

en: For example, in one chapter she exposes a myth that I've heard taught by university physics professors.
cn: 比如，她在某一章里揭露了一个我曾听大学物理教授讲授过的谬误。

en: I've often heard that medieval glass windows are thicker at the bottom because glass "flows" like a fluid.
cn: 我常听说中世纪的玻璃窗底部更厚是因为玻璃会像液体一样“流动”。

en: This, she shows, is not true; the distortion is actually thanks to a peculiarity of the glassmaker's process.
cn: 她表示，这并非事实；这种变形实际上是由于玻璃制造工艺的特殊性造成的。

en: Yeah, I like how she cultivates scientific engagement by providing a host of do-it-yourself experiments that bring the same foundational principles of classical physics that govern everything from the solar system to your kitchen table.
cn: 是的，我喜欢她通过提供大量DIY实验来培养人们的科学参与意识，这些实验将支配太阳系种种物质的经典物理学相同基本原理运用到寻常百姓餐桌上。

en: From using complex laws of physics to test whether a spinning egg is cooked to measuring atmospheric pressure by lifting a piece of cardboard, her hands-on examples make her book a truly interactive read.
cn: 从运用复杂物理定律来测试旋转的鸡蛋是否煮熟，到通过举起一块硬纸板来测量大气压，她的这些实操例子使得这本书给人带来一种真正的交互式阅读体验。

en: Yes, I must say this equation-free book is an ideal read for scientists of all stripes, anyone teaching science and even people who dislike physics.
cn: 是的，我必须要说这本无等式书是各行各业科学家、是每一位科学教师、甚至是不喜欢物理之人的理想读物。

en: Hi professor!
cn: 嗨，教授！

en: I was hoping I could have a moment of your time if you are not too busy.
cn: 要是您不太忙的话，我想占用您一点时间。

en: I'm having some problems getting started on my dissertation and I was hoping you could give me some advice on how to begin.
cn: 我的学位论文开题遇到了一些问题，希望您能给我一些建议，告诉我该怎么办。

en: Sure.
cn: 当然可以。

en: I have quite a few students though.
cn: 不过我学生有点多。

en: So can you remind me what your topic is?
cn: 能告诉我你的论题是什么吗？

en: The general topic I chose is aesthetics.
cn: 我选的大论题是美学。

en: But that's as far as I've got.
cn: 但目前为止我就做了这么个选择。

en: I don't really know where to go from there.
cn: 我其实不太清楚接下去该往哪个方向下手。

en: Yeah, that's much too large a topic.
cn: 是的，这个论题太大了。

en: You really need to narrow it down in order to make it more accessible, otherwise you will be writing a book.
cn: 你的确需要把论题缩小，让它更易着手，否则你得写成一本书了。

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: That's what I wanted to ask you about.
cn: 这就是我想问您的。

en: I was hoping it would be possible for me to change topics.
cn: 我希望能换个论题。

en: I'm really more interested in nature than beauty.
cn: 比起美学，我实际上对自然更感兴趣。

en: I'm afraid you have to adhere to the assigned topic.
cn: 恐怕你还是得继续研究指定的论题。

en: Still, if you are interested in nature, then that certainly can be worked into your dissertation.
cn: 不过，如果你对自然感兴趣，当然也可以把它写进论文里。

en: We've talked about Hume before in class, right?
cn: 我们之前在课上讲过休谟，不是吗？

en: Oh yeah.
cn: 哦，对。

en: He's the philosopher who wrote about where our ideas of beauty come from.
cn: 他就是那位著述过我们对美的看法从何而来的哲学家。

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: I suggest you go to the library and get a copy of his biography.
cn: 我建议你去图书馆借一本他的传记。

en: Start from there.
cn: 以此为起点。

en: But remember to stick to the parameters of the assignment.
cn: 但要记住，必须遵守作业规范。

en: This paper is a large part of your cumulative grade, so make sure to follow the instructions.
cn: 这篇论文在你的总成绩里占很大比重，所以一定要遵循要求。

en: If you take a look at his biography, you can get a good idea of how his life experiences manifest themselves in his theories of beauty, specifically, the way he looked towards nature as the origin of what we find beautiful.
cn: 如果你读了他的传记，就能很好地了解他的生活经历如何体现在他的美学理论中，确切地说，是他如何将自然看作美好事物的起源。

en: Great!
cn: 太好了！

en: Thanks for taking the time to answer my questions, professor.
cn: 感谢您花时间回答我的问题，教授。

en: I'll let you get back to class now.
cn: 现在您可以回去上课了。

en: If there is anything else you need, please come see me in my office anytime.
cn: 如果你还有其他需要，欢迎随时来我的办公室。

en: During the Arctic winter from October to March, the average temperature in the frozen north typically hovers around minus 20 degrees Celsius.
cn: 在北极的冬季（10月至次年3月），冰封的北方平均气温通常徘徊在零下20摄氏度左右。

en: But this year, the Arctic is experiencing much higher temperatures.
cn: 但今年，北极正在经历高得多的温度。

en: On February 20th, the temperature in Greenland climbed above freezing or zero degrees Celsius and it stayed there for over 24 hours.
cn: 2月20日，格陵兰岛的气温攀升至冰点（零摄氏度）以上，且持续时间超过24小时。

en: Then, on February 24th, the temperature on Greenland's northern tip reached 6 degrees Celsius.
cn: 随后，在2月24日，格陵兰岛最北端气温达到了6摄氏度。

en: Climate scientists described the phenomenon as "stunning".
cn: 气候学家认为这一现象令人震惊。

en: Weather conditions that drive this bizarre temperature surge have visited the Arctic before.
cn: 造成气温异常升高的各种天气条件此前也曾造访北极。

en: They typically appear about once in a decade.
cn: 它们通常十年一遇。

en: However, the last such increase in temperature took place two years ago.
cn: 但上次出现这样的气温上升却是在两年前。

en: This is troubling as climbing Arctic temperatures combined with rapid sea-ice loss are creating a new type of climate feedback loop which could accelerate Arctic warming.
cn: 这一现象引人担忧，因为北极气温攀升，连同海面浮冰迅速减少，正在建立起一种新的气候反馈环路，进而加速北极变暖。

en: Indeed, sea-ice cover in the Arctic is melting faster than expected.
cn: 事实上，覆盖北极海面的浮冰融化速度比预想的更快。

en: Without those masses of cooling sea ice, warm air brought to the Arctic can penetrate further inland than it ever did before.
cn: 没有这些起冷却作用的大片海面浮冰，被带到北极的暖空气就能深入至之前它从未到达的内陆地区。

en: The air can stay warmer longer, too.
cn: 暖空气会保持在更高温度，停留时间也会变长。

en: This drives additional melting.
cn: 这将导致（浮冰）进一步融化。

en: Overall, Earth is warming at a rapid pace - 2014 through 2017 rank as the hottest years on record - and the Arctic is warming twice as fast as anyplace else on Earth.
cn: 总的来说，地球正迅速变暖（2014年至2017年被认为是有记录以来最热的年份），北极变暖的速度是地球上其余各地的两倍。

en: This raises unique challenges for Arctic wildlife and indigenous people who depend on Arctic ecosystems to survive.
cn: 这会给依赖北极生态系统生存的当地野生动植物和原住民带来极不寻常的挑战。

en: Previously, climate forecasts predicted that Arctic summer ice would disappear entirely by around 2060.
cn: 此前，气候预测曾指出，北极夏季的浮冰到2060年左右将会完全消失。

en: But based on what scientists are seeing now, the Arctic may be facing summers without ice within 20 years.
cn: 但根据科学家如今的观测，20年之内北极或许就会面临没有浮冰的夏季。

en: A good dose of willpower is often necessary to see any task through, whether it's sticking to a spending plan or finishing a great novel.
cn: 要完成任何一项任务，强大的意志力往往必不可少，无论是坚持执行一项支出计划还是坚持读完一部伟大小说。

en: And if you want to increase that willpower, a new study suggests you just simply have to believe you have it.
cn: 而且一项新研究表明，如果想要提升这种意志力，你仅仅需要相信自己拥有它。

en: According to the study, what matters most is what we think about our willpower.
cn: 根据这项研究，最重要的是我们如何看待自己的意志力。

en: If we believe it's a finite resource, we act that way.
cn: 如果我们认为它是一种有限的资源，那我们便会以此行事。

en: We feel exhausted and need breaks between demanding mental tasks.
cn: 我们会在费力的脑力劳动之间感到精疲力竭，需要暂停。

en: However, people who view their willpower as a limitless resource get energized instead.
cn: 然而，将自己的意志力视为永不枯竭的资源的人却能保持精力充沛。

en: The researchers used a psychological assessment tool to test the validity of the study.
cn: 研究者使用一种心理评估工具对研究的效度进行了测试。

en: They asked one thousand one hundred Americans and one thousand six hundred Europeans to grade different statements such as "After a challenging mental activity, my energy is depleted and I must rest to get it refueled again" or "I can focus on a mental task for long periods without feeling tired".
cn: 他们让1100名美国人和1600名欧洲人给不同的表述打分，如“在一项挑战性脑力活动之后，我的能量会耗尽，我必须休息以补充能量”或“我可以长时间专注于一项脑力工作而不感到疲惫”。

en: Although there was little difference between men and women overall, Americans were more likely to admit to needing breaks after completing mentally challenging tasks.
cn: 尽管总体上男性和女性几乎没有差异，但美国人更可能承认自己在完成挑战性脑力任务后需要休息。

en: European participants, on the other hand, claimed they were able to keep going.
cn: 欧洲参与者则声称自己能够继续坚持。

en: Based on the findings, the researchers suggest that the key to boosting your willpower is to believe that you have an abundant supply of it.
cn: 基于以上发现，研究者表示提升意志力的关键在于相信自己有充足的意志力供应。

en: Your feelings about your willpower affect the way you behave.
cn: 你对自己意志力的感受会影响你的行为方式。

en: But these feelings are changeable, they said.
cn: 但这些感受是可变的，他们说道。

en: Changing your beliefs about the nature of your self-control can have positive effects on character development.
cn: 改变你对于自控力本质的信念可以对人格发展产生积极效应。

en: This leads to healthier behaviors and perceptions of other people.
cn: 这会带来更健康的行为，以及对他人更健全的认知。

en: Here is my baby niece Sarah.
cn: 这是我的小侄女萨拉。

en: Her mom is a doctor and her dad is a lawyer.
cn: 她的妈妈是医生，爸爸是律师。

en: By the time Sarah goes to college, the jobs her parents do are going to look dramatically different.
cn: 到萨拉上大学的时候，她父母的工作看起来将会非常不同。

en: In 2013, researchers at Oxford University did a study on the future of work.
cn: 2013年，牛津大学的研究人员开展过一项关于工作未来的研究。

en: They concluded that almost one in every two jobs has a high risk of being automated by machines.
cn: 他们的结论是，几乎每两份工作中就有一份面临着被机器自动化的高风险。

en: Machine learning is the technology that's responsible for most of this disruption.
cn: 机器学习这项技术是造成这一动荡的主要原因。

en: It's the most powerful branch of artificial intelligence.
cn: 它是人工智能最强大的分支。

en: It allows machines to learn from data and copy some of the things that humans can do.
cn: 它使得机器能够从数据中学习，并模仿人类能做的一部分事情。

en: My company, Kaggle, operates on the cutting edge of machine learning.
cn: 我所在的公司Kaggle就走在机器学习的最前沿。

en: We bring together hundreds of thousands of experts to solve important problems for industry and academia.
cn: 我们集结了成千上万名专家为业界和学界解决重大问题。

en: This gives us a unique perspective on what machines can do, what they can't do and what jobs they might automate or threaten.
cn: 这让我们对机器能做什么、不能做什么、哪些工作岗位会被自动化或受威胁等问题形成了独特的视角。

en: Machine learning started making its way into industry in the early '90s.
cn: 机器学习在90年代早期进入产业界。

en: It started with relatively simple tasks.
cn: 它最初所做的工作相对简单。

en: It started with things like assessing credit risk from loan applications, sorting the mail by reading handwritten zip codes.
cn: 它一开始用于评估贷款申请的信用风险、识别手写邮编以分类信件。

en: Over the past few years, we have made dramatic breakthroughs.
cn: 在过去的几年中，我们已取得巨大进展。

en: Machine learning is now capable of far, far more complex tasks.
cn: 机器学习如今足以胜任复杂得多的工作。

en: In 2012, Kaggle challenged its community to build a program that could grade high-school essays.
cn: 2012年，Kaggle向它的社群发布一项挑战，号召开发能对高中作文进行评分的程序。

en: The winning programs were able to match the grades given by human teachers.
cn: 胜出程序给出的分数与人类教师的评分结果相契合。

en: Now, given the right data, machines are going to outperform humans at tasks like this.
cn: 如今，输入适当的数据后，机器在此类任务上的表现要优于人类。

en: A teacher might read 10,000 essays over a 40-year career.
cn: 一名教师在40年的教学生涯中大概能看1万篇作文。

en: A machine can read millions of essays within minutes.
cn: 一台机器几分钟就能看上百万篇作文。

en: We have no chance of competing against machines on frequent, high-volume tasks.
cn: 在大批量重复性任务方面，我们面对机器毫无胜算。

en: But there are things we can do that machines cannot.
cn: 但是，有一些事情我们能做而机器做不来。

en: Where machines have made very little progress is in tackling novel situations.
cn: 在应对新情况方面机器的进展甚微。

en: Machines can't handle things they haven't seen many times before.
cn: 机器无从应对那些没怎么见过的情况。

en: The fundamental limitation of machine learning is that it needs to learn from large volumes of past data.
cn: 机器学习的根本局限性在于，机器需要从大量的过往数据中学习。

en: But humans don't.
cn: 但是人类不需要。

en: We have the ability to connect seemingly different threads to solve problems we've never seen before.
cn: 我们有能力把看似不同的各种细节串联起来，解决我们从未遇到过的问题。

en: We've talked recently about the importance of sustainable energy.
cn: 最近，我们已经谈论过可持续能源的重要性。

en: We've also talked about the different theories on how that can be done.
cn: 也谈到了关于“如何实现能源可持续”的各种理论。

en: So far, our discussions have all been theoretical.
cn: 迄今为止，我们的讨论都是理论性的。

en: Now I have a practical question for you all.
cn: 现在，我要问你们所有人一个实际性的问题。

en: Can you run a 140,000 kilogram train on just the steam generated by solar power?
cn: 你们能完全依靠太阳能产生的蒸汽来驱动一辆重达140吨的火车吗？

en: Well, one engineer, Tim Castleman, believes it's possible.
cn: 工程师蒂姆·卡斯尔曼相信这是可以实现的。

en: And his home city of Sacramento, California should see the technology's first test.
cn: 他的家乡，加州的萨克拉门托，将见证这一技术的首次测试。

en: As part of the upgrading of its rail yard, Castleman, who is an inventor and self-proclaimed steam visionary, is campaigning for a new steam train that runs without any fire and could run on an existing 10-kilometer line, drawing tourists and perhaps offering city commuters a green alternative to their cars.
cn: 作为萨克拉门托铁路段升级的一部分，发明家、同时又自命为蒸汽动力梦想家的卡斯尔曼正发起一场新型蒸汽火车运动，这种火车运行时无需火力推动，且能在现有的10公里路段上行驶，可以吸引游客，也可为城市通勤者提供一种替代汽车的绿色交通工具。

en: Castleman wants to build an array of solar magnifying mirrors at the end of the line to collect and focus heat onto water-filled tubes.
cn: 卡斯尔曼想在这条路段的一端建造太阳能聚光镜，收集热量并将其集中到装满水的管道之上。

en: This would generate steam that could be used to fill tanks on a small steam train without the use of fire.
cn: 这样无需用火就会产生蒸汽，蒸汽可用以填充小型蒸汽火车上的水罐。

en: Supplying power to trains in this way would offer "the shortest distance from well to wheels," he says, with the least amount of energy lost.
cn: 他说，以这种方式为火车提供动力能提供“从油井到车轮”的最短路径，能量损耗最小。

en: According to Harry Valentine, a Canadian engineer who is researching modern steam technology, a special tank measuring 2 by 10 metres could store over 750 kilowatt-hours of energy as high-pressure steam, enough to pull a two-car train for an hour or so.
cn: 据哈里·瓦伦汀（一名研究现代蒸汽技术的加拿大工程师）称，一个2×10米的专用罐体可以以高压蒸汽的形式储存超过750千瓦时能量，这足以驱动一列两节车厢的火车行驶一小时左右。

en: Energy to drive a steam locomotive can be stored in other materials besides water.
cn: 驱动蒸汽机车的能量也可以储存在除“水”以外的其它物质中。

en: For example, a team at Tohoku University in Japan has studied materials that can store large amounts of heat.
cn: 比如，日本东北大学的一个团队对多种能储存大量热的物质进行了研究。

en: When heated, these materials turn from a solid into a liquid absorbing energy as they change phase.
cn: 受热时，这些物质会由固体转化为液体，物态转化过程中会吸收能量。

en: The liquid is maintained above its melting point until steam is required, at which point the liquid is allowed to turn back into a solid, releasing its stored energy.
cn: 液体被保持在熔点以上，直到需要蒸汽时才被转化为固体，同时释放其储存的能量。

en: Another team, at Nagoya University in Japan, has tested calcium compound as an energy storage material.
cn: 日本名古屋大学的另一团队测试了钙化合物能否用作储能材料。

en: Heating this chemical compound drives off carbon dioxide gas, leaving calcium oxide.
cn: 加热钙化合物会释放二氧化碳气体，留下氧化钙。

en: The gas can be stored under pressure in a tank.
cn: 二氧化碳气体可以在一定压力下储存于罐中。

en: To recover the energy, the gas is fed back over the calcium oxide.
cn: 要回收能量时，再将气体通入氧化钙。

en: In theory, says Valeriano, this can create a light enough temperature to generate superheated steam.
cn: 瓦伦汀说，理论上，这一过程产生的高温足以生成过热蒸汽。

en: Today's crisis in care for older people in England has two main causes.
cn: 如今英国的老年人护理危机有两个主要原因。

en: First, people are living longer with a lot more complex needs.
cn: 首先，人们的寿命更长，需求更复杂。

en: Second, they rely on a system that has long been marked by a poor relation between national health and social care services.
cn: 其次，他们依赖的是一个长期以来“国民医疗保健和社会护理服务关系欠佳”为特征的体系。

en: Current services originate in two key measures.
cn: 当前服务源于两项重要法案。

en: They are the National Health Service and the 1948 National Assistance Act.
cn: 即《国民医疗服务法》和1948年的《国民救助法》。

en: This required local governments to provide residential accommodation for older people and supervise care homes run by independent organizations.
cn: 这要求地方政府为老年人提供住宿，并对由独立机构经营的养老院进行监督。

en: They also provided home and community services, including meals, day centres and home helpers and other subsidized services.
cn: 它们还提供家庭和社区服务，包括膳食、日托中心和家庭帮佣以及其他补贴服务。

en: The National Health Service was free and wholly publicly provided.
cn: 国民医疗服务免费，完全由政府提供。

en: It delivered the best health care for all.
cn: 它为所有人提供最好的医疗保健。

en: No such vision guided residential and community care though.
cn: 然而，没有这样的愿景来指导院舍护理及社区护理。

en: The care was substantially provided by voluntary services which worked together with local authorities as they long had, with eligibility based on income.
cn: 这些护理大部分是由志愿服务机构提供的，这些机构长期与地方政府合作，根据收入多少确定公民是否有资格得到护理。

en: Today, life expectancy has risen from 66 for a male at best in 1948 to around 80 now.
cn: 今天，男性平均寿命已经从1948年的最高66岁提高到现在的约80岁。

en: In addition, there is better overall health and improved medical knowledge in care.
cn: 此外，人们的整体健康水平和护理方面的医学知识均得以提升。

en: This means an unprecedented number of people are surviving longer in conditions requiring experts' support.
cn: 这意味着数量空前的人口在依赖于专家支持的环境中活得更加长久。

en: Families provide at least as much care as they ever did.
cn: 家庭所提供的照护至少和以前一样多。

en: Even so, they can rarely, without subsidized support, address serious personal needs.
cn: 但即便如此，若没有补贴性援助，他们依然很难解决重大个人需求。

en: Care for older people faced persistent criticism as these trends became apparent.
cn: 随着这些趋势越来越明显，老年人护理面对的批评从未中断。

en: From the early 1960s, local authorities were required to plan health and welfare services.
cn: 从20世纪60年代初开始，地方政府被要求对健康及福利服务进行规划。

en: The aim was to enable older people to remain in their own homes for as long as possible.
cn: 目的是使老年人尽可能长时间地生活在自己的家里。

en: But this increased concern about the lack of coordination between free health and paid-for social care.
cn: 但这增加了人们对“免费医疗服务与有偿社会护理之间缺乏协调”的担忧。

en: Through the 1970s, a number of measures sought to improve matters.
cn: 在整个20世纪70年代，政府出台了大量措施致力于改善这一状况。

en: However, at a time of financial crisis, funding diminished and little changed.
cn: 然而，金融危机期间，资金持续减少、情况几乎未变。

en: In the 1980s, the government cut spending.
cn: 20世纪80年代，政府削减支出。

en: Meanwhile, preference for private over public services made management even more difficult.
cn: 而且，“人们青睐私营服务胜于公共服务”使得管理更加困难。

en: Simultaneously, the number of sick older people grew.
cn: 与此同时，患病老人数量也在增加。

en: Governments emphasized the need to improve services.
cn: 政府强调需要改进服务。

en: They did so, though, while doing little to stop the erosion of available aid.
cn: 然而他们这样做的同时却并未采取什么措施来阻止可用援助的削弱。

en: Services were irregular across authorities.
cn: 各个部门的服务都是非正规的。

en: Unless you were prepared to pay, they were increasingly difficult to obtain for any but the most severely disabled.
cn: 除非你打算付钱，否则除最严重的残障人士外，人们越来越难以获得服务。

en: Why has sixty years of criticism produced so little change?
cn: 为什么持续60年的批评只带来了如此小的改变？

en: Discrimination against older people has a long history.
cn: 对老年人的歧视由来已久。

en: Additionally, those affected by inadequate health and social care are too vulnerable to launch the protests that have addressed other forms of discrimination.
cn: 此外，受“医疗服务及社会护理不足”影响的群体极为弱势，难以发起解决其他形式的歧视问题所使用的抗议活动。

en: Do you mind taking my photo with the statue over there?
cn: 你介意帮我和那边的雕像拍张照吗？

en: I think it will make a great shot.
cn: 我觉得这样拍出来的照片会很棒。

en: Sure, no worries.
cn: 当然，没问题。

en: You're always taking photos.
cn: 你一直在拍照。

en: What do you do with all the photos you take?
cn: 你都怎么处理拍出来的那些照片呢？

en: Well, don't laugh.
cn: 嗯，别笑我。

en: My dream is to become an online celebrity of sorts.
cn: 我的梦想是成为一个不那么红的网红。

en: You are not serious, are you?
cn: 你该不会是认真的吧？

en: I am, completely.
cn: 认真，非常认真。

en: I just got the idea a few months ago after posting some holiday photos on my social media accounts.
cn: 我几个月前才有了这个想法。当时我在自己的社交媒体账号上发布了一些度假照片。

en: A lot of people liked my photos and started asking me for travel tips.
cn: 很多人给我的照片点赞并向我要旅行攻略。

en: So I figured I'd give it a go.
cn: 所以我想我应该试试。

en: I post a lot on social media anyway.
cn: 反正我会在社交媒体上发很多东西。

en: So I've got nothing to lose.
cn: 所以我也没什么损失。

en: I guess that's true.
cn: 我想你说的对。

en: So what do you have to do to become Internet famous?
cn: 那么，你要怎么做才能成为网红呢？

en: Surprisingly a lot more than I did as a hobby.
cn: 没想到的是，这比我当初仅把它作为业余爱好要多做很多。

en: Recently, I've been spending a lot more time editing photos, posting online and clearing storage on my phone.
cn: 最近，我花了大量时间修图、发帖、以及清理手机存储空间。

en: It's always full now.
cn: 我的手机存储空间现在总是占满。

en: That doesn't sound like too much work.
cn: 听起来工作量并不大呀。

en: Well, there's more to it.
cn: 当然远不止这些。

en: I spent all last weekend researching what topics are popular, what words to use in captions and similar accounts to follow.
cn: 上周整个周末我都在研究什么话题热门，什么词可用于标题，以及要关注哪些相似账号。

en: It really was a lot to take in.
cn: 的确有很多东西要去领会。

en: And I was up well past midnight.
cn: 过了半夜我都还没睡。

en: I'd say it's paying off though.
cn: 不过我得说这是值得的。

en: I increased the number of people following my accounts by 15% already.
cn: 我把关注我账号的人数提升了15%。

en: That is impressive.
cn: 真了不起。

en: I guess I never thought much about all the effort behind the scene.
cn: 我想我从未考虑过需要这么多的幕后努力。

en: Now that I think about it, there's always something wrong with my photos as it is — half smiles, closed eyes, messy hair.
cn: 现在回想起来，我的照片里总有些瑕疵——似笑非笑，闭着眼睛，头发凌乱。

en: I hope you have better luck than I do.
cn: 我希望你运气比我好。

en: Then again, I think the only person interested in my photos is my mom.
cn: 不过话又说回来，我觉得唯一对我的照片感兴趣的人就是我妈。

en: Good evening and welcome to Physics Today.
cn: 晚上好，欢迎来到“今日物理”。

en: Here we interview some of the greatest minds in physics as they help us to understand some of the most complicated theories.
cn: 节目中我们采访一些物理学界首屈一指的学者，他们会帮助我们理解一些最为复杂的理论。

en: Today, I'm very pleased to welcome Dr. Melissa Phillips, professor of theoretical physics.
cn: 今天，我十分高兴地欢迎理论物理学教授，梅丽莎·菲利普斯博士。

en: She's here to tell us a little about what it is she studies.
cn: 她来到这里是为和我们聊聊她的研究。

en: Dr. Phillips, you seem to study everything.
cn: 菲利普斯博士，您似乎什么都研究啊。

en: I guess that would be fair to say I spend most of my time studying the Big Bang theory and where our universe came from.
cn: 我想这么说会比较恰当——我大部分时间都在研究“宇宙大爆炸”理论以及我们的宇宙从何而来。

en: Can you tell us a little about that?
cn: 您能就此问题跟我们谈谈吗？

en: Well, I'm very interested in why the universe exists at all.
cn: 唔，我对“宇宙究竟为何存在”很感兴趣。

en: That may sound odd, but the fact is at the moment of the Big Bang, both matter and anti-matter were created for a short time, and I mean just a fraction of a second.
cn: 这可能听着奇怪，但事实上，在大爆炸的那一刻，物质和反物质在短时间内同时生成，我是说仅在几分之一秒的功夫里。

en: The whole universe was a super-hot soup of radiation filled with these particles.
cn: 整个宇宙当时就是一盆超高温的放射物浓汤，里面充满了这些放射物粒子。

en: So what's baffled scientists for so long is "why is there a universe at all?"
cn: 所以长久以来困惑科学家的是“到底为什么会有宇宙？”

en: That's because matter and anti-matter are basically opposites of each other.
cn: 因为物质和反物质从根本上是相反的。

en: They are exactly alike, except that they have opposite electrical charges.
cn: 它们具有相反的电荷，除此之外完全一样。

en: So when they collide, they destroy each other?
cn: 所以当碰撞时，他们会摧毁彼此？

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: So during the first few moments of the Big Bang, the universe was extremely hot and very small.
cn: 所以大爆炸之初的刹那间，整个宇宙温度极高，空间极其狭小。

en: Matter and the now more exotic anti-matter would have had little space to avoid each other.
cn: 物质和如今更显奇异的反物质本没有什么空间能避开对方。

en: This means that they should have totally wiped each other out, leaving the universe completely barren.
cn: 也就是说，它们本应完全湮灭彼此，徒留一片荒凉世界。

en: But a recent study seems to point to the fact that when matter and anti-matter were first created, there were slightly more particles of matter, which allowed the universe we all live in to form?
cn: 但是一项新研究似乎指出一项事实：物质和反物质最初生成之时，物质粒子稍稍多了一些，这就让我们所生存的宇宙得以形成？

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: Because there was slightly more matter, the collisions quickly depleted all the anti-matter and left just enough matter to create stars, planets, and eventually us.
cn: 因为物质多了那么一点点，碰撞很快把所有的反物质清除一空，留下刚好足量的物质，生成了恒星、行星，并最终造就了我们。

en: In this week's edition of special series on Bizarre Medical Conditions, there is a report of the case of Michelle Myers.
cn: 本周“奇疾怪症”特别系列为您带来一篇关于米歇尔·迈尔斯的报道。

en: Myers is an American woman who woke up one day speaking with a British accent, even though she's lived in the United States all her life.
cn: 迈尔斯女士是一名美国人，某天醒来后讲话突然变成了英式口音，尽管她一直生活在美国。

en: In 2015, Myers went to bed with a terrible headache.
cn: 2015年某日，迈尔斯带着严重头痛上床睡觉。

en: She woke up sounding like someone from England.
cn: 她醒来后说话听起来更像是英国人。

en: Her British accent has remained for the past two years.
cn: 她的英式口音在过去两年里一直保持未变。

en: Previously, Myers had woken up speaking in Irish and Australian accents.
cn: 在此之前，迈尔斯曾一觉醒来变成爱尔兰腔和澳大利亚腔。

en: However, on both of those occasions, the accents lasted for only a week.
cn: 然而，那两次口音突变都只持续了一周。

en: Myers has been diagnosed with Foreign Accent Syndrome.
cn: 迈尔斯被诊断出患有外国口音综合征。

en: It's a disorder in which a person experiences a sudden change to their speech so that they sound like they are speaking in a foreign accent.
cn: 这是一种疾病，患有这种疾病的人说话方式会突然大变，听起来就像是外国口音。

en: The condition is most often caused by a stroke or traumatic brain injury.
cn: 这种病症通常由中风或颅脑损伤引起。

en: Although people with the syndrome have intelligible speech, their manner of speaking is altered in terms of timing and tongue placement, which may distort their pronunciation.
cn: 虽然这种综合征患者的讲话内容可以理解，但说话方式（包括说话的节奏以及舌头的位置）发生了改变，这会扭曲他们的发音。

en: The result is that they may sound foreign when speaking their native language.
cn: 结果便是，他们说母语时可能听起来像外国人。

en: It's not clear whether Myers has experienced a stroke or other brain damage, but she also has a separate medical condition, which can result in loose joints, easily bruised skin and other problems.
cn: 目前还不清楚迈尔斯是否曾经中风或有其他脑损伤，但她有另外的病症，这种病症可能导致关节松动，皮肤容易擦伤和其他问题。

en: Foreign Accent Syndrome is rare, with only about 60 cases reported within the past century.
cn: 外国口音综合征非常罕见，上个世纪只出现约60例报道。

en: However, a different American woman reportedly spoke with a Russian accent in 2010 after she fell down the stairs and hit her head.
cn: 然而，据报道，2010年另一名美国女性从楼梯上摔下撞到头部后，说话就带上了俄罗斯口音。

en: There is something about water that makes it a good metaphor for life.
cn: 水的某些特质使其成为了生命的恰当隐喻。

en: That may be one reason why so many people find relief in swimming when life's seas get rough.
cn: 这也许就是为什么当生活的海洋变得处境艰难时，会有那么多的人在游泳中得到宽慰的原因之一。

en: And it goes some way towards explaining why books about swimming, in which people tackle icy lakes, race in rivers and overcome oceans while reflecting on their lives, have recently become so popular.
cn: 它还在某种程度上解释了为什么关于游泳的书籍最近越来越受欢迎，这些书的主题为：人们挑战冰冷的湖泊、在河流中比赛、征服海洋，同时反思自己的人生。

en: These books reflect a trend, particularly strong in Britain, where swimming in pools is declining, but more and more folks are opting for open water.
cn: 这些书反映了一种趋势——去泳池游泳的人越来越少，而选择开放水域的人越来越多，这一趋势在英国尤为明显。

en: "Wild swimming" seems to be especially popular among women.
cn: “野泳”似乎特别受女性欢迎。

en: Jenny Landreth recently published a guide to the best swimming spots in London.
cn: 珍妮·兰德雷斯最近出版了一本伦敦最佳游泳场所指南。

en: Her new book, Swell, interweaves her own story with a history of female pioneers who accomplished remarkable feats and paved the way for future generations.
cn: 其新作《浪涌》将“她自己的故事”与“那些取得了非凡成就、并为后代铺平道路的女性先驱的历史”交织在一起。

en: Notions of modesty restricted women in the Victorian era, but they still swam.
cn: 在维多利亚时代，“端庄”的概念限制着当时的女性，但她们依然游泳。

en: A "bathing machine" was rolled down to the seashore so women would not be seen in swimwear.
cn: “游泳更衣车”会被推到海边，使女性不被看到身着泳衣的样子。

en: In 1892, The Gentleman's Book of Sport described a woman swimming in a heavy dress, boots, hat, gloves and carrying an umbrella.
cn: 1892年，《淑女运动指南》描述了一位女性游泳时的形象：身着厚重的裙子、靴子，戴着帽子和手套，手里还撑把雨伞。

en: Eventually, swimming became freer.
cn: 终于，游泳变得不那么受限了。

en: Mixed bathing was permitted on British beaches in 1901.
cn: 1901年，英国海滩开始允许（男女）混泳。

en: Women won the right to swim in public pools, learned to swim properly, created appropriate swimwear and, in time, even competed against men.
cn: 女性赢得了在公共泳池游泳的权利，学习了游泳技巧，设计出了得体的泳衣，最后甚至与男性竞赛。

en: The first woman to cross the English Channel was Gertrude Ederle in 1926.
cn: 1926年，格特鲁德·埃德勒成为首位横渡英吉利海峡的女性。

en: She beat the record by almost two hours and her father rewarded her with a red sports car.
cn: 她以近两小时的优势打破了记录，父亲奖励了她一辆红色跑车。

en: Today I'm going to talk about a very special kind of person.
cn: 今天我要谈论一类非常特殊的人。

en: Psychologists call them "masters of deception", those rare individuals with a natural ability to tell with complete confidence when someone is telling a lie.
cn: 心理学家称其为“骗术大师”，这些罕见的个体有一种天赋：若有人说谎，他们能相当自信地识破。

en: For decades, researchers and law enforcement agencies have tried to build a machine that will do the same thing.
cn: 几十年来，研究人员和执法机构一直致力于建造一台具有同样功能的机器。

en: Now a company in Massachusetts says that by using magnetic brain scans they can determine with 97% accuracy whether someone is telling the truth.
cn: 现在马萨诸塞州的一家公司表示，他们能通过脑部磁扫描测定一个人是否在说实话，准确率达97%。

en: They hope that the technology will be cleared for use in American courts by early next year.
cn: 他们希望该技术能够于明年初在美国法庭获准投入使用。

en: But is this really the ultimate tool for you, the lawyers of tomorrow?
cn: 但这真的是你的终极工具，也就是明日律师吗？

en: You'll not find many brain scientists celebrating this breakthrough.
cn: 你会发现，没有多少脑科学家赞美该项突破。

en: The company might be very optimistic, but the ability of their machine to detect deception has not provided credible proof.
cn: 该公司也许相当乐观，但是其机器的识骗能力未提供可信任证明。

en: That's because the technology has not been properly tested in real-world situations.
cn: 这是因为该技术尚未在现实情境中进行充分测试。

en: In life, there are different kinds of lies and diverse context in which they're told.
cn: 生活中有形形色色的谎言，而这些谎言又有着各式各样的生成语境。

en: These differences may elicit different brain responses.
cn: 这些区别可能引起大脑的不同反应。

en: Does their hypothesis behind the test apply in every case?
cn: 他们试验背后的假设能应用于每一个案件吗？

en: We don't know the answer, because studies done on how reliable this machine is have not yet been duplicated.
cn: 我们并不知道答案，因为关于这台机器可信度如何的研究尚未被复制。

en: Much more research is badly needed.
cn: 急需更多的研究。

en: Whether the technology is eventually deemed reliable enough for the courts will ultimately be decided by the judges.
cn: 此项技术最后是否会被视为对法庭足够可靠，最终将由法官决定。

en: Let's hope they're wise enough not to be fooled by a machine that claims to determine truthfulness at the flick of a switch.
cn: 但愿法官们足够明智，别被一个声称只须轻按开关便能确定（某人）诚实与否的机器愚弄。

en: They should also be sceptical of the growing tendency to try to reduce all human traits and actions to the level of brain activity.
cn: 他们也应该对“将人类所有性格特性和行为简化为大脑活动水平”的渐强趋势保持怀疑。

en: Often, they do not map that easily.
cn: 通常来说，性格行为和大脑活动水平并不能轻易匹配。

en: Moreover, understanding the brain is not the same as understanding the mind.
cn: 再者，理解大脑和理解思维是两码事。

en: Some researchers have suggested that thoughts cannot properly be seen as purely "internal".
cn: 一些研究人员已指出，不能将思想完全视为纯粹“内部的”。

en: Instead, thoughts make sense only in reference to the individual's external world.
cn: 相反，只有和个体的外部世界相联系，思想才有意义。

en: So while there may be insights to be gained from matching behavior to brain activity, those insights will not necessarily lead to justice in a court of law.
cn: 因此，尽管将行为和大脑活动进行匹配可能会获得一些洞见，但这些见解未必能实现法庭上的公正。

en: Problems surround the use of machines to spot deception, at least until it has been rigorously tested.
cn: 至少在严格测试前，使用机器识骗还存在诸多问题。

en: A high-tech test that can tell when a person is not telling the truth sounds too good to be true.
cn: 用高科技测试判断一个人没说实话听上去好得不真实。

en: And when something sounds too good to be true, it usually is.
cn: 如果某件事听起来好得不真实，它往往确实如此。

en: Last week I attended a research workshop on an island in the South Pacific.
cn: 上周我在南太平洋一个小岛上参加了一场研讨会。

en: Thirty people were present and all except me came from the island, called Makelua, in the nation of Vanuatu.
cn: 当时有三十人出席，除我之外的所有人都来自瓦努阿图国一个叫作马卡鲁瓦的岛屿。

en: They live in 16 different communities and speak 16 distinct languages.
cn: 他们生活在16个不同的社群，说16种不同的语言。

en: In many cases, you could stand at the edge of one village and see the outskirts of the next community.
cn: 在许多情况下，站在一个村庄的村头，你能看到另一个社群的郊野。

en: Yet the residents of each village speak a completely different language.
cn: 然而，每个村庄的居民都说着完全不同的语言。

en: According to recent work by my colleagues at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History, this island, just 100 kilometers long and 20 kilometers wide, is home to speakers of perhaps 40 different indigenous languages.
cn: 根据我在马克斯·普朗克人类历史科学研究所的同事们的最新研究，在这座仅100公里长、20公里宽的岛屿上，栖居着大概40种不同的土著语言的使用者。

en: Why so many?
cn: 为什么有这么多种语言呢？

en: We could ask the same question of the entire globe.
cn: 我们可以对全世界提出同样的问题。

en: People don't speak one universal language, or even a handful.
cn: 人们没有一种通用语言，甚至也不是只说几种语言。

en: Instead, today our species collectively speaks over 7,000 distinct languages.
cn: 相反，今天我们人类一共有7000多种不同的语言。

en: And these languages are not spread randomly across the planet.
cn: 而这些语言在地球上并不是随意分布的。

en: For example, far more languages are found in tropical regions than in the mild zones.
cn: 例如，在热带地区发现的语言种类远多于温带地区。

en: The tropical island of New Guinea is home to over 900 languages.
cn: 热带岛屿新几内亚有900多种语言。

en: Russia, 20 times larger, has 105 indigenous languages.
cn: 而面积是新几内亚20倍的俄罗斯则只有105种土著语言。

en: Even within the tropics, language diversity varies widely.
cn: 甚至在热带地区内部，语言多样性也有很大差异。

en: For example, the 250,000 people who live on Vanuatu's 80 islands speak 110 different languages, but in Bangladesh, a population 600 times greater speaks only 41 languages.
cn: 例如，生活在瓦努阿图80个岛屿上的25万人讲着110种不同的语言，但在人口是瓦努阿图600倍的孟加拉国，却只有41种语言。

en: How come humans speak so many languages?
cn: 为什么人类会有这么多种语言？

en: And why are they so unevenly spread across the planet?
cn: 为什么这些语言在地球上的分布如此不均衡？

en: As it turns out, we have few clear answers to these fundamental questions about how humanity communicates.
cn: 事实证明，我们对人类是如何交流的这类基本问题尚无明确的答案。

en: Most people can easily brainstorm possible answers to these intriguing questions.
cn: 大多数人能轻松地通过头脑风暴对这些有趣的问题做出可能的解释。

en: They hypothesize that language diversity must be about history, cultural differences, mountains or oceans dividing populations.
cn: 他们假定语言的多样性一定与历史、文化差异、山川或海洋分隔人口有关。

en: But when our diverse team of researchers from six different disciplines and eight different countries began to review what was known, we were shocked that only a dozen previous studies had been done, including one we ourselves completed on language diversity in the Pacific.
cn: 但是，当来自6个不同学科、8个不同国家的研究人员组成的多元化团队开始回顾已知内容时，我们震惊地发现，在此之前只有12项相关研究，其中还包括一项我们自己完成的关于太平洋地区语言多样性的研究。

en: These prior efforts all examined the degree to which different environmental, social, and geographic variables correlated with the number of languages found in a given location.
cn: 此前的这些研究都是在检验不同环境、社会和地理变量与某既定地区所发现的语言数量之间的相关程度。

en: The results varied a lot from one study to another, and no clear patterns emerged.
cn: 不同研究的结果各不相同，并未发现明确的模式。

en: The studies also ran up against many methodological challenges, the biggest of which centered on the old statistical saying—correlation does not equal causation.
cn: 这些研究还遭遇了许多方法论上的挑战，其中最大的挑战集中在那句古老的统计学箴言上——相关关系并不等于因果关系。

en: We often hear people say that America is a land of opportunity, a country built on hope to aspire the greatness on the American dream.
cn: 我们常听人说美国是一个机遇之地，一个建立在“追求伟大美国梦”希望之上的国家。

en: But is the dream as we once knew it dying?
cn: 但我们曾经的梦想是否正在破灭？

en: Today's demographics show that the middle-class is disappearing and now the richest 1% of the population has mastered more wealth than the bottom 90%.
cn: 当今的人口统计资料显示，中产阶级正在消失，现在1%最富裕人口的财富量超过90%底层人口的总和。

en: Once upon a time, Americans thought that if they worked hard enough, even in the phase of adversity, they would be rewarded with success.
cn: 过去，美国人认为只要他们足够努力，即便是在困境中也能收获成功。

en: These days, though, the divide between rich and poor is greater than it has ever been.
cn: 然而，现如今贫富差距比以往任何时候都大。

en: The question is, what is it going to take to change things?
cn: 问题是，怎么做才能改变现状？

en: Maybe one day soon real change will actually be made in our nation and the gap will be eradicated.
cn: 也许在不久后的某一天，我们的国家将真正发生改变，贫富差距将会被消除。

en: But what happens in the meantime?
cn: 但在此期间呢？

en: Is there something that we can do to help close the gap?
cn: 我们能否做些什么来帮助缩小差距？

en: Is there something that we can do to prove that a little compassion goes a long way?
cn: 我们能否做些什么来证实些许同情心能产生深远的影响呢？

en: If we want to fix the problem of the income gap, first, we have to understand it.
cn: 如果我们想要解决收入差距问题，首先得理解这些问题。

en: It is a grim reality that you can have one person who only makes around $13,000 a year, or across town, another is making millions.
cn: 一个残酷的现实是，有人一年只能挣大约1.3万美金，而在城镇的另一边，有人正在挣着几百万。

en: For me, it is kind of astonishing.
cn: 对我来说，这有些令人吃惊。

en: And if you ask low-income people what's the one thing that will change their life, they'll say a "full-time job".
cn: 如果你问低收入群体，什么会改变他们的生活，他们会说一份“全职工作”。

en: That's all they aspire to.
cn: 这就是他们所渴望的全部。

en: So why is it so difficult for so many people to find employment?
cn: 那么为什么这么多人都难以找到工作呢？

en: It partly comes down to profit-driven business models that are built around low-wage work and part-time jobs that don't provide benefits.
cn: 这部分归因于利润驱动的商业模式，它基于低薪工作和不提供福利的兼职工作而建立。

en: Businesses, in order to boost profits, hire employees as part-time workers only.
cn: 企业为了增加利润只雇用兼职员工。

en: This means they are paid the lowest legal wage and receive no health care or other benefits provided to full-time employees.
cn: 这意味着他们（兼职员工）只能领到法定最低工资，也没有全职员工所享有的医疗保健或其他福利。

en: Simultaneously, technological advancement and a global economy has reduced the demand for well-paying blue-collar jobs here in the United States.
cn: 与此同时，技术进步和全球化经济减少了美国对高薪蓝领工作的需求。

en: The cumulative effect of these two factors is that many Americans are forced to take two or more part-time jobs, just to make ends meet.
cn: 这两个因素的累加效应就是，许多美国人被迫从事两份或两份以上兼职工作，而这仅仅能维持收支平衡。

en: What has become obvious to me when it comes to the income gap is that there needs to be an opportunity for the people at the bottom to push them back up and push them into the middle-class to give them hope in their lives.
cn: 在收入差距问题上，我认为显而易见的一点是，底层群体需要有机会将自己重新推回上一阶层、挤入中产阶层，以此获得生活的希望。

en: Hi, my name's Cathy.
cn: 嗨，我是凯茜。

en: Nice to meet you!
cn: 很高兴见到你！

en: Nice to meet you too, Cathy.
cn: 我也很高兴见到你，凯茜。

en: My name's John.
cn: 我叫约翰。

en: I'm a university friend of the bride.
cn: 我是新娘的大学朋友。

en: What about you?
cn: 你呢？

en: Who do you know at this party?
cn: 你在这个派对上认识谁？

en: I am a colleague of Brenda.
cn: 我是布伦达的同事。

en: I was a little surprised to be invited, to be honest.
cn: 说实话，收到邀请我有点惊讶。

en: We've only been working together the last six months, but we quickly became good friends.
cn: 我们半年前才开始一起工作，但很快成为了好朋友。

en: We just wrapped up a project with a difficult client last week.
cn: 我们上周刚结束了一个难缠客户的项目。

en: I bet Brenda is glad it's done with, and she can focus on wedding preparations.
cn: 我敢打赌布伦达一定很高兴项目完成了，这样她就可以专心准备婚礼了。

en: Oh, yes, so you're Cathy from the office.
cn: 噢，没错，所以你就是办公室里的凯茜。

en: Actually I've heard a lot about you, and that project.
cn: 其实，我听说了很多关于你和那个项目的事情。

en: The client sounded like a real nightmare.
cn: 那个客户听上去可真是个噩梦。

en: Oh, he was.
cn: 噢，他就是。

en: I mean we deal with all kinds of people on a regular basis.
cn: 我是说，我们经常跟各种人打交道。

en: It's part of the job, but he was especially particular, enough about that.
cn: 这是工作的一部分，但他尤其挑剔，不说他了。

en: What line of work are you in?
cn: 你从事哪个行业呢？

en: Well, right out of college, I worked in advertising for a while.
cn: 大学刚毕业时，我在广告行业工作过一段时间。

en: Recently though, I turn my photography hobby into a small business.
cn: 但最近，我把自己的摄影爱好变成了一桩小生意。

en: I'll actually be taking photos during the big event as a wedding gift.
cn: 实际上，我会在这个重大活动（婚礼）中拍摄照片作为给新人的结婚礼物。

en: That sounds wonderful, and very thoughtful of you.
cn: 听起来很棒，你想得真周到。

en: I bake just as a hobby but Brenda has asked me to do the cake for the wedding.
cn: 我只是把烘焙作为爱好，但布伦达让我制作婚礼用的蛋糕。

en: I was a bit nervous saying yes, because I'm far from a professional.
cn: 答应她时我有点紧张，因为我远不够专业。

en: Did you bake the cookies here at the party tonight?
cn: 今晚派对上的饼干都是你烤的？

en: Yes, I got the idea from a magazine.
cn: 是的，我从一本杂志上得到的灵感。

en: They're delicious.
cn: 饼干很好吃。

en: You've got nothing to worry about.
cn: 你没什么好担心的。

en: You're a natural.
cn: 你有烘焙天赋。

en: You really think so?
cn: 你真的这么觉得？

en: If you hadn't told me that, I would have guessed they were baked by the restaurant.
cn: 如果你不告诉我，我还以为饼干是餐馆烤的。

en: You know, with your event planning experience, you could very well open your own shop.
cn: 要知道，你还有活动策划的经验，所以你完全可以自己开店。

en: One step at a time.
cn: 一步一步来吧。

en: First I'll see how baking the wedding cake goes.
cn: 我先看看婚礼蛋糕烤得怎么样。

en: If it's not a disaster, maybe I'll give it some more thought.
cn: 如果不是太糟糕的话，或许我会认真考虑开店。

en: You are heading for a completely different world now that you are about to graduate from high school.
cn: 既然你就要高中毕业了，你将迈向一个完全不同的世界。

en: I know it's the end of high school, but many of my classmates are going on to the same university and we are still required to study hard, so what's the difference?
cn: 我知道高中生活结束了，不过我的好多同学都会到同一所大学继续念书，而且我们仍然需要努力学习，那么大学和高中比有什么不同呢？

en: Many aspects are different here at university.
cn: 在大学有很多方面与高中不同。

en: The most important one is that you have to take more individual responsibility for your actions.
cn: 最重要的区别在于，你必须为自己的行为独立承担更多责任。

en: It's up to your own self-discipline how much effort you put into study.
cn: 你在学习上付出多少努力取决于你的自律能力。

en: Living in college dormitories, there are no parents to tell you to study harder or stop wasting time.
cn: 住在大学宿舍，就不会有父母告诫你要更加努力学习，别再浪费时间。

en: Lecturers have hundreds of students and they are not going to follow you up or question you if you miss their lectures.
cn: 老师有好几百个学生，他们才不会跟进你的情况，要是你没去上课，他们也不会质问你什么。

en: Nobody cares, you mean?
cn: 你是说，没有人在意我？

en: It's not that nobody is concerned about you.
cn: 并不是没有人关心你。

en: It's just that suddenly at university you are expected to behave like an adult, that means concentrating on the direction of your life in general and your own academic performance specifically.
cn: 只是在大学，突然之间你就被期待像成年人那样处事，这意味着你既要专注于自己人生的总体方向，还要特别专注于自己的学业表现。

en: For example?
cn: 比如说呢？

en: Well, like you need to manage your daily, weekly and monthly schedules so that you will study regularly.
cn: 唔，例如你要做好每日、每周、每月的安排，以便有规律地学习。

en: Be sure to attend all classes and leave enough time to finish assignments and prepare well for examinations.
cn: 保证每堂课都出勤，并预留充足的时间完成作业、好好准备考试。

en: Okay, and what else is different?
cn: 好吧，还有哪些不同呢？

en: Well, in college there are lots of distractions and you need to control yourself.
cn: 唔，在大学有很多事会让你分心，你需要自我控制。

en: You will make interesting friends, but you need only keep the friends who respect your student commitments.
cn: 你会交到有趣的朋友，但你只需与顾及你学生身份的那些朋友交往下去。

en: Also, there are a lot of wonderful clubs, but you shouldn't allocate too much time to club activities, unless they are directly related to your study.
cn: 此外，还有许多很棒的社团，但你不应将过多时间拨给社团活动，除非它们与你的学业直接相关。

en: It's also your choice if you want to go out at night, but you will be foolish to let that affect your class performance during the day.
cn: 如果想晚上出去玩也随你，但要是影响到你白天的课堂表现就太傻了。

en: Well, I'm determined to do well at university and I guess I am going to have to grow up fast.
cn: 唔，我决心要在大学好好表现，我想我得快快长大成人了。

en: Most successful people are unorthodox persons whose minds wander outside traditional ways of thinking.
cn: 大多数成功人士都是在思维上偏离传统思维方式的非正统人士。

en: Instead of trying to refine old formulas, they invent new ones.
cn: 他们不是设法改进旧惯例，而是努力建立新惯例。

en: When Jean-Claude Killy made the French national ski team in the early 1960s, he was prepared to work harder than anyone else to be the best.
cn: 让-克劳德·基利在20世纪60年代初期加入法国国家滑雪队时，他愿意比其他人付出更多努力以成为最优秀的运动员。

en: At the crack of dawn he would run up the slopes with his skis on, an unbelievably backbreaking activity.
cn: 每天天刚亮，他就穿着滑雪板登坡，这是一项异常费力的活动。

en: In the evening he would do weight lifting and running.
cn: 每天晚上他会做举重和跑步运动。

en: But the other team members were working as hard and long as he was.
cn: 但其他队员和他一样也在进行同等强度和时长的训练。

en: He realized instinctively that simply training harder would never be enough.
cn: 他凭直觉意识到单靠更努力的训练绝对不够。

en: Killy then began challenging the basic theories of racing technique.
cn: 基利随后开始质疑竞赛技术的基础理论。

en: Each week he would try something different to see if he could find a better, faster way down the mountain.
cn: 每周他都会尝试不同的东西，看是否能找到更好、更快的下坡方式。

en: His experiments resulted in a new style that was almost exactly opposite the accepted technique of the time.
cn: 他通过多次试验找到了一种几乎与当时的常规技术完全相反的新方式。

en: It involved skiing with his legs apart for better balance and sitting back on the skis when he came to a turn.
cn: 它包括滑雪时双腿分开以获得更好的平衡，转弯时向后坐于滑雪板上。

en: He also used ski poles in an unorthodox way—to propel himself as he skied.
cn: 他还以非正统的方式使用滑雪杆——滑雪时用其给自己提供推力。

en: The explosive new style helped cut Killy's racing time dramatically.
cn: 这一爆炸性的新方式大幅缩短了基利的比赛时间。

en: In 1966 and 1967 he captured virtually every major skiing trophy.
cn: 在1966年和1967年，他几乎斩获了所有滑雪大奖。

en: The next year he won three gold medals in the Winter Olympics, a record in ski racing that has never been topped.
cn: 第二年，他在冬奥会上获得了三枚金牌，这是滑雪赛事中从未被打破过的最高纪录。

en: Killy learned an important secret shared by many creative people: innovations don't require genius, just a willingness to question the way things have always been done.
cn: 基利掌握了许多有创造力的人士都知道的一个重要奥秘：创新不需要天赋，只需要一种质疑常规行事方式的意愿。

en: Scientific experiments have demonstrated incredible ways to kill a guinea pig, a small furry animal.
cn: 科学实验展示了杀害豚鼠（一种毛茸茸的小动物）的惊人方式。

en: Emotional upsets generate powerful and deadly toxic substances.
cn: 情绪失落会产生强大而又致命的毒素。

en: Blood samples taken from persons experiencing intense fear or anger when injected into guinea pigs have killed them in less than two minutes.
cn: 将从正经历强烈恐惧或愤怒情绪的人身上提取的血样注射到豚鼠体内，豚鼠会在两分钟之内毙命。

en: Imagine what these poisonous substances can do to your own body.
cn: 想象一下这些有毒物质会对你自己的身体造成什么影响。

en: Every thought that you have affects your body chemistry within a split second.
cn: 你的每个想法都会在瞬息之间影响到你身体的化学反应。

en: Remember how you feel when you're speeding down the highway and a big truck suddenly brakes twenty meters in front of you.
cn: 回想你在高速公路上疾驰、前方20米处突然有辆大卡车急刹车时的感觉。

en: A shockwave shoots through your whole system.
cn: 一股骇浪涌遍全身。

en: Your mind produces instant reactions in your body.
cn: 大脑令身体做出即时反应。

en: The toxic substances that fear, anger, frustration, and stress produce not only kill guinea pigs but kill us off in a similar manner.
cn: 恐惧、愤怒、沮丧和压力产生的有毒物质不仅会杀死豚鼠，也会以类似的方式杀死我们。

en: It is impossible to be fearful, anxious, irritated, and healthy at the same time.
cn: 想在恐惧、焦虑、愤怒的同时拥有健康那是不可能的。

en: It is not just difficult, it is impossible.
cn: 不是难，而是根本不可能。

en: Simply put, your body's health is a reflection of your mental health.
cn: 简单地说，身体健康是心理健康的反映。

en: Sickness will often then be a result of unresolved inner conflicts which in time show up in the body.
cn: 病痛往往是未解决的内心斗争适时暴露于体外的结果。

en: It is also fascinating how our subconscious minds shapes our health.
cn: 潜意识如何影响健康也让人着迷。

en: Do you recall falling sick on a day when you didn't want to go to school?
cn: 是否还记得有天不想上学身体就生病？

en: Headaches brought on by fear?
cn: 是否还记得因恐惧而头疼？

en: The mind-body connection is such that if, for example, we want to avoid something, very often our subconscious mind will arrange it.
cn: 身心关联如此紧密，以至于，打个比方，我们想规避某事，潜意识通常就会筹划。

en: Once we recognize that these things happen to us, we are halfway to doing something about them.
cn: 一旦意识到这些事情发生在我们身上，我们其实已经在着手处理这些事情了。

en: Teachers and students alike have experienced the curious paradox that beginners, as a rule, tend to think too little about what they are doing because they think too much about what they are doing.
cn: 老师和学生都经历过一种奇特的矛盾情形：通常来说，初学者对于所做之事（的本质）往往想得太少，因为他们对于这件事（的细节）想得太多。

en: Take, for example, people who are learning to play basketball or the piano.
cn: 以篮球或钢琴初学者为例。

en: They have to give so much thought and attention to the low-level mechanics of handling the ball or fingering the keys or reading the music, that they are unable to give any thought to the thing that matters—the game, or the music, respectively.
cn: 他们不得不花许多心思和注意力在控球、指法、识谱等初级技术性细节上，以至于各自不能对篮球、音乐这类至关重要的事情做出任何思考。

en: With experts, it's just the other way around.
cn: 对行家来说则正好相反。

en: They're open to the tactical possibilities and the musical challenges precisely because they're freed, through skill, from the need to pay attention to the low-level details of how to play.
cn: 他们之所以乐于接受各种战术手段以及音乐挑战，恰恰是因为他们能够凭借自身技艺使自己无需关注如何打球/弹奏的初级细节。

en: Indeed, when the expert pays attention to the mechanics, this is liable to disrupt performance.
cn: 确实，如果行家把注意力放在技术性细节上，这很可能会影响发挥。

en: This has led some to say that the expert operates in a zone “beyond thought”, in a state of flow.
cn: 这让一些人认为，行家运动/弹奏时不假思索，处于一种心流状态。

en: But this is misleading.
cn: 但这种说法会令人误解。

en: Expert performance is not beyond thought.
cn: 行家的表现并非没有思考。

en: Smart basketball players or skilled musicians need to pay close attention to the demands of high performance, to the challenges to be overcome.
cn: 聪明的篮球运动员或是娴熟的音乐家需要密切关注的是对上佳表现的要求以及需要克服的挑战。

en: What they don't need to do—what would be a distraction—is to have to think about where their fingers are, or how to control the ball while running.
cn: 他们不需要做的——会让他们分心的——是思考手指放在何处，或在跑动时如何控球。

en: It's not mechanics, but the play itself, that absorbs the expert's intelligence.
cn: 行家将才智倾注于运动/弹奏本身，而不是各种技术性细节。

en: A nice video published online last month sheds light on expertise and the conscious mind.
cn: 上个月网上发布的一段不错的视频阐明了专业技能与意识头脑（之间的关系）。

en: The video reports a new study using an eye-tracking device.
cn: 视频公布了一项使用眼动仪的新研究。
