en: Early travelers on the Missouri river reported that shores and bars were often lined with the decaying bodies of buffalo that had died during spring floods.
cn: 密苏里河的早期旅行者反映，岸滩和沙洲上经常排列着在春季洪水中死去的水牛腐尸。

en: I would like particularly to talk about the need to develop a new style of aging in our own society.
cn: 我特别想谈一谈在我们社会发展一种新的老去方式必要性。

en: Young people in this country have been accused of not caring for their parents the way they would have in the old country.
cn: 在我们国家（美国），年轻人被指责不会像过去那样关心照料父母。

en: And this is true.
cn: 这是事实。

en: But it is also true that old people have been influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy.
cn: 但另一个事实是，老年人一直以来都深受独立自主这一理想的影响。

en: So we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation, in time without friends, but we are independent.
cn: 为此，我们独自生活，或濒于饿死，或无友可依，但是我们独立。

en: This standard American style has been forced on every ethnic group, although there are many groups for whom the ideal is not practical.
cn: 这一标准的美国变老方式被强加给各个族群，哪怕这个理想对于许多族群而言不切实际。

en: It is a poor ideal and pursuing it does a great deal of harm.
cn: 这是一个糟糕的理想，追求它会造成极大伤害。

en: This ideal of independence also contains a tremendous amount of unselfishness.
cn: 这个独立自主的理想还要求（人们）具备极度的无私奉献精神。

en: In talking to today's young mothers, I have asked them what kind of grandmothers they think they are going to be.
cn: 在与当今年轻母亲的交谈中，我问她们觉着自己将会成为怎样的祖母。

en: I hear devoted, loving mothers say that when they are through raising their children, they have no intention of becoming grandmothers.
cn: 我听尽心尽责又慈爱的母亲说，她们抚育孩子长大成人后无意要做祖母。

en: They are astonished to hear that in most of the world throughout most of its history, families have been three- or four- generation families, living under the same roof.
cn: 当听说世界上大多数国家在大部分历史时期都是三代或四代同堂的家庭模式时，她们感到十分震惊。

en: We have over- emphasized the small family unit—father, mother, small children.
cn: 我们过度强调要以小家庭为单位——父亲、母亲和孩子。

en: We think it is wonderful if grandma and grandpa, if they're still alive, can live alone.
cn: 我们认为，祖母和祖父（倘若还在世）能独自生活是一件极好的事。

en: We have reached the point where we think the only thing we can do for our children is to stay out of their way and the only thing we can do for our daughter- in- law is to see as little of her as possible.
cn: 我们已经到了这样一种地步：我们认为唯一可为孩子做的事就是不涉入他们的生活，唯一可为儿媳做的事就是尽可能少与她会面。

en: Old people's nursing homes, even the best run, are filled with older people who believe the only thing they can do for their children is to look cheerful when they come to visit.
cn: 养老院，甚至是那些经营至善的养老院，挤满了一群认为唯一可为孩子做的事就是在他们前来探望时笑脸相迎的老年人。

en: So in the end, older people have to devote all their energies to 'not being a burden'.
cn: 所以到最后，老年人不得不竭尽全力让自己'别成为累赘'。

en: We are beginning to see what a tremendous price we've paid for our emphasis on independence and autonomy.
cn: 我们开始认识到，对独立自主的重视让我们付出了极为惨重的代价。

en: We've isolated old people and we've cut off the children from their grandparents.
cn: 我们使老年人陷于孤立，切断了孩子与祖父母的联系。

en: One of the reasons we have as bad a generation gap today as we do is that grandparents have stepped out.
cn: 现今我们之所以会有如此严重的代沟，原因之一就在于祖父母的缺位。

en: Young people are being deprived of the thing they need most—perspective, to know why their parents behave so peculiarly and why their grandparents say the things they do.
cn: 年轻人被剥夺了他们最需要的东西——客观判断能力，他们无法了解父母行事为何这般独特，祖父母为何说出那样的话。

en: You are a professor of physics at the University of Oxford.
cn: 您是牛津大学的物理学教授。

en: You're a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research.
cn: 您担任着欧洲核子研究中心的高级顾问。

en: You also seem to tour the globe tirelessly, giving talks.
cn: 您似乎还在世界各地不知疲倦地做演讲。

en: And in addition, you have your own weekly TV show on science.
cn: 此外，您每周还有自己的科普电视节目。

en: Where do you get the energy?
cn: 您怎么会有这么多精力呢？

en: Oh, well.
cn: 哦，唔。

en: I just love what I do.
cn: 我真的热爱我所做的一切。

en: I'm extremely fortunate to have this life, doing what I love doing.
cn: 能过这样的生活，做我热爱做的事，我非常幸运。

en: Professor, what exactly is your goal?
cn: 教授，您的目标到底是什么？

en: Why do you do all of these?
cn: 您为什么要做这些事情？

en: Well, as you said, I do have different things going on.
cn: 嗯，正如你所说，我确实在做很多不同的事情。

en: But these, I think, can be divided into two groups: the education of science and the further understanding of science.
cn: 但我认为，这些事情可以分为两类：科学教育和对科学的进一步了解。

en: Don't these two things get in the way of each other?
cn: 这两件事难道不会互相妨碍吗？

en: What I mean is, doesn't giving lectures take time away from the lab?
cn: 我的意思是，讲课不会占用做实验的时间吗？

en: Not really, no.
cn: 不会的，不会。

en: I love teaching, and I don't mind spending more time doing that now than in the past.
cn: 我喜欢教学，我不介意现在比过去花更多的时间去做这件事。

en: Also, what I will say is that teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself.
cn: 另外，我想说的是，教授一门学科有助于我更好地理解这门学科。

en: I find that it furthers my own knowledge when I have to explain something clearly, when I have to aid others in understanding it, and when I have to answer questions about it.
cn: 我发现，当我不得不解释清楚某事物、帮助别人理解它、回答关于它的问题时，教学能帮我进一步加深对它的理解。

en: Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating for anyone, no matter how much expertise they may already have in the field they are instructing.
cn: 高阶段的教学对任何人来讲都是非常具有启发性的，不论他们在自己所教授的领域已有多少专业知识。

en: Are there any scientific breakthroughs that you see on the near horizon, a significant discovery or invention we can expect soon?
cn: 您认为近期会有什么科学突破吗？或者说我们很快就能盼来的重大发现或发明？

en: The world is always conducting science, and there are constantly new things being discovered.
cn: 全世界一直都在开展科学研究，新事物不断地被发现。

en: In fact, right now we have too much data sitting in computers.
cn: 事实上，我们当前有太多的数据存放在电脑里。

en: For example, we have thousands of photos of planet Mars taken by telescopes that nobody has ever seen.
cn: 例如，我们有成千上万张用望远镜拍摄的火星照片，却没人看过它们。

en: We have them, yet nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them.
cn: 我们有这些照片，却没人有时间去看一眼，更不用说去分析它们了。

en: Do you think dreams have special meanings?
cn: 你觉得梦有特殊含义吗？

en: No, I don't think they do.
cn: 不，我不觉得它们有什么特殊含义。

en: I don't either.
cn: 我也不觉得。

en: But some people do.
cn: 但有些人确实这么认为。

en: I would say people who believe that dreams have special meanings are superstitious, especially nowadays.
cn: 我不得不说那些相信梦有特殊含义的人太迷信了，尤其是现在还这么认为的。

en: In the past, during the times of ancient Egypt, Greece or China, people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future.
cn: 过去，在古埃及、古希腊和古中国时代，人们往往相信梦境可以预见未来。

en: But today, with all the scientific knowledge that we have, I think it's much harder to believe in these sorts of things.
cn: 但今天，我们已掌握了如此多的科学知识，我觉得很难再相信这些说法。

en: My grandmother is superstitious, and she thinks dreams can predict the future.
cn: 我祖母就很迷信，而且她认为梦可以预测未来。

en: Once she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed.
cn: 有一次她梦到第二天自己要乘坐的飞机失事了。

en: Can you guess what she did?
cn: 你能猜到她做了什么吗？

en: She didn't take that flight.
cn: 她没去搭乘那趟航班。

en: She didn't even bother to go to the airport the following day.
cn: 她甚至第二天连机场都不愿去。

en: Instead, she took the same flight but a week later.
cn: 她转而乘坐了一周之后的同一航班。

en: And everything was fine, of course.
cn: 当然，什么事都没发生。

en: No plane ever crashed.
cn: 没有飞机坠毁。

en: How funny!
cn: 真滑稽！

en: Did you know that flying is actually safer than any other mode of transport?
cn: 你知道乘坐飞机实际上要比其他任何交通方式都安全吗？

en: It's been statistically proven.
cn: 这是经过数据证实的。

en: People can be so irrational sometimes.
cn: 人们有时候竟然可以荒唐至此。

en: Yes, absolutely.
cn: 是啊，就是这样。

en: But even if we think they are ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking.
cn: 但即便我们认为他们很离谱，情感也确实会和理性思维一样影响强大。

en: Exactly.
cn: 正是如此。

en: People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings.
cn: 人们会因为不理性的感受而做出各种疯狂的事情。

en: But in fact, some psychologists believe that our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day.
cn: 但其实，一些心理学家认为我们的梦来自于当天的情感和记忆。

en: I think it was Sigmund Freud who said that children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes, things they wished would happen.
cn: 我想是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德曾说过，儿童的梦境通常是他们的愿望、他们所希望发生之事的直接展现。

en: But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments.
cn: 但对于成年人，梦境则是对他们更丰富情感的更复杂的反映。

en: Isn't it interesting how psychologists try to understand using the scientific method something as bizarre as dreams?
cn: 心理学家如何试图用科学的方法来理解梦境这么古怪的东西，这难道不是很有趣吗？

en: Psychology is like the rational study of irrational feelings.
cn: 心理学就像是对非理性情感进行理性的研究。

en: While some scientists explore the surface of Antarctica, others are learning more about a giant body of water four kilometers beneath the ice pack.
cn: 当一些科学家在探索南极洲表面时，另一些科学家正在研究南极洲冰层下4千米处的巨大水体。

en: Scientists first discovered Lake Vostok in the 1970s by using radio waves that penetrate the ice.
cn: 20世纪70年代，科学家们使用可透过冰层的无线电波首次发现了沃斯托克湖。

en: Since then, they have used sound waves and even satellites to map this massive body of water.
cn: 自那以后，他们曾使用声波甚至卫星来测绘这片巨大的水域。

en: How does the water in Lake Vostok remain liquid beneath an ice sheet?
cn: 沃斯托克湖中的水是如何在冰盖下保持液态的？

en: "The thick glacier above acts like an insulating blanket and keeps the water from freezing," says Martin Siegert, a glaciologist from the University of Wales.
cn: 威尔士大学的冰川学家马丁·西格特说：'上面这层厚厚的冰盖就像一条隔热毯一样防止水结冰。'

en: In addition, geothermal heat from deep within the earth may warm the hidden lake.
cn: 此外，来自地下深处的地热可能暖化了这个隐蔽的湖。

en: The scientists suspect that micro- organisms may be living in Lake Vostok, closed off from the outside world for more than 2 million years.
cn: 科学家们猜测可能有微生物生活在沃斯托克湖，从而与外界隔绝了200多万年。

en: Anything found there will be totally alien to what's on the surface of the earth, says Siegert.
cn: 西格特说，在沃斯托克湖发现的一切都将与地表上的情形截然不同。

en: Scientists are trying to find a way to drill into the ice and draw water samples without causing contamination.
cn: 科学家们正试图找到一种方法，可以在不造成污染的情况下钻入冰层提取水样。

en: Again, robots might be the solution.
cn: 又一次，机器人成了可能的解决方案。

en: If all goes as planned, a drill- shaped robot will melt through the surface ice.
cn: 倘若一切按计划进行，一个钻孔机形状的机器人会融穿表面的冰。

en: When it reaches the lake, it will release another robot that can swim in the lake, take pictures, and look for signs of life.
cn: 当它进入湖中后会卸下另一个机器人，这个机器人会徜徉在湖中拍照并寻找生命的迹象。

en: The scientists hope their discoveries will shed light on life in outer space, which might exist in similar dark and airless conditions.
cn: 科学家们希望他们的发现将有助于人们进一步了解外太空的生命，它们可能存在于类似的黑暗、无空气环境下。

en: Recently, close- up pictures of Jupiter's moon, Europa, show signs of water beneath its icy surface.
cn: 最近，木卫欧罗巴的特写图像显示，其冰冻表面下有水的迹象。

en: Once tested in Antarctica, robots could be sent to Europa to search for life there too.
cn: 一旦在南极洲完成了测试，机器人也可以被送往欧罗巴去寻找生命。

en: The idea to study the American Indian tribe Tarahumaras came to James Copeland in 1984 when he discovered that very little research had been done on their language.
cn: 1984年，詹姆斯·科普兰发现有关美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉语言的研究少之又少，便萌生了研究该部落的想法。

en: He contacted a tribe member through a social worker who worked with the tribesmen in Mexico.
cn: 他通过一名在墨西哥做部落成员工作的社工联系到了一位部落成员。

en: At first, the tribe member, named Gonzalez, was very reluctant to cooperate.
cn: 起初，这位名叫冈萨雷斯的部落成员非常不愿意配合。

en: He told Copeland that no amount of money could buy his language.
cn: 他告诉科普兰，再多的钱也买不到他的语言。

en: But after Copeland explained to him what he intended to do with his research and how it would benefit the Tarahumaras, Gonzalez agreed to help.
cn: 不过，在科普兰向他解释了'自己打算用这项研究做些什么'以及'这项研究将如何使塔拉乌马拉受益'之后，冈萨雷斯就答应帮忙了。

en: He took Copeland to his village and served as an intermediary.
cn: 他把科普兰带到村庄，充当起了中间人。

en: Copeland says, "Thanks to him, the Tarahumaras understood what our mission was and started trusting us."
cn: 科普兰说：'多亏了他，塔拉乌马拉人才明白了我们的使命是什么，而后开始信任我们。'

en: Entering the world of the Tarahumaras has been a laborious project for Copeland.
cn: 于科普兰而言，进入塔拉乌马拉人的世界是个艰辛的任务。

en: To reach their homeland he must drive two and a half days from Huston, Texas.
cn: 他必须从德克萨斯州休斯顿出发，开两天半的车才能抵达他们的家乡。

en: He loads up his vehicle with goods that the tribesmen can't easily get, and gives the goods to them as a gesture of friendship.
cn: 他把部落成员无法轻易获得的东西装上车，再将这些东西送给他们以示友谊。

en: The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth, take the food and share it among themselves.
cn: 塔拉乌马拉人不赞成财富积累，他们会接受那些食物并彼此分享。

en: For Copeland, the experience has not only been academically satisfying, but also has enriched his life in several ways.
cn: 对于科普兰来说，这一经历不仅在学术上令人满意，也在多个方面丰富了他的生活。

en: "I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard, traditional life, which offers me another notion about the meaning of progress in the western tradition," he says.
cn: 他说：'我看到人们拒绝科技，过着极为艰苦的传统生活，这让我对西方传统中'发展'的内涵有了不同的理解。'

en: "I experience the simplicity of living in nature that I would otherwise only be able to read about.
cn: '我体验了那种（不然只能在书本上读到的）大自然里简单淳朴的生活。'

en: I see a lot of beauty in their sense of sharing and concern for each other."
cn: 我从他们的分享意识以及相互关心中发现了许多的美。'

en: What is a radical?
cn: 什么是'激进分子'？

en: It seems today that people are terrified of the term, particularly of having the label attached to them.
cn: 如今，人们似乎很害怕这个词，特别是害怕被贴上这个标签。

en: Accusing individuals or groups of being radical often serves to silence them into submission, thereby maintaining the existing state of affairs, and, more important, preserving the power of a select minority who are mostly wealthy white males in western society.
cn: 指责个人或团体激进往往会压制他们的声音，进而使他们屈服，从而维持事态现状，更重要的是，这样会维护少部分精英人士的权力，而这些人在西方社会中大多是富有的白人男性。

en: Feminism is a perfect example of this phenomenon.
cn: 女权主义就是这种现象的一个典型例子。

en: The women's movement has been plagued by stereotypes, misrepresentations by the media, and accusations of man- hating and radicalism, when the basic foundation of feminism is simply that women deserve equal rights in all facets of life.
cn: 女性运动一直困扰于人们的刻板印象、媒体的歪曲以及外界对其厌男和激进主义的指责，尽管女权主义的基本诉求仅仅是女性在生活的各个方面享有平等的权利。

en: When faced with the threat of being labelled radical, women back down from their worthy calls and consequently participate in their own oppression.
cn: 当面临被贴上激进分子标签的威胁时，女性就会放弃呼吁自己应有的权益，从而加入到对自己的压迫中去。

en: It has gotten to the point that many women are afraid to call themselves feminists because of the stigma attached to the word.
cn: 现在已经到了许多女性不敢自称女权主义者的地步，因为这个词自带污名。

en: If people refuse to be controlled and intimidated by stigmas, the stigmas lose all their power.
cn: 如果人们拒绝被污名控制和恐吓，污名就会失去其所有的影响力。

en: Without fear on which they feed, such stigmas can only die.
cn: 没有了赖以生存的恐惧，这些污名就只能消亡。

en: To me, a radical is simply someone who rebels against the norm or advocates a change in the existing state of affairs.
cn: 对我来说，激进分子就是那些反抗常态或主张改变事态现状的人。

en: On close inspection, it becomes clear that the norm is constantly evolving and therefore is not a constant entity.
cn: 仔细观察就会发现，常态很明显是在不断演变的，因此，它不是一个恒定的存在。

en: So why then is deviation from the present situation such a threat when the state of affairs itself is unstable and subject to relentless transformation?
cn: 那么，为什么在事态本身状况就不稳定、会不断变化的情况下，背离现状是一种威胁呢？

en: It all goes back to maintaining the power of those who have it and preventing the right of those who don't.
cn: 这一切都源于要维护那些拥有权力的人的权力，阻止那些没有权力的人拥有权利。

en: In fact, when we look at the word 'radical' in a historical context, nearly every figure we now hold up as a hero was considered a radical in his or her time.
cn: 事实上，当我们在历史背景下看'激进分子'这个词时，几乎每一个我们现在视为英雄的人物在他或她的时代都被认为是激进分子。

en: Radicals are people who effect change.
cn: 激进分子是那些引燃变革的人。

en: They are the people about whom history is written.
cn: 他们是历史书写的对象。

en: Abolitionists were radicals; civil rights activists were radicals; even the founders of our country in their fight to win independence from England were radicals.
cn: 废奴主义者是激进分子；民权活动家是激进分子；甚至我们国家的开国元勋在争取脱离英国、赢得独立时也是激进分子。

en: Their presence in history has changed the way our society functions, mainly by shifting the balance of power that previously existed.
cn: 他们在历史上的存在改变了我们社会的运作方式，主要通过改变先前存在的权力天平。

en: Of course, there are some radicals who've made a negative impact on humanity.
cn: 当然，也有一些激进分子对人类造成了负面影响。

en: But undeniably, there would simply be no progress without radicals.
cn: 但不可否认的是，没有激进分子就没有进步。

en: That being said, next time someone calls me a radical, I will accept that label with pride.
cn: 话虽如此，如果下次有人叫我激进分子，我会骄傲地接受这个称呼。

en: We are very susceptible to the influence of the people around us.
cn: 我们很容易受到周围人的影响。

en: For instance, you may have known somebody who has gone overseas for a year or so and has returned with an accent, perhaps.
cn: 举个例子，你或许认识一个出国一年左右的人，这个人回国后说话可能会带着异国腔调。

en: We become part of our immediate environment.
cn: 我们会融入我们当下所处的环境。

en: None of us are immune to the influences of our own world, and let us not kid ourselves that we are untouched by the things and the people in our life.
cn: 没有人能免受自身所处世界的影响，所以不要自欺欺人地认为'自己没有受到生活中的事与人的影响'。

en: Fred goes off to his new job at a factory.
cn: 弗雷德到一个新工厂工作。

en: Fred takes his 10- minute coffee break, but the other workers take a half an hour.
cn: 他一般会花10分钟喝咖啡休息，但其余工人却会花上半个小时。

en: Fred says, 'What's the matter with you guys?'
cn: 弗雷德说：'你们这帮人怎么回事？'

en: Two weeks later, Fred is taking 20- minute breaks.
cn: 两周后，弗雷德花20分钟休息。

en: A month later, Fred takes his half hour.
cn: 一个月后，他也花半个小时休息了。

en: Fred is saying, 'If you can't beat them, join them.
cn: 他说：'如果你没办法改变别人，就加入他们。'

en: Why should I work any harder than the next guy?'
cn: 我为什么要比其他人更卖力干活呢？

en: The fascinating thing about being human is that generally we are unaware that there are changes taking place in our mentality.
cn: 人类的奇妙之处在于：我们通常无法意识到自己的心态正在发生转变。

en: It is like returning to the city smog after some weeks in the fresh air—only then do we realize that we have become accustomed to the nasty smells.
cn: 这就像是呼吸了数周的新鲜空气后再度呼吸城市的雾霾，直到那时我们才意识到——我们已经习惯了这些难闻的气味。

en: Mix with critical people and we learn to criticize; mix with happy people and we learn about happiness.
cn: 和挑剔的人生活相处，我们学会了批判；和快乐的人生活相处，我们懂得了幸福。

en: What this means is that we need to decide what we want from life and then choose our company accordingly.
cn: 这意味着，我们需要确定我们想从生活中获得什么，然后相应地选择我们的伙伴。

en: You may well say, 'That is going to take some effort.
cn: 你很可能会说，'这么做挺耗精力。'

en: It may not be comfortable.
cn: 可能并不轻松。

en: I may offend some of my present company.'
cn: 我可能会因此得罪我现有的一些伙伴。'

en: Right, but it is your life.
cn: 也没错，但这可是你自己的生活啊。

en: Fred may say, 'I'm always broke, frequently depressed.
cn: 弗雷德要是说：'我总是没钱花，也经常沮丧。'

en: I'm going nowhere and I never do anything exciting.'
cn: 我一事无成，生活也枯燥无味。'

en: Then we discover that Fred's best friends are always broke, frequently depressed, going nowhere and wishing that life was more exciting.
cn: 那么我们会发现，弗雷德的挚友们也总是囊中羞涩、时时沮丧、无所事事，希望生活能更精彩。

en: This is not a coincidence.
cn: 这并不是巧合。

en: Nor is it our business to stand in judgment of Fred.
cn: 当然，这也不是我们能评头论足的。

en: However, if Fred ever wants to improve his quality of life, the first thing he'll need to do is recognize what has been going on all these years.
cn: 然而，如果弗雷德想改善其生活品质，他首先要做的就是认清他这些年都受到了哪些影响。

en: It's no surprise that doctors as a profession suffer a lot of ill health because they spend their lives around sick people.
cn: 医生是一个罹患诸多疾病的职业，这不足为奇，毕竟他们一生都在和病人打交道。

en: Psychiatrists have a higher incidence of suicide in their profession for related reasons.
cn: 同样，精神病医生也会有更高的几率在其职业生涯中选择自杀。

en: Traditionally, 9 out of 10 children whose parents smoke smoke themselves.
cn: 那些父母抽烟的孩子，历来都是十个里有九个自己也会抽烟。

en: Obesity is in part an environmental problem.
cn: 肥胖在某种程度上也是一个环境问题。

en: Successful people have successful friends.
cn: 成功人士也会结交成功的朋友。

en: And so the story goes on.
cn: 这样的例子真是数不胜数。

en: Virtually every American can recognize a dollar bill at a mere glance.
cn: 几乎每个美国人都能一眼认出美钞。

en: Many can identify it by its sound or texture.
cn: 许多人可以通过声音或质地将其识别。

en: But few people indeed can accurately describe the world's most powerful, important currency.
cn: 但实际上，几乎没有人能够准确描述这种世上最强大、最重要的货币。

en: The American dollar bill is colored with black ink on one side and green on the other; the exact composition of the paper and ink is a closely guarded government secret.
cn: 美钞一面用黑墨着色，另一面用绿墨着色；纸张和墨水的确切成分是政府严守的秘密。

en: Despite its weighty importance, the dollar bill actually weighs little.
cn: 尽管美钞的重要性非常'重'，但实际上它的重量却很'轻'。

en: It requires nearly 500 bills to tip the scales at a pound.
cn: 达到一磅需要近500张钞票。

en: Not only is the dollar bill lightweight, but it also has a brief life span.
cn: 美钞不仅重量轻，而且寿命短。

en: Few dollar bills survive longer than 18 months.
cn: 很少有美钞能使用18个月以上。

en: The word 'dollar' is taken from the German word 'thaler,' the name for the world's most important currency in the 16th century.
cn: 'dollar（美元）'一词取自德语单词'thaler（泰勒）'，后者是16世纪世界上最重要货币的名称。

en: The thaler was a silver coin first minted in 1518 under the reign of Charles V, Emperor of Germany.
cn: thaler是一种银币，于1518年德国皇帝查理五世统治时期首次铸造。

en: The concept of paper money is a relatively recent innovation in the history of American currency.
cn: 纸币的概念是美国货币史上相对较近的一项创新。

en: When the Constitution was signed, people had little regard for paper money because of its steadily decreasing value during the colonial era.
cn: 宪法签署时，鉴于纸币的价值在殖民时代已是逐步衰减，人们几乎不重视它。

en: Because of this lack of faith, the new American government minted only coins for common currency.
cn: 由于这种信任匮乏，美国新政府仅铸造了硬币作为通用货币。

en: Interest- bearing bank notes were issued at the same time, but their purpose was limited to providing money for urgent government crises, such as American involvement in the War of 1812.
cn: 虽然同时也发行了计息纸币，但其用途仅限于为紧急政府危机提供资金，如美国卷入1812年战争。

en: The first noninterest- bearing paper currency was authorized by Congress in 1862, at the height of the Civil War.
cn: 1862年，在美国内战最激烈之际，国会批准发行了首批无息纸币。

en: At this point, citizens' old fears of devalued paper currency had calmed, and the dollar bill was born.
cn: 此时，市民对纸币贬值的旧日恐惧已经平息，美钞就此诞生。

en: The new green colored paper money quickly earned the nickname 'greenback.'
cn: 新的绿色纸币很快赢得了'绿背纸币'的绰号。

en: Today, the American dollar bill is a product of the Federal Reserve, and is issued from the twelve Federal Reserve banks around the United States.
cn: 如今，美钞是美联储的'产品'，并由美国各地的12家联邦储备银行发行。

en: The government keeps a steady supply of approximately two billion bills in circulation at all times.
cn: 政府在任何时候都保持着约20亿张流通纸币的稳定供应。

en: Controversy continues to surround the true value of the dollar bill.
cn: 围绕着美钞真正价值的争论仍在继续。

en: American history has seen generations of politicians argue in favor of a gold standard for American currency.
cn: 历代美国政治家都主张美国货币实行金本位制。

en: However, for the present, the American dollar bill holds the value that is printed on it, and little more.
cn: 然而，就目前而言，美钞的价值仅等于所印面值，除此之外几乎再无其他价值。

en: The only other guarantee on the bill is a Federal Reserve pledge as a confirmation in the form of government securities.
cn: 美钞另外的唯一担保便是以政府证券形式作为保证的美联储质押。

en: Good morning, Safe house Insurance.
cn: 早上好，安全屋保险公司。

en: My name is Paul.
cn: 我叫保罗。

en: How can I help you today?
cn: 今天我能为您做些什么？

en: Morning.
cn: 早上好。

en: I wouldn't say that it's good from where I'm standing.
cn: 从我的角度来看，这可不算是好。

en: This is Miss Wilson and this is the third time I've called this week since receiving your letter about our insurance claim.
cn: 我是威尔逊小姐，这是我本周第三次打电话了，自从收到你们关于我们保险索赔的信件以来。

en: I'm getting a little fed up with my calls about my claim being completely disregarded.
cn: 我有点受够了，我的索赔电话完全被忽视了。

en: Miss Wilson, thank you for calling back.
cn: 威尔逊小姐，谢谢您回电。

en: Can I take some details to help me look at your claim?
cn: 我能记录一些详细信息来查看您的索赔吗？

en: It's Miss May Wilson of 15 South Sea Road in Cornwall.
cn: 我是康沃尔郡南海路15号的梅·威尔逊小姐。

en: And the details are that our village was extensively flooded 2 months ago.
cn: 具体情况是，我们的村庄两个月前遭遇了大规模洪水。

en: The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water and five of us have been living in a caravan ever since.
cn: 我们小屋的整个底层都被水淹没了，我们五个人从那以后就一直住在拖车里。

en: You people are still withholding the money we are entitled to over a bizarre technical detail.
cn: 你们仍然因为一个奇怪的技术细节而扣留我们应该得到的钱。

en: And it's not acceptable, Paul!
cn: 这是不可接受的，保罗！

en: Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident.
cn: 威尔逊小姐，根据您账户上的记录，您提到的那个奇怪的技术细节指的是您在事发前一个月没有缴纳房屋保险费这一事实。

en: That money left our account, and now that you should be paying out, you're suddenly saying that you didn't receive it on time.
cn: 那笔钱已经从我们的账户中扣除了，现在你们应该赔付了，你们却突然说没有按时收到。

en: I'm really skeptical about this claim.
cn: 我对这种说法非常怀疑。

en: The contract does say that any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract and may affect claims.
cn: 合同确实规定，一年内的任何逾期付款都会影响保险合同的条款和条件，并可能影响索赔。

en: Of course, I can pass you on to my manager to talk to you more about this.
cn: 当然，我可以把您转给我的经理，让他和您进一步讨论这件事。

en: I've already spoken to him and you can tell him I'm furious now and that your company has a lawsuit on its hands.
cn: 我已经和他谈过了，你可以告诉他我现在非常愤怒，你们公司要打官司了。

en: You will be hearing from my lawyer.
cn: 你会收到我律师的函件。

en: Goodbye.
cn: 再见。

en: How do you feel about the future of artificial intelligence?
cn: 你对人工智能的未来怎么看？

en: Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it.
cn: 就我个人而言，我感到相当乐观。

en: AI?
cn: 人工智能？

en: I'm not so optimistic actually.
cn: 实际上我并不那么乐观。

en: In fact, it's something we should be concerned about.
cn: 事实上，这是我们应当关注的问题。

en: Well, it will help us humans understand ourselves better.
cn: 嗯，它会帮助我们人类更好地了解自己。

en: And, when we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can improve the world.
cn: 而且，当我们对自己有了更好的了解，我们就能改善世界。

en: Well, one thing is for sure: Technology is evolving faster than our ability to understand it.
cn: 嗯，有一件事是确定的：技术发展的速度比我们理解它的能力要快。

en: And in the future, AI will make jobs kind of pointless.
cn: 而在未来，人工智能会让工作变得有点毫无意义。

en: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time and allow us to be centered on creative tasks.
cn: 我认为人工智能实际上会帮助创造新型工作，这些工作会占用我们更少的时间，让我们能够专注于创造性的任务。

en: I doubt that very much.
cn: 我非常怀疑这一点。

en: Probably the last job that we will remain will be writing AI software.
cn: 可能我们最后保留的工作将是编写人工智能软件。

en: And then eventually, AI will just write its own software.
cn: 然后最终，人工智能会自己编写自己的软件。

en: At that time, we're going to have a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do, so we'll need artificial intelligence for the robots to take care of the old guys, like us.
cn: 到那时，将会有很多没人想做的工作，所以我们需要人工智能让机器人来照顾像我们这样的老人。

en: I don't know.
cn: 我不知道。

en: There's a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life.
cn: 有一种风险，人类文明可能会被更高级的数字生命形式所取代。

en: AI will be able to completely simulate a person in every way possible.
cn: 人工智能将能够以各种可能的方式完全模拟一个人。

en: In fact, some people think we are in the simulation, right now.
cn: 事实上，有些人认为我们现在就处于模拟之中。

en: That's impossible.
cn: 那不可能。

en: Humans can't even make a mosquito.
cn: 人类连蚊子都造不出来。

en: Computers only have chips.
cn: 电脑只有芯片。

en: People have brains, and that's where the wisdom comes from.
cn: 人有大脑，那是智慧的来源。

en: Once it's fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison.
cn: 一旦它完全发展成熟，人工智能就会厌倦试图与人类交流，因为相比之下我们的思维速度要慢得多。

en: I'm not so sure.
cn: 我不太确定。

en: A computer is a computer, and a computer is just a toy.
cn: 电脑就是电脑，电脑只是一个玩具。

en: Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast, so the computer will just get impatient talking to humans.
cn: 电脑可以非常快地沟通，所以电脑会变得不耐烦与人类交谈。

en: It will be barely getting any information out.
cn: 它将几乎无法获取任何信息。

en: Well, I believe there is a benevolent future with AI.
cn: 嗯，我相信人工智能会带来一个仁慈的未来。

en: I also think you watch too many science fiction films.
cn: 我也觉得你看太多科幻电影了。

en: To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
cn: 为了实现财务安全，你存下多少钱总是比你赚多少钱或投资多精明更重要。

en: If you are under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
cn: 如果你在30岁以下，你的目标应该是存下每月税后收入的20%。

en: This is irrespective of how much you earn.
cn: 这与你的收入多少无关。

en: Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
cn: 大约50%应该用于食物和住宿等必需品。

en: The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
cn: 剩下的30%用于休闲娱乐。

en: But for many young people, it'll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
cn: 但对许多年轻人来说，将这么大比例的收入用于储蓄是很困难的。

en: If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending.
cn: 如果你发现根本存不下钱，就从削减所有不必要的开支开始。

en: Allocate a tiny amount of 1 or 2 percent for savings, and gradually increase that amount.
cn: 将1%或2%的少量收入用于储蓄，然后逐渐增加这个数额。

en: Always keep that 20% goal in mind to prevent yourself from becoming complacent.
cn: 始终牢记20%的目标，以防自己变得自满。

en: It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan.
cn: 坚持如此严格的计划可能具有挑战性。

en: But if you adopt the right mindset, you should be able to make it work for you.
cn: 但如果你树立了正确的心态，你应该能让它为你所用。

en: So, what should you be doing with the money that you're saving?
cn: 那么，你应该如何处理你存下来的钱呢？

en: Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
cn: 一部分必须保持易于取用，以防紧急情况下需要现金。

en: The largest proportion should be invested in retirement plans, either through your employer or privately.
cn: 最大的一部分应该投资于退休计划，可以通过雇主或私人方式。

en: And you can keep some money for high-risk but potentially lucrative investments.
cn: 你也可以留一些钱用于高风险但潜在回报丰厚的投资。

en: Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
cn: 股息可以再投资或用于购买你喜欢的东西。

en: By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now, and still be financially secure in the future.
cn: 遵循这个计划，你有望能够享受现在的生活，同时在未来仍能保持财务安全。

en: I work in advertising and I like to keep up with current trends, mainly because I'm aware that we live in an image-obsessed world.
cn: 我在广告行业工作，我喜欢跟上当前的潮流，主要是因为我知道我们生活在一个痴迷于形象的世界里。

en: However, when I first started my job, occasionally I'd catch a glimpse of myself in the lifts, and find myself thinking that I looked a total mess.
cn: 然而，当我刚开始工作时，偶尔我会在电梯里瞥见自己，然后发现自己觉得自己看起来一团糟。

en: Was I being held back by my choice of clothing?
cn: 我是否因为着装选择而受到阻碍？

en: The short answer is yes, especially when clients are quick to judge you on your style rather than your work.
cn: 简短的回答是肯定的，尤其是当客户倾向于根据你的风格而非你的工作来评判你时。

en: But no one can be unique with their outfit every day.
cn: 但没有人能每天都穿得与众不同。

en: I mean, that's why uniforms were invented.
cn: 我的意思是，这就是制服被发明出来的原因。

en: So, here's what I did.
cn: 所以，我是这样做的。

en: I created my own uniform.
cn: 我创造了属于自己的制服。

en: To do this, I chose an appropriate outfit.
cn: 为此，我选择了一套合适的着装。

en: Then I bought multiple items of the same style in different shades.
cn: 然后我买了同一款式不同颜色的多件单品。

en: Now, I never worry about what I'm wearing in the morning even if I do get a bit tired of just wearing the same classic pieces.
cn: 现在，我早上从不担心穿什么，即使我确实有点厌倦了总是穿同样的经典款。

en: Overall, when it comes to work, you have to ask yourself: will looking smarter enhance my ability to do my job?
cn: 总的来说，谈到工作，你必须问自己：看起来更聪明会提升我工作的能力吗？

en: For some, this question may not be an issue at all.
cn: 对一些人来说，这个问题可能根本不是问题。

en: Especially if you work remotely and rarely see your colleagues or clients face to face.
cn: 尤其是如果你远程工作，很少与同事或客户面对面交流。

en: But if your job involves interacting with other people, the answer to this is often yes.
cn: 但如果你的工作涉及与他人互动，答案往往是肯定的。

en: So rather than fighting the system, I think we should just do whatever helps us to achieve our goals at work.
cn: 所以我认为，与其与体制对抗，不如做任何能帮助我们在工作中实现目标的事情。

en: If that means playing it safe with your image, then let's face it.
cn: 如果那意味着在形象上保持稳妥，那就让我们面对它吧。

en: It's probably worth it.
cn: 这可能是值得的。

en: Did you know that Americans have approximately three times the amount of space we had 50 years ago?
cn: 你知道美国人的居住空间大约是50年前的三倍吗？

en: Therefore, you'd think we'd have sufficient room for all of our possessions.
cn: 因此，你会认为我们会有足够的空间来存放所有物品。

en: On the contrary, the personal storage business is now a growing industry.
cn: 恰恰相反，个人仓储业务现在是一个不断增长的行业。

en: We've got triple the space, but we've become such enthusiastic consumers that we require even more.
cn: 我们的空间增加了两倍，但我们已经成为了如此狂热的消费者，以至于我们需要更多。

en: This phenomenon has resulted in significant credit card debt, enormous environmental footprints, and perhaps not coincidentally, our happiness levels have failed to increase over the same half century.
cn: 这种现象导致了大量的信用卡债务、巨大的环境足迹，而且也许并非巧合的是，我们的幸福水平在同一半个世纪里并未提高。

en: I'm here to suggest an alternative that having less might actually be a preferable decision.
cn: 我在这里提出一个替代方案：拥有更少实际上可能是更可取的决定。

en: Many of us have experienced, at some stage, the pleasure of possessing less.
cn: 我们中的许多人在某个阶段都体验过拥有更少的乐趣。

en: I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economize, but also simplify your life.
cn: 我认为，更少的物品和更少的空间不仅能帮助你节省开支，还能简化你的生活。

en: I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
cn: 我最近开始了一个创新项目，以发现一些能提供我所需要的一切的创造性解决方案。

en: By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square meters instead of 60, I immediately saved $200,000.
cn: 通过购买一套40平方米而不是60平方米的公寓，我立即节省了20万美元。

en: Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills, and also a smaller carbon footprint.
cn: 更小的空间带来更低的水电费，也更小的碳足迹。

en: Because it is designed around an edited collection of possessions, limited to my favorite stuff, I'm really excited to live there.
cn: 因为它是围绕着一套精选的物品设计的，只限于我最喜欢的东西，我真的很兴奋能住在那里。

en: How can we live more basically?
cn: 我们怎样才能更基本地生活？

en: Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
cn: 首先，我们必须无情地将不必要的物品从生活中剔除。

en: To stem consumption, we should think before we buy, and ask ourselves, 'Will it truly make me happier?'
cn: 为了抑制消费，我们应该在购买前三思，问自己：'它真的会让我更快乐吗？'

en: Obviously, we should possess some great stuff, but we want belongings that we're going to love for years.
cn: 显然，我们应该拥有一些好东西，但我们想要的是我们会喜爱多年的物品。

en: Secondly, we require space efficiency.
cn: 其次，我们需要空间效率。

en: We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
cn: 我们想要的是设计为大多数时间都能使用的电器，而不是偶尔使用的。

en: Why own a six- burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
cn: 当你连三个炉头都很少用时，为什么要拥有一个六炉头的炉灶呢？

en: Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.
cn: 最后，我们需要多功能的空间和家居用品。

en: I combined a movable wall with transforming furniture to get more out of my limited space.
cn: 我把可移动的墙壁和可变形的家具结合起来，以充分利用我有限的空间。

en: Consider my coffee table.
cn: 看看我的咖啡桌。

en: It increases in size to accommodate ten.
cn: 它可以扩大尺寸以容纳十个人。

en: My office is tucked away, easily hidden.
cn: 我的办公室被收起来了，很容易隐藏。

en: My bed simply pops out of the wall.
cn: 我的床可以直接从墙里弹出来。

en: For guests, I can relocate the movable wall and utilize the foldable guest beds I installed.
cn: 对于客人，我可以移动可移动的墙壁，并使用我安装的可折叠客床。

en: I'm not saying we should all live in tiny apartments, but consider the benefits of an edited life.
cn: 我不是说我们都应该住在小公寓里，但请考虑精简生活的益处。

en: When you return home and walk through your front door, take a moment to ask yourselves, 'Could I do with a little life editing? Would that give me more freedom and more time?'
cn: 当你回到家，走进前门时，花点时间问问自己：'我是否需要对生活做些精简？那会给我更多的自由和更多的时间吗？'

en: Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation—even if it hurts them to do so.
cn: 现在，信不信由你，人们有时为了保持良好的、诚实的声誉而撒谎——即使这样做会伤害他们自己。

en: At least, this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
cn: 至少，这是一个科学家团队提出的观点，并有证据可以证明。

en: Picture this scenario: You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
cn: 想象一下这个场景：你经常因工作开车，每月最多可报销400英里的里程。

en: Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month.
cn: 你公司的大多数人每月开车约300英里。

en: But this month, you drove 400 miles.
cn: 但这个月，你开了400英里。

en: How many miles do you think you'd claim in your expense report?
cn: 你觉得你会在费用报告里申报多少英里？

en: The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we're discussing today.
cn: 科学家们正是问了这个问题，作为我们今天讨论的研究的一部分。

en: With surprising results, they found that 12% of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
cn: 结果令人惊讶，他们发现12%的受访者报告的驾驶里程低于实际数字，给出的平均答案是384英里。

en: In other words, they lied about their number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
cn: 换句话说，他们在里程数上撒了谎，即使他们会失去本应得到的钱。

en: The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high expense claim.
cn: 研究人员认为，这样做是为了显得诚实，因为他们假设其他人会怀疑高额的报销申请。

en: But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
cn: 但为什么人们会编造数字来损害自己的利益呢？

en: The researchers explain that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they'll be judged by others.
cn: 研究人员解释说，许多人非常关心自己的声誉以及别人会如何评价他们。

en: If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
cn: 如果他们足够在意，他们对显得诚实和不失去他人尊重的担忧可能大于他们真正诚实的愿望。

en: The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people's suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
cn: 研究人员断言，这些发现表明，当人们获得非常有利的结果时，他们会预料到他人的怀疑反应，并且宁愿撒谎以显得诚实，也不愿说实话而显得像是自私的骗子。

en: So why is this research important?
cn: 那么这项研究为什么重要呢？

en: Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie- selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others.
cn: 嗯，专家们普遍认为有两种主要类型的谎言——自私的谎言和旨在造福他人的谎言。

en: The first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company, while the second involves lying to help others or not offend others, for example, telling a friend whose outfit you don't like that they look great.
cn: 第一种，正如你所预料的，是为了自私的利益，比如向保险公司提交欺诈性索赔，而第二种涉及撒谎来帮助他人或不冒犯他人，例如，告诉你穿着你不喜欢的衣服的朋友说他们看起来很棒。

en: But the researchers are suggesting a third type of lying- lying to maintain a good reputation.
cn: 但研究人员提出第三种类型的谎言——为了保持良好的声誉而撒谎。

en: Now this hypothesis is new and some skeptics argue that this isn't a whole new category of lie.
cn: 现在这个假设是新的，一些怀疑论者认为这并非一个全新的谎言类别。

en: But the findings seem intuitive to me.
cn: 但这些发现对我来说似乎很直观。

en: After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others.
cn: 毕竟，撒谎的主要动机之一是为了增加我们在他人眼中的价值。

en: So it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.
cn: 所以人们很可能会为了显得诚实而撒谎。

en: Why do old people dislike new music?
cn: 为什么老年人不喜欢新音乐？

en: As I've grown older, I often hear people my age say things like 'They just don't make good music like they used to'.
cn: 随着我年龄的增长，我经常听到同龄人说这样的话：'他们就是不像过去那样做出好音乐了'。

en: Why does this happen?
cn: 为什么会这样？

en: Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
cn: 幸运的是，心理学能给我们一些关于这个难题的见解。

en: Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14.
cn: 音乐品味早在13或14岁时就开始定型。

en: By the time we're in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
cn: 到我们20岁出头的时候，这些品味就已经相当牢固地固定下来了。

en: In fact, studies have found that by the time we turn 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
cn: 事实上，研究发现，到我们33岁时，我们中的大多数人已经停止听新音乐了。

en: Meanwhile, popular songs released when you're in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group through the rest of your life.
cn: 与此同时，在你十几岁早期发行的流行歌曲很可能在你的同龄人群体中保持相当高的受欢迎度，贯穿你的余生。

en: There could be a biological explanation for this, as there's evidence that the brain's ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms and melodies deteriorates with age.
cn: 这可能有一个生物学上的解释，因为有证据表明，大脑区分不同和弦、节奏和旋律的细微差别的能力会随着年龄的增长而退化。

en: So to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all 'sound the same'.
cn: 所以对老年人来说，较新的、不太熟悉的歌曲可能都'听起来一样'。

en: But there may be some simpler reasons for older people's aversion to newer music.
cn: 但老年人厌恶新音乐可能还有一些更简单的原因。

en: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the 'mere exposure effect', which, in essence, means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
cn: 社会心理学中研究最多的法则之一是所谓的'纯粹接触效应'，其本质上意味着我们接触某事物越多，我们就越倾向于喜欢它。

en: This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see and the songs we listen to.
cn: 这发生在我们认识的人、我们看到的广告和我们听的歌曲上。

en: When you're in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos.
cn: 当你十几岁时，你可能会花相当多的时间听音乐或看音乐视频。

en: Your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
cn: 你最喜欢的歌曲和艺术家成为你日常生活中熟悉、令人舒适的一部分。

en: For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase, so there's less time to spend discovering new music.
cn: 对于许多30岁以上的人来说，工作和家庭责任增加了，所以花在发现新音乐上的时间更少了。

en: Instead, many will simply listen to old, familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
cn: 相反，许多人只会听他们生活中那段有更多空闲时间时的老的、熟悉的最爱。

en: Of course, those teen years weren't necessarily carefree.
cn: 当然，那些青少年时期并不一定是无忧无虑的。

en: They're famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.
cn: 它们以混乱著称，这就是为什么这么多电视节目和电影都以高中混乱为中心。

en: Psychology research has shown that the emotions that we experience as teens seem more intense than those that come later.
cn: 心理学研究表明，我们在青少年时期经历的情感似乎比之后经历的情感更强烈。

en: And we also know that intense emotions are associated with stronger memories and preferences.
cn: 我们也知道强烈的情感与更强的记忆和偏好相关。

en: Both of these might explain why the songs we listen to during this period become so memorable and beloved.
cn: 这两点或许可以解释为什么我们在这段时期听的歌曲变得如此令人难忘和深受喜爱。

en: So there's nothing wrong with your parents because they don't like your music.
cn: 所以你的父母不喜欢你的音乐并没有错。

en: Rather it's all part of the natural order of things.
cn: 相反，这完全是自然秩序的一部分。

en: This is unbelievable.
cn: 这真是令人难以置信。

en: Unlike any video game I've ever played before, it's so boring, yet so relaxing at the same time.
cn: 它和我以前玩过的任何一款电子游戏都不同，既很无聊，同时又很令人放松。

en: How did you hear about this driving simulator?
cn: 你是怎么知道这个模拟驾驶游戏的？

en: My brother introduced it to me last year.
cn: 我哥哥去年介绍给我的。

en: I was surprised to find how educational and realistic it was.
cn: 我惊讶地发现它非常有教育意义，而且很逼真。

en: It's called Euro Truck Simulator, but they have other versions as well for America and so on.
cn: 它叫《欧洲卡车模拟》，但他们也有美国等其他地区的版本。

en: I was really drawn to the scenery.
cn: 我真的很喜欢那里的风景。

en: The routes go through parts of the country you don't normally see as a tourist.
cn: 路线会经过这个国家的一些地方，作为游客通常看不到。

en: Yeah, I can see that.
cn: 是的，我能看出来。

en: It seems so simple, just transporting cargo from point A to point B, driving from one city to another.
cn: 看起来很简单，只是把货物从A点运到B点，从一个城市开到另一个城市。

en: But I really appreciate all the details that go into the game.
cn: 但我真的很欣赏游戏中所有的细节。

en: It's even given me a new appreciation for the logistics industry and traffic on the road.
cn: 它甚至让我对物流行业和道路交通有了新的认识。

en: I completely agree.
cn: 我完全同意。

en: My brother also introduced me to some videos of someone that streams their game online.
cn: 我哥哥还给我介绍了一些有人在网上直播游戏视频。

en: It was fascinating to watch, really.
cn: 看起来真的很吸引人。

en: This guy drove very carefully, obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules—such a contrast to most violent games.
cn: 这家伙开车非常小心，遵守所有的路标和交通规则——与大多数暴力游戏形成了鲜明对比。

en: Honestly, playing has inspired me to look into the industry more.
cn: 说实话，玩游戏激发了我对这个行业更多的探索。

en: I've read articles about how self- driving trucks may soon be available and could greatly impact cargo logistics.
cn: 我读过一些关于自动驾驶卡车可能很快就会问世并可能对货运物流产生巨大影响的文章。

en: Considering all that goes into driving these larger vehicles, it's amazing that we could soon have that kind of technology.
cn: 考虑到驾驶这些大型车辆所需的一切，我们很快就能拥有这种技术，真是令人惊叹。

en: Ha.
cn: 哈。

en: I've got one step further.
cn: 我又进了一步。

en: I registered to take a safe driving course to improve my real- life driving skills.
cn: 我报名参加了一个安全驾驶课程，以提高我在现实生活中的驾驶技能。

en: In a way, I feel like I have a head start compared to other students in the class.
cn: 在某种程度上，我觉得自己比班上的其他学生有了一个先发优势。

en: Playing this video game has given me some maneuvering practices already.
cn: 玩这个电子游戏已经给了我一些操控练习。

en: I'm not sure how accurate the video game is compared to real- life situations.
cn: 我不确定这款电子游戏与现实情况相比有多准确。

en: But if it results in more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection, I'd say that's a positive outcome.
cn: 但如果它能让更多的司机在进入十字路口前观察两侧情况，我会说这是一个积极的结果。

en: How do you like being self- employed?
cn: 你觉得自雇怎么样？

en: There are obvious benefits, though I don't seem to have the freedom I anticipated as I just don't seem able to decline work offers.
cn: 有明显的好处，尽管我似乎没有我预期的那么自由，因为我似乎无法拒绝工作机会。

en: And working alone, there have been times when I've found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
cn: 而且独自工作，有时我发现单靠金钱提供的动力不足。

en: Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
cn: 自从你开始为自己工作以来，你是否也有同样的经历？

en: Sometimes, yes.
cn: 有时是的。

en: Unlike the rest of the workforce who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they're feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
cn: 不像其他有经理的员工在感到懒惰或无聊时可以提振动力，我们自雇员工在没有经理鼓舞士气的情况下工作。

en: There's no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
cn: 身边没有人给予赞扬或发起合作，没有人能更好地利用我们的兴趣和才能。

en: That's a fact.
cn: 这是事实。

en: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course.
cn: 当然，并不是每个经理都有这样的意识和关怀。

en: And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
cn: 而且肯定也不是所有的经理都知道怎么激励员工。

en: Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there's an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
cn: 尽管如此，身边有一位经理至少意味着，当你的精力和专注力开始耗尽时，他们有机会足够体面地为你着想。

en: The motivator I value most is autonomy.
cn: 我最看重的激励因素是自主权。

en: I've learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
cn: 我学会了不为了全天候工作和答应每一位客户的要求而牺牲我珍视的自主权。

en: Yes, I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independence.
cn: 是的，我需要提醒自己，我选择这种生活方式是为了独立。

en: I don't miss aspects of permanent full- time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours and so on.
cn: 我并不怀念我不喜欢的长期全职工作的那些方面，比如办公室政治、工作不安全感、不灵活的工作时间等等。

en: I wouldn't mind a bit more in the form of praise though, praise which is on the record.
cn: 不过，我不介意多一些表扬，那些有记录的表扬。

en: That'll come with time.
cn: 那会随着时间而来的。

en: Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction.
cn: 人际关系是通过人与人之间的互动不可避免地培养起来的。

en: Engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards, these are things you'll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation.
cn: 与客户打交道、获得书面证明和推荐、之后与客户保持联系，这些你会发现都会适时到来，并为你提供动力。

en: You're right.
cn: 你说得对。

en: That's an area I do need to put some more effort into—building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills.
cn: 那是我确实需要付出更多努力的领域——与那些需要我服务和技能的人建立更密切的关系。

en: Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there is little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
cn: 天气是我们生活中一股持续的力量，但关于它如何影响商业的营销研究却很少。

en: Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
cn: 现在，一项新研究揭示了晴天和下雪天如何影响消费者行为。

en: Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
cn: 这些天气条件会促使消费者在脑海中想象使用与相应天气相关的产品。

en: This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
cn: 这导致消费者对这些产品赋予更高的价值。

en: That is, they're willing to pay more money for them.
cn: 也就是说，他们愿意为它们支付更多的钱。

en: But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside.
cn: 但这种关联只在与户外活动相关的产品中被发现。

en: How does this work?
cn: 这是如何起作用的？

en: Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
cn: 研究人员以沙滩巾为例。

en: On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself, they are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
cn: 在晴天，看到该产品的消费者不仅仅是在看毛巾本身，他们很可能在想象自己躺在阳光下毛巾上的场景。

en: This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumers mind.
cn: 这种使用毛巾的心理画面会增加产品在消费者心目中的价值。

en: Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
cn: 研究人员提出以下假设来解释他们的发现。

en: They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
cn: 他们认为这种心理画面在阳光和雪天中起作用，因为这些天气条件与户外活动有积极的关联。

en: The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
cn: 这种效果在雨天中没有被观察到。

en: Researchers assert this is because there aren't many activities that are enabled by rain.
cn: 研究人员断言，这是因为雨天能够开展的户外活动不多。

en: Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather, and not for any activities.
cn: 大多数与雨相关的产品，如雨伞，只用于防雨，而不用于任何活动。

en: Researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
cn: 研究人员认为，在网上销售多种产品的公司可以从这项研究提供的见解中获益最多。

en: Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price these products.
cn: 线上商家经常使用复杂的数学公式来决定要主推何种产品以及如何定价。

en: Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
cn: 纳入更多与天气相关的数据能让他们作出更好的决策。

en: This could bolster sales.
cn: 这可能会提振销售。

en: Setting the office air- conditioning at about 22°C has become standard practice across the world.
cn: 将办公室空调温度设定在22摄氏度左右已成为世界各地的标准做法。

en: Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation and air- conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
cn: 世界各地许多关于供暖、通风和空调的指南手册都声称，办公室的工作效率在22度时达到顶峰。

en: Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air- conditioned offices.
cn: 许多人确实在装有空调的办公室里从飙升的夏季高温中得到了缓解。

en: But recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
cn: 但最近的研究对'凉快的办公室工作效率更高'这一公认看法提出了质疑。

en: The reality is more complex.
cn: 现实情况更为复杂。

en: Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air- conditioning and productivity.
cn: 研究人员对所有关于空调和工作效率的研究进行了回顾。

en: They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
cn: 他们发现，即使在盛夏，22度可能也有点冷。

en: For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees.
cn: 对于穿着典型夏装的人来说，最佳温度范围是在23到26度之间。

en: And people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
cn: 只要人们能够调整衣物和预期，他们甚至能忍受超出这一舒适区的温度。

en: In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air- conditioning up.
cn: 事实上，即使是在很热的日子里，调高空调温度也是合理的。

en: People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot.
cn: 人们常常只追求一个最佳温度，这在人们感到热的时候是可以理解的。

en: But there is a range of at least three to four degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
cn: 但存在至少三到四度的范围，不会产生任何负面影响。

en: Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
cn: 与此相关的另一个问题是，人们可能会在心理上依赖空调。

en: If they're used to the environment which is air- conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures.
cn: 如果他们习惯了有空调的环境，他们就会倾向于喜欢较低的温度。

en: But the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
cn: 但研究发现，几乎所有人类都能适应新的温度。

en: It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people's productivity suffered.
cn: 只有在温度范围的极端情况下，人们的工作效率才会受到影响。

en: This range was above 26 degrees and below 19 degrees.
cn: 这个范围是高于26度和低于19度。

en: Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience.
cn: 心理学研究往往将独处描绘为一种消极的体验。

en: Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
cn: 20世纪70年代和90年代进行的研究表明，与与他人在一起时相比，人们独处时感到不那么快乐。

en: However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
cn: 然而，一篇新论文展示了对独处的另一种观点，一种认为独处可以是积极的观点。

en: Let's start by looking at the earlier research.
cn: 让我们先来看看早期的研究。

en: It had a couple of shortcomings.
cn: 它有几个缺点。

en: First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
cn: 首先，它在一个从积极到消极的量表上测量情绪，忽视了我们的积极情绪和消极情绪可以独立波动的可能性。

en: Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
cn: 此外，它将情绪简单地分为积极或消极。

en: It didn't consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees, and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
cn: 它没有考虑到情绪会在不同程度上激发我们，而且积极和消极情绪都可能让我们受到很大或很小的激发。

en: That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high- arousal or low- arousal.
cn: 也就是说，无论是积极的还是消极的，情绪都可以是高激发或低激发的。

en: High- arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low- arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
cn: 高激发情绪包括积极方面的兴奋或消极方面的愤怒，而低激发情绪包括积极方面的平静或消极方面的孤独。

en: This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
cn: 这项新研究试图克服这些缺点。

en: Researchers began with a simple study.
cn: 研究人员从一项简单的研究开始。

en: They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity, and measured how this solitude influences their emotional state.
cn: 他们要求参与者独自坐15分钟，不参与任何活动，并测量这种独处如何影响他们的情绪状态。

en: This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high- arousal emotions.
cn: 这个实验特别旨在确定独处对高激发情绪的影响。

en: It looked at positive emotions such as being excited or interested, and negative emotions including being scared or distressed.
cn: 它考察了积极情绪，如兴奋或感兴趣，以及消极情绪，包括害怕或痛苦。

en: The results were clear.
cn: 结果很明确。

en: After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
cn: 独处15分钟后，参与者的两种情绪都有所减弱。

en: A second study measured the effects of solitude on low- arousal emotions.
cn: 第二项研究测量了独处对低激发情绪的影响。

en: These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad or lonely.
cn: 这些情绪包括积极和消极的情绪，如平静、放松、悲伤或孤独。

en: That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
cn: 那个实验发现，所有这些情绪都因独处而增强了。

en: Thus it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
cn: 因此，过去对独处的描绘似乎是错误的。

en: It doesn't have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
cn: 它并没有一个可以简单地定性为好或坏的情绪效应。

en: Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience.
cn: 相反，它改变了我们内心体验的强度。

en: It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
cn: 它放大了更平静的情绪，但减弱了更强烈情感的强度。

en: It's worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
cn: 值得澄清的是，这些发现涉及相对短暂的独处时期。

en: This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
cn: 这与长期的孤独不同。

en: Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects.
cn: 研究表明，后者与一系列负面的生理和心理影响相关。

en: How can people benefit from being alone?
cn: 人们如何从独处中受益？

en: The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
cn: 这里的发现表明，人们可以利用独处来调节情绪。

en: Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
cn: 独处可以帮助我们在兴奋后安静下来，在愤怒后平静下来，或者只是感到平和。

en: In 1984, the World Chess Championship was called off abruptly, due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
cn: 1984年，世界象棋锦标赛突然取消，原因是争夺冠军的一位选手身体状况不佳。

en: He wasn't alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
cn: 他并不是唯一一个经历这项运动极端身体影响的人。

en: Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6,000 calories in one day.
cn: 据报道，精英选手一天可以消耗高达惊人的6000卡路里。

en: Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
cn: 这是否意味着更努力地思考是一条简单的减肥途径？

en: Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20% to 25% of the body's overall energy.
cn: 嗯，当身体处于休息状态时，我们知道大脑消耗了身体总能量的20%到25%，这个数字令人吃惊。

en: This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy- expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body's weight overall.
cn: 这种利用水平实际上使大脑成为身体中耗能最多的器官，然而它只占身体总重量的2%。

en: So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we'll burn?
cn: 所以我们越让这个器官工作，就会燃烧越多的卡路里？

en: Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
cn: 从技术上讲，对于认知困难的任务，答案是肯定的。

en: What counts as a 'difficult' mental task varies between individuals.
cn: 什么算作'困难'的脑力任务因人而异。

en: But generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines, or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
cn: 但一般来说，它可以被描述为大脑无法轻易用先前学到的常规方法解决的事情，或者不断改变条件的任务。

en: However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack.
cn: 然而，深度思考并不会消耗掉吃含糖零食所获得的热量。

en: Because in relation to the brain's huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
cn: 因为相对于大脑用于大量任务的大量总能量消耗而言，仅仅更努力思考所需的能量实际上相对微小。

en: We're unconscious of most of what uses up the brain's energy.
cn: 我们意识不到大部分消耗大脑能量的活动。

en: A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
cn: 其中很多活动与有意识的活动无关，比如学习唱歌或弹吉他。

en: The brain is able to allocate blood (and thus energy) to particular regions that are being active at that point.
cn: 大脑能够将血液（从而也是能量）分配到当时活跃的特定区域。

en: But the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant.
cn: 但大脑中可利用的总能量被认为是恒定的。

en: So, while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain's energy budget overall, these activities don't significantly alter it.
cn: 因此，虽然当我们执行困难的认知任务时，大脑局部区域的能量使用可能会有显著增加，但就整个大脑的总能量预算而言，这些活动并不会显著改变它。

en: So, why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition?
cn: 那么，为什么国际象棋冠军变得太瘦而无法参加比赛呢？

en: The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
cn: 普遍的共识是，这主要归结为压力和食物摄入减少，而不是精神疲惫。

en: Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
cn: 长时间让身体保持准备行动的状态是非常耗能的。

en: If you can't eat as often or as much as you can or would normally—then you might lose weight.
cn: 如果你不能像平常一样频繁或大量地进食，那么你可能会体重下降。

en: When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their résumé, so they don't need to repeat the information.
cn: 当一个人去面试时，面试官大概已经看过他们的简历了，所以他们不需要重复那些信息。

en: But that's what most people will do, as it's their instinct to recite things that are already on their résumé.
cn: 但大多数人都会这么做，因为背诵简历上已有的内容是他们的本能。

en: It's important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
cn: 求职者做好两个关键方面的功课很重要。

en: First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves.
cn: 第一，他们不只是告诉别人一个关于自己的事实。

en: They're telling a story, and stories take work to create.
cn: 他们在讲述一个故事，而故事需要花心思去创作。

en: Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments something they're proud of and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
cn: 想出一个好故事意味着要反思是什么让他们的事业成就成为他们引以为豪的东西，以及这些成就能突出什么优势。

en: Candidates shouldn't pick a broad general strength to elaborate on, such as 'I'm smart, I work hard and I get things done.'
cn: 求职者不应该选一个宽泛的通用优点来阐述，比如‘我很聪明，我工作努力，我能把事情做好。’

en: To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends or co- workers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
cn: 为了想出多个职业成就或例子来应对不同的面试问题，求职者应该与他人交谈，尤其是了解他们的人——伴侣、朋友或同事，他们会提出与他们记忆中不同的故事。

en: Secondly, candidates should know what's at stake for the company with this job opening.
cn: 第二，求职者应该知道这个职位空缺对公司来说关系重大的是什么。

en: What they really are asking you is 'Tell me why you are going to help me.'
cn: 他们真正在问的是‘告诉我你为什么会帮助我。’

en: If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
cn: 如果这个人是一个准备充分的求职者，他们应该已经弄清楚了这些事情。

en: They've read the job description and researched the company on the Internet.
cn: 他们读过职位描述，并在网上研究过这家公司。

en: What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
cn: 求职者应该寻找的是公司在做什么，他们试图完成什么，以及是什么阻碍了他们完成这些事情。

en: How long should it take to answer?
cn: 回答应该花多长时间？

en: Around a minute.
cn: 大约一分钟。

en: That's about right for most people's attention spans.
cn: 这对大多数人的注意力持续时间来说差不多合适。

en: Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes will start to feel more like a speech.
cn: 不到一分钟可能会显得仓促，而超过两分钟则会开始感觉像在演讲。

en: But the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
cn: 但答案的长度并不是一门精确的科学，求职者需要让自己的职业故事保持重点明确，并根据听众进行调整。

en: It's my last day at work tomorrow.
cn: 明天是我最后一天上班。

en: I start my new job in two weeks.
cn: 我两周后开始新工作。

en: My human resources manager wants to conduct an interview with me before I leave.
cn: 我的人力资源经理想在我离开之前和我面谈一次。

en: Ah, an exit interview.
cn: 啊，离职面谈。

en: Are you looking forward to it?
cn: 你期待吗？

en: I'm not sure how I feel about it.
cn: 我不确定我对此是什么感觉。

en: I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time, but I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel.
cn: 我辞职是因为我在那家公司不开心很久了，但我不确定是否应该告诉他们我的真实感受。

en: To my way of thinking, there are two main potential benefits that come from unleashing an agitated stream of truth during an exit interview.
cn: 依我看，在离职面谈中倾吐激动的真话有两个主要的潜在好处。

en: The first is release.
cn: 第一个是释放。

en: Unburdening yourself of frustration and perhaps even anger to someone who isn't a friend or close colleague can be wonderfully freeing.
cn: 向一个不是朋友或亲密同事的人倾诉挫折甚至愤怒，会让人感到无比解脱。

en: And let me guess.
cn: 让我猜猜。

en: The second is that the criticism will, theoretically, help the organization I'm leaving to improve, making sure employees of the future are less likely to encounter what I did?
cn: 第二个是，理论上，批评将有助于我离开的组织改进，确保未来的员工不太可能遇到我遇到过的问题？

en: That's right.
cn: 没错。

en: But the problem with the company improvement part is that very often it doesn't happen.
cn: 但公司改进这部分的问题在于，它往往不会发生。

en: An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't.
cn: 离职面谈应该是保密的，但往往不是。

en: In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential, and the information is used as dirt against another manager, or can be traded among senior managers.
cn: 在我的公司，从这些面谈中获得的信息往往不是保密的，这些信息被用作对付另一位经理的把柄，或者可以在高级经理之间交易。

en: Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose in the interview.
cn: 现在你让我重新考虑在面谈中要透露什么。

en: There is always the chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry.
cn: 这总是有可能影响我的声誉和我在行业内建立人脉的能力。

en: It is a pretty small industry after all.
cn: 毕竟这个行业相当小。

en: Anything you initially gained from the instant satisfaction of telling it like it is, you might lose down the track by injuring your future career prospects.
cn: 你最初从如实相告的即时满足中获得的任何东西，以后都可能因为损害你未来的职业前景而失去。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: Perhaps it'll be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate- your- employer websites.
cn: 也许去那些给雇主打分的网站上发泄一下会更好。

en: You could.
cn: 你可以。

en: And don't do the interview at all.
cn: 或者根本不做面谈。

en: Exit interviews are not mandatory.
cn: 离职面谈不是强制性的。

en: Today, I'm talking to the renowned botanist, Jane Forster.
cn: 今天，我在和著名的植物学家简·福斯特交谈。

en: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry.
cn: 谢谢你邀请我参加节目，亨利。

en: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary.
cn: 最近，简，自从你最新的纪录片发行以来，你成了名人。

en: Can you tell us a little about it?
cn: 你能给我们简单介绍一下吗？

en: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rain forest in equatorial areas of southeast Asia.
cn: 嗯，它记录了我研究东南亚赤道地区雨林本土植被的考察。

en: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations.
cn: 你确实去了一些非常有异国情调的地方旅行。

en: It was far from glamorous, to be honest.
cn: 说实话，这远非光鲜。

en: The area we visited was accessible only by canoe.
cn: 我们访问的地区只有乘独木舟才能到达。

en: And the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least.
cn: 而且小屋的生活条件至少可以说是原始的。

en: There was no electricity, and our water supply was a nearby stream.
cn: 没有电，我们的供水来自附近的一条小溪。

en: How were the weather conditions while you were there?
cn: 你在那里的时候天气怎么样？

en: The weather was not conducive to our work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable.
cn: 天气根本不利于我们的工作，因为湿度几乎让人无法忍受。

en: At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing.
cn: 中午时分，我们待在小屋里什么也不做。

en: It was too humid to either work or sleep.
cn: 太潮湿了，既无法工作也无法睡觉。

en: How long did your team spend in the jungle?
cn: 你的团队在丛林中待了多长时间？

en: Originally, we planned to be there for a month.
cn: 最初，我们计划在那里待一个月。

en: But in the end, we stayed for only two weeks.
cn: 但最后，我们只待了两周。

en: Why did you cut the expedition short.
cn: 你们为什么缩短了考察时间？

en: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching.
cn: 行程进行到一半时，我们收到消息说飓风正在逼近。

en: And we had to evacuate at very short notice.
cn: 我们不得不在极短的时间内撤离。

en: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote.
cn: 那听起来像是个有趣的轶事。

en: It was frightening.
cn: 很吓人。

en: The fastest evacuation route was through river rapids.
cn: 最快的撤离路线是穿过河流急流。

en: We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment.
cn: 我们不得不带着所有设备在急流中穿行。

en: So overall, was the journey unsuccessful?
cn: 那么总的来说，这次旅程不成功吗？

en: Absolutely not.
cn: 当然不是。

en: We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.
cn: 我们收集了大量关于当地植物的数据。

en: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions?
cn: 你为什么能忍受这样恶劣的条件？

en: Botany is an obsession for me.
cn: 植物学对我来说是一种痴迷。

en: Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery, and I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world.
cn: 我访问的许多目的地都有令人惊叹的风景，而且我能遇到来自世界各地的各种各样的人。

en: So where will your next destination be?
cn: 那么你的下一个目的地是哪里？

en: I haven't decided yet.
cn: 我还没决定。

en: Then we can leave it for another vacation.
cn: 那我们可以留到下次再说。

en: Thanks.
cn: 谢谢。

en: Scientists often use specialized jargon terms while communicating with laymen.
cn: 科学家在与外行人交流时经常使用专业术语。

en: Most of them don't realize the harmful effects of this practice.
cn: 他们大多没有意识到这种做法的有害影响。

en: In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms.
cn: 在一项新研究中，阅读自动驾驶汽车和外科手术机器人等主题时接触到术语的人，后来表示他们比阅读相同主题但未使用专业术语的人对科学的兴趣更低。

en: They also felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics.
cn: 他们也觉得自己对科学了解较少，更没有资格讨论科学话题。

en: It's noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text.
cn: 值得注意的是，即使文本中定义了术语，结果也没有区别。

en: Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn't explained.
cn: 即使术语被定义了，读者仍然和阅读未解释术语的读者一样感到缺乏参与感。

en: The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers.
cn: 问题是，仅仅术语的存在就给读者发出了令人沮丧的信息。

en: Hillary Shulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialized words are a signal.
cn: 该研究的作者希拉里·舒尔曼断言，专业词汇是一种信号。

en: Jargon tells people that the message isn't for them.
cn: 术语告诉人们，这条信息不是给他们的。

en: There is an even darker side to how people react to jargon.
cn: 人们对术语的反应还有更阴暗的一面。

en: In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science.
cn: 在另一项研究中，研究人员发现，阅读含有术语的科学文章会让人怀疑真正的科学。

en: They found the opposite when a text is easier to read, then people are more persuaded.
cn: 他们发现，当文本更容易阅读时，情况正好相反，人们更容易被说服。

en: Thus, it's important to communicate clearly when talking about complex science subjects.
cn: 因此，在讨论复杂的科学主题时，清晰地沟通很重要。

en: This is especially true with issues related to public health, like the safety of new medications and the benefits of vaccines.
cn: 在与公共健康相关的问题上尤其如此，比如新药的安全性和疫苗的益处。

en: Shulman concedes that the use of jargon is appropriate with scientific audiences.
cn: 舒尔曼承认，使用术语适用于科学领域的读者。

en: But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language.
cn: 但是，想要与公众交流的科学家需要修改他们的语言。

en: They need to eliminate jargon.
cn: 他们需要消除术语。

en: At the beginning of the 20th century, on the Gulf Coast in the US State of Texas, there was a hill where gas leakage was so noticeable that schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire.
cn: 20世纪初，在美国得克萨斯州的海湾沿岸，有一座小山，那里的气体泄漏非常明显，男学生们有时会放火烧山。

en: Pattillo Higgins, a disreputable local businessman, became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill.
cn: 帕蒂罗·希金斯，当地一个声名狼藉的商人，确信这座充满天然气的小山下面有石油。

en: Oil wells weren't drilled back then; they were essentially dug.
cn: 当时的油井不是钻取的，基本上是挖出来的。

en: The sand under the hill defeated several attempts by Higgins' workers to make a proper hole.
cn: 山下的沙子挫败了希金斯的工人们几次挖出合适洞口的尝试。

en: Higgins had forecast oil at a thousand feet, a totally made- up figure.
cn: 希金斯曾预测石油在一千英尺深处，这是一个完全编造的数字。

en: Higgins subsequently hired a mining engineer, Captain Anthony Lucas.
cn: 希金斯随后聘请了一位采矿工程师，安东尼·卢卡斯上尉。

en: After encountering several setbacks, Captain Lucas decided to use a drill, and his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry.
cn: 在经历了几次挫折后，卢卡斯上尉决定使用钻机，他的创新创造了现代石油钻探行业。

en: In January 1901, at 1,020 feet, almost precisely the depth predicted by Higgins' wild guess, the well roared and suddenly ejected mud and six tons of drilling pipe out of the ground, terrifying those present.
cn: 1901年1月，在1020英尺深处，几乎恰好是希金斯胡乱猜测的深度，油井轰鸣，突然将泥浆和六吨钻杆喷出地面，吓坏了在场的人。

en: For the next nine days, until the well was capped, the well poured out more oil than all the wells in America combined.
cn: 在接下来的九天里，直到油井被封住，这口井喷出的石油比美国所有油井的总和还要多。

en: In those days, Texas was almost entirely rural with no large cities and practically no industry; cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy.
cn: 在那些日子里，得克萨斯州几乎完全是农村，没有大城市，几乎没有工业；棉花和牛肉是经济的基础。

en: Higgins' well changed that.
cn: 希金斯的油井改变了这一点。

en: The boom made some prospectors millionaires, but the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas.
cn: 繁荣使一些勘探者成为百万富翁，但石油的突然过剩并不完全是得克萨斯州的福音。

en: In the 1930s, prices crashed, to the point that, in some parts of the country, oil was cheaper than water.
cn: 20世纪30年代，油价暴跌，以至于在美国某些地区，石油比水还便宜。

en: That would become a familiar pattern of the boom- or- bust Texas economy.
cn: 这将成为得克萨斯州经济繁荣或萧条的常见模式。

en: Most people dislike their jobs.
cn: 大多数人不喜欢自己的工作。

en: It's an astonishing (but statistical) fact.
cn: 这是一个令人惊讶的（但统计上确凿的）事实。

en: A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers.
cn: 根据最新研究，导致员工不满的一个主要原因是，许多人认为自己有一个糟糕的经理。

en: Few describe their managers as malicious or manipulative, though, while those types certainly exist, they are minority.
cn: 很少有人把他们的经理描述为恶意或操控型的，尽管这类人确实存在，但他们是少数。

en: The majority of managers seemingly just don't know any better.
cn: 大多数经理似乎只是不知道更好的做法。

en: They're often emulating bad managers they've had in the past.
cn: 他们经常模仿他们过去遇到的糟糕经理。

en: It's likely they've never read a management book or attended a management course.
cn: 他们很可能从未读过管理类书籍或参加过管理课程。

en: They might not have even reflected on what good management looks like and how it would influence their own management style.
cn: 他们甚至可能没有反思过好的管理是什么样的，以及它如何影响自己的管理风格。

en: The researchers interviewed employees about their managers, beginning with a question about the worst manager they had ever had.
cn: 研究人员就经理问题采访了员工，从他们遇到的最差经理的问题开始。

en: From this, the researchers came up with four main causes of why some managers are perceived as being simply awful at their jobs.
cn: 由此，研究人员得出了为什么一些经理被认为工作表现糟糕的四个主要原因。

en: The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices.
cn: 第一个原因是公司文化，员工认为这种文化助长了糟糕的管理做法。

en: It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy.
cn: 尤其是有压力的工作环境、极少的培训和缺乏问责制被发现是最应受到谴责的。

en: Often a manager's superiors can effectively encourage a manager's distasteful behavior when they fail to discipline the person's wrongdoings.
cn: 通常，当经理的上司未能惩戒其错误行为时，实际上是在鼓励该经理令人反感的行为。

en: Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.
cn: 这样的工作场所有时被描述为有毒的。

en: The second cause was attributed to the managers' characteristics.
cn: 第二个原因归因于经理的性格特点。

en: Those deemed to be most destructive were odd people, those without drive, those who allow personal problems into the workplace and those with an unpleasant temperament or personality in general.
cn: 那些被认为最具破坏性的是古怪的人、没有干劲的人、把个人问题带入工作场所的人以及总体上性格或个性令人不快的人。

en: The third cause of poor management was associated with a deficiency of qualifications.
cn: 管理不善的第三个原因与资历不足有关。

en: Not so much the formal variety one obtains from a university but the informal variety that comes from credible work experience and professional accomplishments.
cn: 与其说是在大学获得的正规资历，不如说是来自可靠的工作经验和专业成就的非正规资历。

en: The fourth cause concerned managers who've been promoted for reasons other than potential.
cn: 第四个原因涉及那些因潜力以外的原因而被提拔的经理。

en: One reason in particular why these people had been promoted was that they had been around the longest.
cn: 这些人被提拔的一个特别原因是他们在公司待得最久。

en: It wasn't their skillset or other merits that got them the job.
cn: 不是他们的技能或其他优点让他们得到了这份工作。

en: It was their tenure.
cn: 而是他们的任期。

en: A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees.
cn: 值得指出的一点是，这项研究只是基于员工的视角。

en: The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers.
cn: 研究人员没有询问高层领导对一线经理的看法。

en: It's quite possible they're content with how the individuals they promoted are now performing, merrily ignorant of the damage they're actually causing, which might explain why, as the researchers conclude, those same middle managers are usually unaware that they are a bad manager.
cn: 他们很可能对他们提拔的人现在的表现感到满意，愉快地忽视了他们实际上造成的损害，这或许可以解释为什么，正如研究人员总结的那样，那些中层经理通常没有意识到自己是个糟糕的经理。

en: With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.
cn: 随着无人驾驶车辆的使用似乎不可避免，澳大利亚广袤的沙漠州西澳大利亚州的矿业公司无疑走在了前列。

en: Iron ore is a key ingredient in steel making.
cn: 铁矿石是炼钢的关键原料。

en: The mining companies here produce almost 300 million tons of iron ore a year.
cn: 这里的矿业公司每年生产近3亿吨铁矿石。

en: The 240 giant autonomous trucks in use, in the Western Australian mines, can weigh 400 tonnes fully loaded, and travel at speeds of up to 60 kilometers per hour.
cn: 西澳大利亚州矿山中使用的240辆巨型自动驾驶卡车，满载时可重达400吨，行驶速度可达每小时60公里。

en: They are a technological leap, transporting iron ore along routes which run for hundreds of kilometers from mines to their destinations.
cn: 它们是一个技术飞跃，沿着从矿山到目的地长达数百公里的路线运输铁矿石。

en: Here, when the truck arrives at its destination, staff in the operation center direct it precisely where to unload.
cn: 在这里，当卡车到达目的地时，操作中心的工作人员会精确地指示它在何处卸货。

en: Vast quantities of iron ore are then transported by autonomous trains to ocean ports.
cn: 大量铁矿石随后由自动驾驶列车运往海港。

en: Advocates argue these automated vehicles will change mining forever.
cn: 支持者认为，这些自动化车辆将永远改变采矿业。

en: It may only be five years before the use of automation technology leads to a fully robotic mine.
cn: 自动化技术的应用可能只需要五年时间就能实现全机器人采矿。

en: A range of factors has pushed Western Australia's desert region to the lead of this automation revolution.
cn: 一系列因素已将西澳大利亚沙漠地区推向自动化革命的前沿。

en: These include the huge size of the mines, the scale of equipment, and the repetitive nature of some of the work.
cn: 这些因素包括矿山的巨大规模、设备的规模以及某些工作的重复性。

en: Then there's the area's remoteness—at 502,000 square kilometers—it can sometimes make recruiting staff a challenge.
cn: 还有就是该地区的偏远——面积达50.2万平方公里——有时会让招聘员工成为一项挑战。

en: Another consideration is the risks when humans interact with large machinery.
cn: 另一个考虑因素是人与大型机械互动时的风险。

en: There are also the financial imperatives.
cn: 还有财务方面的迫切需求。

en: The ongoing push by the mining corporations to be more productive and more efficient is another powerful driver in embracing automation technology.
cn: 矿业公司为提高生产力和效率而不断推进的努力，是拥抱自动化技术的另一个强大动力。

en: The digitization and automation of the industry has created demand for different kinds of workers.
cn: 该行业的数字化和自动化创造了对不同类型工人的需求。

en: Workers have to learn new skills and use specialized software programs to perform their jobs.
cn: 工人们必须学习新技能并使用专门的软件程序来完成工作。

en: The unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology, but they have reservations about the rise of automation technology.
cn: 工会已经接受了新技术引入的必然性，但它们对自动化技术的兴起仍持保留态度。

en: Their primary concern is the potential impact on remote communities.
cn: 他们主要担心的是对偏远社区的潜在影响。

en: According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road- death rate is almost double the global average.
cn: 据官方统计，泰国每年的交通事故死亡率几乎是全球平均水平的两倍。

en: Thai people know that their roads are dangerous, but they don't know this could easily be changed.
cn: 泰国人知道他们的道路很危险，但他们不知道这很容易改变。

en: Globally, road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease.
cn: 在全球范围内，每年交通事故造成的死亡人数比任何一种传染病都多。

en: Researchers at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in America, put the death toll in 2017 at 1.24 million.
cn: 美国健康指标与评估研究所的研究人员将2017年的死亡人数定为124万。

en: According to the institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century.
cn: 据该研究所称，自世纪之交以来，死亡总人数或多或少保持不变。

en: But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries.
cn: 但这掩盖了各个国家的许多变化。

en: In many poor countries, road accidents are killing more people than ever before.
cn: 在许多贫穷国家，交通事故造成的死亡人数比以往任何时候都多。

en: Those countries have swelling young populations of fast- growing fleet of cars and motorbikes and a limited supply of surgeons.
cn: 这些国家拥有不断增长的年轻人口，汽车和摩托车数量快速增长，但外科医生供应有限。

en: It is impossible to know for sure, because official statistics are so inadequate.
cn: 无法确切知道，因为官方统计数据非常不充分。

en: But deaths are thought to have risen by 40% since 1990 in many low income countries.
cn: 但据认为，自1990年以来，许多低收入国家的死亡人数已经上升了40%。

en: In many rich- countries, by contrast, roads are becoming even safer.
cn: 相比之下，在许多富裕国家，道路正变得更加安全。

en: In Estonia and Ireland, for example, the number of death has fallen by about two thirds since the late 1990s.
cn: 例如，在爱沙尼亚和爱尔兰，自20世纪90年代末以来，死亡人数已经下降了约三分之二。

en: But the most important and intriguing changes are taking place in middle income countries, which contain most of the world's people and have some of the most dangerous roads.
cn: 但最重要和最有趣的变化正在中等收入国家发生，这些国家的人口占世界人口的大多数，道路也最危险。

en: According to researchers, in China and South Africa traffic deaths have been falling since 2000, and in India since 2012, and the Philippines reached its peak four years ago.
cn: 据研究人员称，中国和南非的交通事故死亡人数自2000年以来一直在下降，印度自2012年以来也在下降，菲律宾在四年前达到峰值。

en: The question is whether Thailand can soon follow suit.
cn: 问题是泰国能否很快效仿。

en: Rob McKinney, head of the International Road Assessment Program, says that all countries tend to go through three phases.
cn: 国际道路评估项目负责人罗布·麦金尼表示，所有国家都倾向于经历三个阶段。

en: They begin with poor, slow roads.
cn: 它们从糟糕、缓慢的道路开始。

en: In the second phase, as they grow wealthier, they pave the roads, allowing traffic to move faster and pushing up the death rate.
cn: 在第二阶段，随着国家变得更加富裕，他们铺设道路，使交通速度加快，推高了死亡率。

en: Lastly, in the third phase, countries act to make their roads safer.
cn: 最后，在第三阶段，国家采取措施使道路更加安全。

en: The trick, then, is to reach the third stage sooner by focusing earlier and more closely on fatal accidents.
cn: 因此，诀窍是通过更早、更密切地关注致命事故，更快地达到第三阶段。

en: How to do that?
cn: 如何做到这一点？

en: The solution lies not just in better infrastructure, but in better social incentives.
cn: 解决之道不仅在于改善基础设施，还在于改善社会激励机制。

en: Safe driving habits are practices which people know they should follow but often don't.
cn: 安全驾驶习惯是人们知道应该遵循但往往没有遵循的做法。

en: Dangerous driving is not a fixed cultural trait as some imagine.
cn: 危险驾驶并非像某些人想象的那样是一种固定的文化特征。

en: People respond to incentives such as traffic laws that are actually enforced.
cn: 人们会对实际执行的交通法规等激励措施做出反应。
