en: How are you enjoying your new job?
cn: 你的新工作怎么样？

en: So far, so good.
cn: 到目前为止，还不错。

en: I don't miss having managers who deliver blunt, harsh feedback in the name of efficiency.
cn: 我一点儿也不怀念那些以效率为名给出直接、严厉反馈的经理。

en: From the way you described your last company, no wonder they had a problem with high staff turnover.
cn: 从你描述上一家公司的方式来看，难怪他们有很高的员工流失率。

en: Yeah.
cn: 是啊。

en: I couldn't wait to get out of there once my contract expired.
cn: 我的合同一到期，我就迫不及待地离开了那里。

en: The problem with a company culture that prizes directness above all else is that it creates a toxic culture of brilliant jerks that drives people out and erodes itself from within.
cn: 把直接置于一切之上的公司文化的问题在于，它创造了一种有毒的、满是聪明混蛋的文化，把员工逼走，从内部侵蚀自身。

en: My company's managers tend to be accommodating and kind, overlooking mistakes or issues so as not to hurt feelings.
cn: 我公司的经理们往往很随和、友善，为了不伤害感情而忽视错误或问题。

en: Issues often get ignored there until they build up and reach a crisis point.
cn: 问题在那里经常被忽视，直到它们累积到危机点。

en: That's not surprising.
cn: 那并不奇怪。

en: My new company seems to employ a feedback policy that combines compassion and directness.
cn: 我的新公司似乎采用了一种将同情和直接相结合的反馈政策。

en: Employees have the power to speak up, give feedback, disagree and discuss problems in real time.
cn: 员工有权发表意见、提供反馈、表达不同意见并实时讨论问题。

en: It seems to help us to course correct, improve and meet challenges while also building teams that collaborate and care for one another.
cn: 这似乎有助于我们纠正方向、改进并迎接挑战，同时建立相互合作和关爱的团队。

en: But that would be based on an atmosphere of mutual trust, wouldn't it?
cn: 但那要以相互信任的氛围为基础，不是吗？

en: Otherwise, people might interpret feedback as some kind of personal attack.
cn: 否则，人们可能会把反馈解读为某种人身攻击。

en: True.
cn: 没错。

en: Without an atmosphere of trust, feedback can create stress and self- doubt.
cn: 没有信任的氛围，反馈会产生压力和自我怀疑。

en: But I think when we get feedback from someone we trust, we understand that the feedback isn't some kind of personal attack.
cn: 但我认为，当我们从信任的人那里得到反馈时，我们明白反馈不是某种人身攻击。

en: It's actually a kind of support because it's offered in the spirit of helping us improve.
cn: 这实际上是一种支持，因为它是本着帮助我们改进的精神提供的。

en: I think sometimes people need to shift their mindsets around how they receive feedback.
cn: 我认为有时人们需要改变他们接受反馈的心态。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow.
cn: 毕竟，建设性反馈是我们学习和成长的方式。

en: It's the basis for healthy parenting, lasting friendships, career development, and so much more.
cn: 它是健康育儿、持久友谊、职业发展等许多事情的基础。

en: If we shelter our children, friends and colleagues from information that might enrich and enhance their lives, we are not being caring.
cn: 如果我们保护孩子、朋友和同事，不让他们接触可能丰富和改善他们生活的信息，我们并不是在关心他们。

en: We're actually doing harm to them.
cn: 我们实际上是在伤害他们。

en: That's exactly right.
cn: 完全正确。

en: How was your holiday?
cn: 你的假期过得怎么样？

en: Not too many other tourists around, were there?
cn: 周围其他游客不多吧？

en: No, very few, relatively.
cn: 不，相对很少。

en: But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place.
cn: 但我发现自己从一个住处搬到另一个住处，试图找到完美的地方。

en: It made me realize that indecision is a big problem for me.
cn: 这让我意识到优柔寡断对我来说是个大问题。

en: Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot.
cn: 我没有放松，而是在寻找最好的地方。

en: It seems you suffer from 'Fear of Better Options.'
cn: 看来你得了‘害怕错过更好选择’症。

en: I've read about it.
cn: 我读过相关文章。

en: It describes this loop of indecision as part of our programming.
cn: 它把这种优柔寡断的循环描述为我们程序的一部分。

en: Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision- making process.
cn: 本质上，我们倾向于不断延长决策过程。

en: Because as human beings, we are hard- wired to optimize.
cn: 因为作为人类，我们天生就追求最优。

en: We have always looked to get the best things we can as a sort of survival of the fittest.
cn: 我们一直在寻求得到最好的东西，这是一种适者生存。

en: Optimizing isn't the problem, but rather the process that we go through.
cn: 追求最优不是问题，而是我们所经历的过程。

en: Well, that makes me feel better.
cn: 嗯，这让我感觉好多了。

en: But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization.
cn: 但我认为，由于科技的发展，我们可以更容易地进行比较，有更多的选择和定制。

en: We can now see what we could have, how we might get it and what others have that we might want.
cn: 我们现在可以看到我们可能拥有什么，如何得到它，以及别人拥有什么我们可能想要的东西。

en: We keep looking over and return to the same options again and again.
cn: 我们不断地查看，一次又一次地回到相同的选项。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: Fear of better options offers little benefit.
cn: 害怕错过更好的选择没什么好处。

en: It's an ailment of abundance.
cn: 这是富足的弊病。

en: You must have choices to have that fear of missing out on better options.
cn: 你必须要有选择，才会有害怕错过更好选择的情况。

en: Yes, I need to note when I'm worrying about inconsequential things, I guess.
cn: 是的，我想我需要注意什么时候我在为不重要的事情担忧。

en: If I'm spending too much time worrying over what to have for lunch, I'm robbing myself of the energy to focus on the things that matter.
cn: 如果我花太多时间担心午餐吃什么，我就是在剥夺自己专注于重要事情的能量。

en: Exactly.
cn: 完全正确。

en: But for more important matters, I think gut instinct might be overrated.
cn: 但对于更重要的事情，我认为直觉可能被高估了。

en: When you have 30 odd options, trusting your gut is not practical.
cn: 当你有30多个选项时，相信你的直觉是不现实的。

en: What you need to do is research—have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can.
cn: 你需要做的是研究——有一个过程，投入时间探索你的选项，并尽可能多地排除。

en: The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again.
cn: 决策中最有害的部分是一遍又一遍地纠结在相同的选项上。

en: The role of homework in classrooms is not a new debate.
cn: 家庭作业在课堂中的作用并不是一个新争论。

en: Many parents and teachers are ardent supporters of homework.
cn: 许多家长和老师都是家庭作业的热心支持者。

en: But do all students benefit from homework?
cn: 但所有学生都能从家庭作业中受益吗？

en: A 2006 research paper suggested some correlation between the amount of homework done by a student and future academic achievement for middle and high school students—but not so much for younger kids.
cn: 一篇2006年的研究论文表明，初中生和高中生的家庭作业量与其未来的学业成就之间存在一定的相关性——但对年幼的孩子来说则不然。

en: A Stanford study in 2014 suggested the same was true for students in California's affluent communities.
cn: 2014年斯坦福大学的一项研究表明，加州富裕社区的学生情况也是如此。

en: The findings challenged the idea that homework was 'inherently good.'
cn: 这些发现挑战了家庭作业‘本身是好的’这一观点。

en: The researchers concluded that there was an upper limit to the correlation between homework and achievement, suggesting that high school students shouldn't be doing more than two hours of homework a night.
cn: 研究人员得出结论，家庭作业与学业成就之间的相关性存在上限，表明高中生每晚不应该做超过两个小时的作业。

en: And the most valuable kind of homework for elementary level children was simply assigned free reading.
cn: 而对于小学生来说，最有价值的家庭作业就是布置自由阅读。

en: The topic gets more complicated when we talk about the divide between rural and urban communities.
cn: 当我们谈论城乡社区之间的差异时，这个话题变得更加复杂。

en: Studies found that in remote areas the poor quality or lack of Internet access can put students at a disadvantage, because 70% of teachers in these areas assign homework that requires Internet access.
cn: 研究发现，在偏远地区，网络质量差或缺乏网络连接可能会让学生处于不利地位，因为这些地区70%的老师布置需要上网的作业。

en: But one in three households doesn't have Internet.
cn: 但三分之一的家庭没有网络。

en: Experts assert homework requiring the Internet isn't fair.
cn: 专家认为，需要网络才能完成的家庭作业是不公平的。

en: While the debate continues about the effect of homework on academic achievements, there are studies focusing on other benefits of homework.
cn: 虽然关于家庭作业对学业成绩影响的争论仍在继续，但也有研究关注家庭作业的其他好处。

en: A study in Germany found that homework could have an effect on students' personalities, suggesting that doing homework might help kids to become more conscientious and independent learners.
cn: 德国的一项研究发现，家庭作业可能会影响学生的个性，表明做作业可能有助于孩子成为更认真、更独立的学习者。

en: Robert Goddard, an American born in 1882, is widely regarded as the world's first rocket scientist.
cn: 罗伯特·戈达德，1882年出生的美国人，被广泛认为是世界上第一位火箭科学家。

en: At age 27, Goddard published his first book, in which he hypothesized that a rocket launched from Earth could reach the moon.
cn: 27岁时，戈达德出版了他的第一本书，在书中他假设从地球发射的火箭可以到达月球。

en: Like many visionaries, the young scientist encountered numerous skeptics.
cn: 像许多有远见的人一样，这位年轻的科学家遇到了许多怀疑论者。

en: In January 1920, the New York Times ridiculed Goddard's theory that rockets could be utilized for space exploration.
cn: 1920年1月，《纽约时报》嘲笑戈达德关于火箭可以用于太空探索的理论。

en: 49 years later, Apollo 11 reached the moon, and the famed newspaper published an apology to Goddard.
cn: 49年后，阿波罗11号登上了月球，这家著名报纸向戈达德发表了道歉声明。

en: Goddard launched his first rocket from an aunt's farm in his native Massachusetts in March 1926.
cn: 1926年3月，戈达德在他家乡马萨诸塞州一个姑姑的农场上发射了他的第一枚火箭。

en: His maiden rocket voyage lasted a mere three seconds.
cn: 他的首次火箭飞行只持续了三秒钟。

en: It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters.
cn: 它只飞到了12米的高度。

en: Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science.
cn: 尽管如此，这仍然是火箭科学中的一个里程碑。

en: Goddard later consulted with a weather expert and determined that the climate of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches.
cn: 戈达德后来咨询了一位气象专家，确定新墨西哥州的气候全年都适合发射火箭。

en: In 1930, Goddard and his family relocated there to a remote valley in the southwest of the country.
cn: 1930年，戈达德和他的家人搬到了那里，在美国西南部一个偏远的山谷。

en: There he established a laboratory and test range.
cn: 在那里他建立了一个实验室和试验场。

en: However, the ambitious scientist received negligible support from the government.
cn: 然而，这位雄心勃勃的科学家从政府那里得到的支持微乎其微。

en: For four years, wealthy businessman Daniel Guggenheim provided Goddard with an annual $25,000 grant to pursue his dreams.
cn: 四年间，富商丹尼尔·古根海姆每年向戈达德提供25000美元的资助，以追求他的梦想。

en: Other rocket enthusiasts also raised funds for him.
cn: 其他火箭爱好者也为他筹集资金。

en: Over time, Goddard's rockets grew more sophisticated and included the installation of instruments.
cn: 随着时间的推移，戈达德的火箭变得越来越精密，并安装了仪器。

en: In spite of his many successes, Goddard was never able to interest the US military in rocket - propelled weapons.
cn: 尽管取得了许多成功，戈达德始终未能引起美国军方对火箭推进武器的兴趣。

en: He was granted over 200 patents and continued to pioneer rocket technology until his death in 1945.
cn: 他获得了200多项专利，并继续开拓火箭技术，直到1945年去世。

en: Working for a new venture comes with a lot of risks—that is, instability, unclear responsibilities and the need to be a master of all trades.
cn: 在一家新企业工作伴随着很多风险——比如不稳定、责任不清以及需要成为多面手。

en: But the primary benefit is usually the passion and excitement associated with playing a role in a promising new company.
cn: 但主要的好处通常是在一家有前途的新公司中发挥作用所带来的热情和兴奋。

en: The person to thank for that passion and excitement is almost always the entrepreneur.
cn: 这种热情和兴奋几乎总是要归功于企业家。

en: There's something about the founder's energy and enthusiasm that infects the rest of the team.
cn: 创始人的精力和热情会感染团队的其他成员。

en: The willingness to take risks may inspire others to be more courageous.
cn: 承担风险的意愿可能会激励他人更加勇敢。

en: The optimism and positivity may motivate people to focus less on trivial and unimportant matters.
cn: 乐观和积极的态度可能会促使人们减少对琐碎不重要事情的关注。

en: The celebration of milestones may prompt staff to be more grateful about their own accomplishments and privileges.
cn: 对里程碑的庆祝可能会促使员工对自己的成就和特权更加感恩。

en: What becomes set in the firm's culture is a contagious collection of affirmative and positive emotions which are usually shared among the team.
cn: 公司文化中固定下来的是一套有感染力的、肯定和积极的情绪，通常在团队中共享。

en: Science has already done a good job of proving the results that follow.
cn: 科学已经很好地证明了随之而来的结果。

en: These include better processes, greater team cohesion, reduced conflict and sharper alertness.
cn: 这些包括更好的流程、更强的团队凝聚力、更少的冲突和更敏锐的警觉性。

en: But what is yet to be demonstrated is whether the founder's passion leads to increased team performance.
cn: 但尚未得到证明的是，创始人的热情是否能提高团队绩效。

en: This was recently tested in research, which analyzed the teams of 73 new companies across a range of industries such as IT, medicine and energy.
cn: 这一点最近在研究中得到了测试，该研究分析了IT、医药和能源等多个行业的73家新公司的团队。

en: The CEOs were consulted once again, years after the initial analysis, and most shared their firm's performance reports, so that their success could be more objectively measured.
cn: 在最初分析数年后，这些首席执行官再次接受了咨询，大多数人分享了他们公司的业绩报告，以便更客观地衡量他们的成功。

en: Entrepreneurial teams generally progress through three phases.
cn: 创业团队通常会经历三个阶段。

en: The first is inventing a product or service, the second is founding the venture to sell that product or service, and the third is developing the firm so it continues to grow.
cn: 第一阶段是发明一种产品或服务，第二阶段是创建企业来销售该产品或服务，第三阶段是发展公司使其持续增长。

en: The researchers discovered that when the team is passionate about the third phase—developing a firm—there's a clear link to performance.
cn: 研究人员发现，当团队对第三阶段——发展公司——充满热情时，这与绩效有明显的联系。

en: But the first phase—a passion for invention—is not a reliable indicator that the firm will still be open for business a few years later.
cn: 但第一阶段——对发明的热情——并不能可靠地表明几年后这家公司仍在营业。

en: Likewise, the second—a passion for founding the venture—doesn't necessarily translate into great success.
cn: 同样，第二阶段——对创建企业的热情——也不一定能转化为巨大的成功。

en: The solution to great team performance stems from a willingness to recruit others who could direct their passion towards the third phase of entrepreneurialism; developing the business.
cn: 优秀团队绩效的解决方案源于愿意招募那些能将热情引导到创业第三阶段——发展业务——的人。

en: Employing more staff can, in itself, be a risk for an entrepreneur, as is paying them big dollars to attract them.
cn: 雇用更多员工本身对企业家来说可能是一种风险，支付高薪吸引他们也是如此。

en: On many occasions, the entrepreneurs reported not paying themselves a wage at all initially in order to cover salaries and expenses.
cn: 在很多情况下，企业家报告说，为了支付工资和开销，他们一开始根本不给自己发工资。

en: Ageing is a curious thing, and people's desire to beat it and death has become an industry worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
cn: 衰老是一件奇怪的事情，人们战胜衰老和死亡的渴望已经成为一个价值数千亿美元的产业。

en: Despite the huge investment into research, ageing remains somewhat obscure, although there are certain things researchers do understand.
cn: 尽管在研究上投入了巨资，衰老仍然有些神秘，尽管研究人员确实了解某些事情。

en: They know that women tend to have longer life spans, living on average six years longer than men.
cn: 他们知道女性往往寿命更长，平均比男性多活六年。

en: No one is really certain of the reason for this, although the speculation centers around the idea that women are more capable of surviving or handling disease than men.
cn: 没有人确切知道原因，尽管猜测集中在女性比男性更有能力生存或应对疾病这一观点上。

en: For virtually every disease, the effects are greater on men than they are on women.
cn: 实际上，对于每一种疾病，对男性的影响都比对女性大。

en: Some suggest that women's immune systems benefit from their tendency to prioritize and nurture social connections.
cn: 有些人认为，女性的免疫系统受益于她们优先考虑和培养社会关系的倾向。

en: But for me, this explanation is hardly convincing.
cn: 但对我来说，这种解释很难令人信服。

en: Researchers also know to an extent what causes ageing.
cn: 研究人员在一定程度上也知道是什么导致了衰老。

en: For 60 years, it was believed that cells would continue to divide forever.
cn: 60年来，人们一直认为细胞会永远分裂下去。

en: It was only uncovered in relatively recent times that older people's cells divide a smaller number of times than younger people's.
cn: 直到相对较近的时期才发现，老年人的细胞分裂次数比年轻人少。

en: Only cancer cells, in fact, are capable of dividing forever.
cn: 事实上，只有癌细胞能够永远分裂。

en: Human cells have a limited reproductive ability.
cn: 人类细胞的繁殖能力有限。

en: To an extent, we can postpone the eventual stop of cells' dividing through nutrition, exercise, good sleep and even relaxation techniques, but we cannot stop the ageing process.
cn: 在一定程度上，我们可以通过营养、锻炼、良好的睡眠甚至放松技巧来推迟细胞分裂的最终停止，但我们无法阻止衰老的过程。

en: And researchers are yet to answer the ultimate question of ageing: why does the body ultimately fall to pieces?
cn: 研究人员尚未回答衰老的终极问题：为什么身体最终会崩溃？

en: In the opinion of some of the world's best scientific minds on the subject, part of the reason we don't yet have any answer is because many researchers are looking in the wrong direction.
cn: 在这个问题上，世界上一些最优秀的科学头脑认为，我们还没有答案的部分原因是许多研究人员在错误的方向上寻找。

en: Many public health policymakers believe that by finding a cure for age- related diseases, they will be able to get to the heart of ageing and unlock its mystery.
cn: 许多公共卫生政策制定者认为，通过找到与年龄相关的疾病的治疗方法，他们将能够触及衰老的核心并解开它的奥秘。

en: But some gerontologists warn that trying to treat individual diseases is like trying to treat the individual symptoms of a dying man.
cn: 但一些老年学家警告说，试图治疗个别疾病就像试图治疗一个垂死之人的个别症状。

en: They believe the body is a system of multiple causes and effects, and they hold that by the time we reach old age, the body's entire system has changed so much that it's wrong to look at age- related problems in isolation.
cn: 他们认为身体是一个多因果的系统，并且他们认为到了老年，身体的整个系统已经发生了很大的变化，孤立地看待与年龄相关的问题是错误的。

en: Perhaps, more attention should be paid to the central mechanism of ageing itself.
cn: 也许，应该更多地关注衰老本身的核心机制。

en: Good afternoon.
cn: 下午好。

en: In today's talk, we'll discuss how managers can get their staff to do what they are asked.
cn: 在今天的讲座中，我们将讨论经理如何让员工按照要求去做事。

en: Much to their frustration, managers often struggle to get their staff to comply with even simple instructions.
cn: 令他们非常沮丧的是，经理们往往连简单的指令都很难让员工服从。

en: Often, they blame their employees: 'They don't read emails, they don't listen, they don't care'—that kind of thing.
cn: 他们常常责怪员工：‘他们不看邮件，他们不听，他们不在乎’——诸如此类。

en: But according to recent research conducted in Australia, it looks like it's not the employees' fault, but the managers'.
cn: 但根据最近在澳大利亚进行的研究，看起来这不是员工的错，而是经理的错。

en: It's easy to understand why people sometimes disobey procedures intentionally.
cn: 人们有时故意不遵守程序，原因很容易理解。

en: Occasionally, it's because they're pressured to finish in a short time.
cn: 有时，是因为他们被迫在短时间内完成。

en: At other times, they may disagree with the spirit of the procedure—the effort demanded, the time consumed, the lack of potential effectiveness.
cn: 在其他时候，他们可能不同意程序的精神——所要求的努力、所消耗的时间、缺乏潜在的效力。

en: And every now and then, they just don't want to, maybe deliberately or out of stubbornness.
cn: 偶尔，他们就是不想做，也许是故意的，或者是出于固执。

en: So apart from that, what else gets in the way of procedural compliance?
cn: 那么除此之外，还有什么阻碍了程序合规呢？

en: The research scholars surveyed 152 blue- collar workers from two separate sites in the mining industry.
cn: 研究学者调查了采矿业两个不同地点的152名蓝领工人。

en: They asked the workers a range of procedure- related questions, such as whether they found the procedures useful, how confident they felt in their job, how comfortable they were to speak up in the workplace, and how closely they followed any new procedures set by their managers.
cn: 他们向工人询问了一系列与程序相关的问题，比如他们是否觉得程序有用，他们对工作有多自信，他们在工作场所发言有多自在，以及他们有多严格遵守经理制定的任何新程序。

en: They were also asked to rate the extent to which they perceived their supervisors to be helpful.
cn: 他们还被要求评价他们认为主管有帮助的程度。

en: That last statement was the most instructive because, as the researchers found, there was a remarkably strong correlation between how helpful supervisors were perceived to be and how likely their employees were to follow their directors.
cn: 最后一项最具启发性，因为研究人员发现，主管被认为有帮助的程度与员工服从指示的可能性之间存在非常强的相关性。

en: Supervisors' helping behavior was found to be motivational in nature.
cn: 主管的帮助行为本质上是激励性的。

en: It increased employees' perception of the likelihood of success in the attainment of job goals, and therefore fostered a willingness to dedicate their effort and ability to their work.
cn: 它增加了员工对实现工作目标成功可能性的认知，从而培养了他们将努力和能力投入到工作中的意愿。

en: In short, managers should be ongoing role models for the change.
cn: 简而言之，经理应该一直是变革的榜样。

en: As the saying goes: Do as I do, not as I say.
cn: 俗话说：照我做的做，而不是照我说的做。

en: To affect behavioral change, what's most required is interaction and involvement—the human touch—and, naturally, processes that add value.
cn: 要影响行为改变，最需要的是互动和参与——人情味——以及自然能增加价值的过程。

en: Although procedures are designed to guide and support employees' work, employees, it seems, can't always be expected to comply with procedures that are not seen as useful.
cn: 虽然程序旨在指导和支持员工的工作，但似乎不能总是期望员工遵守那些不被视为有用的程序。

en: And of course, managers shouldn't keep resending emails.
cn: 当然，经理们也不应该不停地重新发送邮件。

en: They are an effective tool for the sharing of data reports, but they are a hopeless tool if what a manager's desiring is a change in behavior.
cn: 它们是共享数据报告的有效工具，但如果经理想要的是行为的改变，那它们就是一个无望的工具。

en: Hi, David.
cn: 嗨，大卫。

en: I haven't seen you in class for almost two weeks.
cn: 我差不多两个星期没在课堂上见到你了。

en: We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.
cn: 我们还以为你提前去度假了或是别的什么。

en: Hi, Sarah.
cn: 嗨，莎拉。

en: Well, it's a bit of a long story I'm afraid.
cn: 唉，恐怕说来话长。

en: I got a throat infection last week and had to go to the hospital to get some antibiotics as I really wasn't getting any better.
cn: 我上周喉咙感染了，不得不去医院拿些抗生素，因为我真的没有好转。

en: Oh yeah.
cn: 哦，是啊。

en: There have been so many viruses going around this winter.
cn: 这个冬天有太多病毒在传播了。

en: The weather has been so awful for the last few weeks.
cn: 过去几周的天气一直很糟糕。

en: And, on the way back from the hospital, I slipped on some ice and fell and then had to go to the hospital to get an X- ray because I basically thought I broke my wrist, although, thankfully, it's not broken.
cn: 而且，从医院回来的路上，我在冰上滑倒了，然后不得不去医院拍X光片，因为我以为我摔断了手腕，不过谢天谢地，并没有断。

en: But I need to be careful with it for the next few weeks.
cn: 但接下来的几周我需要小心一点。

en: Oh, that's too bad!
cn: 哦，那太糟糕了！

en: How unfortunate!
cn: 真不幸！

en: To make things worse, I managed to fall right in front of four girls from the ninth grade.
cn: 更糟的是，我正好摔在四个九年级女生的面前。

en: So I was utterly humiliated.
cn: 所以我丢尽了脸。

en: Plus, the laptop in my bag was broken too.
cn: 另外，我包里的笔记本电脑也摔坏了。

en: No, what a complete catastrophe!
cn: 不会吧，真是彻底的灾难！

en: Is the laptop still under warranty?
cn: 笔记本电脑还在保修期内吗？

en: If it is, then you can easily send it back to the manufacturer, and they'll send you a brand- new one for free surely.
cn: 如果在的话，你可以把它寄回给制造商，他们肯定会免费给你寄一台全新的。

en: The warranty ran out three days before I broke it.
cn: 保修期在我摔坏它的前三天就到期了。

en: And all my essays are in there, and I need to hand them in before we break for the Christmas holidays.
cn: 我所有的论文都在里面，我需要在圣诞假期前交上去。

en: Listen, I have the number of a really good, affordable computer repair shop at home.
cn: 听着，我家里有一家非常好而且收费合理的电脑维修店的电话。

en: My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles.
cn: 我爸爸以前找过他，他能创造奇迹。

en: Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop, and you can have some tea and cookies too.
cn: 我们回我家吧，我们可以给维修店打电话，你也可以喝点茶，吃点曲奇。

en: Wow, thanks, Sara!
cn: 哇，谢谢，莎拉！

en: That would be great!
cn: 那太好了！

en: Let me just call my mom and let her know I'll be home a little bit later.
cn: 让我给我妈打个电话，告诉她我会晚一点回家。

en: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk.
cn: 欢迎来到本周的《书话》节目。

en: With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.
cn: 今天和我在一起的是海蒂·布朗，一位历史学家，她写了五本广受好评的军事史著作。

en: Thanks for having me, John.
cn: 谢谢你邀请我，约翰。

en: I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month.
cn: 我很兴奋能谈论我的新书，上个月出版的。

en: So this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre.
cn: 所以这本书是一部小说，是你第一次尝试这种体裁。

en: I thought it was a bit of a departure for you.
cn: 我觉得这对你来说有点改变。

en: I'd say it's a major departure as it's not just a work of fiction.
cn: 我会说这是一个重大的改变，因为它不仅仅是一部虚构作品。

en: It's set 200 years in the future.
cn: 它设定在200年后的未来。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: So how did that happen?
cn: 那是怎么发生的？

en: You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries.
cn: 你花了三十年写关于过去的事，专注于18和19世纪。

en: And now you're speculating about the future.
cn: 现在你在推测未来。

en: Well, after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.
cn: 嗯，经过多年研究士兵并记录他们在战争中的生活后，我开始好奇他们生活的其他方面，尤其是他们的个人生活。

en: I can see that.
cn: 我能看出来。

en: Your novel is about soldiers and it focuses on their relationships, especially the bond between sons and mothers and men and their wives.
cn: 你的小说是关于士兵的，聚焦于他们的关系，尤其是儿子与母亲之间以及男人与妻子之间的纽带。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history.
cn: 这个焦点是在我还打算写另一本历史书时出现的。

en: I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.
cn: 我从研究士兵真实的私人生活开始，研究他们寄回家的信。

en: So how did that history book become a novel?
cn: 那么那本历史书是怎么变成小说的？

en: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete.
cn: 嗯，我意识到历史记录是不完整的。

en: So I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.
cn: 所以我要么留下很多空白，要么做出比历史学家应该做的多得多的假设。

en: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel?
cn: 但为什么要在你的资历非常适合写历史小说的时候，写一部以未来为背景的小说呢？

en: As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.
cn: 作为历史学家，你写的任何历史小说都会有很高的可信度。

en: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.
cn: 和过去打交道让我感觉太受约束了，就好像我写的东西必须是事实而不是虚构，但写未来给了我更多想象和创造的自由。

en: Well, having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction.
cn: 嗯，读了你的书后，我很高兴你做出了转向虚构小说的选择。

en: Whether it's in the hands of animated polar bears or Santa Claus, there's one thing you'll find in nearly all ads for Coca-Cola: the characteristic glass bottle.
cn: 无论是在动画北极熊的手中还是在圣诞老人的手中，几乎所有的可口可乐广告中你都会发现一样东西：标志性的玻璃瓶。

en: Most Americans don't drink soda out of the glass bottles seen in Coke's ads anymore.
cn: 大多数美国人不再用可口可乐广告中看到的玻璃瓶喝汽水了。

en: But this week, the company is celebrating a century of the bottle that's been sold in more than 200 countries.
cn: 但本周，该公司正在庆祝这款已在200多个国家销售的瓶子的百年纪念。

en: Flash back to 1915, when a bottle of Coca- Cola cost just a nickel.
cn: 回到1915年，当时一瓶可口可乐只卖五分钱。

en: As the soft drink gained in popularity, it faced a growing number of competitors—counterfeits even trying to copy Coke's logo.
cn: 随着这款软饮料越来越受欢迎，它面临越来越多的竞争对手——仿冒品甚至试图复制可口可乐的商标。

en: So, according to Coca- Cola historian Ted Ryan, the company decided to come up with packaging that couldn't be duplicated.
cn: 所以，根据可口可乐历史学家泰德·瑞安的说法，公司决定发明一种无法复制的包装。

en: A product request was sent to eight different glass makers.
cn: 一份产品需求被发送给了八家不同的玻璃制造商。

en: Workers at the Root Glass Company got the request and began flipping through the encyclopedia at the local library, landing on cocoa seed.
cn: 鲁特玻璃公司的员工接到了这个请求，开始在当地图书馆翻阅百科全书，最后找到了可可种子。

en: Though cocoa seed is not an ingredient of the soda, they designed their bottle based on the seed's shape and large middle.
cn: 虽然可可种子不是这种汽水的原料，但他们根据种子的形状和中间较大部分设计了瓶子。

en: It won over Coke executives in Atlanta and would go on to receive its own trademark, spur collections and earn Coca- Cola an iconic image that made it part of American culture for a century.
cn: 它赢得了亚特兰大可口可乐高管的青睐，后来获得了自己的商标，激发了收藏热潮，为可口可乐赢得了一个标志性的形象，使其成为美国文化的一部分长达一个世纪。

en: It was 100 years ago this week that the bottle earned a patent.
cn: 就在一百年前的这周，这个瓶子获得了专利。

en: By World War II, Coke bottle sales had ballooned into billions.
cn: 到二战时，可口可乐瓶的销量已激增至数十亿。

en: Americans mostly consume Coke out of aluminum or plastic today, but the glass bottle remains a symbol of America that's readily recognized around the world.
cn: 如今美国人主要用铝罐或塑料瓶喝可乐，但玻璃瓶仍然是美国的一个标志，在世界各地都很容易被认出来。

en: Research shows that a few moments of conversation with a stranger creates a measurable improvement in mood.
cn: 研究表明，和陌生人聊上片刻可以明显改善情绪。

en: But most of us are reluctant to start these conversations because we presume the opposite.
cn: 但我们大多数人不愿开始这些对话，因为我们推测情况恰恰相反。

en: In an experiment, commuters who talked to nearby strangers found their commute more enjoyable than those who didn't.
cn: 在一项实验中，与附近陌生人交谈的通勤者发现他们的通勤比那些没有交谈的人更愉快。

en: They were asked to predict whether they'd enjoy the commute more if they conversed with other people.
cn: 他们被要求预测如果与他人交谈，他们是否会更喜欢通勤。

en: Intriguingly, most expected the more solitary experience to be more pleasurable.
cn: 有趣的是，大多数人预计独处的体验会更愉快。

en: Why is this?
cn: 这是为什么？

en: Social anxiety appears to be the problem.
cn: 社交焦虑似乎是问题所在。

en: People's reluctance to start conversations with nearby strangers comes partly from 'underestimating others' interest in connecting'.
cn: 人们不愿与附近陌生人交谈，部分原因是'低估了他人建立联系的兴趣'。

en: The sad thing is that people presume that a nearby stranger doesn't want to converse and don't start a conversation.
cn: 可悲的是，人们认为附近的陌生人不想交谈，所以不开始对话。

en: Only those who forced themselves to chat because it was required by the experiment found out what a pleasant experience it could be.
cn: 只有那些因为实验要求而强迫自己聊天的人才发现那是一种多么愉快的体验。

en: Human beings are social animals.
cn: 人类是社交动物。

en: Those who misunderstand the impact of social interactions may not, in some contexts, be social enough for their own well- being.
cn: 那些误解社交互动影响的人，在某些情况下，可能不够社交，不利于自己的幸福。

en: You should be chatting with the strangers you encounter.
cn: 你应该和你遇到的陌生人聊天。

en: You may occasionally have a negative encounter that might stick in your memory.
cn: 你可能偶尔会有一次不愉快的邂逅，可能会留在你的记忆中。

en: This is because the human brain is biased to dwell on negative events.
cn: 这是因为人类的大脑偏向于思考负面事件。

en: But starting conversations with strangers is still well worth the risk of rejection.
cn: 但开始与陌生人交谈仍然非常值得冒被拒绝的风险。

en: It may surprise you that conversing with strangers will make them happier too.
cn: 与陌生人交谈也会让他们更快乐，这可能会让你感到惊讶。

en: The pleasure of connection seems contagious.
cn: 联系的乐趣似乎具有感染力。

en: People who are talked to have equally positive experiences as those who initiate a conversation.
cn: 被交谈的人与主动开始对话的人有同样积极的体验。

en: The Caribbean islands are divided into two worlds, a rich one and a poor one.
cn: 加勒比群岛分为两个世界，一个富有的，一个贫穷的。

en: This tropical region's economy is based mainly on farming.
cn: 这个热带地区的经济主要以农业为基础。

en: Farmers are of two types.
cn: 农民有两种类型。

en: One is the plantation owner who may have hundreds of thousands of acres.
cn: 一种是种植园主，可能拥有数十万英亩的土地。

en: In contrast, the small cultivator is working only a few acres of land.
cn: 相比之下，小农只耕种几英亩土地。

en: Most visitors to the Caribbean are rich, like the plantation owner.
cn: 大多数去加勒比海的游客都是富人，就像种植园主一样。

en: They do not realize or do not want to realize that many farm families barely managed to get by on what they grow.
cn: 他们没有意识到或不想意识到，许多农户靠他们种的东西勉强度日。

en: The Caribbean produces many things.
cn: 加勒比地区生产许多东西。

en: Sugar is the main product.
cn: 糖是主要产品。

en: Other export crops are tobacco, coffee, bananas, spices and citrus fruits, such as orange, lemon or grapefruit.
cn: 其他出口作物有烟草、咖啡、香蕉、香料和柑橘类水果，如橙子、柠檬或葡萄柚。

en: From the West Indies also come oil, mineral pitch and many forest products.
cn: 西印度群岛还出产石油、矿物沥青和许多林产品。

en: Jamaica's aluminum ore supplies are the world's largest.
cn: 牙买加的铝矿供应量居世界首位。

en: Oil comes from Trinidad, Aruba and Curacao.
cn: 石油来自特立尼达、阿鲁巴和库拉索。

en: But for many of the smaller islands, sugar is the only export.
cn: 但对许多较小的岛屿来说，糖是唯一的出口产品。

en: Rum, a strong alcoholic drink, which is distilled from sugar cane, is also an export.
cn: 朗姆酒，一种用甘蔗蒸馏而成的烈性酒精饮料，也是一种出口产品。

en: The world's best rum comes from this area.
cn: 世界上最好的朗姆酒来自这个地区。

en: Local kinds vary from the light rums of Puerto Rico to the heavier darker rums of Barbados and Jamaica.
cn: 当地种类从波多黎各的淡朗姆酒到巴巴多斯和牙买加的浓烈深色朗姆酒不等。

en: American tourists enjoy stocking up on inexpensive high quality Caribbean rum while they're on vacation.
cn: 美国游客喜欢在度假时囤积便宜优质的加勒比朗姆酒。

en: In Curacao, the well- known liquor of that name is made from the thick outer skin of a native orange.
cn: 在库拉索，同名的知名利口酒是用当地橙子的厚外皮制成的。

en: Ever since America's colonial days, the Caribbean islands have been favorite places to visit.
cn: 自美国殖民时代以来，加勒比群岛一直是人们喜欢游览的地方。

en: Since World War II, tourism has increased rapidly.
cn: 自二战以来，旅游业迅速发展。

en: Because great numbers of people go there, the islanders have built elaborate resorts, developed harbors and airfields, improved the beaches and have expanded sea and air routes.
cn: 因为大量的人去那里，岛民们建造了精致的度假村，开发了港口和机场，改善了海滩，并扩大了海空航线。

en: Everything is at the resort- hotel, beach, shopping and recreation.
cn: 一切都在度假村——酒店、海滩、购物和娱乐。

en: The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island.
cn: 度假者没有任何理由去探索这个岛屿。

en: As in most places, those who have money live well indeed.
cn: 和大多数地方一样，有钱人确实过得很好。

en: Those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty.
cn: 没钱的人生活在不同程度的贫困中。

en: But here the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy.
cn: 但在这里，穷人的数量远远超过富人。

en: A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside.
cn: 游客会发现富人住在海边或乡村的公寓或西班牙风格的房子里。

en: Their servants might include a cook, a maid, and a nurse for their children.
cn: 他们的仆人可能包括一个厨师、一个女佣和一个照顾孩子的保姆。

en: Most of the people live well below the poverty level.
cn: 大多数人生活在贫困线以下。

en: In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses.
cn: 在城镇里，他们拥挤地住在狭小的房子里。

en: Islanders make the best they can of what they have.
cn: 岛民们尽可能地利用他们拥有的东西。

en: Their homes are quite shabby.
cn: 他们的房子相当破旧。

en: Sadly, most tourists never see the side of the Caribbean.
cn: 遗憾的是，大多数游客从未见过加勒比海的这一面。

en: Talk to anyone who's a generation not too older and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days.
cn: 和任何年龄不太大的人交谈，他们很可能会说现在的孩子更被宠坏了。

en: No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish and spoiled children, those who get bad- tempered or silently- brute when they are not given everything they want immediately.
cn: 没有人想要拥有或待在苛求、自私和被宠坏的孩子身边，那些没有立即得到想要的一切就会发脾气或默默粗暴的孩子。

en: Paradoxically, the parents of such children encourage this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can their children will be happy.
cn: 矛盾的是，这些孩子的父母鼓励这种苛求的行为，错误地认为给孩子他们能给的一切，孩子就会快乐。

en: In the short term, perhaps they are right.
cn: 短期内，也许他们是对的。

en: But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.
cn: 但从长远来看，这样的孩子最终会孤独、依赖、长期不满，并且怨恨那些拼命取悦他们的父母。

en: Undoubtedly parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable and likable rather than spoiled and miserable.
cn: 毫无疑问，父母想要培养快乐、自信、能干、可爱的孩子，而不是被宠坏和痛苦的孩子。

en: One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids, and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets and the like.
cn: 阻碍这一点的一个因素是，父母不能或没有花足够的高质量时间与孩子相处，并用玩具、游戏、小玩意儿等来弥补这种不足。

en: Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention.
cn: 与其得到物质的东西，孩子们更需要父母的全心关注。

en: The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time.
cn: 一起度过的时长的多少不如这段时间的内容重要。

en: Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have.
cn: 父母不应立即满足他们的愿望，而应帮助他们制定一个计划，去赢得他们想要的东西。

en: This teaches them to value the effort as well as what it achieves.
cn: 这教会他们珍视努力以及努力所取得的成就。

en: Allow them to enjoy anticipation.
cn: 让他们享受期待。

en: Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life.
cn: 大量心理学研究表明，学会等待他们想要的东西的孩子更有可能在以后的生活中在许多方面取得成功。

en: One famous experiment in the 1960s involved 3- to 6- year- old children.
cn: 20世纪60年代的一个著名实验涉及3到6岁的儿童。

en: They were given a choice between receiving a small reward, such as a cookie, immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two.
cn: 他们可以选择立即获得一个小奖励，比如一块饼干，或者如果他们等待15分钟，可以得到两块。

en: Follow up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater self- worth, and even tend to be healthier.
cn: 后续研究发现，那些选择延迟满足的人现在在学业上更成功，有更高的自我价值感，甚至往往更健康。

en: If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result.
cn: 如果他们失败了，如果孩子们真的想要预期的结果，应该鼓励他们继续努力而不是放弃。

en: This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially and in personal relationships.
cn: 这教会他们如何处理失望并从中恢复，这与学业、经济和个人关系上更大的成功和满足相关。

en: And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view, as well as their own.
cn: 最后，父母应该鼓励孩子从其他角度以及自己的角度看待生活。

en: This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others—qualities sure to take them a long way in life.
cn: 这教会他们理解他人、同情他人——这些品质一定会让他们在人生中走得很远。

en: It is not hard to mess up an interview.
cn: 搞砸一场面试并不难。

en: Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment.
cn: 大多数人坐在招聘经理对面，回答那些实际上让他们接受评判的问题时都会感到紧张。

en: And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
cn: 只要在错误的时间说了错误的话，你被更仔细考虑录用的机会就会迅速下降。

en: The most obvious thing not to do is complain.
cn: 最明显不能做的事情就是抱怨。

en: Employers want to hire positive people.
cn: 雇主想雇用积极的人。

en: Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance.
cn: 消极地谈论上一份工作会引起担忧，你可能很难管理，或者你可能是一个把自己表现不佳归咎于管理层的人。

en: Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough.
cn: 不要说你在工作中跳来跳去是因为没有找到合适的岗位或觉得挑战不够。

en: Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost.
cn: 诸如此类的话会让你听起来漫无目的、迷失方向。

en: An interviewer may well think, why would this role be any different for you?
cn: 面试官很可能会想，这个职位对你来说会有什么不同呢？

en: You will probably leave here in six months.
cn: 你很可能六个月后就会离开这里。

en: It also begs the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager.
cn: 这也引出了一个问题：你和经理的关系是怎样的。

en: It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her.
cn: 听起来你和经理之间没有开放的沟通。

en: Managers usually love people who can self- sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through their work, and who bring ideas and solutions to the table.
cn: 经理们通常喜欢那些能够自我维持并通过主动行动实现成长的人，那些善于完成工作的人，以及那些能提出想法和解决方案的人。

en: If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements.
cn: 如果你处于管理或领导职位，在讨论你当前的职位时，绝不要把所有的成就归功于自己。

en: Emphasize your team and how through their talents, your vision was realized.
cn: 强调你的团队，以及如何通过他们的才能实现了你的愿景。

en: Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team.
cn: 大多数成功的领导者都知道，他们和他们的团队一样优秀。

en: And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.
cn: 在面试中承认这一点将大大有助于表明你可能是你所申请职位的合适人选。

en: Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try and convey the idea that you're flexible.
cn: 最后，要清楚自己的角色是什么，并努力传达你很灵活这一信息。

en: Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you.
cn: 询问你的角色是什么，意味着你会把自己局限在别人对你的期望中。

en: In reality, your role is whatever you make of it.
cn: 在现实中，你的角色取决于你如何塑造它。

en: This is especially true in small companies, where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued.
cn: 在小公司尤其如此，适应能力和承担新职责的能力受到高度重视。

en: And this is equally important if you're just starting out.
cn: 如果你刚刚起步，这也同样重要。

en: Entry level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews.
cn: 入门级面试者在大多数面试中最好展示广泛的技能。

en: It's important to have a wide skill set as many startups and small companies are moving really fast.
cn: 拥有广泛的技能很重要，因为许多初创公司和小公司发展非常快。

en: Employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.
cn: 雇主正在寻找聪明的候选人，他们能够快速适应并在成长中的公司中表现出色。

en: Good morning and welcome to People in the News.
cn: 早上好，欢迎收看《新闻人物》。

en: With me today is Meghan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines.
cn: 今天和我一起的是梅根·布朗，一位环保活动家，她备受争议的新书《超越回收》正成为头条新闻。

en: Hi, Brian.
cn: 嗨，布莱恩。

en: Thanks for having me today.
cn: 谢谢你今天邀请我。

en: I'm excited to explain to the audience what my book is really about.
cn: 我很兴奋能向观众解释我的书到底是关于什么的。

en: Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country.
cn: 你这本书的评论家们断言，你正试图迫使整个国家做出彻底的改变。

en: Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal.
cn: 有些人声称你想强迫每个人吃素，并使私人交通非法。

en: I'm aware of those claims, but they simply aren't true.
cn: 我知道这些说法，但它们根本不是真的。

en: People who haven't read the book are making assumptions about my arguments.
cn: 没读过这本书的人在对我的论点进行假设。

en: They know I'm a vegetarian, that I don't wear leather or fur, and that I always use public transportation.
cn: 他们知道我是素食主义者，不穿皮革或皮草，而且我总是使用公共交通。

en: So they're depicting me as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist determined to force my beliefs on others.
cn: 所以他们把我描绘成一个激进的动物权利活动家和环保主义者，决心把我的信仰强加给别人。

en: But don't you want others to adopt your practices?
cn: 但你不希望别人采纳你的做法吗？

en: You've campaigned for animal rights and the environment for decades.
cn: 你为动物权利和环境奔走呼吁了几十年。

en: I'd love it if people choose to live as I do.
cn: 如果人们选择像我一样生活，我会很高兴。

en: But my life choices are based on my personal convictions.
cn: 但我的生活选择是基于我个人的信念。

en: They aren't my recommendations for others who don't share those convictions.
cn: 它们不是我对那些不认同这些信念的人的建议。

en: Well, in this excerpt from your book, you argue that meat consumption and private transport are devastating the environment and that the best choices for the planet are vegetarian diets and public transport.
cn: 嗯，在你书的这段摘录中，你主张肉类消费和私人交通正在破坏环境，而对地球最好的选择是素食和公共交通。

en: I did write that.
cn: 我确实写了那些。

en: But those are examples of what I call best practices, not what I'm actually suggesting.
cn: 但那些是我所说的最佳实践的例子，而不是我实际上建议的。

en: In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week.
cn: 在我拯救环境的指南中，我建议适度的改变，比如每周吃两天素食。

en: You also endorse high taxes on meat and other animal products and increased taxes on gasoline.
cn: 你也支持对肉类和其他动物产品征收高额税费，并增加汽油税。

en: Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices.
cn: 这些税收可能会迫使穷人接受你的生活选择。

en: But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than 3% only.
cn: 但我建议的税收没那么高，只有不到3%。

en: Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection, which benefits everyone.
cn: 另外，产生的资金将被用于环境保护，这惠及每个人。

en: With me in the studio today is Ms. Jane Logan, author of a new book, Secrets to Success.
cn: 今天在演播室和我一起的是简·洛根女士，新书《成功的秘诀》的作者。

en: She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success.
cn: 她自称已经揭示了人们是如何取得成功的。

en: So Ms. Logan, in your book, you claim that successful people have many things in common.
cn: 那么洛根女士，在你的书中，你声称成功人士有许多共同点。

en: For instance, they know their strengths when pursuing a goal.
cn: 例如，他们在追求目标时知道自己的优势。

en: That's right.
cn: 没错。

en: They also tend to be motivated by a negative or positive life event.
cn: 他们也倾向于被生活中的负面或正面事件所激励。

en: They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.
cn: 他们把自己的成功归功于生活中有人相信他们。

en: You also write that there are a number of different factors related to success.
cn: 你还写到，有许多不同的因素与成功有关。

en: And while successful people are driven to achieve their goals, the ultra successful have even greater ambition.
cn: 虽然成功人士被驱使去实现他们的目标，但极其成功的人有更大的抱负。

en: Yes, greater ambition as well as a burning desire to be the best of the best is also a common characteristic.
cn: 是的，更大的抱负以及成为精英中的精英的强烈渴望也是一个共同特征。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: So those who are determined don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome.
cn: 所以那些有决心的人不把障碍视为阻碍成功的东西，而只是需要克服的不便。

en: Absolutely.
cn: 完全正确。

en: Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals.
cn: 成功人士也很乐观，因为保持积极的心态很重要，同时也要意识到那些可能阻止我们实现目标的障碍。

en: That's a good point.
cn: 说得好。

en: All too often, people give up at the first hurdle.
cn: 人们常常在第一个障碍面前就放弃了。

en: Would you say then that most successful people make it all by themselves?
cn: 那么你会说大多数成功人士都是靠自己成功的吗？

en: Not exactly.
cn: 不完全是。

en: They are usually good at cooperating with people and understanding the needs of others.
cn: 他们通常善于与人合作，理解他人的需求。

en: So people will be willing to help them, I guess.
cn: 所以人们会愿意帮助他们，我猜。

en: That's correct.
cn: 没错。

en: And this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect, whether it's with a colleague, an assistant or even a receptionist.
cn: 这往往带来大量的相互尊重，无论是与同事、助理还是接待员。

en: Most successful people I know are very passionate about their work.
cn: 我认识的大多数成功人士都对他们的工作充满热情。

en: Would you say that passion is the single biggest key to success?
cn: 你会说热情是成功唯一最重要的关键吗？

en: Not entirely.
cn: 不完全是。

en: There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion.
cn: 有一个先决条件，那就是你必须在培养热情的环境中工作。

en: If that exists, success will follow.
cn: 如果那存在，成功就会随之而来。

en: The saying 'blind as a bat' simply isn't correct.
cn: '像蝙蝠一样瞎'这种说法根本是不正确的。

en: The truth is that all 1,100 bat species can see and often their vision is pretty good, although not as excellent as other night- hunting animals.
cn: 事实是，所有1100种蝙蝠都能看见，而且它们的视力通常相当好，尽管不如其他夜间捕食的动物那么优秀。

en: There are two main groups of bats, which are believed to have evolved independently of each other, but both from a common ancestor.
cn: 蝙蝠主要有两大类，据信它们各自独立进化，但都来自一个共同的祖先。

en: The first group, known as the mega bats, are mostly medium- sized or large bats who eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish.
cn: 第一类，被称为巨型蝙蝠，大多是中型或大型蝙蝠，吃水果、花朵，有时也吃小动物或鱼。

en: These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes.
cn: 这些物种有独特的视觉中心和大的眼睛。

en: They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey.
cn: 它们利用视觉和嗅觉来捕捉猎物。

en: For example, Flying Foxes not only see well during daylight, but can also distinguish colors.
cn: 例如，狐蝠不仅在白天看得清楚，还能辨别颜色。

en: They actually rely on their daylight vision and cannot fly during the night with no moonlight.
cn: 它们实际上依赖它们的日间视力，在没有月光的夜晚无法飞行。

en: The second group, called micro bats, are smaller in size and mostly eat insects.
cn: 第二类，被称为微型蝙蝠，体型较小，主要吃昆虫。

en: These species use echolocation to find their way and identify food.
cn: 这些物种利用回声定位来探路和识别食物。

en: Scientists have proven that despite their poorly developed small eyes, these bats still can see during the day.
cn: 科学家已经证明，尽管它们的小眼睛发育不良，但这些蝙蝠在白天仍然能看见。

en: When we consider the nightly lifestyle of these bats, we will see they have to be sensitive to the changing light levels because this is how they sense when to start hunting.
cn: 当我们考虑这些蝙蝠的夜间生活方式时，我们会发现它们必须对光线变化敏感，因为这是它们感知何时开始捕猎的方式。

en: Moreover, vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances, beyond the range of echolocation.
cn: 此外，微型蝙蝠利用视觉进行长距离旅行，超出回声定位的范围。

en: So the truth is, there are no bats which are naturally blind.
cn: 所以事实是，没有天生失明的蝙蝠。

en: Some species use their sense of hearing more than their eyes as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle, but their eyes are still functional.
cn: 有些物种更多地使用听觉而非视觉，这是为了适应特定的生活方式，但它们的眼睛仍然有功能。

en: A study has found that educational TV shows come with an added lesson that influences the child's behavior.
cn: 一项研究发现，教育类电视节目附带一个额外的课程，会影响孩子的行为。

en: Children spending more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children.
cn: 花更多时间观看教育节目的孩子对其他孩子表现出更多的情绪攻击性。

en: This shows that children can learn the educational lesson that was intended.
cn: 这表明孩子们可以学到节目想要传达的教育内容。

en: However, they're also learning other things along the way.
cn: 然而，他们也在过程中学到了其他东西。

en: This unintended impact has to do with the portrayal of conflict in media and how preschool- age children comprehend that conflict.
cn: 这种意外的影响与媒体中冲突的描绘以及学龄前儿童如何理解这种冲突有关。

en: TV and movie producers often incorporate an element of bad behavior.
cn: 电视和电影制作人经常加入不良行为的元素。

en: This is to teach children a lesson at the end of the program.
cn: 这是为了在节目结束时给孩子们一个教训。

en: Educational shows have pro- education and pro- social goals.
cn: 教育类节目有支持教育和亲社会的目标。

en: However, conflict between characters is often depicted with characters being unkind to each other or they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other.
cn: 然而，角色之间的冲突通常被描绘成角色彼此不友善，或者他们可能对彼此使用情绪攻击的策略。

en: Preschool children really don't get the moral of the story.
cn: 学龄前儿童真的无法理解故事的寓意。

en: That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together.
cn: 那是因为这要求他们理解节目的所有部分是如何组合在一起的。

en: You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that.
cn: 你需要相当复杂的认知技能和记忆技能才能做到这一点。

en: These are still developing in young children.
cn: 这些在幼儿身上仍在发展中。

en: However, parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing.
cn: 然而，父母不应该完全限制孩子的观看。

en: Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot.
cn: 相反，父母应该和孩子们一起观看，帮助他们理解剧情。

en: Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end.
cn: 父母可以在观看过程中评论，然后在结尾解释其中的信息。

en: They should explain how certain type of behavior was not appropriate.
cn: 他们应该解释某些类型的行为是不恰当的。

en: This will help children interpret and get the message and help them learn to watch the show for those messages.
cn: 这将帮助孩子们理解并获取信息，并帮助他们学会为获取这些信息而观看节目。

en: While it has long been a practice in Asian countries, many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no- shoes- in- the- house rule.
cn: 虽然在亚洲国家这早已是一种习惯，但许多西方国家的人还没有接受进屋脱鞋的规矩。

en: For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is regarded as sufficient.
cn: 对那些国家的许多人来说，进屋前把鞋擦一擦就被认为足够了。

en: After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone.
cn: 毕竟，他们可能认为一点污垢不会伤害任何人。

en: But I can give you several good reasons why people should remove their shoes before going inside their homes.
cn: 但我可以给你几个充分的理由，说明为什么人们应该在进屋前脱掉鞋子。

en: Bacteria are everywhere.
cn: 细菌无处不在。

en: They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets.
cn: 当你走在人行道、公共卫生间的地板甚至办公室的地毯上时，它们会聚集在你的鞋子上。

en: In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear.
cn: 在美国一所大学进行的一项研究中，研究人员从鞋子上收集了微生物细菌。

en: They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe.
cn: 他们发现，仅一只鞋子的外部就可以聚集多达42.1万单位的细菌。

en: And it only takes a little bit of dirt to damage your timber floors.
cn: 而且只需要一点点污垢就能损坏你的木地板。

en: The more dirt you track in, the more it scratches and the more often you'd have to clean.
cn: 你带进来的泥土越多，划痕就越多，你就需要更频繁地清洁。

en: The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time.
cn: 额外的擦洗会随着时间的推移损害你的地板。

en: Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointed or hard parts.
cn: 鞋子也会在地板上留下痕迹和划痕，尤其是高跟鞋或有尖头或硬部件的鞋子。

en: These can dent and scratch your floor.
cn: 这些会使地板凹陷和刮伤。

en: And if you live in an apartment building, removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors.
cn: 如果你住在公寓楼里，脱掉吵闹的鞋子是礼貌的做法，是为了体谅楼下的邻居。

en: Walking around with bare feet is actually better for your feet.
cn: 光着脚走路实际上对你的脚更好。

en: It strengthens the muscles in your feet.
cn: 它能增强你脚部的肌肉。

en: Though many people are accustomed to wearing shoes during all their waking hours, the more time you spend wearing shoes, the more likely you are to incur foot injuries as a result.
cn: 虽然许多人习惯在醒着的时候一直穿鞋，但你穿鞋的时间越长，就越有可能因此导致脚部受伤。

en: And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason.
cn: 如果人们还不信服我的论点，我可以给出最后一个理由。

en: The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home.
cn: 你通过鞋子带进屋的灰尘和有毒化学物质会恶化你家的空气质量。

en: Toxic chemicals are everywhere in our lives; insect- killing chemicals used on public grass areas, cleaning chemicals on the floors of public areas.
cn: 有毒化学物质在我们的生活中无处不在；公共草地上的杀虫剂，公共区域地板上的清洁化学品。

en: By kicking off your shoes before you enter the home, you are denying entry to these harmful chemicals.
cn: 在进屋前脱掉鞋子，你就是在阻止这些有害化学物质进入。

en: Given the amount of time we spend in classrooms, and the number of shoes that pass through them every day, you may well understand me if I were to propose a no- shoes- in- the- classroom rule.
cn: 考虑到我们花在教室里的时间，以及每天穿行其中的鞋子数量，如果我提议一项'教室脱鞋'的规定，你很可能就会理解我了。

en: Emotions are an essential and inseparable part of our consciousness.
cn: 情感是我们意识中不可或缺的一部分。

en: They are part of a built- in mechanism, which allows us to cope with the ups and downs of our lives both physically and mentally.
cn: 它们是内置机制的一部分，使我们能够在身体上和精神上应对生活中的起伏。

en: When we hide our emotions and our true feelings, we stop being genuine, spontaneous and authentic in our relationships.
cn: 当我们隐藏情绪和真实感受时，我们在人际关系中就不再真诚、自发和真实。

en: When we put on cultivated and polished faces in the company of others, we stop being true to ourselves.
cn: 当我们在他人面前表现出有教养和修饰过的面孔时，我们就不再忠于自己。

en: Socially, it may be a good tactic to hide our true emotions, but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust.
cn: 从社会角度来说，隐藏真实情绪可能是个好策略，但从道德角度来说，这也是对信念和信任的违背。

en: Although humans are more advanced and intelligent, animals are more genuine and authentic in their behavior and responses than human beings.
cn: 虽然人类更先进、更聪明，但动物在行为和反应上比人类更真诚、更真实。

en: The more educated we are, the less transparent and reliable we become.
cn: 我们受的教育越多，就越不透明、越不可靠。

en: We are drawn to our pets because pets do not lie.
cn: 我们被宠物吸引，因为宠物不说谎。

en: One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human.
cn: 处理愤怒或恐惧等情绪的第一步是承认它们是正常的、人性的。

en: There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional, unless your emotions make you inhuman, insensitive and cruel to others.
cn: 情绪化并没有什么罪恶或不道德的，除非你的情绪让你变得不人道、冷漠和残忍。

en: Feelings of guilt associated with emotions are more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself.
cn: 与情绪相关的内疚感比情绪体验本身更具破坏性和伤害性。

en: So when you deal with the problem of emotions, you should learn not only how to control them but also how to accept them and manage the guilt and anguish arising from them.
cn: 所以当你处理情绪问题时，你不仅应该学会如何控制它们，还应该学会如何接受它们，并管理由此产生的内疚和痛苦。

en: Our brains are made up of a primitive inner core and a more evolved and rational outer core.
cn: 我们的大脑由原始的内心核和更进化、更理性的外层核组成。

en: Most of the time, the rational part of the mind controls the information coming from the primitive core and makes its own decisions as to what to do and how to respond.
cn: 大多数时候，大脑的理性部分控制着来自原始核心的信息，并就做什么和如何回应做出自己的决定。

en: However, during critical situations, especially when a threat is present, the rational part is overridden by the primitive core.
cn: 然而，在危急情况下，尤其是当威胁存在时，理性部分会被原始核心所覆盖。

en: And this is when we experience emotions, the fight- or- flight response.
cn: 这就是我们体验情绪的时候，即战斗或逃跑反应。

en: When emotions arise, it is useless to suppress them.
cn: 当情绪出现时，压抑它们是无用的。

en: Instead, we should pay attention to them and try to understand the message they are trying to convey.
cn: 相反，我们应该关注它们，并试着理解它们试图传达的信息。

en: For this, we need to make use of the rational part of the brain to examine our emotions and decide whether they are proportionate to the situation at hand.
cn: 为此，我们需要利用大脑的理性部分来审视我们的情绪，并判断它们是否与当前情况相称。

en: This way, we can control our emotions better and manage our behavior.
cn: 这样，我们就能更好地控制情绪，管理行为。

en: Good morning, class.
cn: 早上好，同学们。

en: My topic today is how to feed a hungry world.
cn: 我今天的话题是如何养活一个饥饿的世界。

en: The world's population is expected to grow from 6.8 billion today to 9.1 billion by 2050.
cn: 世界人口预计将从现在的68亿增长到2050年的91亿。

en: Meanwhile, the world's population more than doubled from 3 billion between 1961 and 2007.
cn: 与此同时，世界人口从1961年到2007年间从30亿增加了一倍多。

en: Simultaneously, food production has been constrained by a lack of scientific research.
cn: 同时，粮食生产因缺乏科学研究而受到限制。

en: Still, the task of feeding the world's population in 2050 seems easily possible.
cn: 尽管如此，在2050年养活世界人口的任务似乎很容易实现。

en: What is needed is a second green revolution.
cn: 需要的是第二次绿色革命。

en: This is an approach that is described as the sustainable growth of global agriculture.
cn: 这是一种被称为全球农业可持续增长的方法。

en: Such a revolution will require a wholesale shift of priorities in agricultural research.
cn: 这样一场革命将需要农业研究重点的全面转变。

en: There is an urgent need for new crop varieties.
cn: 迫切需要新的作物品种。

en: They must offer higher yields but use less water, nitrogen- rich fertilizers or other inputs.
cn: 它们必须提供更高的产量，但使用更少的水、氮肥或其他投入。

en: These new crops must also be more resistant to drought, heat and pests.
cn: 这些新作物还必须更抗旱、耐热和抗虫害。

en: Equally crucial is lower- tech research into basics such as crop rotation and mixed farming of animals and plants on small farms.
cn: 同样关键的是对基础知识的低技术研究，如轮作和小农场动植物的混合种植。

en: Developing nations could score substantial gains in productivity by making better use of modern technologies and practices.
cn: 发展中国家可以通过更好地利用现代技术和实践，在生产效率上取得可观的收益。

en: But that requires money.
cn: 但这需要资金。

en: It is estimated that to meet the 2050 challenge, investment must double to 83 billion US dollars a year.
cn: 据估计，要应对2050年的挑战，投资必须翻倍，达到每年830亿美元。

en: Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure.
cn: 大部分资金需要用于改善农业基础设施。

en: Everything from production to storage and processing must improve.
cn: 从生产到储存和加工的一切都必须改善。

en: However, research agendas need to be focused on the needs of the poorest and most resource- limited countries.
cn: 然而，研究议程需要聚焦于最贫穷和资源最有限国家的需求。

en: It is there that most of the world's population lives and it is there the population growth over the next decades will be the greatest.
cn: 世界上大多数人口生活在那里，未来几十年人口增长最多的也是在那些地方。

en: To their credit, the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view.
cn: 值得赞扬的是，世界各地的农业科学家正在接受这种广阔的观点。

en: In March, for example, they came together at the first Global Conference on Agricultural Research to begin working out how to change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations.
cn: 例如，今年3月，他们齐聚首届全球农业研究会议，开始研究如何改变研究议程，以帮助满足贫穷国家农民的需求。

en: But these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policy- makers.
cn: 但这些计划除非得到政策制定者的大力支持，否则不会产生成果。

en: The growth in public agricultural- research spending peaked in the 1970s and has been shrinking ever since.
cn: 公共农业研究支出的增长在20世纪70年代达到顶峰，此后一直在萎缩。

en: The big exception is China, where spending has far surpassed other countries over the past decade.
cn: 一个主要的例外是中国，在过去十年中，其支出远远超过了其他国家。

en: China seems set to transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology to poorer countries.
cn: 中国似乎即将转型，成为向贫穷国家提供相关科学技术的关键供应国。

en: But developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility too.
cn: 但发达国家也有人道主义责任。

en: Calls by scientists for large increases in the appropriation of funds for public spending on agricultural research are more than justified.
cn: 科学家们呼吁大幅增加农业研究公共支出的拨款，这完全合理。

en: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non- fiction books of adventure.
cn: 大卫·杰克逊先生是《纽约客》的特约撰稿人，以非虚构类冒险书籍而闻名。

en: Today, we go on a different kind of adventure; Jackson's life of parenting his offspring.
cn: 今天，我们将进行一次不同寻常的冒险：杰克逊养育子女的生活。

en: David, as a parent of an 11- and a 14- year- old, what is the most interesting issue you are dealing with right now?
cn: 大卫，作为11岁和14岁孩子的父亲，你现在正在处理的最有趣的问题是什么？

en: It's easy to focus on the challenges, but so far, I find these ages to be kind of wonderful.
cn: 人们很容易关注挑战，但到目前为止，我发现这个年龄段的孩子还挺棒的。

en: They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions.
cn: 他们很独立，有自己好奇和着迷的事物。

en: You can talk to them about fairly sophisticated subject matter such as politics.
cn: 你可以和他们谈论相当复杂的话题，比如政治。

en: Yes, that does sound refreshing compared with talking to younger children.
cn: 是的，与和年幼的孩子交谈相比，这听起来确实令人耳目一新。

en: Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
cn: 他们会请你校对他们的文章吗？

en: Certainly, with writing they do.
cn: 当然，写作方面他们会。

en: I really just try to be encouraging.
cn: 我真的只是尽力鼓励他们。

en: I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.
cn: 我认为在这个年龄，编辑方面的指导不如鼓励重要。

en: Are there books that you think are important that your children read, and that all children read?
cn: 有没有你认为重要的书，你的孩子在读，所有孩子也都应该读？

en: My general thought is to read widely and to incorporate a love for reading.
cn: 我总的想法是广泛阅读，并培养对阅读的热爱。

en: Learning to love to read, I think, is the optimal thing, because it gives you a skill you can take anywhere.
cn: 学会爱上阅读，我认为是最好的事情，因为它能给你一种可以随身携带的技能。

en: So you're not too concerned like some parents with the content they're reading?
cn: 所以你不像有些父母那样担心他们阅读的内容？

en: I know I have some worries about that.
cn: 我知道我对此有些担心。

en: Yeah, read what you like.
cn: 是的，喜欢读什么就读什么。

en: If a child loves graphic novels or comic books, whatever it is, that is turning them on to read and turning on their imagination.
cn: 如果一个孩子喜欢图画小说或漫画书，不管是什么，那都会激发他们阅读的兴趣，点燃他们的想象力。

en: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence.
cn: 我觉得孩子们对书的品味会随着进入青春期而改变。

en: I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager.
cn: 我知道我十几岁的时候确实是这样。

en: What do you think?
cn: 你怎么看？

en: I think it's especially important as they get older to read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world and people.
cn: 我认为随着他们长大，阅读能开阔他们对世界和人的眼界的主题尤为重要。

en: So I think both fiction and non- fiction are really important because they give you the power to begin to perceive the world through the lives of others.
cn: 所以我认为小说和非小说都非常重要，因为它们能给你一种力量，让你开始通过他人的生活来感知世界。

en: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur.
cn: 在本期《金钱对话》中，我们的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一名大学生，也是一位成功的年轻企业家。

en: Molly, tell us about your business.
cn: 莫莉，给我们讲讲你的生意吧。

en: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight.
cn: 嗯，我通过网站销售特色服装，主要面向那些因为身高或体重而在商业街商店难以找到合适衣服的女性。

en: But I do some men's clothes too.
cn: 但我也做一些男装。

en: How did you get started in this business at such a young age?
cn: 你这么年轻是怎么开始做这行的？

en: Are you studying fashion design?
cn: 你学的是时装设计吗？

en: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes.
cn: 实际上，我主修金融，但我一直很喜欢衣服。

en: And I started making my own at 14.
cn: 我14岁就开始自己做衣服了。

en: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing?
cn: 你受过设计或缝纫方面的培训吗？

en: Or was it a natural ability?
cn: 还是天生的能力？

en: I'd have to say no to both.
cn: 我对两个问题的回答都是没有。

en: No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.
cn: 没人教我做过衣服，我刚开始做的大部分东西都是一团糟。

en: Why did you persevere?
cn: 你为什么能坚持下来？

en: I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age.
cn: 我想大多数人如果一直失败就会放弃，尤其是在那个年纪。

en: I kept on out of necessity.
cn: 我是出于需要才坚持下去的。

en: As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops.
cn: 正如你所见，我个子很高，在普通商店里找不到适合我的衣服。

en: So I kept trying and developed my skills over time.
cn: 所以我不断尝试，随着时间的推移提高了我的技能。

en: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20- year- old student.
cn: 嗯，我的笔记显示你去年赚了5万美元的利润，对于一个20岁的学生来说，这是一个非凡的数字。

en: How did that happen?
cn: 那是怎么发生的？

en: Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it?
cn: 你看到了市场空白并决定填补它吗？

en: No.
cn: 没有。

en: When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes.
cn: 我上大学时，一些同学称赞我的衣服。

en: And when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs.
cn: 当我说是我自己做的时，其他高个子女性开始问我能不能给她们做。

en: And I did.
cn: 我做了。

en: And before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur.
cn: 不知不觉中，我就成了一名企业家。

en: So what are your plans for the future?
cn: 那你对将来有什么计划？

en: Do you intend to open a physical store?
cn: 你打算开一家实体店吗？

en: No.
cn: 不。

en: I'll keep things online to keep costs down.
cn: 我会继续在网上经营以降低成本。

en: But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants.
cn: 但我会增加更多童装，包括女孩和男孩的，甚至可能还有婴儿的。

en: And I hope to add to my range of designs for men.
cn: 我还希望增加男士服装的设计系列。

en: Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence.
cn: 研究人员利用人工智能发现了一种强效的新型抗生素化合物。

en: The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria.
cn: 这种抗生素可以杀死非常危险的细菌。

en: According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
cn: 根据发表在《细胞》杂志上的一项研究，这种化合物成功清除了小鼠体内对所有已知抗生素都具有耐药性的致命菌株。

en: The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule.
cn: 研究人员表示，这是人工智能首次被用来寻找一种强大的新型抗生素分子。

en: Why does this matter?
cn: 这为什么重要？

en: The answer is antibiotic resistance.
cn: 答案是抗生素耐药性。

en: This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them.
cn: 当细菌产生对旨在杀死它们的药物的存活能力时，就会发生这种情况。

en: Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing.
cn: 抗生素耐药性是对健康的严重威胁，而且这个问题正在加剧。

en: This makes finding new antibiotics very important.
cn: 这使得寻找新型抗生素变得非常重要。

en: However, in recent decades, very few have been developed, and those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available.
cn: 然而，近几十年来，开发出的新型抗生素很少，而且开发出来的往往与已有药物非常相似。

en: The searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds, but this is where artificial intelligence comes in.
cn: 搜索也往往只关注狭窄范围内的化合物，但这正是人工智能发挥作用的地方。

en: Why?
cn: 为什么？

en: To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be.
cn: 为了寻找新药，科学家会筛选分子来预测它们可能有多有效。

en: Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow.
cn: 通常，这种筛选是由人在实验室完成的，既昂贵又缓慢。

en: Artificial intelligence is different.
cn: 人工智能不同。

en: It's fast, and it can process a high volume.
cn: 它速度快，而且可以处理大量数据。

en: It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing.
cn: 它可以筛选数亿种化合物，以识别出几个需要实验测试的有趣候选分子。

en: Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic.
cn: 人工智能还能够预测化合物是否可能有毒。

en: Some experts assert that this work signifies a paradigm shift in antibiotic discovery.
cn: 一些专家断言，这项工作标志着抗生素发现领域的范式转变。

en: It could change drug discovery more generally.
cn: 它可能在更广泛的范围内改变药物发现。

en: A recent study overturned what we think we know about lying.
cn: 最近的一项研究推翻了我们自以为对说谎的了解。

en: Most of us have a theory about how to tell if someone is telling a lie.
cn: 我们大多数人都有一套关于如何判断某人是否在说谎的理论。

en: We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.
cn: 我们可能会通过观察那些我们熟悉并经常见到的人来发展出这套理论，但我们倾向于将那些从非科学的日常研究中收集到的信息加以概括，使其成为一种普遍理论。

en: So we might imagine that liars have evasive eyes, or the opposite—they simply stare at you.
cn: 所以我们可能会想象说谎者眼神躲闪，或者相反——他们只是盯着你看。

en: Or perhaps it is more generally nervous behavior we associate with lies.
cn: 或者也许是我们通常与谎言联系在一起的紧张行为。

en: Whatever the particular theory, it's usually based on close observation of people we know.
cn: 不管具体的理论是什么，它通常是基于对我们认识的人的密切观察。

en: And we get lots of practice.
cn: 而且我们有很多练习机会。

en: On average, we're lied to some 200 times per day.
cn: 平均而言，我们每天要面对大约200次谎言。

en: These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless.
cn: 这些大多是无害的谎言，但终归是谎言。

en: But there's a problem with our theories, even though they're based on all these observations.
cn: 但我们的理论存在一个问题，即使它们基于所有这些观察。

en: The average person—you and me—tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance.
cn: 普通人——你和我——在辨别谎言的严格测试中，表现得并不比碰运气更好。

en: That's well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies.
cn: 这在许多研究以及研究人员为找出可靠的测谎方法所做的许多尝试中都已得到充分证实。

en: It's even relatively easy to fool lie detectors, the gold standard of lie detection, by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.
cn: 甚至通过训练呼吸技巧和抑制症状来欺骗测谎仪——测谎的黄金标准——也相对容易。

en: Is there any way to get better at detecting lies?
cn: 有什么方法能更好地辨别谎言吗？

en: The new research offers some surprising advice.
cn: 这项新研究提供了一些令人惊讶的建议。

en: Stop looking and listen instead.
cn: 不要用眼睛看，而是用耳朵听。

en: It turns out that if we're unable to see the face, but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.
cn: 事实证明，如果我们看不到对方的脸，而是专注于对方的声音，我们的准确率会大大提高。

en: Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding; show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless.
cn: 表现得顺从、谦卑、感恩且要求不高；当医生走进你的房间时表现出极大的愉悦，即使探访短暂且毫无用处。

en: Don't challenge anyone with authority unless you are famous or very rich.
cn: 不要挑战任何有权威的人，除非你很有名或非常富有。

en: Those are a few strategies for dealing with today's American medical establishment.
cn: 这些是与当今美国医疗机构打交道的一些策略。

en: What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration.
cn: 患者想要的是得到尊重和体谅。

en: But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that.
cn: 但根据我的经验，很少有医院和医生愿意这样做。

en: In his book, A Whole New Life, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumor on his spinal cord.
cn: 在他的书《全新的生活》中，小说家雷诺兹·普莱斯回忆说，他的医生选择了一个拥挤的走廊作为告知他脊髓上可能有肿瘤的地方。

en: It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.
cn: 这两位医生没有想到走廊并不是传递这条特定消息的最合适场所。

en: My surgeon, who is in his mid- thirties, looks tired.
cn: 我的外科医生三十多岁，看起来很疲惫。

en: He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice.
cn: 他因冬天在冰上摔倒的病人而不堪重负。

en: He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.
cn: 他是个风趣的人，但有时他的风趣不受欢迎。

en: "The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon," he tells me after I have been in the hospital for more than a week.
cn: 在我住院一个多星期后，他告诉我：“蓝十字健康保险公司要我明天下午把你扔到雪地里去。”

en: I'm terrified because I have no idea where to go.
cn: 我很害怕，因为我不知道该去哪里。

en: I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches.
cn: 我无法行走，甚至连抬腿几英寸都做不到。

en: The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot.
cn: 医院的社工给我的印象是个白痴。

en: But my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon.
cn: 但我对她的抱怨只会惹恼我的外科医生。

en: "I have to work with these people," he tells my friend, Dr. Karen Brudney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.
cn: 当我的朋友凯伦·布鲁德尼医生仁慈地代表我出面干预并安排我转院时，他告诉她：“我必须和这些人一起工作。”

en: "If you say one negative thing, they get defensive," she tells me later.
cn: 后来她告诉我：“如果你说一句负面的话，他们就会变得防御性很强。”

en: "They have this kind of institutional loyalty.
cn: 他们有这种机构忠诚。

en: Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse.
cn: 一定要带一个支持者，也就是任何其他人一起去医院，并记下每一个问题和答案，每一位医生和护士的名字。

en: When people know you have their names, they behave better.
cn: 当人们知道你有他们的名字时，他们会表现得更好。

en: And," Brudney adds, "if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult.
cn: 布鲁德尼补充道：“而且，如果你作为一名患者，暗示你可能想要控制哪怕部分情况，或者想要被咨询或被告知，那么你就会被认为是难缠的。”

en: They want you to be totally passive.
cn: 他们希望你是完全被动的。

en: The entire health care system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients.
cn: 整个医疗保健系统，尤其是医院和疗养院，其存在的原因与照顾患者无关。

en: Patients are incidental.
cn: 患者只是附属品。

en: There are probably teams you've worked with but you never want to work with again.
cn: 可能有些团队你曾与之共事过，但你再也不想和他们合作了。

en: But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally.
cn: 但也一定还有其他团队，你会珍视与他们再次进行专业合作。

en: In other words, your team had vitality.
cn: 换句话说，你的团队有活力。

en: Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
cn: 当人们与团队成员之间形成的联系使得即使在团队解散后他们仍能保持联系时，活力便产生了。

en: What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together?
cn: 团队的哪些特征使其成员即使不再一起工作也更有可能保持联系？

en: This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal.
cn: 这个问题最近在一本商业期刊上发表的一项研究中得到了回答。

en: One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness.
cn: 研究团队发现的两个关键因素之一是相似性。

en: Specifically, sharing the same gender or ethnic origin.
cn: 具体来说，就是拥有相同的性别或种族背景。

en: The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they will be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose.
cn: 一个团队中拥有相似人口统计特征的成员越多，他们在团队达成目标后很长一段时间内就越倾向于保持联系。

en: After ties are established, similarity strengthens them.
cn: 联系建立后，相似性会加强它们。

en: As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration.
cn: 因此，他们以更大的信任和相互理解来看待这些人，这促使他们寻求进一步的合作机会。

en: In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer- lasting connections with similar others.
cn: 实际上，人们倾向于与相似的人建立更牢固、更持久的联系。

en: Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful.
cn: 一个看起来和听起来与我们不同的人可能拥有我们取得更大成功所需的资源。

en: Yet, we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different.
cn: 然而，我们仅仅因为他们不同就觉得他们明显不那么可信。

en: If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.
cn: 如果你是职场多元化的坚定倡导者，你无疑会被这样的发现吓到。

en: The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members.
cn: 研究人员发现的第二个因素是团队成员之间关系的质量。

en: The more they trust one another, share the same goals and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections, despite no longer working as one team.
cn: 他们越是互相信任，拥有共同的目标，并为了实现这些目标而相互依赖，他们就越有可能在不再作为一个团队工作时仍能保持联系。

en: Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each other, and their members are obliged to share the workload and help out.
cn: 拥有高质量关系的团队有一种共同的信念，即彼此一起承担风险是安全的，而且他们的成员有义务分担工作量和提供帮助。

en: The current team I'm working in is the most successful and cohesive team I've ever experienced.
cn: 我目前所在的团队是我经历过的最成功、最有凝聚力的团队。

en: We have the quality relationships, but demographically the four of us couldn't be more different.
cn: 我们拥有高质量的关系，但从人口统计特征来看，我们四个人差异巨大。

en: I wouldn't question the value of diversity among my employees.
cn: 我不会质疑员工多元化的价值。

en: An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors.
cn: 一位研究过600位百万富翁的美国研究人员发现，你能有多富有归结为六个财富因素。

en: She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income.
cn: 她发现，无论年龄或收入如何，有六种行为与净资产潜力有关。

en: These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus and social indifference.
cn: 它们是节俭、自信、责任、计划、专注和社交冷漠。

en: Being thrifty comes as no great surprise.
cn: 节俭并不令人意外。

en: Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck.
cn: 入不敷出、花钱而不为退休储蓄、花未来的钱，这些都会让你成为工资的奴隶。

en: "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%."
cn: 她写道：“即使收入达到天文数字，为了正确地积累财富，专家建议将收入的20%存起来，靠剩下的80%生活。”

en: Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty.
cn: 拥有自信是另一个关键特征，因为它有助于人们节俭。

en: It takes confidence to live within your means.
cn: 量入为出需要自信。

en: It also takes confidence to invest properly.
cn: 合理投资也需要自信。

en: Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long- term investment plan.
cn: 理财规划师建议，不要凭感情做出投资决策，而应该减少对投资的干预，专注于长期投资计划。

en: But people can't invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes.
cn: 但人们不能不接受结果的责任就去投资或管理自己的钱。

en: Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self- made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck.
cn: 许多百万富翁承担个人责任，而且大多数也恰好是白手起家的，这意味着他们不是通过运气获得财富的。

en: Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short.
cn: 百万富翁不指望别人让他们富有，如果他们达不到目标，也不会责怪任何人。

en: They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves.
cn: 他们专注于自己可以控制的事情，并将日常习惯与自己设定的目标保持一致。

en: They tend to be goal- oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through.
cn: 他们往往以目标为导向且努力工作，这使他们能够制定财务计划并专注于完成这些计划。

en: 92% of the millionaires surveyed developed a long- term plan for their money and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.
cn: 92%的受访百万富翁为他们的钱制定了长期计划，97%的人几乎总是实现了他们为自己设定的目标。

en: And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent.
cn: 正是这些行为让他们容易变得社交冷漠。

en: They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more.
cn: 他们抵制生活方式的膨胀，即赚得越多花得越多的倾向。

en: Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired.
cn: 本质上，他们不会屈服于购买最新产品的压力，也不会试图跟上其他人或他们已经拥有的东西。

en: Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long- term wealth- building plan.
cn: 他们没有专注于今天可能让他们快乐的事情，而是专注于他们的长期财富积累计划。

en: Welcome to Money Matters, a weekly program that helps you manage your money.
cn: 欢迎收听《金钱很重要》，这是一档帮助你管理财务的每周节目。

en: Tonight, I'll be talking to Mary Johnson about budgeting.
cn: 今晚，我将与玛丽·约翰逊讨论预算问题。

en: Hello, everyone.
cn: 大家好。

en: There's a magic about money.
cn: 金钱有一种魔力。

en: When it's not planned for, tracked and kept a record of, it literally disappears.
cn: 当它没有被计划、追踪和记录时，它真的会消失。

en: What are some of the steps we can take to prevent this from happening?
cn: 我们可以采取哪些步骤来防止这种情况发生？

en: Well, it's all about keeping track of your money.
cn: 嗯，这一切都关乎追踪你的钱。

en: If you don't do that, you'll never be able to set any goals for your budget or have the discipline to stick to them.
cn: 如果你不这样做，你就永远无法为预算设定任何目标，也无法有纪律地去坚持。

en: That's easier said than done.
cn: 说起来容易做起来难。

en: I read recently that only 41% of Americans adhere to a budget.
cn: 我最近看到只有41%的美国人坚持执行预算。

en: Yes, but knowing what you earn and what you spend can give you reassurance that you won't get into debt in the first place.
cn: 是的，但了解你的收入和支出可以让你放心，你不会一开始就陷入债务。

en: You can do this by adding up all of your sources of income you have and writing them all down on a piece of paper.
cn: 你可以通过把你所有的收入来源加起来，并把它们写在一张纸上来做到这一点。

en: On the same page, write down all of your monthly expenses.
cn: 在同一页纸上，写下你所有的月度支出。

en: I'm always amazed at how much my expenses add up.
cn: 我总是惊讶于我的支出加起来有那么多。

en: But designating each item as an income or an expense really helps me have a much better sense of all my spending.
cn: 但把每一项都指定为收入或支出确实帮助我更好地了解我的所有开销。

en: Right, most people have no idea how much they spend each day, let alone each week or month, no matter how careful they are.
cn: 没错，大多数人不知道自己每天花多少钱，更不用说每周或每月了，不管他们有多小心。

en: Next, subtract your monthly expenses from income.
cn: 接下来，用收入减去月度支出。

en: If the result is positive, you are living within your means.
cn: 如果结果是正数，你就是量入为出。

en: If the result is a negative number, you're going to have to cut back on your spending.
cn: 如果结果是负数，你就必须削减开支。

en: I'm usually a negative number.
cn: 我通常是负数。

en: I just can't resist the allure of all those prestigious goods.
cn: 我就是无法抗拒那些名牌商品的诱惑。

en: Well, it's not a catastrophe.
cn: 嗯，这不是一场灾难。

en: But you do have to make some changes; try cutting back on those non- essential items, sell some stuff in your attic or shop online to avoid unnecessary temptations like chocolate.
cn: 但你必须做出一些改变；试着削减那些非必需品的开支，卖掉阁楼里的一些东西，或者网购以避免不必要的诱惑，比如巧克力。

en: Failing that you can always find yourself a part- time job.
cn: 如果不行，你还可以给自己找份兼职工作。

en: Hi there.
cn: 你好。

en: I've come to see the flat.
cn: 我是来看公寓的。

en: My name is Mark Adams.
cn: 我叫马克·亚当斯。

en: We spoke on the phone on Wednesday.
cn: 我们周三通过电话。

en: Hi, Mark, come on up.
cn: 嗨，马克，上来吧。

en: I'll buzz you in.
cn: 我给你开门。

en: Green door on the second floor on the right side.
cn: 二楼右侧的绿色门。

en: Nice to meet you.
cn: 很高兴见到你。

en: I spoke to all your references and they all checked out okay.
cn: 我和你所有的推荐人都谈过了，他们都没问题。

en: So let me show you around.
cn: 所以让我带你四处看看。

en: The place actually belongs to my mother.
cn: 这地方实际上属于我母亲。

en: But her health isn't great.
cn: 但她身体不太好。

en: So we finally managed to persuade her to move in with us and rent this old place out.
