cn: 所以我们终于说服了她搬来和我们一起住，把这个老地方租出去。

en: It's a great size.
cn: 大小很合适。

en: Plenty of space.
cn: 空间很大。

en: Very versatile.
cn: 非常多功能。

en: I think it's a winner for us.
cn: 我觉得对我们来说是个好选择。

en: Yes, all the appliances are brand- new.
cn: 是的，所有电器都是全新的。

en: There's a washing machine and a tumble dryer in the utility room next to the kitchen.
cn: 厨房旁边的杂物间里有一台洗衣机和一台烘干机。

en: Lots of closet space too, which is fabulous.
cn: 还有很多壁橱空间，太棒了。

en: My wife has a ridiculous number of shoes.
cn: 我妻子的鞋子多得离谱。

en: Now the big question, what about noise and the neighbours?
cn: 现在最大的问题，噪音和邻居怎么样？

en: Well, all the neighbours are elderly, so no noisy kids.
cn: 嗯，所有邻居都是老年人，所以没有吵闹的孩子。

en: And the back of the house overlooks a clear and peaceful pond.
cn: 房子的后面俯瞰着一个清澈宁静的池塘。

en: So it's perfect if tranquility is what you are looking for.
cn: 所以如果你追求宁静，那就太完美了。

en: That's good news.
cn: 这是个好消息。

en: We've been living in a less than glamorous part of Aberdeen, constantly harassed day and night by noisy neighbours.
cn: 我们一直住在阿伯丁一个不太好的地方，日夜被吵闹的邻居骚扰。

en: Getting to work was a nightmare too, as we only have one car and my wife has to use it as she works nights at the hospital.
cn: 上班也是一场噩梦，因为我们只有一辆车，而我妻子上夜班需要用车。

en: Well, if you like the place, it's yours as soon as I get a contract drawn up with a solicitor.
cn: 嗯，如果你喜欢这个地方，一旦我和律师拟定好合同，它就是你的了。

en: The first month's rent and a deposit are mandatory on signing the contract.
cn: 签合同时必须支付第一个月的租金和押金。

en: Then we can work out when is the best day for you to pay rent each month.
cn: 然后我们可以商定你每月哪天交房租最合适。

en: We'll be incredibly happy to be your new tenants.
cn: 我们会非常高兴成为你的新租户。

en: Thank you so much.
cn: 非常感谢。

en: My wife will be thrilled to get out of the shabby place we are now in and start filling those wardrobes with all those shoes.
cn: 我妻子会很高兴能搬出我们现在住的破地方，开始用那些鞋子填满衣柜。

en: A new study has found a positive correlation between how much television children watch and their parents' stress levels.
cn: 一项新研究发现，孩子看电视的时间与父母的压力水平之间存在正向关联。

en: Why?
cn: 为什么？

en: Because the more television kids watch, the more they're exposed to advertising.
cn: 因为孩子看电视越多，他们接触到的广告就越多。

en: The more advertising they see, the more likely they are to insist on purchasing items when they go with their parents to the store.
cn: 他们看到的广告越多，和父母一起去商店时就越有可能坚持要买东西。

en: This could generate conflict if the parents refuse.
cn: 如果父母拒绝，这可能产生冲突。

en: All that, researchers say, can contribute to parents' overall stress levels.
cn: 研究人员说，所有这些都会导致父母的整体压力水平上升。

en: What's the solution?
cn: 解决办法是什么？

en: Perhaps the most obvious is curtailing screen time.
cn: 也许最明显的是减少屏幕时间。

en: Commercial content is there for a reason—to elicit purchasing behavior.
cn: 商业内容的存在是有原因的——为了引发购买行为。

en: So parents might want to shut off the TV.
cn: 所以父母可能需要关掉电视。

en: Researchers concede that this is easier said than done.
cn: 研究人员承认这说起来容易做起来难。

en: So they suggest another option.
cn: 所以他们建议另一种选择。

en: Parents can change how they talk to their kids about purchases.
cn: 父母可以改变他们与孩子谈论购物的方式。

en: The researchers suggest that parents seek input from their children on family purchasing decisions.
cn: 研究人员建议父母在家庭购买决策上征求孩子的意见。

en: They shouldn't try to control all purchases.
cn: 他们不应该试图控制所有的购买。

en: Instead, parents might tell their children things like 'I will listen to your advice on certain products or brands.'
cn: 相反，父母可以告诉孩子诸如'我会听取你对某些产品或品牌的建议'之类的话。

en: This type of communication, the researchers assert, can lead to children making fewer purchasing demands.
cn: 研究人员断言，这种类型的沟通可以减少孩子的购买需求。

en: That means less parents' stress.
cn: 那意味着父母的压力更小。

en: However, the protective effect of this kind of communication diminishes with greater exposure to television.
cn: 然而，这种沟通的保护效果随着看电视时间的增加而减弱。

en: This is because advertising aimed at children is especially persuasive.
cn: 这是因为针对儿童的广告特别有说服力。

en: Advertisers use an assortment of tactics, such as bright colors, happy music and celebrity endorsements to appeal to children.
cn: 广告商使用各种各样的策略，比如鲜艳的色彩、欢快的音乐和名人代言来吸引儿童。

en: Plus, children don't have the cognitive ability to fully understand advertising's intent.
cn: 此外，儿童没有充分理解广告意图的认知能力。

en: That makes them particularly vulnerable to advertisements.
cn: 这使他们特别容易受到广告的影响。

en: Everyone is supposed to cheer for good guys, and we should only punish the bad guys.
cn: 每个人都应该为好人大声喝彩，我们只应该惩罚坏人。

en: But that's not what we always do.
cn: 但这并不总是我们所做的。

en: Most of the time, we do indeed reward good people.
cn: 大多数时候，我们确实奖励好人。

en: We also often punish people who harm others or who aren't good team players.
cn: 我们也经常惩罚那些伤害他人或不是好的团队成员的人。

en: But sometimes the good guys also get punished or criticized, specifically because they are so good.
cn: 但有时好人也受到惩罚或批评，特别是因为他们太好了。

en: This seems baffling, because it's detrimental to group cooperation.
cn: 这似乎令人费解，因为它不利于团队合作。

en: However, the phenomenon has been discovered in multiple fields, and it has been found in every society.
cn: 然而，这种现象已在多个领域被发现，而且在每个社会都有发现。

en: Why does this happen?
cn: 为什么会发生这种情况？

en: Research suggests a simple reason.
cn: 研究表明一个简单的原因。

en: When one person looks really good, others look bad by comparison.
cn: 当一个人看起来真的很好时，其他人相比之下就显得不好了。

en: Those others then have an incentive in stopping that person from looking good, especially if they can't or won't compete.
cn: 那些其他人就有动机阻止那个人看起来好，特别是如果他们不能或不愿竞争的话。

en: After all, we're all judged in comparison with others.
cn: 毕竟，我们都是通过与他人的比较来被评判的。

en: When faced with someone better, what can a normal person do?
cn: 当面对更好的人时，一个正常人能做什么？

en: One option is to actively compete.
cn: 一种选择是积极竞争。

en: A second option is to bring that person down.
cn: 第二种选择是把那个人打倒。

en: That is to suppress their cooperation or work ethic, infer selfish motives for their actions, or imply real or imagined hypocrisy.
cn: 那就是压制他们的合作或职业道德，推断他们行为的自私动机，或暗示真实或想象的虚伪。

en: Other tactics include attacking them on unrelated dimensions or punishing them outright.
cn: 其他策略包括在不相关的方面攻击他们或直接惩罚他们。

en: Why does this matter?
cn: 这为什么重要？

en: Critics often attack the motives of people who protect the environment, donate money or work too hard.
cn: 批评者经常攻击那些保护环境、捐款或工作太努力的人的动机。

en: Such good deeds are dismissed as naive or hypocritical by those who do not perform those deeds.
cn: 这种善举被那些不做好事的人视为幼稚或虚伪。

en: This criticism may ultimately discourage people from doing good deeds.
cn: 这种批评最终可能会阻止人们做好事。

en: So it's important to recognize these attacks for what they are.
cn: 所以认识到这些攻击的本质是很重要的。

en: In America, most researchers concede that boys and girls are brought up in different ways, taught different skills and rewarded for different acts.
cn: 在美国，大多数研究人员承认，男孩和女孩以不同的方式被抚养长大，被教授不同的技能，因不同的行为而受到奖励。

en: Women, it is agreed, excel at certain tasks, men at others.
cn: 人们一致认为，女性擅长某些任务，男性擅长其他任务。

en: There's little argument that some personality traits appear more dominant in one sex than in the other.
cn: 几乎没有争议的是，某些性格特征在一种性别中比在另一种性别中表现得更为突出。

en: All of this notwithstanding, gender differences are very much in the media these days.
cn: 尽管如此，性别差异如今在媒体中非常普遍。

en: Since the rise of the women's movement, gender role behavior has come under closer scrutiny.
cn: 自妇女运动兴起以来，性别角色行为受到了更密切的审视。

en: How has this affected friendship?
cn: 这对友谊有什么影响？

en: How do the sexes differ in their friendship relations?
cn: 两性在友谊关系上有什么不同？

en: Most preteen children have a best friend who is usually someone of the same sex and similar age.
cn: 大多数十一二岁的孩子都有一个最好的朋友，通常是同性别、年龄相仿的人。

en: Both sexes share an essentially positive recollection of these childhood friendships.
cn: 两性对这些童年友谊都有着基本积极的回忆。

en: They do not differ in this respect.
cn: 他们在这方面没有区别。

en: However, the type of play engaged in during these early friendships is telling of the difference to come.
cn: 然而，在这些早期友谊中进行的游戏类型预示着即将到来的差异。

en: Boys tend to form play groups that are competitive in nature.
cn: 男孩倾向于形成具有竞争性的游戏小组。

en: Girls' groups more frequently revolve around cooperative enterprises.
cn: 女孩的小组更常围绕合作活动展开。

en: Thus at an early age, boys become concerned with trying hard and winning, while girls, by contrast, playhouse and school, engaging in roles that require complementary support.
cn: 因此，在很小的时候，男孩就开始关注努力和获胜，而相比之下，女孩则玩过家家和学校游戏，扮演需要互补支持的角色。

en: Speaking of their childhood, men recall being highly responsive to and aware of the gender- role opinions of other boys.
cn: 谈到他们的童年，男性回忆起他们对其他男孩的性别角色观点高度敏感和清醒。

en: Girls in preteen years appear to be less susceptible to gender- role pressure.
cn: 青春前期的女孩似乎不太容易受到性别角色压力的影响。

en: It is not until the dating years that women report being concerned with feminine behavior.
cn: 直到约会年龄，女性才报告开始关注女性行为。

en: Males, for the most part, are responsive to the suggestion that their behavior is unmanly at almost any age.
cn: 男性在大部分情况下，几乎在任何年龄段都对他们的行为不够男子气概的暗示有反应。

en: These early attitudes reinforced by social conditioning continue to play an active part in the friendships of both sexes during adolescence.
cn: 这些被社会条件强化的早期态度在青春期两性的友谊中继续发挥积极作用。

en: This is a period when the majority of males once again report a closer alliance with same- sex friends.
cn: 这是一个大多数男性再次报告与同性朋友关系更密切的时期。

en: Now, however, with heightened intensity, considerable energy is devoted to competing for position and a definite undercurrent of competition permeates the relationship.
cn: 然而，现在，随着强度的增加，相当大的精力投入到争夺职位的竞争中，一股明确的竞争暗流渗透到关系中。

en: Although in dissimilar fashion, females share equally fragile relationships at this age.
cn: 尽管方式不同，女性在这个年龄段同样拥有脆弱的关系。

en: For them, the bond of loyalty extends only to the line of romantic involvement.
cn: 对她们来说，忠诚的纽带只延伸到浪漫关系这条线。

en: This is most apt to be the case in late adolescence when dating and relationships with boys take sharper precedence over sisterhood.
cn: 这种情况最常发生在青春后期，那时与男孩的约会和关系比姐妹情谊更为优先。

en: Actually dating dilutes the intensity of same- sex friendships for men also.
cn: 实际上，约会也削弱了男性同性友谊的强度。

en: For the majority of us, the moment we begin to date seriously, there's a competition between romance and friendship.
cn: 对我们大多数人来说，一旦我们开始认真约会，浪漫和友谊之间就存在竞争。

en: Good afternoon.
cn: 下午好。

en: In today's lecture, we'll be talking about how and when to disclose a disability when applying for a job.
cn: 在今天的讲座中，我们将讨论在求职时如何以及何时披露残疾。

en: On average, about 20 percent of the population has some form of disability.
cn: 平均而言，大约20%的人口有某种形式的残疾。

en: Most countries, these days, have equal opportunity and non- discrimination laws.
cn: 如今，大多数国家都有平等机会和非歧视法律。

en: Yet disabled people often find it hard to decide when, how and if at all to raise their disability problem with the potential employer.
cn: 然而，残疾人常常发现很难决定何时、如何以及是否向潜在雇主提出他们的残疾问题。

en: There is uncertainty about how a recruiter will perceive their disability.
cn: 招聘人员将如何看待他们的残疾存在不确定性。

en: In reality, many candidates fear they wouldn't be considered for a position as a result of disclosing this personal information.
cn: 在现实中，许多求职者担心，由于披露这些个人信息，他们不会被考虑录用。

en: And research has validated this as a genuine concern for many job applicants.
cn: 研究已经证实这是许多求职者的真实担忧。

en: It's a natural reaction, but it shouldn't be a reason to stay quiet.
cn: 这是一种自然的反应，但不应该成为保持沉默的理由。

en: People need to remember that they are applying for a position they have the skills and experience to excel in.
cn: 人们需要记住，他们申请的职位是他们具备技能和经验能够胜任的。

en: Discussing a disability with the potential employer may help them make reasonable workplace adjustments in their favor.
cn: 与潜在雇主讨论残疾问题可能有助于他们做出有利于自己的合理工作场所调整。

en: The most appropriate time to share this information is probably when an interview is scheduled.
cn: 分享这些信息最合适的时间可能是在安排面试的时候。

en: This information needn't be put upfront in their cover letter or resume, because it's probably not relevant to the position itself.
cn: 这些信息不必放在求职信或简历的最前面，因为它可能与职位本身无关。

en: Candidates with disabilities should feel they have the power to make their own decisions around sharing this information free from prejudice.
cn: 残疾求职者应该感到他们有权自主决定是否分享这些信息，不受偏见影响。

en: If they find an organization that doesn't celebrate diversity and inclusion, it could say a lot about the company's culture.
cn: 如果他们发现一个不提倡多样性和包容性的组织，这能说明很多关于公司文化的问题。

en: Perhaps the organization isn't the right fit.
cn: 也许这个组织不太合适。

en: It's important for them to remember that they are seeking a manager, an employer that's going to be supportive and continue to give them a great employment experience.
cn: 重要的是他们要记住，他们正在寻找一位经理，一位能够给予支持并继续给他们良好就业体验的雇主。

en: Companies sometimes offer candidates the chance to disclose disabilities on their application form, but people shouldn't feel restricted by this method or timing.
cn: 公司有时会给求职者提供在申请表上披露残疾的机会，但人们不应觉得受这种方法或时间的限制。

en: If people don't think their disability will impact their ability to perform in the advertised position, then it's entirely their entitlement to choose when and whether to share this information.
cn: 如果人们认为他们的残疾不会影响他们在招聘职位上的工作能力，那么选择何时以及是否分享这些信息完全是他们的权利。

en: It is important to be aware that recruiters may find the disability information that people have previously shared online.
cn: 重要的是要意识到，招聘人员可能会找到人们以前在网上分享的残疾信息。

en: There is always the risk that the recruiter will research information that is inaccurate or irrelevant.
cn: 招聘人员总是有可能搜索到不准确或不相关的信息。

en: If people don't think their disability will impact their ability to perform in the advertised position, then it's entirely their entitlement to choose when and whether to share this information.
cn: 如果人们认为他们的残疾不会影响他们在招聘职位上的工作能力，那么选择何时以及是否分享这些信息完全是他们的权利。

en: Smartphones distract attention and reduce learning because of their potential to offer activities more inviting than study.
cn: 智能手机分散注意力并降低学习效果，因为它们有可能提供比学习更有吸引力的活动。

en: But what about background sound alone?
cn: 但仅就背景声音而言呢？

en: A group of American researchers compared students' comprehension of verbal material when reading in the presence of background speech, instrumental music or general noise.
cn: 一组美国研究人员比较了学生在背景语音、器乐或一般噪音环境下阅读时对文字材料的理解情况。

en: General noise is neutral, such as that from the sound of an air conditioner or fan.
cn: 一般噪音是中性的，比如空调或风扇的声音。

en: Students' comprehension scores were most depressed in the presence of background speech.
cn: 在有背景语音的情况下，学生的理解成绩下降最多。

en: Comprehension was slightly better with the presence of music than with speech.
cn: 有音乐时的理解情况比有语音时略好一些。

en: However, when they were asked to identify melodies rather than understand text, background music interfered more.
cn: 然而，当他们被要求识别旋律而不是理解文本时，背景音乐的干扰更大。

en: When the background speech was in a language unfamiliar to participants, there was little if any hindrance of reading comprehension.
cn: 当背景语音是参与者不熟悉的语言时，阅读理解几乎没有受到阻碍。

en: British researchers compared the effects of background speech, vocal music, instrumental music, general background noise and silence on short- term memory.
cn: 英国研究人员比较了背景语音、声乐、器乐、一般背景噪音和安静对短期记忆的影响。

en: Background speech had the biggest negative effect.
cn: 背景语音的负面影响最大。

en: Vocal music was slightly more disruptive than instrumental.
cn: 声乐比器乐稍微更具干扰性。

en: In general, background noise and silence were least disruptive.
cn: 一般来说，背景噪音和安静干扰最小。

en: The degree of interference from background noise seems to depend on the extent to which the processing required on the task and the processing required to screen out the background noise overlap.
cn: 背景噪音的干扰程度似乎取决于任务所需的处理与屏蔽背景噪音所需的处理重叠的程度。

en: The studies suggest that when people read and when they try to remember any verbal material, background speech will inhibit their ability.
cn: 研究表明，当人们阅读和试图记忆任何文字材料时，背景语音会抑制他们的能力。

en: Instrumental music will have at worst a slight effect.
cn: 器乐最多有轻微的影响。

en: When writing an essay, however, other research has found it is best to reduce all background noise as much as possible.
cn: 然而，在写文章时，其他研究发现最好是尽可能减少所有背景噪音。

en: Not everyone reacts in the same way to distractions.
cn: 不是每个人对干扰的反应都一样。

en: Other studies suggest some aspects of personality may make a difference.
cn: 其他研究表明，性格的某些方面可能会产生影响。

en: The researchers subjected shy quiet people and confident outgoing ones to higher arousal or lower arousal background music, general noise or silence while asking them to remember words.
cn: 研究人员让害羞安静的人和自信外向的人分别在高唤醒或低唤醒的背景音乐、一般噪音或安静环境下记忆单词。

en: Everyone scored worse with higher arousal music, but the less sociable people were far more adversely affected by these distractions.
cn: 每个人在高唤醒音乐下得分都更差，但不太善于社交的人受到这些干扰的负面影响要大得多。

en: How's your dissertation going?
cn: 你的论文进展如何？

en: I'm proofreading my first draft and will submit it to my professor tomorrow.
cn: 我正在校对初稿，明天交给教授。

en: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.
cn: 哦，我还没开始写我的呢，所以我很担心下学期末之前能不能完成。

en: You mean you haven't even begun yours yet?
cn: 你的意思是你还没开始？

en: The final draft is due in five months.
cn: 终稿五个月后就要交了。

en: Of course I've started it, but I can't get to the writing yet as I haven't found enough resources to use, so I'm still researching the topic.
cn: 我当然开始了，但我还不能动笔写，因为我还没找到足够的资料，所以我还在研究这个课题。

en: Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research.
cn: 也许问题出在你做研究的方式上。

en: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information.
cn: 我开始时先和教授讨论了去哪里查找资料。

en: And based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.
cn: 基于此，我在图书馆找到了书籍，也在网上找到了大量有信誉的期刊文章。

en: I've tried all that, but don't have enough to write the dissertation as my department's minimum length is 70 pages.
cn: 你说的这些我都试过了，但还是不够写论文，因为我们系要求至少70页。

en: I think the problem is that my topic isn't viable.
cn: 我觉得问题在于我的选题不可行。

en: And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material.
cn: 老实说，我的教授一开始确实警告过我，说我可能找不到足够的材料。

en: But I was so interested in the topic that I didn't let his advice to turn me.
cn: 但我对这个课题太感兴趣了，所以没有听他的建议。

en: Well, I suggest you find a new topic.
cn: 嗯，我建议你换个新课题。

en: After all, our professors are here to guide us, so it's best to listen to them.
cn: 毕竟，教授们在这里是为了指导我们，所以最好听他们的。

en: In retrospect, I wish I had listened to him, but I didn't.
cn: 回想起来，我真希望当时听他的话了，但我没有。

en: And now I don't want to give up my topic as I've already invested so much time and energy.
cn: 现在我不想放弃我的课题，因为我已经投入了太多时间和精力。

en: If you're committed to your current topic, maybe you could make some adjustments rather than abandon it completely.
cn: 如果你坚持现在的课题，也许你可以做些调整，而不是完全放弃。

en: What is your topic?
cn: 你的课题是什么？

en: It's 'Depictions of Femininity and Folklore from the South of the Country'.
cn: 是'该国南部地区女性气质与民间传说的描绘'。

en: That's pretty narrow.
cn: 那相当窄。

en: You could find more material if you made the topic broader, maybe by including other kinds of depictions.
cn: 如果你把题目放宽一些，可能会找到更多资料，也许可以包括其他类型的描绘。

en: Broadening the topic is a great idea.
cn: 扩大题目是个好主意。

en: I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.
cn: 我会先从包括该国其他地区的民间传说开始。

en: Today, on Book Talk, we are lucky enough to host John Robbins and discuss his new book, Why Americans Are Fat and How We Can Lose Weight.
cn: 今天，在《书话》节目中，我们非常幸运地邀请到约翰·罗宾斯，讨论他的新书《美国人为什么肥胖以及我们如何减肥》。

en: John isn't just a respected writer; he's also one of the rare celebrity authors writing about science today.
cn: 约翰不仅是一位受人尊敬的作家，他还是当今为数不多的撰写科学类书籍的名人作家之一。

en: Thanks for having me, Rebecca, but I'm hardly a celebrity.
cn: 谢谢邀请我，Rebecca，但我算不上什么名人。

en: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages.
cn: 你这么说真是太谦虚了，考虑到你的四本书在全球总共售出了七百万册，而且被翻译成了12种不同的语言。

en: What makes people so fascinated with your work?
cn: 是什么让人们对你的作品如此着迷？

en: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight or obese.
cn: 嗯，人们读我的书是因为超过60%的美国人超重或肥胖。

en: And other countries are facing similar problems.
cn: 其他国家也面临类似的问题。

en: Basically, we all want to know how to fix things.
cn: 基本上，我们都想知道如何解决这个问题。

en: We certainly do.
cn: 我们确实如此。

en: I've read your new book and it's fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand.
cn: 我读了你的新书，非常棒，尤其是你让外行人也能理解深奥科学的方式。

en: That's no small achievement.
cn: 这可不是个小成就。

en: I'm glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried when I wrote it that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience.
cn: 很高兴听到你觉得我的作品通俗易懂，因为我写的时候担心讨论科学内容会让这本书更适合专业读者。

en: My last book was written primarily for the medical community.
cn: 我上一本书主要是为医学界写的。

en: But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight.
cn: 但这一次，我想帮助普通人控制体重。

en: And how do you suggest they do that?
cn: 那你建议他们怎么做呢？

en: Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight?
cn: 你能给我们讲讲你对想减肥的人的基本建议吗？

en: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs.
cn: 简而言之，我认为每个人都需要考虑自己的新陈代谢，吃适合自己身体需求的食物。

en: I don't advocate one single diet.
cn: 我不提倡单一的饮食方案。

en: Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others.
cn: 有些人应该比其他人摄入更多的碳水化合物。

en: And different people need different amounts of protein and fat.
cn: 不同的人需要不同量的蛋白质和脂肪。

en: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating ten servings of vegetables and three of fruit a day.
cn: 但你确实有一些对所有人的建议，包括每天吃十份蔬菜和三份水果。

en: We'll talk about those recommendations next, but now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor.
cn: 我们接下来会讨论这些建议，但现在我们需要短暂休息一下，播放一段赞助商的广告。

en: Stress is often depicted as negative, but research shows that moderate amounts of it can be beneficial for your brain and your body.
cn: 压力通常被描述为负面的，但研究表明适量的压力对你的大脑和身体都是有益的。

en: First, the benefits for the brain.
cn: 首先，是对大脑的益处。

en: Studies have shown that short periods of stress can actually bolster cognitive functioning.
cn: 研究表明，短时间的压力实际上可以增强认知功能。

en: Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells.
cn: 研究人员发现，将老鼠置于压力状态下仅仅几个小时，就能使新脑细胞的生长翻倍。

en: The rats also did better on a memory test later on.
cn: 这些老鼠在随后的记忆测试中也表现得更好。

en: Scientists think the same thing happens in humans.
cn: 科学家认为同样的事情也发生在人类身上。

en: But how does stress improve memory?
cn: 但压力是如何改善记忆的呢？

en: It's simple.
cn: 很简单。

en: When your brain cells multiply, your memory can improve.
cn: 当你的脑细胞增殖时，你的记忆力就会提高。

en: Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense, because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future.
cn: 从生物学的角度看，这是有道理的，因为更善于记住危险情况的动物将来可以避开它们。

en: If an animal encounters a predator and escapes, for example, it's important to remember where and when that encounter happened.
cn: 例如，如果一只动物遇到捕食者并逃脱了，记住这次遭遇发生的地点和时间是很重要的。

en: Experts assert that the same principle applies to humans.
cn: 专家断言，同样的原则也适用于人类。

en: Now, let's turn to how stress benefits the body.
cn: 现在，让我们来看看压力对身体的好处。

en: This may come as a surprise to laymen.
cn: 这对外行人来说可能很惊讶。

en: But experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick.
cn: 但专家说压力可以让你不生病。

en: Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness.
cn: 科学家承认，长期压力会让你更容易生病。

en: But research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning.
cn: 但研究表明，短时间的压力实际上可以提供一些抵御疾病的保护，因为它能增强免疫功能。

en: One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness.
cn: 一项研究表明，经历短暂压力的老鼠免疫细胞反应激增，这使得免疫系统能更好地对抗疾病。

en: For humans, there's even evidence that experiencing stress before getting vaccinated could help make vaccines more effective.
cn: 对于人类来说，甚至有证据表明在接种疫苗前经历压力可以帮助疫苗更有效。

en: For many managers and people who work in leadership positions, dealing with emails is a dilemma.
cn: 对于许多经理和担任领导职务的人来说，处理电子邮件是一个两难问题。

en: It's likely the unpredictable, uncontrollable and ongoing nature of day- to- day email in terms of volume, importance and urgency contributes to their levels of anxiety and to diminished leadership skills.
cn: 日常电子邮件在数量、重要性和紧急性方面的不可预测性、不可控性和持续性，很可能导致了他们的焦虑程度上升和领导能力下降。

en: That's because it's not unusual for many leaders to prioritize email management over people management.
cn: 这是因为许多领导者优先处理电子邮件管理而非人员管理的情况并不少见。

en: An obsession with managing their inbox prevents them from dealing with their employees.
cn: 沉迷于管理收件箱阻碍了他们与员工打交道。

en: As a result, they ignore the issues that might only be mild problems at first, until unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis by virtue of neglect.
cn: 结果，他们忽视了起初可能只是小问题的事情，直到不幸的是，这些事由于疏忽而不可避免地变成了重大问题或危机。

en: As leaders, they are expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer term strategic goals and also, less ambitiously but more practically, to monitor their daily output, to set clear expectations, and to give regular feedback.
cn: 作为领导者，他们应该激励团队追求长期战略目标，同时，不那么雄心勃勃但更实际的是，监控团队的日常产出、设定明确的期望并定期提供反馈。

en: When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter.
cn: 当面临在收件箱的吸引力和其他更重要活动之间做选择时，许多人牺牲了后者。

en: Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress.
cn: 日常的邮件需求对他们的目标进展产生了负面影响。

en: This is because leaders must divert resources from other tasks to check, filter and respond to emails.
cn: 这是因为领导者必须从其他任务中转移资源来查看、筛选和回复邮件。

en: The solution is cultivating self- control which is like a muscle—it can be strengthened or improved over time through exercise.
cn: 解决方案是培养自制力，它就像一块肌肉——可以通过锻炼随着时间的推移得到加强或改善。

en: Some suggestions include making space in your diary for the only periods during which you'll be checking emails, setting a timer for yourself so you don't become distracted by your inbox for too long, turning off email alerts so you're not interrupted by them.
cn: 一些建议包括：在日程表中专门留出查看邮件的时间段，为自己设置定时器以免被收件箱分散注意力太久，关闭邮件提醒以免被打断。

en: In last week's lecture, we talked about the problems caused by poor eating habits, focusing on how medical professionals are trying to solve these problems.
cn: 在上周的讲座中，我们讨论了不良饮食习惯造成的问题，重点讨论了医疗专业人员如何努力解决这些问题。

en: Today, we'll continue with the topic, but focus on research from a different field—marketing.
cn: 今天，我们将继续这个话题，但重点关注来自不同领域——市场营销的研究。

en: Now, what can marketing tell us about improving nutrition?
cn: 那么，市场营销能告诉我们关于改善营养的什么呢？

en: Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices.
cn: 嗯，一个营销学教授团队研究了食物视觉方面的重要性以及它如何影响食物选择。

en: Those marketing experts assert that the impact of the appearance of food is greater than we might presume, and might hold the key to encouraging better eating.
cn: 这些营销专家断言，食物外观的影响比我们可能想象的更大，并且可能是鼓励更好饮食的关键。

en: So how important is the appearance of food?
cn: 那么食物的外观有多重要呢？

en: Research shows that just seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement, for example, can cause individuals to imagine the taste or smell of that hamburger.
cn: 研究表明，例如，仅仅在广告中看到一张诱人的汉堡照片，就能让人想象那个汉堡的味道或气味。

en: This can make them more likely to purchase and consume it.
cn: 这会使他们更有可能购买和消费它。

en: Of course, that's the point of advertisements.
cn: 当然，这就是广告的目的。

en: So isn't that a good thing?
cn: 那这难道不是件好事吗？

en: Well, the marketing professors argue that this is actually a problem, because the combination of pleasing aesthetics of and easy access to unhealthy foods, such as hamburgers and pizza, may be contributing to a worldwide health crisis.
cn: 嗯，营销学教授认为这实际上是个问题，因为不健康食品（如汉堡和比萨）的诱人外观和易得性相结合，可能正在助长一场全球性的健康危机。

en: In fact, statistics show that 39% of all adults in the world weigh too much and another 13% are obese.
cn: 事实上，统计数据显示，全世界39%的成年人超重，另有13%的人肥胖。

en: Now, as we discussed last time, medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar and calorie content.
cn: 现在，正如我们上次讨论的，医疗专业人员试图通过关注不同食物中的营养成分来对抗肥胖流行病，强调碳水化合物、脂肪、糖和卡路里含量等。

en: But they've had limited success.
cn: 但他们的成功有限。

en: The marketing professors believe that the real solution to obesity is making food look appealing and focusing on the pleasure of both looking at and eating that food.
cn: 营销学教授认为，解决肥胖的真正方法是让食物看起来有吸引力，并关注观看和食用这种食物的愉悦感。

en: That pleasure can be used as a tool to promote healthy food choices.
cn: 这种愉悦感可以作为促进健康食物选择的工具。

en: In fact, the research done by the team showed that associating healthy food with pleasant images, experiences and emotions led to greater interest in purchasing or eating it.
cn: 事实上，该团队所做的研究表明，将健康食品与愉快的图像、体验和情感联系起来，会引发人们对其购买或食用的更大兴趣。

en: "This is a better strategy," they claim, then reminding consumers that a certain food is good for them.
cn: '这是一个更好的策略，'他们声称，然后提醒消费者某种食物对他们有好处。

en: But are they right?
cn: 但他们说得对吗？

en: Well, the researchers cited a marketing campaign designed to reverse the sales decline of carrots.
cn: 嗯，研究人员引用了一项旨在扭转胡萝卜销量下滑的营销活动。

en: The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities, but embrace their beauty and the pleasure derived from eating them.
cn: 该活动没有强调胡萝卜的健康品质，而是赞美它们的美丽和食用它们的愉悦感。

en: For example, the ads focused on the bright, beautiful orange color and crisp texture of the carrots.
cn: 例如，广告聚焦于胡萝卜明亮美丽的橙色和脆爽的口感。

en: The campaign led to an impressive increase in product sales of more than 10%.
cn: 该活动带来了超过10%的产品销量增长，令人印象深刻。

en: The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.
cn: 研究人员认为，其他公司可以通过类似的广告来增加健康食品的销量，将他们的产品描述为有吸引力和快乐的来源。

en: The household cleaning products industry really began to take off in the 1950s.
cn: 家用清洁产品行业真正开始起飞是在20世纪50年代。

en: Prior to that resourceful housewives, who had grown up in a less prosperous era, relied on substances that they used in their kitchens such as vinegar used to clean windows.
cn: 在此之前，在不太富裕的时代长大的足智多谋的家庭主妇们依靠厨房里使用的物质，比如用醋来清洁窗户。

en: Today, the household cleaning products industry is worth billions of dollars a year and is dominated by large global companies.
cn: 如今，家用清洁产品行业每年价值数十亿美元，由全球大型公司主导。

en: In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment- friendly cleaning products, and they're doing good business, too.
cn: 然而，近年来，许多国家提供更环保清洁产品的小型企业和公司数量激增，而且它们的生意也很好。

en: One reason for this is that consumers are becoming more aware of environment and sustainability issues.
cn: 原因之一是消费者越来越意识到环境和可持续性问题。

en: They also want to make their home a safe place, free from toxic chemicals.
cn: 他们也希望让自己的家成为一个安全的地方，远离有毒化学物质。

en: The third reason is people's awareness of a knowledge about technology has never been greater.
cn: 第三个原因是人们对技术的认知和了解从未如此之高。

en: In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible.
cn: 过去，人们可能会对声称能够达到惊人清洁效果的新产品持怀疑态度，但他们现在相信技术有能力完成曾经被认为不可能的事情。

en: There is perhaps no better example of this than a patented cloth sold by one company, which remarkably uses only water rather than traditional cleaning products.
cn: 也许没有比一家公司销售的专利抹布更好的例子了，它显著地只用水而不是传统清洁产品。

en: The company claims its cloth lifts, traps and removes dirt and bacteria.
cn: 该公司声称其抹布能提起、捕获并去除污垢和细菌。

en: And considering that people don't see these products in shops, or advertised on TV or in the press, it has been a pretty steep rise.
cn: 考虑到人们在商店里看不到这些产品，在电视或媒体上也没有广告，它的增长已经相当可观了。

en: Many of the people behind these companies began testing the viability of their products by selling them at local markets.
cn: 这些公司背后的许多人开始通过在本地市场销售产品来测试其可行性。

en: Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues.
cn: 然后，在很多情况下，顾客通过在社交媒体上留言评论、赞扬其优点来为这些产品做营销。

en: There are also TV shows and books dedicated to maintaining home tidiness and cleanliness and the benefits of having a clean home.
cn: 还有专门介绍保持家居整洁和清洁好处的电视节目和书籍。

en: Having a safe and clean home might be one thing people all agree on.
cn: 拥有一个安全干净的家可能是人们都认同的一件事。

en: Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time- honored ritual; throw a penny into the water, and your wish might come true.
cn: 把零钱扔进喷泉是一个历史悠久的仪式；把一便士扔进水里，你的愿望可能会实现。

en: But all that money has to go somewhere.
cn: 但所有这些钱都得去往某个地方。

en: Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountain's works.
cn: 否则，越来越多的便士、25美分硬币和欧元可能会堵塞喷泉的装置。

en: Today, I'm going to talk about where all the coins go.
cn: 今天，我要谈谈所有硬币都去了哪里。

en: Well, the coins collected can go to all sorts of different places- from fountain maintenance to charity or public service.
cn: 嗯，收集到的硬币可以去各种不同的地方——从喷泉维护到慈善或公共服务。

en: In New York City, for example, coins collected from fountains in public parks often go towards the fountains' maintenance itself, though entrepreneurs who don't mind getting their hands wet often get to it first.
cn: 例如，在纽约市，从公园喷泉收集的硬币通常用于喷泉本身的维护，尽管不介意把手弄湿的创业者们往往会先下手。

en: There are over 50 beautiful, decorative display fountains in New York City parks.
cn: 纽约市的公园里有超过50个美丽的装饰性喷泉。

en: They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks.
cn: 它们每隔几周由公园工作人员清洁一次。

en: But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.
cn: 但大多数硬币已经被有创业精神的纽约人取走了，剩下的数量不多。

en: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul.
cn: 不过，其他城市可以收获更丰厚的金额。

en: Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain; for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return.
cn: 以罗马著名的特雷维喷泉为例；数百年来，游客们将硬币从肩后扔进喷泉，以确保他们会重返罗马。

en: So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day.
cn: 如此多的游客投掷硬币，以至于罗马官员每晚都要清理喷泉，据报道每天能收集到来自世界各地多达4000美元的零钱。

en: Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy.
cn: 每晚收集到的大部分钱都用于经营一家为有需要的人服务的超市。

en: And collecting that cash is serious business.
cn: 收集这些现金是严肃的事情。

en: Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain.
cn: 众所周知，罗马官员对任何被抓到从喷泉中偷取硬币的人都很严厉。

en: In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them.
cn: 在2005年的一个案例中，警方逮捕了四名喷泉清洁工，他们被发现收集硬币后将其滑入自己的口袋。

en: Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.
cn: 当局最终抓住了一个名叫托马斯·摩根的臭名昭著的小偷，并禁止他进入喷泉，因为他用一根磁力棒在34年里捞出了数千美元的零钱。

en: For the most part, money collected from privately- owned fountains in the United States also goes to charity.
cn: 在美国，从私人拥有的喷泉收集的钱大多也用于慈善事业。

en: The fountain in New York City's Bryant Park is owned and operated by a not- for- profit corporation, which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance.
cn: 纽约市布莱恩特公园的喷泉由一家非营利公司拥有和运营，该公司将清洁工收集的现金用于喷泉自身的维护。

en: Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children living in the state.
cn: 每年从佛罗里达州华特迪士尼世界的许愿井、喷泉和池塘中取出的数万美元硬币被捐赠出来，用于支持该州的寄养儿童。

en: Whether or not your wish comes true after tossing a coin into a fountain, you can rest assured knowing that the change is likely going to someone who needs it.
cn: 无论你把硬币扔进喷泉后愿望是否实现，你都可以放心，这些零钱很可能会给到需要它的人。

en: Welcome to the Book Club.
cn: 欢迎来到读书俱乐部。

en: Today's guest is Susan Lane, the author of a new book on personal finances that has already sold half a million copies.
cn: 今天的嘉宾是苏珊·莱恩，她是一本关于个人理财的新书的作者，该书已售出50万册。

en: Hi, Susan, your book is extremely successful.
cn: 嗨，苏珊，你的书非常成功。

en: Why do you think that is?
cn: 你觉得这是为什么？

en: I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.
cn: 我想那是因为我传达的信息，即把幸福置于金钱之上。

en: So many of us in my generation have spent decades trying to earn more money, just to consume more, but it made us more miserable.
cn: 我们这一代人中有太多人花了几十年时间试图赚更多的钱，只是为了消费更多，但这让我们更加痛苦。

en: You yourself were once caught in that cycle, working for two decades as an executive and earning a high salary, but still accumulating debt.
cn: 你自己也曾陷入那个循环，做了二十年的高管，拿着高薪，但仍在积累债务。

en: I most certainly was.
cn: 我确实是的。

en: I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.
cn: 我赚了几百万，但四年前我辞职成为一名作家时，我欠了3万多美元。

en: So how did you escape that pattern?
cn: 那么你是如何摆脱那种模式的？

en: And what would you advise other people to do?
cn: 你会建议其他人怎么做？

en: The first change is in what we value.
cn: 第一个改变在于我们的价值观。

en: We need to emphasize things that actually make us happy, like relationships, the environment or even our hobbies.
cn: 我们需要强调那些真正让我们快乐的事物，比如人际关系、环境甚至我们的爱好。

en: Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change and so will our financial behavior.
cn: 一旦我们把正确的事情放在首位，我们的目标就会改变，我们的财务行为也会随之改变。

en: How does that translate into practical action?
cn: 这如何转化为实际行动呢？

en: Can you give our audience examples of what you are talking about on an everyday basis?
cn: 你能给我们观众举一些日常生活中的例子吗？

en: The major areas for action are usually housing, food and transportation.
cn: 行动的主要领域通常是住房、食物和交通。

en: So people might share a home with friends instead of living on their own, bring lunch from home instead of going to restaurants, and use public transport instead of owning a car.
cn: 所以人们可能会和朋友合住而不是独居，从家里带午餐而不是去餐馆，使用公共交通而不是拥有汽车。

en: Those sound like major sacrifices.
cn: 这些听起来像是重大的牺牲。

en: I could never share my home.
cn: 我永远无法与人合住。

en: I need my own space.
cn: 我需要自己的空间。

en: But they aren't sacrifices.
cn: 但它们不是牺牲。

en: When people change their values, their desires change.
cn: 当人们改变他们的价值观时，他们的欲望也会改变。

en: So in the example of housing, if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space, but giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones.
cn: 所以在住房的例子中，如果我们重视人际关系，合住并不是剥夺我们的空间，而是给我们一个与所爱之人共度更多时光的机会。

en: Indeed it is.
cn: 确实如此。

en: Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher.
cn: 谢谢你邀请我来画廊，克里斯托弗。

en: I haven't visited here since your predecessor's retirement functioned.
cn: 自从你前任的退休仪式后，我就没来过这里了。

en: Would you like to see the newest additions to our collection first, Catherine?
cn: 凯瑟琳，你想先看看我们收藏的最新藏品吗？

en: Are those the landscapes by Daniel Gregory?
cn: 那些是丹尼尔·格雷戈里的风景画吗？

en: I absolutely adore her work.
cn: 我非常喜欢她的作品。

en: This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself, and it's quite exquisite.
cn: 这第一件作品是艺术家本人赠送给画廊的礼物，非常精致。

en: I love how she depicts the barren landscape.
cn: 我喜欢她描绘荒芜景观的方式。

en: The colors complement each other perfectly.
cn: 色彩相互映衬得完美无缺。

en: You can sense the desolation in the picture.
cn: 你能感受到画面中的荒凉。

en: This piece was inspired by Gregory's recent trek in the Gobi Desert.
cn: 这幅作品的灵感来自格雷戈里最近在戈壁沙漠的徒步旅行。

en: And how did you obtain her other piece, over here?
cn: 那你是怎么得到她的另一幅作品的，那边那幅？

en: It was purchased at auction by an anonymous collector who lent it to the gallery for display.
cn: 它是由一位匿名收藏家在拍卖会上购得，并借给画廊展出的。

en: This composition is one of her most acclaimed paintings.
cn: 这幅作品是她最受赞誉的画作之一。

en: It must have cost that collector a small fortune to purchase this.
cn: 那位收藏家买下这幅画一定花了一大笔钱。

en: Obviously.
cn: 显然。

en: I can't disclose the exact amount he paid, but it was substantial.
cn: 我不能透露他支付的确切金额，但数目相当可观。

en: There's so much detail in this painting.
cn: 这幅画中有太多细节了。

en: I feel like I can really immerse myself in the scene.
cn: 我觉得我真的可以沉浸在这场景中。

en: I particularly like the symmetry created by the reflection of the mountain in the lake.
cn: 我特别喜欢湖中倒影所创造的对称之美。

en: This particular piece was the one that was nominated for a Gateway Award.
cn: 这幅特别的作品曾被提名门户奖。

en: I was lucky enough to attend the awards ceremony as Gregory's guest.
cn: 我很幸运作为格雷戈里的嘉宾出席了颁奖典礼。

en: So you know her personally.
cn: 所以你私下认识她。

en: I assume she is an eccentric artist.
cn: 我猜她是个古怪的艺术家。

en: Quite the opposite.
cn: 恰恰相反。

en: In fact, she's not at all eccentric.
cn: 事实上，她一点也不古怪。

en: I would say she's one of the most easygoing and intelligent people I know.
cn: 我会说她是我认识的最随和、最聪明的人之一。

en: I'd love to be able to meet her.
cn: 我很想能见到她。

en: There are so many questions I'd like to ask.
cn: 我有太多问题想问。

en: What a coincidence!
cn: 真巧！

en: I'm meeting her for dinner tonight.
cn: 我今晚要和她共进晚餐。

en: Would you like to come along?
cn: 你愿意一起来吗？

en: I'd love to.
cn: 我很乐意。

en: Thank you.
cn: 谢谢。

en: Forgiveness is the release of resentment or anger.
cn: 宽恕是释放怨恨或愤怒。

en: Forgiveness doesn't mean reconciliation.
cn: 宽恕并不意味着和解。

en: We don't have to return to the same relationship, nor do we have to accept the same harmful behaviors from an offender.
cn: 我们不必回到原来的关系，也不必接受冒犯者同样的有害行为。

en: Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims.
cn: 宽恕对某些受害者的心理健康至关重要。

en: It propels people forward rather than keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma.
cn: 它推动人们前进，而不是让他们在情感上陷入不公正或创伤之中。

en: Carrying the hurt or anger of an offense leads the body to release stress chemicals.
cn: 带着伤害或愤怒会让身体释放压力化学物质。

en: Eliminating the perpetual flow of those chemicals may also explain why forgiveness provides physical health benefits.
cn: 消除这些化学物质的持续流动也可以解释为什么宽恕对身体健康有益。

en: There are scenarios in which forgiveness is not the best course.
cn: 有些情况下宽恕不是最好的选择。

en: Sometimes the victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive.
cn: 有时，当受害者允许自己不原谅时，他们会变得更有力量。

en: Forgiveness can be challenging.
cn: 宽恕可能具有挑战性。

en: This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all.
cn: 当冒犯方给出不真诚的道歉，或者他们根本没有道歉时，尤其如此。

en: However, it's often the healthiest path forward.
cn: 然而，这通常是最健康的前进道路。

en: It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender, reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life.
cn: 培养宽恕很重要，可以通过对冒犯者产生同情，反思该行为是出于恶意，还是由冒犯者生活中充满挑战的环境造成的。

en: What about forgiving ourselves?
cn: 那原谅自己呢？

en: We sometimes need to take responsibility for mistakes, but intense guilt and shame aren't a desirable outcome in the long run.
cn: 我们有时需要为错误承担责任，但强烈的内疚和羞耻从长远来看并不是理想的结果。

en: Forgiving yourself may seem like an ambiguous process.
cn: 原谅自己可能看起来是一个模糊的过程。

en: You can begin by acknowledging that you are at fault, take responsibility for the hurt you caused, then reflect on why the event occurred.
cn: 你可以从承认自己有过错开始，为你造成的伤害承担责任，然后反思事件发生的原因。

en: Draw the lessons you learned and try to avoid committing a similar offense in the future.
cn: 吸取教训，并努力避免将来再犯类似的错误。

en: The Glasgow subway first opened in 1896 as a cable- hauled system.
cn: 格拉斯哥地铁于1896年首次开通，当时是一个电缆牵引系统。

en: It is generally recognized as the world's third underground railway, after London and Budapest.
cn: 它被普遍认为是世界上第三条地下铁路，仅次于伦敦和布达佩斯。

en: In its long history, it has never been expanded remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations.
cn: 在其漫长的历史中，它从未扩建过，仍然是一条只有15个车站的单环线。

en: At its peak, it served the shipyard workers on the south side of the city.
cn: 在鼎盛时期，它为城市南部的造船厂工人提供服务。

en: In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry, and the popularity of private transport grew.
cn: 在20世纪60年代，造船业出现衰退，私人交通的普及率上升。

en: As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership.
cn: 结果，地铁乘客量迅速下降。

en: It ran with little further change until 1977 when its new operators closed it for major modernization investment.
cn: 它几乎没有进一步变化地运营着，直到1977年新的运营商为了重大现代化投资而关闭了它。

en: Carriages were replaced, ventilation was improved, and the main depot was also renovated and fitted with connecting tracks to replace the outdated crane transfer mechanism.
cn: 车厢被更换，通风得到改善，主站场也得到了翻新，并安装了连接轨道以取代过时的起重机转运机制。

en: The subway in its present form reopened for operation in April 1980.
cn: 现在形式的地铁于1980年4月重新开放运营。

en: Since its relaunch, the subway has seen a revival in its fortunes.
cn: 自重新开通以来，地铁的命运出现了复苏。

en: It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city center.
cn: 它作为其他交通方式的可行替代方案，在很大程度上缓解了市中心的交通拥堵。

en: In 1996, the system reached an important milestone—100 years.
cn: 1996年，该系统达到了一个重要的里程碑——100周年。

en: To commemorate this special event, the color scheme of the train carriages was updated.
cn: 为了纪念这一特殊事件，火车车厢的配色方案得到了更新。

en: Recently, high- tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations.
cn: 最近，智能卡售票机和智能闸机等高科技系统在所有地铁站投入使用。

en: The smart card provides more convenient travel and passengers simply top up their cards and tap them to get in and out the subway.
cn: 智能卡提供了更方便的出行，乘客只需充值并刷卡即可进出地铁。

en: Since its launch, the technology has been adopted by more than 100,000 subway customers.
cn: 自推出以来，该技术已被超过10万名地铁乘客采用。

en: If you visit the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, chances are you will remember the roadside or campground bears above all else.
cn: 如果你参观大烟山国家公园，你很可能会记住路边的熊或露营地的熊，而不是其他任何东西。

en: Bears are the most popular animals in a number of our national parks.
cn: 熊是我们许多国家公园中最受欢迎的动物。

en: In these mountains, where the population of bears runs into the hundreds, opportunities to observe these large wild animals are plentiful during the summer.
cn: 在这些山脉中，熊的数量达到数百只，夏季观察这些大型野生动物的机会非常多。

en: Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans.
cn: 由于国家公园是野生动物保护区，不允许干扰当地动物，多年的保护已经打破了野生熊类对人类的恐惧。

en: Now, instead of depending on their own resources for a living, many bears patrol park roads and campgrounds.
cn: 现在，许多熊不再依靠自己的资源谋生，而是在公园道路和露营地巡逻。

en: They give the garbage cans a frequent going over.
cn: 它们经常翻找垃圾桶。

en: An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them.
cn: 公园游客偶尔提供食物，这是一种非法且危险的做法，使它们变成了乞丐。

en: Bears are very often hungry and since they will feed on almost any kind of plant or animal, garbage is quite acceptable.
cn: 熊经常饥饿，而且它们几乎以任何种类的植物或动物为食，所以垃圾是完全可以接受的。

en: Feeding them, however, represents misguided kindness because the bears come to expect such generosity from everyone and consequently, trouble could lie ahead.
cn: 然而，喂食它们代表着被误导的善意，因为熊会开始期待每个人的慷慨，因此麻烦可能就在前方。

en: Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.
cn: 公园规则禁止喂食熊。

en: Violators are arrested.
cn: 违规者会被逮捕。

en: Every year, doctors who have offices near the park treat a number of cases of bear bites and bear scratches.
cn: 每年，在公园附近开诊的医生都会治疗许多熊咬伤和熊抓伤的病例。

en: Some of the accidents have come about in strange ways.
cn: 有些事故是以奇怪的方式发生的。

en: One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs, when the mother bear appeared and insisted upon having some of the food.
cn: 一名男子正在喂两只小熊时，母熊出现了并坚持要分一些食物。

en: Shoving the big bear aside with one hand, the man continued feeding the cubs when suddenly he was struck a fierce blow in the face.
cn: 该男子一只手将大熊推开，继续喂小熊，突然他的脸被狠狠击打了一下。

en: A bear, prompted by the food that a lady kept offering to him, entered the car where the generous person was sitting.
cn: 一只熊被一位女士不断提供的食物所吸引，进入了那位慷慨之人所坐的汽车。

en: Her efforts to push the bear out of the car resulted in injuries.
cn: 她试图把熊推出车外，结果受了伤。

en: A man required medical attention after he applied a lighted cigarette to a bear's nose.
cn: 一名男子将点燃的香烟戳向熊的鼻子后需要接受医疗救治。

en: Another man tried to boost a bear into the front seat of his car so that he might take a picture of a bear sitting beside his wife who was behind the wheel.
cn: 另一名男子试图把一只熊推到他汽车的前座上，以便拍一张熊坐在他开车的妻子旁边的照片。

en: Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small, but there's always that chance, for a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar.
cn: 因为熊更喜欢道路和露营地，徒步旅行者在公园小路上遇到熊的可能性很小，但总有机会，因为熊似乎能知道你是否带了午餐或糖果棒。

en: He may even insist on taking it.
cn: 它甚至可能会坚持要拿走。

en: Why do we form opinions or attitudes about someone or something without really knowing much about them?
cn: 为什么我们在不太了解某人或某事的情况下就对他们形成看法或态度？

en: Just hearing something good or bad about a person, a place or thing can influence our opinions positively or negatively.
cn: 仅仅听到关于一个人、一个地方或一件事的好坏，就能积极或消极地影响我们的看法。

en: But letting the opinions of another person determine what our opinions will be is dangerous.
cn: 但让他人的看法决定我们的看法是危险的。

en: Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice.
cn: 在真正了解某人或某事之前就形成对他们的看法被称为偏见。

en: "Pre-" means before and "judice" refers to judgment.
cn: 'Pre-'意思是之前，'judice'指的是判断。

en: Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge.
cn: 因此，偏见意味着在拥有足够知识之前就做出判断。

en: We can be prejudiced toward or against someone or something.
cn: 我们可能对某人或某事有偏见，也可能反对某人或某事。

en: In either case, we are only allowing ourselves to see half of the picture.
cn: 无论哪种情况，我们都只允许自己看到一半的画面。

en: Very few people or things in this world are all good or all bad.
cn: 这个世界上很少有人或事物是全好或全坏的。

en: Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half truths or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.
cn: 偏见态度通常基于神话、半真半假的信息或不正确的信息，而且它们是危险的，因为它们会阻止我们了解某人或某事的真相。

en: People form prejudices against others for many reasons- differences in their race, religion, gender or occupation.
cn: 人们出于许多原因对他人形成偏见——种族、宗教、性别或职业的差异。

en: Prejudices keep people apart.
cn: 偏见使人们疏远。

en: They keep us from really knowing and understanding each other.
cn: 它们阻止我们真正了解和理解彼此。

en: We should feel proud of who we are and the group of people we represent.
cn: 我们应该为自己是谁以及我们代表的群体感到自豪。

en: If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.
cn: 然而，当我们认为自己的群体或信仰比周围的人更好时，如果自豪感开始转变为优越感，那么我们就会开始形成可能有害的偏见态度。

en: For example, the prejudiced attitudes of one group may keep another group from attending certain schools, from living in any neighborhood they want, or from getting a job or a promotion.
cn: 例如，一个群体的偏见态度可能会阻止另一个群体进入某些学校，住在他们想住的任何社区，或者获得工作或晋升。

en: Extreme feelings of prejudice have caused the deaths of innocent people.
cn: 极端的偏见情绪已经导致了无辜者的死亡。

en: We are responsible for our own thoughts and opinions.
cn: 我们对自己的想法和观点负责。

en: When we let someone else tell us what to think about someone or something, we are giving up some control of our own lives.
cn: 当我们让别人告诉我们该对某人或某事持什么看法时，我们就是在放弃对自己生活的一些控制。

en: Before you form an attitude or opinion, find out for yourself about the person or the thing in question.
cn: 在你形成态度或观点之前，自己去了解那个人或那件事。

en: Sometimes we don't realize that we hold prejudiced attitudes toward or against someone or something.
cn: 有时我们没有意识到我们对某人或某事持有偏见态度。

en: We need to carefully examine our lives and our fears, and to ask ourselves whether our attitudes come from our personal knowledge and experience or from rumors and fear of the unknown.
cn: 我们需要仔细审视我们的生活和恐惧，并问自己我们的态度是来自个人知识和经验，还是来自谣言和对未知的恐惧。

en: The good news about prejudice is that we are not born with it.
cn: 关于偏见的好消息是，我们并非生来就有偏见。

en: Prejudiced attitudes and opinions develop over time.
cn: 偏见态度和观点是随着时间的推移而形成的。

en: But with education and knowledge, we can replace our prejudices with cooperation and understanding.
cn: 但通过教育和知识，我们可以用合作和理解取代偏见。

en: When I started high school, it was a shock.
cn: 当我开始上高中时，那是一种震撼。

en: I had spent eight years fighting my way to be the most popular kid in the Catholic school student body.
cn: 我花了八年时间努力成为天主教学校学生群体中最受欢迎的孩子。

en: I had been a big, tough 8th grader and suddenly I was a lonely 9th grader bullied by the big, tough 12th grade seniors who ran the high school.
cn: 我曾是一个高大、强悍的八年级学生，突然我成了一个孤独的九年级学生，被那些管理高中的高大、强悍的十二年级高年级学生欺负。

en: I realized then that it's nice to strive for something, but that you also have to enjoy the moment you're in and be happy where you are.
cn: 那时我意识到，为某事而努力是好的，但你也必须享受当下，对你所在之处感到快乐。

en: Rock and roll had always been an important part of my life.
cn: 摇滚乐一直是我生活中重要的一部分。

en: I remember my friends and I used to drive around until the late hours of the nights listening to the music of Rock and Roll Legends.
cn: 我记得我和朋友们常常开车兜风直到深夜，听着摇滚传奇的音乐。

en: During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime.
cn: 在那些青少年时期，我建立了我以为会持续一生的友谊。

en: Most people that age think the same thing, but people drift apart.
cn: 大多数那个年纪的人都这么想，但人们会逐渐疏远。

en: Jobs, families and tragedies separate people from those lasting friendships.
cn: 工作、家庭和悲剧将人们与那些持久的友谊分开。

en: The tragedy that separated me from my friends forever was the Vietnam war.
cn: 将我与朋友们永远分开的悲剧是越南战争。

en: A year after I graduated from high school, I left for Vietnam.
cn: 高中毕业一年后，我前往越南。

en: I came back, burned out, and tired, as though I had lived 10 lifetimes in the short span of 14 months, the 14 months I was in the war.
cn: 我回来了，精疲力竭，疲惫不堪，仿佛在那短暂的14个月里活了十辈子——我在战争中的14个月。

en: I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school.
cn: 我无法与高中时的朋友们产生共鸣。

en: They still seem childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me.
cn: 他们似乎仍然很幼稚，关心那些对我来说不重要的幼稚事情。

en: I was still trying to cope with the death, destruction and evil I had seen in Vietnam.
cn: 我仍在努力应对我在越南看到的死亡、毁灭和邪恶。

en: I felt like we had done terrible things to innocent people there and in turn, I had seen terrible things done to my friends.
cn: 我觉得我们对那里的无辜人民做了可怕的事情，反过来，我也看到可怕的事情发生在我的朋友身上。

en: I withdrew for my friends and started college.
cn: 我从朋友们身边退出，开始了大学生活。

en: Then I quit college and took many different jobs.
cn: 然后我退学了，做了许多不同的工作。

en: I spent a lot of my time and money on alcohol and other drugs.
cn: 我花了很多时间和金钱在酒精和其他毒品上。

en: Finally, in an effort to get my life going in the right direction again, I sold everything and took what little money I had and bought myself an airplane ticket to Israel.
cn: 最后，为了让我的人生再次回到正确的方向，我卖掉了一切，带上仅有的一点钱，给自己买了一张去以色列的机票。

en: I went there to study history.
cn: 我去那里学习历史。

en: While studying at Haifa University, I met my wife, who was also an American student.
cn: 在海法大学学习期间，我遇到了我的妻子，她也是一名美国学生。

en: I now teach in a high school back in America.
cn: 我现在在美国的一所高中教书。

en: I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago.
cn: 我看着我的学生，看到他们在为许多我多年前挣扎过的同样的事情而挣扎。

en: As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.
cn: 作为一名教师，我尽我所能帮助他们渡过难关。

en: Thanks for inviting me out tonight.
cn: 谢谢你今晚邀请我出来。

en: I've been wanting to try this place for weeks.
cn: 我几周前就想试试这个地方了。

en: I usually pass it on my way home from work but never seem to have time to stop.
cn: 我经常在下班回家的路上经过这里，但似乎从来没有时间停留。

en: I've been dying to come here as well.
cn: 我也一直很想来这里。

en: I was worried that the menu might not be accommodating, but one of my close friends ate here last week.
cn: 我担心我可能不适应这里的菜单，不过我的一个密友上周在这里吃过饭。

en: She's a vegetarian.
cn: 她是个素食主义者。

en: She told me that there were a lot of options for her and they offered alternative dishes.
cn: 她告诉我，这里选择很多，饭店会提供替代性的菜品。

en: But you're not vegetarian, are you?
cn: 但你不是素食主义者吗？

en: Well, not entirely.
cn: 嗯，不完全是。

en: I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs.
cn: 我一点肉也不吃，但是鱼、海鲜或者鸡蛋是没有问题的。

en: Isn't that very difficult?
cn: 那这岂不是很艰难？

en: I can't imagine giving up a premium, juicy steak or bacon cheeseburgers.
cn: 我是很难想象，如何能放弃优质、多汁的牛排或培根芝士汉堡。

en: I wouldn't know.
cn: 我不知道。

en: My parents followed the same diet.
cn: 我的父母也遵循同样的饮食习惯。

en: Even when I was younger, we never had meat during meals.
cn: 即使在我小的时候，我们吃饭时也从来不吃肉。

en: And I never really had a craving to try it.
cn: 而且我从来也不想去尝试一下。

en: I bet it would be hard though, giving up something you're accustomed to eating.
cn: 我敢说，放弃你习惯吃的东西其实是很难的。

en: I tried cutting back on coffee in the morning and it was awful.
cn: 我试过在早上减少咖啡的摄入，可情况很糟糕。

en: Come to think of it.
cn: 不过仔细想想。

en: It was probably even worse for my colleagues that had to deal with me at morning meetings.
cn: 对那些需要在晨会上与我打交道的同事来说，情况可能更糟糕。

en: That's even harder to imagine you without coffee.
cn: 更难想象，你居然能不喝咖啡。

en: So you say your parents also followed a partially vegetarian diet.
cn: 你说你的父母也是部分素食主义者。

en: Why did they decide to do that?
cn: 那他们为什么决定这样做？

en: That's an interesting question.
cn: 这个问题很有趣。

en: I never thought to ask them though.
cn: 但是我是从来没想过问他们。

en: My best guess is for health reasons.
cn: 我猜最大的可能是出于健康原因。

en: They're not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts, but they're serious about their health.
cn: 他们对动物保护工作并没有很积极，了解也不多，但他们对自己的健康很重视。

en: Both are in their 70s now, but eat organic as often as possible and take part in regular physical exercise.
cn: 他们现在都已经70多岁了，但尽可能常吃有机食品，并定期参加体育锻炼。

en: Neither of them has any health problems and they hardly ever get sick.
cn: 他们没有任何健康问题，而且几乎没有生病过。

en: In that case, I might give it a try someday.
cn: 既然如此，我也许有一天会试一试。

en: Now back to the menu, what are you going to have?
cn: 那我们说回菜单吧，你打算吃什么？

en: How did your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager go?
cn: 你和经理开的年度绩效评估会进展如何？

en: Did you get much in the way of praise?
cn: 你获得了很多表扬吗？

en: Next to zero.
cn: 几乎没有。

en: When we came to the part about discussing my areas for growth, he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem.
cn: 当我们谈到我的成长空间时，他直截了当地告诉我，我的态度有问题。

en: But he wouldn't really expand on that description.
cn: 但他并没有就这一点做进一步的阐述。

en: He said it's the little things I do and say.
cn: 他说这都是我说话做事方面的小问题。

en: Did you ask him for a specific example?
cn: 你有没有向他询问具体的事例？

en: I did ask him a few more questions to try and narrow it down.
cn: 我确实问了他几个问题以试图缩小范围。

en: He said my constant questioning of him and his decisions was the most obvious example he could give.
cn: 他说我对他和他的决定提出不断质疑就是最明显的例子。

en: Then our conversation was swiftly brought to a close.
cn: 然后我们的谈话就迅速结束了。

en: I had a similar experience once.
cn: 我也曾有过类似的经历。

en: My manager told me I was too honest.
cn: 我的经理告诉我，我太诚实了。

en: In most cases, I thought my honesty was helpful, as did my colleagues.
cn: 大多数情况下，我认为我的诚实是有帮助的。我的同事也这么认为。

en: But my manager thought otherwise.
cn: 但我的经理却并不这么想。

en: Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made.
cn: 有些经理确实会采用操纵性的语言来掩饰他们所做的不合理的选择。

en: They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues of conflict or complaints about unfairness.
cn: 他们不会运用理性的论证能力来解决冲突或者对于不公平的抱怨。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: Some employ their persuasive vocabulary, an influential communication style, to win workplace arguments by compelling people to perform the intended action.
cn: 有些人运用他们的说服性的说辞，运用有支配力的沟通方式，通过迫使人们执行预期的行动方案，来赢得职场中的争论。

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: Too honest, isn't that a good thing?
cn: 太过诚实，这难道不是一件好事吗？

en: I thought that's surely something we should have covered earlier in the section discussing strengths and talents.
cn: 我认为，这确实是我们在讨论优势和天赋这一部分的时候，早就该讨论的内容。

en: But no.
cn: 然而事实并非如此。

en: Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue since it made people feel uncomfortable, or at least it made the most powerful folks feel uncomfortable.
cn: 诚实被认为是一种罪过而不是一种美德，因为它让人们感到不舒服，或者说，至少让最有权势的人感到不舒服。

en: Indeed, rhetoric is viewed by many philosophers as the method through which the powerful accumulate more power.
cn: 的确，许多哲学家认为修辞是权贵们积累更多权力的方法。

en: By virtue of having the loudest voice, they're able to command greater attention and to further assert their dominance, even when what they're saying doesn't really make much sense.
cn: 他们通过获得最响亮的声音，取得了更多的关注，并进一步宣示他们的统治地位，即使他们所说的并没有什么意义。

en: And retaining their power and prestige is their priority.
cn: 而保持他们的权力和威信是他们的首要任务。

en: It's what makes the most sense to a lot of them.
cn: 这对他们中的很多人来说是最有意义的。

en: Athletes are seen as heroes because they can do things that most of us can't do.
cn: 运动员被视为英雄，因为他们能做到我们大多数人做不到的事情。

en: They can hit fast balls coming at them at nearly 100 miles an hour and leap and hang in the air, seemingly defying gravity.
cn: 他们能以每小时近100英里的速度打出快速的球，并在空中飞跃和悬空，仿佛是在挑战地心引力。

en: They get paid millions of dollars for their efforts, and their names and faces appear on everything from running shoes to advertising boards.
cn: 他们的努力得到了数百万美元的报酬，他们的名字和面孔出现在任何一个角落，从跑鞋到广告牌上。

en: Athletes who are champions also show qualities such as perseverance, dedication and the ability to keep their cool under pressure.
cn: 成为冠军的运动员还表现出坚韧不拔、奉献精神和在压力下保持冷静等诸多品质。

en: Many show those same qualities off the playing field too.
cn: 许多运动员在赛场外也表现出了同样的品质。

en: Stories about superstar athletes teach us about working hard and believing in ourselves and then being passionate about what we do.
cn: 超级明星运动员的故事告诉了我们要努力拼搏，相信自己，对自己的所从事的事情要充满热情。

en: Although it's usually bad behavior that gets an athlete a spot on the 6 o'clock news, many high- profile players work hard to be positive role models to children.
cn: 尽管运动员的不良行为通常也会让他们登上6点钟的新闻，但是有许多高知名度的运动员努力拼搏，成为了孩子们的正面榜样。

en: They raise money for charities and act as mentors talking to student groups and volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school.
cn: 他们为慈善机构筹集资金，作为导师与学生团体交流，并自愿花时间参与活动，来帮助孩子们远离毒品，留在校园学习。

en: Still, even the greatest champions have flaws.
cn: 然而，即使是最伟大的冠军也有缺点。

en: Just because an athlete has the perfect golf swing doesn't mean he is the perfect parent, friend or spokesperson.
cn: 运动员能完成完美的高尔夫挥杆动作并不意味着他是完美的父母、朋友或代言人。

en: They also make mistakes.
cn: 他们也会犯错。

en: Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives can be tough.
cn: 将运动员的职业和个人生活区分开来可能很困难。

en: When a sports star gets in trouble with the law or does something wrong in their private life, fans are often left disappointed.
cn: 当一个体育明星在法律上遇到麻烦或在私人生活中做错事时，粉丝们往往会感到失望。

en: Before he died, baseball star, Mickey Mantle who was plagued with alcohol problems told young ball players and the fans who admired him to play like me, don't be like me.
cn: 棒球明星米奇·曼托（Mickey Mantle）在去世前曾告诉年轻的球手和崇拜他的球迷，要像我一样打球，但不要像我一样做人。

en: We don't need to tell you that weddings can get expensive.
cn: 婚礼可以是非常昂贵的，这一点我们不说你也知道。

en: Even with the most meticulous budgeting, a few unexpected costs are bound to occur.
cn: 即使有最细致的预算，也一定会发生一些意想不到的支出。

en: While most brides tend to accept this as fact, one Canadian woman who is only known as Susan attempted to avoid all wedding costs.
cn: 虽然大多数新娘倾向于接受这个事实，但一位我们只知道她叫做苏珊的加拿大女性试图避免所有的婚礼费用。

en: She did this by asking her friends and family to pay up to attend her wedding.
cn: 她的做法是要求她的朋友和家人支付费用来参加她的婚礼。

en: It went about as well as you'd expect.
cn: 事情和你预想的一样。

en: Susan is causing quite the debate online after posting a bizarre Facebook complaint about her now canceled wedding.
cn: 苏珊在脸书上发布了一条怪异的抱怨，是有关于她目前被取消的婚礼的，该抱怨在网上引起了相当大的争论。

en: Yes, the couple called off the wedding just days before their wedding vows.
cn: 没错，这对夫妇在他们的婚礼宣誓日的前几天就取消了婚礼。

en: Since the guest refused to pay the $1,500 attendance fee, the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold.
cn: 由于客人拒绝支付1500美元的出席费，这场所谓的6万美元的梦幻婚礼被永久搁置。

en: In her long explanation filled with cursing and swearing, the bride accused her friends and family of ruining her marriage and her life.
cn: 在她充满诅咒和脏话的长篇解释中，新娘指责她的朋友和家人毁了她的婚姻和生活。

en: She stated that each guest for the day.
cn: 她说，每个客人只需要支付1500美元，而她却为这一天牺牲了一切。

en: Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget, as she was asking too much from her guests.
cn: 她的伴娘告诉她要坚守住预算，因为她要客人支付的钱太多了。

en: But Susan ignored her.
cn: 但苏珊没有理会她。

en: Not surprisingly, only eight people responded positively to the wedding invitations and money requests.
cn: 不出所料，只有八个人对婚礼邀请和出席费用做出了积极的回应。

en: Realizing they would not be able to afford their dream wedding, Susan's future husband suggested getting married in Las Vegas.
cn: 苏珊的未婚夫意识到他们将无法负担他们的梦想婚礼，建议在拉斯维加斯完婚。

en: The bride quickly shut down the idea, saying she did not want a wedding of gambling and heavy drinking.
cn: 新娘很快地拒绝了这个提议，说她不想要一个充斥着赌博和酗酒的婚礼。

en: It seems her dream wedding has now become a nightmare.
cn: 看来，她的梦想婚礼现在已经变成了一场噩梦。

en: It has long been scientifically established that weather changes can affect people's moods.
cn: 天气变化可以影响人们的情绪，这一点早已在科学上得到证实。

en: Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities.
cn: 现在，一项新的研究提供了温度可以影响人们的性格的证据。

en: This study of over 1.6 million people revealed that 22 degrees Celsius is the perfect air temperature to live in.
cn: 这项针对160多万人所做的研究显示，22摄氏度是最适合居住的空气温度。

en: A city with an average annual temperature closer to 22 tends to have a population who are more agreeable, conscientious, emotionally stable, and outgoing.
cn: 一个年平均气温接近22度的城市，当地人口往往更愉悦、勤勉、情绪稳定并且外向。

en: It is the least taxing temperature for the body to regulate its own temperature.
cn: 该温度对身体调节自身温度的负担最小。

en: The study was observational and didn't show cause and effect.
cn: 这项研究是观察性的，并未证明其因果关系。

en: But the scientists behind it theorize that better weather leads people to leave their home more often.
cn: 但其背后的科学家推断，更好的天气会导致人们更频繁地离开家门。

en: This, in turn, leads to more social interaction, which encourages them to develop a friendlier and socially more acceptable personality.
cn: 这反过来又引起了更多的社会互动，从而鼓励他们发展出更加友好以及更容易被社会接受的个性。

en: Warmer climates also make people feel more positive in general.
cn: 温暖的气候也使人们总体上感觉更积极。

en: They tend to be more agreeable and conscientious.
cn: 他们倾向于更加愉悦和勤勉。

en: The findings might help explain why colder and warmer countries tend to produce people with different personalities.
cn: 这些发现可能有助于解释为什么较冷和较暖的国家往往会产生具有不同性格的人。

en: Roughly speaking, about 40% of a person's personality is determined by their genes, the other 60% by their environment.
cn: 粗略地说，一个人的个性大约有40%是由他们的基因决定的，另外60%是由环境决定的。

en: It was already well known that personality traits vary across geographic regions.
cn: 人们已经清楚地知道，不同的地理区域有不同的性格特征。

en: Scientists also knew that these geographic personality traits are associated with a broad range of consequential outcomes.
cn: 科学家们还了解到，这些地理上的性格特征与一系列广泛的重大结果有关。

en: These outcomes include economic activity, for example, entrepreneurial startup rates, and also crime rates, health behaviors, and health outcomes.
cn: 这些结果涵盖经济活动，例如，创业率、犯罪率、健康行为和健康结果。

en: And it is well established that personality traits differ between countries.
cn: 而且，各国之间的性格特质不同，这一点已得到公认。

en: The research team speculated the two might be linked.
cn: 研究小组推测这两者可能存在联系。

en: To test this, they gave online personality tests to 5,587 Chinese students, and 1.66 million Americans.
cn: 为了测试这一点，他们对5587名中国学生和166万美国人进行了在线性格测试。

en: They then compared the results with the average annual temperature where they grew up.
cn: 然后他们将结果与他们成长所在地的年平均温度进行了比较。

en: The tests measured personality along five well- studied characteristics.
cn: 这些测试按照五种得到充分研究的特征来评估性格。

en: The five were agreeability, conscientiousness, emotional stability, outgoingness, and openness to new experiences.
cn: 这五个特征是随和、尽责、情绪稳定、外向和对新经历的开放程度。

en: In both groups, the researchers found the closer a town's average annual temperature was to 22°, the more its population exhibited those personality characteristics.
cn: 研究人员发现，在这两组当中，一个城镇的年平均气温越接近22°，其人口就越能表现出这些性格特征。

en: However, the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans studied, which suggests that though temperature plays a role, it does not play a dominant role.
cn: 然而，相比美国组而言，中国组的研究结果体现得更加强烈，这表明尽管温度起着一定的作用，但它并没有起主导作用。

en: The effects are fairly weak.
cn: 这些影响是相当微弱的。

en: It's unlikely to lead to many arguments over the temperature setting of the office air conditioner.
cn: 它不太可能引发关于办公室空调温度设置的诸多争论。

en: Today we're talking about loneliness.
cn: 今天我们讨论的是孤独。

en: Loneliness and social isolation are growing public health concerns for people of all ages in the United States, from adolescence to the elderly.
cn: 孤独和社会隔离是日益严重的公共健康问题，其涉及美国所有年龄段的人，包括从青少年到老年人。

en: Public health experts are worried because loneliness seems to be on the rise, and studies have long found correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions that threaten health and longevity.
cn: 公共卫生专家非常担忧，因为孤独感似乎持续上升，而且研究早已发现孤独感与威胁健康和长寿的各种医疗问题之间存在关联。

en: The problem of loneliness may be even greater than we thought.
cn: 孤独的问题可能比我们想象的还要严重。

en: A new national poll found that about 1/3 of older Americans are lonely, and almost as many seniors feel isolated.
cn: 一项新的全国性民意调查发现，大约1/3的美国老年人是孤独的，几乎同等人数的老年人感到与世隔绝。

en: This is a serious problem, as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens.
cn: 这是一个严重的问题，因为研究表明，长期的孤独感对老年公民尤其有害。

en: That's because it can impair older adults' memory and damage their physical and mental health.
cn: 这是因为它可以损害老年人的记忆，并危害他们的身体和精神健康。

en: Chronic loneliness even impacts the life expectancy of seniors, increasing their risk of early mortality.
cn: 慢性孤独甚至影响老年人的预期寿命，增加他们早期死亡的风险。

en: Let's take a closer look at that poll now.
cn: 现在让我们仔细看看这项民意调查。

en: More than 1/3 of seniors in the poll said they felt lonely at least some of the time.
cn: 调查中超过1/3的老年人说他们至少在某些时刻会感到孤独。

en: And 27% said they sometimes or often felt isolated.
cn: 而27%的人说他们时而或经常感到与世隔绝。

en: This reflects how much time the seniors spent with others.
cn: 这都反映了老年人有多少时间能与其他人在一起。

en: Almost 30% said they socialized with friends, family or neighbors once a week or less.
cn: 近30%的人说他们每周能与朋友、家人或邻居有一次社交活动，或者还不到一次。

en: Women were more likely than men to report loneliness.
cn: 女性比男性更有可能去反映自己的孤独感。

en: But there is good news.
cn: 但是也有好消息。

en: It looks like loneliness can be reversed.
cn: 那就是，孤独感似乎是可逆的。

en: But researchers are still trying to determine the best way to do so.
cn: 但研究人员仍在试图确定逆转孤独感的最佳方式。

en: Why is that?
cn: 为何如此呢？

en: Resolving the problem of loneliness among seniors often isn't as simple as getting them together with others or moving them in with their children.
cn: 解决老年人的孤独问题往往不是让他们和其他人在一起或让他们和子女一起住那么简单。

en: In fact, the poll found that seniors who lived with their children were more likely to report feeling lonely than those who didn't.
cn: 事实上，民意调查发现，与子女同住的老年人比不与子女同住的老年人更有可能反映自己感到孤独。

en: This may be because loneliness refers to the discrepancy between actual and desired relationships.
cn: 这可能是因为孤独是指实际关系和期望关系之间的差异。

en: So it's possible that someone who lives alone doesn't meet that definition, while someone in a house full of busy people does.
cn: 因此，独居的人有可能并不符合这个定义，而身处一个众人忙碌的房间中的人反而符合。

en: How can we solve the problem?
cn: 那我们该如何解决这个问题？

en: Well, the researchers assert that it's important to address each person's underlying cause of loneliness, whether it's the death of a spouse, medical problems, or social expectations that haven't been fulfilled.
cn: 研究人员表示，解决每个人孤独的根本原因才是重点，无论是配偶的死亡、医疗问题，还是没有得到满足的社会期望。

en: It's noteworthy that there is one general recommendation.
cn: 有一个概括性的建议值得注意。

en: While finding solutions for loneliness is highly personal, research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact at least once a week.
cn: 虽然寻找解决孤独的方法是高度个体化的，但研究表明，最好的干预措施是参加每周至少一次有意义的社会接触。

en: Depending on the person that could mean volunteering, seeing an old friend or something else.
cn: 对于不同的人而言，这个措施可能意味着志愿服务，与老朋友见面或其他方式。

en: Hello.
cn: 大家好。

en: I am co- founder of the popular female travel community: We Are Travel Girls.
cn: 我是备受欢迎的女性旅游社区'我们是旅行女孩'的联合创始人。

en: We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world.
cn: 我们收集并发布女性在世界各地旅行的故事。

en: We promote women's blogs, we host meetings and events, and are getting ready to launch our 'Travel with Us' trips in Bali, Japan, and Malawi.
cn: 我们也推广女性博客，举办会议与活动，并准备在巴厘岛、日本和马拉维推出'与我们一起旅行'的旅行活动。

en: Before I started We Are Travel Girls, I had a successful 10- year career in finance in London where I advised private clients on their investments.
cn: 在创办'我们是旅行女孩'之前，我成功地在伦敦从事了10年的金融工作，为私人客户的投资提供建议。

en: Having always had a huge love for travel, I finally took the leap and left finance to pursue my dream of starting a travel company.
cn: 由于一直对旅行有着巨大的热爱，我终于跃跃欲试，离开了金融业，去追求我的梦想，创办一家旅游公司。

en: For as long as I can remember, I wanted to be a travel writer.
cn: 从我有记忆起，我就想成为一名旅游作家。

en: Before blogs existed and everything we read was online, I would go to travel writing seminars by writers who were published in travel magazines.
cn: 在博客还未曾出现，我们能在网上阅读一些内容之前，我就会去参加旅游写作研讨会，这些研讨会是由在旅游杂志上发表文章的作者举办的。

en: I was desperate to write for one of those magazines, but didn't know how to break into that industry.
cn: 我很想为这些杂志撰写作品，但却不知道如何进入这个行业。

en: After university, I ended up working in finance, but always had a desire to travel and write about it.
cn: 大学毕业后，我最终从事了金融业，但始终抱有一个愿望，那就是旅行和写作。

en: In 2015, I was looking at ways to leave finance.
cn: 2015年，我正在寻找离开金融业的路径。

en: And my best friend Vanessa, who grew up on a ranch on the central coast of California, suggested starting a blog.
cn: 而我最好的朋友瓦妮莎，她在加州中央海岸的一个牧场上长大，建议我们开一个博客。

en: But when we started creating it, we realized that was the same thing every girl was doing.
cn: 但当我们开始创建时，我们意识到，每个女孩都在做的同样的事情。

en: So we turned our attention to creating a community among these women.
cn: 因此，我们转变注意力，选择在这些女性群体中间创建一个社区。

en: This led us to start We Are Travel Girls, which has now grown into a community of over 200,000 followers.
cn: 这就促使我们创办了'我们是旅行女孩'，现在它已经发展成为一个拥有20多万名关注者的社区。

en: To anyone thinking about becoming a travel writer, I would suggest they first try and look for a unique way to enter the industry.
cn: 对于任何考虑成为旅游作家的人，我建议他们首先尝试并寻找一种独特的方式进入这个行业。

en: There are a lot of travel writers now and it can be hard to stand out from the crowd, which is really why we started We Are Travel Girls.
cn: 现在有很多旅行作家，要从人群中脱颖而出可能很困难，这确实是我们创办'我们是旅行女孩'的原因。

en: Be prepared to work hard if you want to turn it into a full- time business and try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience.
cn: 如果你想把它变成全职事业，你就要做好努力耕耘的准备，在你拥有忠实的受众群体之前，尽量不要急于出售广告位。

en: The size of your audience doesn't necessarily need to be huge, but you want them to be engaged.
cn: 你的受众规模不一定要很庞大，但你需要他们能够参与其中。

en: If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off.
cn: 如果你在早期投放了太多的推销活动，就会使得很多受众流失。

en: Hi, Lily, how's the new apartment?
cn: 嗨，Lily，新公寓怎么样？

en: It's okay.
cn: 还可以。

en: What?
cn: 什么？

en: How can it be just okay when last week you were thrilled about the place and kept posting photos of it online?
cn: 上周你还对这地方赞不绝口，还不停地在网上发照片，怎么可能只是还可以？

en: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person.
cn: 唉，上周我搬进来的时候，公寓看起来很舒适，大小刚好适合一个人住。

en: But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.
cn: 但现在看来，它又小又破，而且孤零零的。

en: Ah, that's the problem.
cn: 啊，这就是问题所在。

en: You miss your roommates from university, don't you?
cn: 你很想念大学时的室友吧？

en: I'm going to sound like an idiot, because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me, like watching movies late at night without headphones, or talking loudly early in the morning.
cn: 我说这话可能会特别傻，因为我以前总是向你抱怨我们的寝室有多拥挤，抱怨她们做的所有让我恼火的事情，比如深夜看电影不带耳机，或者清早大声说话。

en: But now I miss them terribly.
cn: 但现在我非常想念她们。

en: Of course you do.
cn: 你当然会想念了。

en: That's perfectly normal.
cn: 这很正常。

en: When I got my first place I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself and get away from my juvenile roommates and all their annoying habits.
cn: 当我有了自己的第一个家时，我记得我迫不及待地想一个人住，远离我那些稚气未脱的室友和他们那些令人讨厌的习惯。

en: But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.
cn: 但后来我开始想念他们，并且感到孤独，觉得我们的宿舍就像天堂一样，尽管我们是六个人挤在一个小房间里。

en: I thought it was just me who felt like that.
cn: 我以为只有我有这种感觉。

en: Look, you lived at home with us, and then you had three roommates, and this is your first time living alone.
cn: 你看，你曾和我们一起住在家里，后来你有了三个室友，这是你第一次独自生活。

en: So it's hard.
cn: 所以这很不容易。

en: But your first apartment is a milestone in your life, and you should celebrate it.
cn: 但是你的第一套公寓是你人生中的一个里程碑，你应该庆祝。

en: Tell me about the apartment.
cn: 跟我说说公寓的情况吧。

en: Actually, it's not bad.
cn: 事实上没那么差。

en: In fact, it's pretty adorable, now that I have decorated it and it has everything I need.
cn: 其实，它还挺可爱的，现在我已经把它装修好了，里面有我需要的一切。

en: I have a kitchen to cook in and a bathroom all to myself, and then another room with my bed at one end, and a sofa, a small table and chairs at the other end.
cn: 我有一个可以做饭的厨房和一个独享的浴室，还有一个房间，一头是我的床，另一头是沙发、小桌子和椅子。

en: That does sound adorable and I can't wait to see it, and neither can mom and dad.
cn: 听起来确实很可爱，我迫不及待地想去看看，爸爸和妈妈也想去。

en: Welcome to our program Book Talk.
cn: 欢迎来到我们的节目BookTalk。

en: Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities.
cn: 今天我们请到的嘉宾是Frank Jones，他是我国教育体制评论家，也是新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。

en: Hello, Susan.
cn: 你好，Susan。

en: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America?
cn: Frank，你支持从根本上改变美国的大学？

en: Yes, I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this.
cn: 是的，我认为高等教育的目的是为年轻人进入劳动力市场做好准备，而我们目前的教育体制没有做到这一点。

en: We're allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers.
cn: 我们把太多的资源分配给了与雇主需求不符的学科。

en: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical, Frank.
cn: Frank，我觉得你对教育的态度有点愤世嫉俗。

en: Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life, rather than just to find well- paid jobs.
cn: 大学的目的肯定是培养年轻人全面参与公民生活，而不仅仅是为了找到高薪工作。

en: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job, let alone a good one.
cn: Susan，许多年轻的毕业生找不到工作，更不用说好工作了。

en: The job market is grim, particularly for students who study the arts.
cn: 就业市场很严峻，对于学习艺术的学生来说尤其如此。

en: I agree that it isn't easy for young people to find work, but you propose closing down all departments that aren't directly related to science and technology.
cn: 我同意年轻人找工作不容易，但你建议关闭所有与科学技术没有直接关系的院系。

en: Is that really the solution?
cn: 这真的是解决办法吗？

en: You're overstating my point.
cn: 你夸大了我的观点。

en: My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering.
cn: 我的观点是，我们需要将更多的预算用于科学和工程等领域。

en: To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music.
cn: 为此，我们需要从文学和音乐等学科中拨款。

en: But the arts have value.
cn: 但艺术是有价值的。

en: They're an important part of our culture.
cn: 它们是我们文化的重要组成部分。

en: Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society.
cn: 学习文学、音乐或雕塑可能不会在这方面找到工作，但它能帮助年轻人更深入地思考世界，从而使他们成为更好的公民，使社会变得更加美好。

en: I agree that the arts are valuable to society, but it's naive to think that not only the most talented, but all students should study them at university level.
cn: 我同意艺术对社会很有价值，但是，认为不只是最有天赋的学生，而是所有学生都应该在大学阶段学习艺术，这种想法太天真了。

en: The arts are very competitive, and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market.
cn: 艺术类专业竞争非常激烈，大多数毕业生最终都会背负大量债务，获得的学位在就业市场上价值不大。

en: Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don't have time to really think anymore?
cn: 你是否曾有过烦恼的感觉，觉得自己没有时间真正地思考了？

en: You're not alone.
cn: 其实你并不孤单。

en: A variety of factors have conspired to rob us of time for reflection about ourselves and our lives.
cn: 各种因素合力剥夺了我们思考自己和生活的 时间。

en: Today, our preoccupied minds are rarely silent.
cn: 如今，我们全神贯注的大脑很少能保持安静。

en: The average person receives hundreds of texts and voice messages a day, and holidays for many of us are action- packed weeks, more likely full of family activities than opportunities for tranquility and contemplation.
cn: 平均每人每天都会收到数百条短信和语音信息，而节日对于我们中的许多人来说，也是充斥着各种活动的一周，更有可能是充满家庭活动的一周，而不是让我们保持宁静和沉思的机会。

en: Regular reflection, however, underlies all great professionals.
cn: 然而，定期反思是所有优秀专业人士的基本准则。

en: It's a prerequisite for you to recharge your mental batteries, see things in a new light and tap into your creativity.
cn: 这是你为自己的精神电池充电、以新的视角看待事物并挖掘创造力的先决条件。

en: Almost all of the great advisors that I have studied have found ways to get away from it all and contemplate their life and work.
cn: 我研究过的几乎所有伟大的导师都会想方设法远离这一切，去深度思考自己的生活和工作。
