en: Some researchers in the field of creativity, in fact, believe that insight occurs during the reflection and relaxation that follows a period of intense activity.
cn: 事实上，一些身处创造领域的研究人员认为，洞察力是在紧张活动之后的反思和放松过程中产生的。

en: Schedule time for reflection about your work, or a particular project you're engaged in.
cn: 我们要安排时间对自己的工作或正在进行的某个项目予以反思。

en: I usually block out half an hour.
cn: 我通常会安排半个小时。

en: Don't answer the phone; push your papers to the side; sketch; make lists; draw mind maps of ideas that come to you.
cn: 不接电话；把文件推到一边；写简述；列清单；把想到的想法画成思维导图。

en: At the end, write down any emerging ideas.
cn: 最后，写下任何新出现的想法。

en: When you're alone, stop worrying and think.
cn: 当你独处时，停止烦恼，静下心来思考。

en: A lot of our down time is spent worrying about troublesome things in our lives or fantasizing about how we'd like our lives to be.
cn: 我们的很多闲暇时间都用来担心生活中的麻烦事，或者幻想我们希望自己的生活是怎样的。

en: Revisit things during moments of relaxation, after a period of intense work.
cn: 在紧张工作之后，利用放松的时刻重新审视事物。

en: This is when we are the most creative.
cn: 这是我们最具创造力的时候。

en: Even before Colorado was a state, it had post offices.
cn: 甚至在科罗拉多成为一个州之前，当地就已经有了邮局。

en: The first opened in 1859 in a settlement founded by migrants searching for gold.
cn: 1859年，第一家邮局在一个由淘金移民建立的聚居地开业。

en: Life could be unpredictable at West- gold failed to appear, drought ruined farmers and settlers clashed with Native Americans.
cn: 西部的生活充满变数——金矿并未出现，干旱毁了农民，定居者与美洲原住民发生冲突。

en: On the settlement's location, now stands a sprawling university campus.
cn: 如今，在聚居地的原址上，矗立着一座占地广阔的大学校园。

en: Amid all the changes, one feature remained constant- the postal service.
cn: 在所有的变化中，有一个特点始终未变，那就是邮政服务。

en: The maps tracing America's westward expansion are telling.
cn: 追溯美国向西扩张的地图就能说明问题。

en: In 1864, there were few postal branches on land controlled by Native Americans, which still accounted for most of the West.
cn: 1864年，美国原住民控制的土地上几乎没有邮政分支机构，而西部的大部分地区仍由原住民控制。

en: Over the next 25 years, post offices grew quickly.
cn: 在接下来的25年里，邮局迅速发展。

en: Colonization of the West could be regarded as a result of big government rather than pioneers.
cn: 西部的殖民化可以说是大政府而非拓荒者的结果。

en: As federal subsidies and land grants tempted people into the deserts and plains, the post kept them connected.
cn: 当联邦补贴和土地赠予吸引人们进入沙漠和平原时，邮政使他们保持了联系。

en: In the mid- 19th century, the post office department was far from a centralized bureaucracy.
cn: 19世纪中期，邮局部门远非一个中央集权的官僚机构。

en: To keep up with migration patterns, postal services were added to existing businesses.
cn: 为了跟上移民模式，邮政服务被添加到现有业务中。

en: The federal government commissioned private wagons to carry the mail.
cn: 联邦政府委托私人马车运送邮件。

en: Short- term contracts were granted to local businessmen to act as postmasters.
cn: 当地商人被授予短期合同，担任邮政局长。

en: These partnerships enabled the mail to quickly follow migrants, helping knit together remote parts of the country.
cn: 这些合作关系使邮件能够迅速跟上移民的脚步，有助于将该国的偏远地区连接起来。

en: Mr. Blevins, a digital historian, wrote a book on the history of the US postal service, he used data science to analyze historical trends.
cn: 数字历史学家布莱文斯先生写了一本关于美国邮政服务历史的书，他利用数据科学分析了历史趋势。

en: Most strikingly, he built an accompanying website, complete with interactive maps.
cn: 最引人注目的是，他建立了一个配套网站，并配有互动地图。

en: They show readers how, within a generation, the postal service helped colonize a continent.
cn: 这些地图向读者展示了邮政服务如何在一代人的时间内帮助殖民了一个大陆。

en: These online interactive maps illustrate the formative power of snail mail.
cn: 这些在线互动地图展示了传统信件邮政的影响力。

en: In last week's lecture, we discussed reasons why people forget things.
cn: 在上周的讲座中，我们讨论了人们忘记事情的原因。

en: This week, we will discuss a surprising reason why we might remember some things- anxiety.
cn: 本周，我们将讨论一个令人惊讶的原因，来解释为什么我们能记住一些事情，那就是焦虑。

en: Think about something as simple as buying a coffee.
cn: 想想诸如买一杯咖啡这样简单的事情。

en: That may not seem like an experience that would make a deep impression on your memory, but anxiety could change that.
cn: 这似乎不会在你的记忆中留下深刻的印象，但焦虑可能会改变这一切。

en: In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels.
cn: 事实上，一项新的研究表明，焦虑水平较高的人可能会比焦虑水平较低的人更好地记住某些信息。

en: That's because higher levels of anxiety may make people more susceptible to negative feelings, putting them in a more negative state of mind.
cn: 这是因为焦虑水平较高的人可能更容易受到负面情绪的影响，使他们处于更加消极的心理状态。

en: That in turn may make them able to better remember some events.
cn: 这反过来又会让他们更好地记住某些事件。

en: Let's take a closer look at that new study now.
cn: 现在让我们来仔细看看这项新研究。

en: In this study, the researchers started by giving 80 undergraduate students an anxiety test.
cn: 在这项研究中，研究人员首先对80名本科生进行了一次焦虑测试。

en: The test measured the participants' anxiety levels over the preceding two weeks.
cn: 测试测量了参与者前两周的焦虑水平。

en: Then, to test memory, the participants were shown a series of neutral words, one at a time.
cn: 然后，为了测试记忆力，研究人员向参与者展示了一系列中性词，每次一个。

en: Some of the words were printed on to photos of negative scenes, meaning images that could affect their emotions negatively, such as a photo of a car accident or a cemetery.
cn: 其中一些单词被印在负面场景的照片上，即可能对他们的情绪产生负面影响的图片，如车祸或墓地的照片。

en: The rest of the words were printed on to photos of neutral scenes, such as a photo of a lake or trees.
cn: 其余的单词则印在中性场景的照片上，如湖泊或树木的照片。

en: Neutral words included words like "table" or "desk" that don't elicit emotion.
cn: 中性词包括'餐桌'或'书桌'等不会引起情绪波动的词。

en: Later, the participants were asked to think back to the words they were shown earlier, which caused them to reenter either a negative or a neutral mindset.
cn: 之后，参与者被要求回想他们之前看到的单词，这使他们重新进入消极或中立的心态当中。

en: The participants were then presented with another set of neutral words, and their memory of these new words was tested.
cn: 然后，参与者又看到了另一组中性词，并测试了他们对这些新词的记忆。

en: The researchers found that the new words presented to people in a negative mindset were better remembered by people with higher levels of anxiety than those with lower levels of anxiety.
cn: 研究人员发现，与焦虑水平较低的人相比，焦虑水平较高的人对呈现给处于消极心态的人的新词记忆更好。

en: In other words, when highly anxious individuals took in otherwise emotionally neutral information that was presented to them, it became colored by their negative mindset, making them remember the information better.
cn: 换句话说，当高度焦虑的人接受了呈现给他们的原本情绪中性的信息时，这些信息就会被他们的消极心态所影响，从而使他们更好地记住这些信息。

en: But these same effects were not seen in people with low levels of anxiety.
cn: 但在焦虑程度低的人身上却看不到同样的效果。

en: Previous studies have found that extreme levels of anxiety, such as those experienced by people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, can be quite detrimental to memory and cognitive performance.
cn: 此前的研究发现，极度焦虑，例如被诊断出患有焦虑症的人所经历的焦虑，会对记忆和认知能力造成相当大的损害。

en: But the highly anxious people in this study represent individuals who are managing their anxiety and for whom anxiety is not a serious problem.
cn: 但本研究中的高度焦虑者代表的是正在控制焦虑的人，对他们来说，焦虑并不是一个严重的问题。

en: Over the past 20 years, the Internet has gradually become a dominant feature of our lives.
cn: 在过去20年里，互联网逐渐成为我们生活的主导特征。

en: It has changed how we communicate with each other, and it has definitely transformed the way we do business with each other.
cn: 它改变了我们相互沟通的方式，也无疑改变了我们经商的方式。

en: Marketing has also changed in a number of ways.
cn: 市场营销也在许多方面发生了变化。

en: For instance, in the past consumers had to call a phone number and patiently wait on hold, in order to get the information they wanted.
cn: 例如，过去消费者必须拨打一个电话号码并耐心等待，才能获得他们想要的信息。

en: Today, they want the information immediately.
cn: 如今，他们会想要立即获得信息。

en: They'll go to the company's social media page and post comments and questions, expecting to receive an immediate response.
cn: 他们会在公司的社交媒体页面上发表评论和提问，希望立即得到回复。

en: If they don't get their questions answered soon, they'll move on to another company that will answer them quickly.
cn: 如果他们的问题不能很快得到回复，他们就会转到另一家能快速回复他们问题的公司。

en: Marketing departments today need to follow technological development.
cn: 如今，营销部门需要紧跟技术发展。

en: For example, this year's smartphone is smarter than last year's; self- driving cars are now on the road.
cn: 例如，今年的智能手机比去年的更智能；自动驾驶汽车已经上路。

en: Marketers have to do research on which technologies are coming into being.
cn: 营销人员必须对即将出现的技术进行研究。

en: Otherwise they risk being left behind in the virtual dust.
cn: 否则，他们就有可能被虚拟尘埃抛在后面。

en: Marketing has also changed due to the importance of video.
cn: 由于视频的重要性，市场营销也发生了变化。

en: People don't just want to read text; they want to watch things happening.
cn: 人们不只想阅读文字，还想观看正在发生的事情。

en: Companies now have to explore how they can use video on a consistent basis to share information about their businesses.
cn: 公司现在必须探索如何持续使用视频来分享业务信息。

en: Fortunately, it's extremely easy to shoot something these days.
cn: 幸运的是，如今拍摄视频非常容易。

en: All you need is a smartphone.
cn: 您只需要一部智能手机。

en: But what's the result of all this?
cn: 但这一切的结果是什么呢？

en: Shorter attention spans.
cn: 注意力持续时间缩短。

en: We are the same people that we were 20 years ago.
cn: 我们还是20年前的我们。

en: Not only have we grown accustomed to getting the information we want instantaneously, our attention spans are much shorter.
cn: 我们不仅已经习惯于即时获取我们想要的信息，而且我们的注意力持续时间也更短了。

en: If something doesn't capture our attention within a few seconds, we're on to the next piece of content.
cn: 如果某样东西不能在几秒钟内吸引我们的注意力，我们就会去看下一个内容。

en: Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customer's emotions and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible.
cn: 营销人员需要想办法直接触动客户的情感，而且要想办法尽快做到这一点。

en: Once people are emotionally engaged, they'll stick with you.
cn: 一旦人们在情感上投入，他们就会跟着你。

en: If marketing has changed this much in the past 20 years, imagine what the next 20 years will bring.
cn: 如果营销在过去20年发生了如此大的变化，那么想象一下未来20年会发生什么变化吧。

en: In a recent survey, only 9% of marketers could say with confidence that their marketing efforts were actually working.
cn: 在最近的一项调查中，只有9%的营销人员可以肯定地说，他们的营销工作确实有效。

en: Their confidence is being shaken, because the rules of the game change every year.
cn: 他们的信心正在动摇，因为游戏规则每年都在变化。

en: That's why it's important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators.
cn: 因此，营销人员必须关注最新的技术发展，并考虑与技术创新者合作。

en: That way, they'll be moving at the same pace as the tech industry.
cn: 这样，他们就能与科技行业同步发展。

en: You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work, which is interesting when considering the extent to which people sacrifice friendships, or at least the time they spend with friends, because of the extended hours they're devoting to work.
cn: 你可能会惊讶地发现，友谊的益处不仅限于人们的社交生活，还延伸到了他们的工作中。考虑到人们因为延长工作时间而牺牲友谊的程度，或者至少牺牲了与朋友相处的时间，这就很有意思了。

en: Just last week, I was remarking to a colleague that I'm content with only one social engagement per week.
cn: 就在上周，我还对一位同事说，我每周只参加一次社交活动就很满足了。

en: But according to recent research, that's evidently not enough.
cn: 但根据最近的研究，这显然是不够的。

en: In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self- esteem and wellbeing.
cn: 在一项对700多名受访者进行的初步研究中，美国一所大学的学者分析了朋友相对于家人对自尊和幸福的影响。

en: Friends came out substantially on top.
cn: 结果显示，朋友的影响最大。

en: That's because to be someone's mate is a voluntary act, unlike family who people rarely get to choose.
cn: 这是因为成为他人的伙伴是一种自愿行为，而家人则不同，人们很少有机会选择家人。

en: The researchers found that when people choose to cultivate and maintain supportive friendships with an individual, it means that the person is valued and worthy of their limited time.
cn: 研究人员发现，当人们选择与某个人培养并保持相互支持的友谊时，这意味着这个人是有价值的，值得他们花费有限的时间。

en: Such sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self- esteem.
cn: 这种重视和值得的情感会增强我们的自尊。

en: The second study comprised more than 300 participants.
cn: 第二项研究有300多人参加。

en: It proved that the better we feel about ourselves, the more likely we'll perform our job confidently and competently.
cn: 研究证明，我们对自己的感觉越好，就越有可能自信、称职地完成工作。

en: This follow- up study found that non- work friends even improve people's job satisfaction.
cn: 这项后续研究发现，工作之外的朋友甚至能提高人们的工作满意度。

en: They have as much of an impact on how much they love their jobs as do the friends they have at work, despite not actually being at our place of work.
cn: 他们对工作热爱程度的影响不亚于工作中的朋友，尽管他们实际上并不在我们的工作场所。

en: These types of friends tend to be our preferred outlet for venting about work- related matters.
cn: 这类朋友往往是我们宣泄工作相关事宜的首选渠道。

en: This is an avenue that may not be available at the office.
cn: 这是在办公室可能无法获得的渠道。

en: So even though friendships can be easy to neglect when confronted by pressures at work, or even pressures at home, neglecting our friends can turn out to be harmful and counterproductive.
cn: 因此，尽管在面对工作压力，甚至是家庭压力时，我们很容易忽视友谊，但忽视朋友可能会造成伤害，适得其反。

en: That's why, when determining how to create a better work- life balance, we need to consider not only how to balance work and family demands, but also how to cultivate and sustain supportive friendships.
cn: 因此，在决定如何更好地平衡工作与生活时，我们不仅要考虑如何平衡工作与家庭的需求，还要考虑如何培养和维持相互支持的友谊。

en: It's for this reason that managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements.
cn: 正因为如此，当员工提出灵活工作安排的要求时，管理者绝不应区别对待。

en: It's irrelevant whether their need for a desired schedule is due to, say, parenting responsibilities, or a craving to hang out with the best mate.
cn: 至于他们是出于养育子女的责任，还是渴望与最好的伙伴出去玩，这都无关紧要。

en: What matters is the opportunity to engage in a nourishing activity outside of work.
cn: 重要的是，他们有机会参与工作之外的有营养的活动。

en: That will definitely have a follow- on effect at work.
cn: 这肯定会在工作中产生后续效应。

en: Have you decided what you wish to study?
cn: 你想好学什么了吗？

en: Yes, professor.
cn: 是的，教授。

en: I wish to study architecture.
cn: 我想学习建筑。

en: Ah, that's a wonderful profession.
cn: 啊，那是个很棒的专业。

en: Why did you choose it?
cn: 你为什么选择它？

en: I gave a lot of thought to things you said during our last discussion, and I decided architecture made the most sense for me.
cn: 在我们上次讨论时，我考虑了很多你说过的话，我觉得建筑对我来说最有意义。

en: In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.
cn: 尤其是，设计与工程的巧妙结合深深吸引了我。

en: That's great, but I seem to remember you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics.
cn: 这很好，但我记得你好像一心专注于高深的数学。

en: You no longer think this aspect will be too hard for you?
cn: 你不再认为这方面对你来说太难了吗？

en: No.
cn: 不了。

en: I was doing some online research and I think I should be able to manage.
cn: 我在网上查到了一些资料，我想我应该可以应付。

en: Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required.
cn: 数学可能是我在课程中遇到的最难的科目，但我只要付出必要的努力就可以了。

en: I'm certain the fruits of my labor will pay off.
cn: 我相信我的付出会有回报的。

en: I'm sure that's true.
cn: 我想这是对的。

en: Due to its material nature, architecture is one field where you will be able to clearly witness the contribution you make to a city.
cn: 由于其物质性，在建筑学这门学科中，你可以清楚地看到自己为城市做出的贡献。

en: And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.
cn: 而你所留下的遗产将比我们这些凡夫俗子更加长久。

en: Yeah, I guess that's true too.
cn: 是的，我也觉得是对的。

en: So what subjects do you think I should start brushing up on in preparation?
cn: 那你认为我应该从哪些科目开始复习准备呢？

en: I have the whole summer.
cn: 我有个暑假的时间。

en: These days, architecture is a very diverse and dynamic degree.
cn: 如今，建筑学是一个非常多元化且充满活力的专业。

en: Most universities will encourage you to learn different things from fields as wide- ranging as philosophy and economics.
cn: 大多数大学都会鼓励你从哲学和经济学等广泛的领域学习不同的知识。

en: Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.
cn: 不过，我建议你先从计算机科学开始，因为在你的项目中会有很多复杂的视觉效果需要你制作。

en: Any software in particular you think I should start with?
cn: 那你觉得我应该具体从哪个软件开始学起？

en: Photoshop is a good place.
cn: Photoshop是个不错的选择。

en: If you aren't yet, try to become as proficient as you can with it.
cn: 如果你还不会，那就尽量熟练掌握它。

en: And another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art.
cn: 另外，我建议你尽可能多地学习美术，尤其是西方艺术史。

en: So as I mentioned over the phone, we are looking for someone who is very discreet.
cn: 正如我在电话里提到的，我们要找的是一个非常谨慎的人。

en: I can't stress this enough.
cn: 这一点怎么强调都不过分。

en: I fully understand.
cn: 我完全理解。

en: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile.
cn: 众所周知，Sanchez先生是皇家马德里俱乐部的著名足球运动员，公众形象非常高。

en: This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.
cn: 这就意味着他出门就会被人认出并且骚扰。

en: Yes, I completely understand how imperative it would be to respect Mr. Sanchez's private life.
cn: 是的，我完全理解尊重Sanchez先生的私生活有多么必要。

en: Good.
cn: 很好。

en: As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office.
cn: 作为他的私人助理，你需要为Sanchez先生打理一些日常琐事，由于他的名气，这些事情他自己是做不了的，比如去超市或邮局。

en: So, well, at first sight it may appear that working for a celebrity is very glamorous.
cn: 因此，乍一看，为名人工作似乎很光鲜。

en: Nothing could be further from the truth.
cn: 但事实并非如此。

en: I'm telling you this so that you don't get any false expectations of what the job has to offer you.
cn: 我告诉你这些，是为了让你不要对这份工作抱有任何错误的期望。

en: Thanks.
cn: 谢谢。

en: I understand this too.
cn: 我也明白这一点。

en: This is my first job after graduating from university.
cn: 这是我大学毕业后的第一份工作。

en: So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience.
cn: 坦率地说，我没有什么工作经验。

en: I am, however, very excited about the prospect of joining this company and very keen to start from the bottom in whatever capacity I may be of use.
cn: 不过，我对我加入贵公司之后的前景感到非常兴奋，而且非常希望能从基层做起，无论做什么，我都能派上用场。

en: That's good to hear.
cn: 很高兴听你这么说。

en: You sound very energetic.
cn: 你听起来很有活力。

en: Tell me why do you think you are well suited for this job?
cn: 告诉我，你为什么认为自己非常适合这份工作？

en: Well, firstly, I love football.
cn: 首先，我热爱足球。

en: I'm a lifelong Real Madrid supporter and go to their games every weekend I can.
cn: 我是皇家马德里的终身支持者，每个周末我都会去看他们的比赛。

en: I would simply love to have a job where I'm involved in some capacity with Real Madrid, regardless of the position and salary.
cn: 无论职位高低，薪水多少，我都希望能有一份与皇家马德里有关的工作。

en: And secondly, I think what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool.
cn: 其次，我认为贵公司在体育咨询方面的业务非常出色。

en: And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.
cn: 而且我认为我的语言能力在未来会非常有用。

en: Please tell me more about your language skills.
cn: 请详细介绍一下你的语言能力吧。

en: I am fully fluent in English and Spanish and have a working proficiency in French.
cn: 我的英语和西班牙语非常流利，法语也能应对工作。

en: Adventure sports are undeniably attractive to many energetic and thrill- seeking kids.
cn: 不可否认，探险运动对许多精力充沛、追求刺激的孩子来说极具吸引力。

en: Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing, and mountain biking, thus have lots of appeal.
cn: 诸如攀岩、冲浪、滑雪和山地自行车都是吸引力很强的运动。

en: They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.
cn: 它们没有传统团队运动的诸多规则和压力，但仍然具有户外体育活动的所有好处。

en: When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life.
cn: 如果监督得当，极限运动可以成为健康、平衡生活的一部分。

en: Some adventure sports may be associated with higher risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks, and when not to.
cn: 有些冒险运动可能会有较高的受伤风险，因此孩子们必须弄清楚什么时候该冒险，什么时候不该冒险。

en: Risk- free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears.
cn: 无风险的活动剥夺了孩子们考验自己和克服恐惧的机会。

en: But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice.
cn: 但在一些人看来，正是风险让这些运动成为了错误的选择。

en: They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill- seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.
cn: 他们说，极限运动往往会导致毁灭性的伤害，尤其是这些年轻的、寻求刺激的人可能会尝试对他们来说过于高难度的动作。

en: But let's be real.
cn: 但我们实话实说。

en: Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not.
cn: 不管你愿不愿意，大多数孩子都会做各种危险的事情。

en: Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children.
cn: 探险运动也有许多同样的风险和危险，但它们蕴含的更多是冒险精神、勇气和自主意识，这对培养孩子非常重要。

en: As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids.
cn: 与往常一样，决定什么对孩子最好取决于他们的父母。

en: But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives.
cn: 不过，如果你觉得冒险运动有点过了，那就尝试在他们的生活中引入其他形式的户外探险。

en: Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self- confidence and risk- taking as in adventure sports.
cn: 在星空下露营、钓鱼、观星，甚至只是在树林里玩耍，都能帮助孩子建立与探险运动相同的自信心和冒险精神。

en: The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow.
cn: 今天闪闪发光的小玩意儿明天就会变成废品。

en: Manufacturers don't talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing.
cn: 而制造商们在宣布他们的新产品将取代你的旧产品时，并不会多谈这一点。

en: In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.
cn: 事实上，科技公司往往故意设计出寿命不长、无法维修的设备，让消费者不得不花钱买新的。

en: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score.
cn: 今年，法国政府开始要求科技制造商列出可维修性评分。

en: If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets.
cn: 如果设备可以维修，那么它的寿命就可以延长，这样既可以为消费者省钱，也可以为地球省去大量废弃的小工具所带来的负担。

en: Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.
cn: 有了这些知识，消费者就能更好地选择购买哪些产品。

en: Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year.
cn: 每年大约有5900万吨旧电视机、电脑、屏幕、智能手机、洗衣机和其他电子产品被丢弃。

en: This waste is dangerous.
cn: 这些废弃物非常危险。

en: Batteries explode in recycling facilities.
cn: 电池会在回收设施中爆炸。

en: Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air.
cn: 汞等有毒物质会渗入土壤和地下水，并在空气中扩散。

en: Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
cn: 平板显示器的生产会增加大气中的温室气体。

en: We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem.
cn: 我们需要科技公司带头解决这个问题。

en: If they won't, governments must make them do so.
cn: 如果它们不愿意，政府就必须迫使它们这样做。

en: Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits.
cn: 尽管科技公司经常谈论环境的可持续发展，但许多公司都游说反对修订法律，担心这会侵吞它们的利润。

en: Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies.
cn: 可持续发展固然重要，但对这些公司来说，有市场价值的设计似乎更重要。

en: Consumers should support right- to- repair legislation.
cn: 消费者应支持维修权立法。

en: In this world, damage is a certainty.
cn: 在这个世界上，损坏是必然的。

en: But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
cn: 但我们不能任由事物损坏：我们创造的产物所引起的问题，是可以得到解决的。

en: On average, US workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online.
cn: 美国工人平均每天花10%的工作日时间上网搜索信息、给朋友发邮件或网上购物。

en: This behavior, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.
cn: 这种行为被称为'网络闲逛'，据说每年给雇主造成的生产力损失高达850亿美元。

en: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies.
cn: 大多数网络闲逛研究都聚焦在如何通过互联网监控和计算机使用政策等干预措施来防止员工从事这种行为。

en: But it turns out, such behaviors may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time.
cn: 但事实证明，这种行为可能并不是员工懒惰或浪费时间的表现。

en: Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction.
cn: 在工作中使用社交媒体与更高的员工参与度和工作满意度有关。

en: New research suggests cyberloafing can help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.
cn: 新的研究表明，网络闲逛可以帮助员工应对异常紧张的工作环境。

en: But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels?
cn: 但网络闲逛真的能有效降低员工的压力水平吗？

en: That's the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study.
cn: 这正是我的研究团队在新研究中想要回答的问题。

en: Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini- break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations.
cn: 我们的假设是，网络闲逛可以作为一种小规模的休息，让员工有机会从紧张的工作环境中恢复过来。

en: To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non- work emails and shopping.
cn: 为了验证这一假设，我们要求员工完成一项在线调查，并对他们在网络闲逛、查看非工作邮件和购物上的时间进行排名。

en: We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit, and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at.
cn: 我们还要求他们对工作满意度、辞职意愿以及在工作中遭受虐待，例如被霸凌、威胁或辱骂的频率进行排名。

en: As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit.
cn: 正如你所预料的那样，我们发现，总体而言，工作中受到的虐待越多，工作满意度就越低，辞职的愿望就越强烈。

en: More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection.
cn: 更有趣的是，我们发现网络闲逛有效地缓解了这种关联。

en: That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn't cyberloaf as much.
cn: 也就是说，与不经常上网的同类人相比，那些花更多时间上网和查看电子邮件的受虐待工人的工作满意度更高，辞职意愿更低。

en: This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.
cn: 这表明，网络闲逛对工人来说是一种解压阀，帮助他们从高压体验中恢复过来。

en: While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress it may not only reduce worker turnover, but also ultimately bolster productivity.
cn: 虽然我们没有直接评估网络闲逛如何影响工人的工作表现，但我们相信，通过缓解压力，网络闲逛不仅可以降低工人的离职率，最终还能提高生产率。

en: This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance.
cn: 这与最近的其他研究相吻合，这些研究表明，短暂的休息与更高水平的日常工作表现相关。

en: That isn't to say cyberloafing is always good.
cn: 这并不是说网络闲逛总是好事。

en: Too much time spent on non- work activities likely causes performance to suffer.
cn: 花太多时间在非工作活动上很可能会影响工作表现。

en: All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees.
cn: 总而言之，管理者应该对员工更加宽容。

en: We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.
cn: 我们相信，从长远来看，上班时间网购或上网搜索信息可能会提高员工的工作效率。

en: When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory: It was a treeless plain.
cn: 1854年，Julius Morton搬到内布拉斯加城，他面临着该地区许多定居者共同面临的问题：这是一片没有树木的平原。

en: That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel.
cn: 这意味着没有树木作为建筑材料或燃料。

en: But Morton was one of the world's first conservationists, stating, "For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed."
cn: 但Morton是世界上最早的环境保护主义者之一，他说：'为了繁荣，我们之前采伐了多少森林，现在就应该尽可能种植多少森林。'

en: So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land.
cn: 所以他开始植树，首先从自己的土地开始。

en: By 1860 Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees.
cn: 到1860年，Morton拥有了一片超过300棵树的森林。

en: A few years later, he had more than 1,000.
cn: 几年后，树木的数量达到了1000棵。

en: As the forest grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska.
cn: 随着森林的生长，Morton在内布拉斯加州的影响力也越来越大。

en: This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting.
cn: 这主要是因为Morton创办了内布拉斯加州的第一份报纸《内布拉斯加城市新闻》，他经常在报纸上撰写社论，介绍植树在实用和美学方面的益处。

en: He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture.
cn: 他还组织了内布拉斯加州园艺协会，并在内布拉斯加州农业委员会任职。

en: While serving on the Board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.
cn: 在农业委员会任职期间，Morton萌生了在全州推广植树理念的想法。

en: On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated day for the planting of trees in the State of Nebraska and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves.
cn: 1872年1月4日，Morton起草了一份决议，将4月10日定为内布拉斯加州的植树日，并呼吁人们亲自去植树。

en: Morton called the special event Arbor Day as "arbor" is Latin for "tree".
cn: Morton将这一特别活动称为植树节，因为'arbor'在拉丁语中是'树'的意思。

en: The state government agreed.
cn: 州政府对此表示同意。

en: And on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska.
cn: 1872年4月10日，整个内布拉斯加州欢度了第一个非正式的植树节。

en: Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees.
cn: 植树数量最多的县、市和个人都获得了奖励。

en: That day, an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska- an average of more than six for every man, woman and child in the state.
cn: 当天，内布拉斯加州令人震惊地种植了100万棵树，平均每名男子、妇女和儿童种植了6棵以上。

en: Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname "the Tree Planters State".
cn: 自1885年以来，内布拉斯加州种植了超过70万英亩的树木，赢得了'植树之州'的美誉。

en: Arbor Day became a legal, civic holiday in the state in 1885.
cn: 植树节于1885年成为该州的法定民间节日。

en: It was held on April 22- Julius Morton's birthday.
cn: 植树节在4月22日—Julius Morton的生日这一天举行。

en: In addition to a parade in Nebraska City, Morton introduced what has since become a long- standing Arbor Day tradition: Schoolchildren went outside and planted trees together.
cn: 除了在内布拉斯加城举行游行外，Morton还推出了植树节这一由来已久的传统：学校的孩子们走到户外一起植树。

en: In 1970, nearly a century after Arbor Day was first celebrated, President Richard Nixon declared the last Friday of every April to be observed as National Arbor Day.
cn: 1970年，在植树节首次庆祝近一个世纪后，Richard Nixon总统宣布将每年四月的最后一个星期五定为全国植树节。

en: All 50 states recognize the April observance, although many hold an additional state Arbor Day in a month more suited to local tree planting.
cn: 美国50个州中有11个州承认每年4月的植树节，不过许多州都会在更适合当地植树的月份额外举办一个州植树节。

en: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago.
cn: 现代人类大约产生于20万年前的非洲。

en: They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago.
cn: 然后，在6万年之后的某个时间，现代人的足迹扩张到了欧洲和亚洲。

en: This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known.
cn: 这就是通常所说的'走出非洲'模型。

en: In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance.
cn: 20世纪90年代，这一假说被广泛接受。

en: But this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.
cn: 但这一流行的观点需要修正，尤其是考虑到过去几十年在亚洲的一些重要发现。

en: For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years.
cn: 例如，许多新发现的人类化石，尤其是在中国发现的人类化石，其年代早已经超过了6万年。

en: This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
cn: 这就对现代人在6万年前才迁出非洲的观点提出了质疑。

en: Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
cn: 以最近在中国广西壮族自治区月亮洞发现的两颗现代人牙齿为例。

en: When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old- a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
cn: 当我和我的研究团队对这两颗牙齿进行测定时，我们发现它们已经有7万多年的历史了——如果现代人类在6万年前才迁出非洲，这种情况显然是不可能发生的。

en: So with such findings, what happened exactly?
cn: 那么，有了这样的发现，一切究竟是如何发生的？

en: Where does the most current data suggest we came from?
cn: 根据最新的数据，我们到底来自哪里？

en: The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with?
cn: 我们应该问的第一个问题是，现代人类为什么要离开非洲？

en: If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change.
cn: 如果一个种群完全适应了某个特定的环境，并且能够获得丰富的资源，那么就真的没有理由迁移或产生变革。

en: For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
cn: 例如，非洲的一些猴子的牙齿在数百万年的时间里几乎没有变化，这表明它们找到了一个适合自己的地方。

en: So what happened with humans?
cn: 那么，人类到底发生了什么呢？

en: Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands.
cn: 一些研究人员认为，人口密度的增加迫使较小的人类群体去探索新的土地。

en: Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures.
cn: 其他研究人员则认为，由于东非发生了重大环境事件，人类被迫寻找更青翠的牧场。

en: Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realizing that they were actually moving from one continent to another.
cn: 然而，另一种解释表明，这一切只是因为早期现代人类猎手在追踪他们赖以生存的大型动物，因此他们迁出了非洲，却没有意识到他们实际上是从一个大陆迁往另一个大陆。

en: Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas.
cn: 人类需要每天获得可靠的淡水，而许多沿海地区似乎没有淡水。

en: This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?
cn: 这就引出了另一个问题：现代人类是通过哪条路线走出非洲的？

en: No clear routes across the Mediterranean from North Africa appear to be present, so the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.
cn: 目前似乎还没有从北非横跨地中海的明确路线，因此，人类早期离开非洲进入欧洲和亚洲的路线可能是横跨阿拉伯半岛。

en: Hello, doctor.
cn: 你好，医生。

en: Hello, please take a seat.
cn: 你好，请坐。

en: I have your test results here.
cn: 我这里有你的检查结果。

en: And it's good news.
cn: 是个好消息。

en: The blood test came back clear.
cn: 验血结果没有问题。

en: There is no indication of any digestive issues.
cn: 没有任何消化系统问题的迹象。

en: So then, why do I feel so poorly all the time?
cn: 那为什么我总是感觉不舒服呢？

en: It's probably due to overwork and stress.
cn: 可能是因为过度工作和压力太大。

en: No, it can't be.
cn: 不，不可能。

en: I've always been working hard but I've never felt stress.
cn: 我一直都在努力工作，但从来没有感到过压力。

en: Other people suffering complain about that, but I don't.
cn: 别人会为此抱怨，但我不会。

en: It must be something else.
cn: 肯定是其他原因。

en: What you have just described is a common sentiment.
cn: 你刚才描述的是一种常见的情绪。

en: Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it.
cn: 很多人在承受压力时都无法意识到这一点。

en: You told me you often work long into the night, right?
cn: 你说过你经常工作到深夜，是吗？

en: Yes, most days, in fact.
cn: 是的，事实上大多数时候都是这样。

en: But I've been doing that for about 20 years now.
cn: 但我这样已经有20年了。

en: That doesn't matter.
cn: 那不影响。

en: You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it.
cn: 你可能已经承受了20年的压力而不自知。

en: And now it's catching up to you.
cn: 而现在，它已经找上你了。

en: But what about my feeling tired all the time and not being able to sleep well at night?
cn: 但是我总是感到疲倦，晚上睡不好怎么办？

en: Those are common consequences of stress.
cn: 这些都是压力造成的常见后果。

en: And if you don't sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued.
cn: 如果你睡不好，当然会感到疲劳。

en: I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you.
cn: 我要给你开一些特殊的安眠药。

en: They have a soft, gentle effect and are made from natural ingredients.
cn: 它们药效柔和，由天然成分制成。

en: So your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn't be any negative side effects.
cn: 所以你的肠胃应该可以承受，也不会有任何副作用。

en: Take one with your dinner and come see me after a month.
cn: 晚饭时吃一片，一个月后来找我。

en: If there is no improvement, I'll give you something stronger.
cn: 如果没有改善，我会给你开一些更强效的药。

en: Thank you, doctor.
cn: 谢谢你，医生。

en: That's not all.
cn: 还不止这些。

en: You should try and work less.
cn: 你应该尽量少工作。

en: Is there any way you can decrease your workload?
cn: 有什么办法可以减少你的工作量吗？

en: Hmm... I'd have to think about it.
cn: 嗯...我得考虑一下。

en: I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive.
cn: 我是一名餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。

en: There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.
cn: 很多事情需要跟进和注意。

en: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else.
cn: 我建议你考虑把一些责任交给别人。

en: I'm not asking you to retire, just to slow down a bit.
cn: 我不是让你退休，只是让你放慢脚步。

en: It's for your own health.
cn: 这是为了你自己的健康。

en: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams.
cn: 今天的'新闻人物'节目，我们邀请到的嘉宾是John Williams。

en: The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player.
cn: 你可能对这个名字不太熟悉，但John曾经是一位备受赞誉的篮球运动员。

en: John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25.
cn: John，你年仅25岁就离开了这项运动，让球迷们大跌眼镜。

en: Why did you retire so early?
cn: 你为什么这么早就退役了？

en: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity.
cn: Meg，我喜欢当运动员，但我不喜欢当名人。

en: I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake.
cn: 当我还是一名高中生的时候，我就已经备受瞩目了，高中毕业后，我立即成为了职业运动员，这是一个错误。

en: I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.
cn: 我是个害羞的孩子，我还没准备好接受所有媒体的关注。

en: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career?
cn: 但在你职业生涯最辉煌的时候，你却放弃了数百万美元的收入？

en: Most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary.
cn: 大多数人都无法抗拒如此高薪的诱惑。

en: When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury.
cn: 当你离开这项运动时，有人猜测你与队友有矛盾，甚至受伤了。

en: Not at all.
cn: 完全不是。

en: It was hard to quit.
cn: 我很难放弃。

en: I was tempted to stay in the game, because I loved basketball and I loved my team.
cn: 我很想继续打球，因为我热爱篮球，热爱我的球队。

en: As for money, I turned professional at 18, so I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it because I had great financial advisors.
cn: 至于钱，我18岁就成为职业球员了，所以实际上我已经赚了很多钱，而且因为我有很好的财务顾问，我把大部分钱都存了起来。

en: I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.
cn: 我知道对大多数球员来说，篮球并不是一个长寿的职业，所以我想趁年轻转行。

en: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news.
cn: 好吧，那是20年前的事了，而现在你又上了新闻。

en: You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports.
cn: 你创建了一个基金会，致力于让更多的孩子参加团队运动。

en: Why?
cn: 为什么？

en: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities.
cn: 我上了大学，学习公共卫生，了解到肥胖症流行的严重性，尤其是在贫困社区的儿童和青少年中。

en: I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem.
cn: 在过去的二十年里，我一直在努力缓解这一问题。

en: The foundation is just the latest attempt.
cn: 基金会只是最新的尝试。

en: The foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right?
cn: 基金会是在利用私人捐款支持小学男女生篮球队，对吗？

en: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students too, and also have some public funding.
cn: 实际上，我们也支持中学生球队，而且也利用了一些公共资金。

en: Kate Atkinson was born in York, England in 1951.
cn: Kate Atkinson于1951年出生于英国约克郡。

en: She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author.
cn: 为了获得作家资格，她付出了艰辛的努力。

en: She studied English Literature at a university in Scotland.
cn: 她曾在苏格兰一所大学学习英国文学。

en: After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature.
cn: 1974年毕业后，她攻读了美国文学博士学位。

en: Later, she taught at the university she graduated from and began writing short stories in 1981.
cn: 后来，她在毕业的大学任教，并于1981年开始创作短篇小说。

en: She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.
cn: 1986年，她在'女性自己的短篇小说'大赛中获奖，之后开始为女性杂志写作。

en: Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award.
cn: 她的第一部小说《博物馆的幕后故事》获得了1995年英国年度图书奖。

en: The book is set in Yorkshire, and has been adapted for radio, theater and TV.
cn: 该书以约克郡为背景，被改编成广播、戏剧和电视作品。

en: She has written two plays for a theater in Edinburgh.
cn: 她为爱丁堡的一家剧院创作了两部剧本。

en: The first was called Nice and the second Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August, 2000.
cn: 第一部名为《美好》，第二部名为《抛弃》，于2000年8月作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分上演。

en: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on.
cn: 无论Atkinson以何种体裁写作，她的作品都涉及爱与失去以及如何继续前行的主题。

en: They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor.
cn: 这些主题总是以巧妙的构思和邪恶的幽默感呈现出来。

en: Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentric who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized.
cn: 她的书中往往都有一些古怪的、有时罪恶、常有缺陷的怪人，这些怪人因其完美的形象而变得可信。

en: Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners, that is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behavior, current and fashionable circles of society where appearances count more than true moral character.
cn: 她的作品经常被描述为'风尚喜剧'，也就是说，喜剧表现的是复杂而精致的行为准则，是当前社会的时尚圈子，在这个圈子里，外表比真正的道德品质更重要。

en: A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters rather than punish their bad deeds.
cn: 风尚喜剧倾向于奖励那些聪明狡诈的人物，而不是惩罚他们的恶行。

en: The humor of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.
cn: 风尚喜剧的幽默依赖于语言的机智和俏皮的戏弄。

en: Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
cn: 为什么说适应能力是工作场所的一项重要技能？

en: Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for.
cn: 简单地说，适应能力是雇主越来越看重的一项技能。

en: When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up.
cn: 当你花时间学习新任务而不是抗拒它时，你的工作效率就会提高。

en: You can also serve as an example to your co- workers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward.
cn: 你还可以为那些可能在适应上遇到困难的同事树立榜样，帮助带领团队前进。

en: Strategy consultant Dorie Clark explains it to us this way: I'd say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because, frankly, circumstances change—competitors introduce new products, the economy might enter a recession, customer preferences differ over time, and more.
cn: 战略顾问Dorie Clark是这样向我们解释的：我认为适应能力是职场中的一项重要技能，因为坦率地说，环境是会变化的—竞争对手会推出新产品，经济可能会进入衰退期，客户的喜好也会随着时间的推移而不同等等。

en: If you shake your fist at the sky and say, "Why can't it stay the same?!", that's not going to do very much good.
cn: 就算你对着天空挥舞拳头说：'为什么不能一直保持不变？！'，也起不到什么作用。

en: Instead, you need to recognize when circumstances have changed so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be.
cn: 相反，你需要认识到环境已经发生了变化，进而才能根据实际情况采取适当的行动，而不是希望世界变成什么样。

en: That enables you to make more accurate, informed, and effective choices.
cn: 这样你才能做出更准确、更明智、更有效的选择。

en: Also, the workplace itself has been evolving.
cn: 此外，工作场所本身也在不断演变。

en: Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy.
cn: 如今的工作文化和管理方式往往基于团队合作，而不是僵化的等级制度。

en: Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem- solving technique.
cn: 需要创造力、灵活性和情商的头脑风暴是一种典型的解决问题的技巧。

en: Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company.
cn: 不能或不愿参与其中的员工将很难在公司取得进步。

en: Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills, too.
cn: 灵活的员工还能展示其他技能。

en: They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something's not working.
cn: 他们能在发生变化时迅速调整优先次序，并在某些事情行不通的时候提出额外的修改建议。

en: They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.
cn: 当遇到挫折时，他们也能迅速重整，自信地适应新环境，而不会反应过度。

en: What makes humans different from other species?
cn: 人类与其他物种有何不同？

en: Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development.
cn: 一些哲学家认为是道德或伦理，而一些科学家则断言是我们的认知能力更发达。

en: But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine.
cn: 但我认为，最主要的区别在于我们渴望打破常规。

en: This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfillment of expectations.
cn: 这使得创造性成为一种生物学使命，因为我们在艺术和技术中追求的是惊喜，而不仅仅是为了满足期望。

en: As a result, a wild imagination has characterized the history of our species: we build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design.
cn: 因此，天马行空的想象力是我们人类历史的特点：我们建造复杂的栖息地，为食物设计复杂的食谱，穿着反映时尚不断变化的衣服，用精心制作的标志、符号和声音进行交流，用自己设计的翅膀和轮子在栖息地之间旅行。

en: To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key.
cn: 为了满足我们的新奇欲望，创新是关键。

en: But who innovates?
cn: 但是，谁来创新呢？

en: Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate.
cn: 现在，许多人，无论是外行还是内行，都认为只有天才才会创新。

en: But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do.
cn: 但我认为，创新并非只有少数人才能做到。

en: The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next.
cn: 每一个人的大脑中都蕴藏着创新的动力，而由此产生的对抗重复的战争，正是区别一代人和下一代人的巨大变化的动力。

en: The drive to create the new is a trait of being human.
cn: 创造新事物是人类的特质。

en: We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions.
cn: 我们建立了数以百计的文化，讲述了数以百万计的新故事。

en: We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not.
cn: 我们创造了前所未有的事物，并将其包围在自己的周围，而动物却不会。

en: But where do our new ideas come from?
cn: 但我们的新想法从何而来？

en: According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere to great minds.
cn: 许多人认为，新创意对于伟大的头脑来说似乎无处不在。

en: From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic.
cn: 从这个角度来看，新创意几乎就像魔法。

en: They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few.
cn: 只有少数人在灵感闪现时才会产生新想法。

en: However, the reality is that across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process.
cn: 然而，现实情况是，在人类的所有活动中，先前的工作都推动着创新过程。

en: We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further.
cn: 我们可能认为创新是灵感或天才的结果，但实际上，创新是进一步发展他人想法的结果。

en: This happens in technology, where one invention enables or inspires further inventions.
cn: 这种情况发生在技术领域，一项发明会促成或激发更多的发明。

en: And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work.
cn: 在艺术领域也是如此，作家、作曲家画家会在自己的作品中使用前辈艺术家的作品。

en: The human brain works from precedent.
cn: 人类的大脑是根据先例工作的。

en: We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.
cn: 我们将继承下来的想法组合在一起，形成新的形态。

en: What is a true creator?
cn: 什么是真正的创造者？

en: Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing?
cn: 创造者是无中生有的天才吗？

en: No.
cn: 不是。

en: Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit, who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures.
cn: 创造者只是利用他们所继承的东西，他们吸收过去，并利用它来创造可能的未来。

en: Thus, humans are creators as a rule, rather than as an exception.
cn: 因此，人类是创造者，这是常规，而不是例外。

en: Many dog owners will tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset.
cn: 许多养狗人士会告诉你，他们的狗能以某种方式知道他们生病或不开心了。

en: And according to researchers who studied dog cognition, those pet owners are right.
cn: 根据研究狗认知能力的研究人员的研究，这些宠物主人是对的。

en: Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time.
cn: 狗确实知道它们的人类同伴什么时候过得不好。

en: Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations, and far more serious physical conditions.
cn: 狗不仅能感知到你感冒了，而且还能察觉到更细微的情绪波动和更严重的身体状况。

en: This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with.
cn: 这是因为狗对它们熟悉的人的变化极为敏感。

en: An illness causes change.
cn: 疾病会引起变化。

en: If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, that odor will be abnormal.
cn: 例如，如果一个人感染了病毒或细菌，那么他身上的气味就会变得不正常。

en: And dogs are able to smell that change even if a human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans.
cn: 即使人类无法嗅到，但狗能够嗅到这种变化，因为狗的嗅觉比人类强大得多。

en: Researchers have also found that a person's mood which can be an indicator of a larger illness triggers a dog's sense of smell.
cn: 研究人员还发现，人的情绪会触发狗的嗅觉，而人的情绪可能是更大疾病的指标。

en: Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body and dogs are able to smell those as well.
cn: 人的情绪会通过身体发出的化学信号表现出来，而狗也能嗅到这些信号。

en: Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes.
cn: 除了嗅觉，狗还能从人的声音中收集信息，以感知变化。

en: In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain similar to one in humans that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone.
cn: 2014年，研究人员发现，狗的大脑中有一块区域与人类的类似，可以让它们理解说话者语气中的情感暗示，这超出了它们仅从熟悉的话语中获得的信息。

en: A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness.
cn: 一个人的声音还能传递疾病的信息。

en: What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes.
cn: 狗对这些变化的理解还不是很清楚。

en: Humans send out lots of cues.
cn: 人类会发出很多暗示。

en: But whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn't clear.
cn: 但尚不清楚狗是否知道其中一些暗示意味着疾病。

en: What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us.
cn: 在我们看来，狗的担忧可能更像是好奇心增强或怀疑我们出了什么问题。

en: And sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation.
cn: 而贴近我们是收集更多相关信息的好方法。

en: Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer.
cn: 一些研究人员断言，狗有朝一日会帮助医生诊断疾病，因为有些狗已经展示了检测各种疾病的能力，包括糖尿病和某些类型的癌症。

en: But those researchers can see that's probably in the distant future.
cn: 但这些研究人员认为这可能是在遥远的未来。

en: For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself.
cn: 目前，研究表明，养狗本身就能带来一系列好处。

en: Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood.
cn: 事实证明，饲养宠物狗可以增强体质和改善情绪。

en: Dogs also help people relax and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.
cn: 狗还能帮助人们放松，对慢性病患者来说更是一种安慰。

en: Earlier this month, the think- tank called Onward published a report, "A Question of Degree", which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money.
cn: 本月早些时候，一个名为Onward的智库发表了一份题为'学位问题'的报告，认为创意艺术专业的学位并不划算。

en: Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold.
cn: Onward认为，部长们应该'打击那些在学生毕业十年后才发现性价比极其有限的课程'，如果毕业生的平均收入低于学生贷款支付门槛，就应该限制这类课程招收新生。

en: Courses like science, technology, engineering and math and economics where the average graduate earns a lot should be favored.
cn: 科学、技术、工程、数学以及经济学等毕业生平均收入较高的课程应受到青睐。

en: The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money.
cn: 该报告深入探讨了政府对如何改革技术教育以及如何确保学生物有所值的审查。

en: At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point.
cn: 乍一看，Onward的观点似乎不无道理。

en: According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than £25,000 a year, ten years after graduation.
cn: 根据他们的数据，大多数创意艺术专业的学生在毕业十年后的年收入不到2.5万英镑。

en: The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would, had they simply never gone to university.
cn: 事实上，创意艺术专业男生的平均收入显然要比他们没上大学时少得多。

en: This isn't really good for anyone—and it's certainly no good for graduates who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.
cn: 这对任何人来说都不是好事，对那些被迫忍受永远无法存钱、永远无法买房、永远无法指望退休的生活方式的毕业生来说当然也不是好事。

en: Onward have identified a real problem.
cn: Onward发现了一个真正的问题。

en: Creative arts graduates from top universities like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately- educated students, have fairly good work prospects, while 40% of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than £25,000 a year, five years after graduation.
cn: 牛津等顶尖大学的创意艺术专业毕业生中，私立教育学生所占比例较高，他们的工作前景相当不错，而40%的毕业生—无论学位高低—毕业五年后的年薪还不到2.5万英镑。

en: This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole.
cn: 这表明，问题其实与攻读特定学位的学生无关，而是与整个经济有关。

en: Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents.
cn: 无论学什么专业，年轻人都很难出人头地，除非他们有幸生在成功的父母身边。

en: If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world.
cn: 如果部长们想让教育为年轻人带来回报，他们就需要将目光从高等教育领域转向更广阔的世界。

en: The rewards that education gives us are not measurable—they are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct.
cn: 教育给我们带来的回报是无法衡量的—它们并不总是一目了然，当然也不总是直接明了的。

en: An education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn't received it.
cn: 教育会让你成为一个与尚未接受教育时截然不同的人。

en: We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life.
cn: 我们不应该从银行存款的角度来看待教育的价值，而应该从生命的角度来看待教育的价值。

en: If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of "value for money", we will all be made poorer as a result.
cn: 如果我们继续被'物有所值'的说法所困扰，我们都将因此而变得更加贫穷。

en: So, I've been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.
cn: 所以，我一直在想，今年夏天我想尝试租一辆露营车，去探索更多的地方，而不是像往常一样租房度假。

en: A camper van?
cn: 露营车？

en: You mean to spend the summer living out of a car?
cn: 你是说整个夏天都住在车里？

en: Yes, a camper van.
cn: 是的，一辆露营车。

en: And no, it's nothing like living out of a car.
cn: 但是，它和汽车完全不一样。

en: These are proper vans with full- size bed to sleep in.
cn: 这些露营车都有全尺寸的床可以睡。

en: Some even have kitchens.
cn: 有些甚至还有厨房。

en: This way, we wouldn't have to be locked into one place during our holiday.
cn: 这样，我们在度假期间就不用被关在一个地方了。

en: We'd be able to visit so many more places and travel at our own pace.
cn: 我们可以去更多的地方，按照自己的节奏旅行。

en: The rates of most hotels and holiday homes really soar in the summer anyway.
cn: 反正大多数酒店和度假屋的价格在夏天都会升。

en: We'd probably save a lot of money as well.
cn: 我们也许还能省下一大笔钱。

en: I think my grandfather had a van like that.
cn: 我想我祖父也有一辆这样的面包车。

en: It doesn't sound that appealing to me.
cn: 我觉得它听起来没那么吸引人。

en: Today's camper vans are completely different.
cn: 现在的露营车已经完全不同了。

en: These days, they're equipped with all the modern comforts.
cn: 如今，它们配备了所有现代化的舒适设施。

en: I've seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you're stopped.
cn: 我见过不少装有太阳能电池板的露营车，可以在停车时提供电力。

en: This way you can still use your computer or charge your phone.
cn: 这样，你仍然可以使用电脑或者给手机充电。

en: And most even have Wi- Fi, so if the weather's not great, you could stream videos.
cn: 大多数还配有Wi-Fi，所以如果天气不好，你还可以播放视频来看。

en: I'm warming up to the idea.
cn: 我已经开始考虑这个主意了。

en: Keep talking.
cn: 你继续说。

en: Loads of people are committing to this trend full time.
cn: 很多人都以全职状态投入到这一趋势中。

en: Check it out online.
cn: 上网看看。

en: Lots of people stream videos of their alternative lifestyles and actually earn a salary.
cn: 很多人通过流媒体视频展示他们的另类生活方式，并实实在在地赚取薪水。

en: Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world.
cn: 试想一下，你可以拥有这样的自由，去任何你想去的地方，在世界任何地方工作。

en: Okay, we can consider it.
cn: 好吧，我们可以考虑。

en: As long as the basic needs like toilets and showers are covered, I'm definitely in.
cn: 只要能满足如厕和淋浴等基本需求，我就肯定同意。

en: Do you think there'll be enough room for my mountain bike?
cn: 你觉得有足够的地方放我的山地自行车吗？

en: What about food delivery?
cn: 送餐服务怎么样？

en: Will we be able to order to the van?
cn: 我们能在车上订餐吗？

en: Will there be enough space for the dog?
cn: 车上有咱们狗狗的位置吗？

en: We wouldn't want to leave him behind.
cn: 我们可不想把它落下。

en: Slow down.
cn: 慢点说。

en: Glad you're excited about it.
cn: 我很高兴你能这么兴奋。

en: Let's start by looking at what's available first.
cn: 我们先来看看有什么可选的。

en: You wanted to see me?
cn: 您想要见我？

en: Yes, I'll get straight to the point.
cn: 是的，我就开门见山了。

en: Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped.
cn: 在过去的一个多月里，你的工作表现明显下滑。

en: You've been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you.
cn: 过去几周，你上班迟到了好几次，这很不符合你的作风。

en: But what really concerns me is your curtailed output.
cn: 但真正让我担心的是你的产出降低了。

en: Lately, you seem to be constantly one step behind.
cn: 最近，你似乎总是慢人一步。

en: What's going on?
cn: 这是怎么回事？

en: I'm sorry.
cn: 对不起。

en: I'm going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment.
cn: 我现在正经历一些不幸的家庭问题。

en: It's a personal matter.
cn: 是私事。

en: So if you don't mind, I much prefer we don't get into it.
cn: 所以，如果您不介意的话，我希望我们可以不要讨论这个问题。

en: Nevertheless, I expect it to have all blown over in another month or so.
cn: 不过，我估计再过一个月左右，一切都会过去的。

en: Do you need some time off?
cn: 你需要休息一段时间吗？

en: Actually, yes.
cn: 事实上，是的。

en: Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off?
cn: 接下来的两个星期一我可以请假吗？

en: I was deliberating whether I should ask for this, but now that we're here...
cn: 我一直在考虑是否应该提出这个要求，但现在我们已经谈到这儿了....

en: Sure thing!
cn: 当然可以！

en: But if you needed some leave, why didn't you ask for it earlier?
cn: 但如果你需要休假，为什么不早点申请呢？

en: I'm not sure why.
cn: 我也不知道为什么。

en: I guess I kind of felt bad asking for it.
cn: 我感觉我有点不好意思开口。

en: You shouldn't feel bad asking for leave, especially if you need it.
cn: 你不应该觉得请假不好，尤其是在你需要的时候。

en: I know.
cn: 我知道。

en: You're right.
cn: 您说得对。

en: I'm sorry.
cn: 我很抱歉。

en: Look, you've been with us almost five years and I personally really value your proficiency at your job.
cn: 听着，你已经在我们这里工作快五年了，我个人非常看重你的工作能力。

en: It makes my job far easier.
cn: 这让我的工作变得轻松很多。

en: In addition, I can assure you that management as a whole also holds you in high regard.
cn: 此外，我可以向你保证，整个管理层对你也非常器重。

en: Thank you.
cn: 谢谢。

en: What I need is for you to be back at your 100%.
cn: 我需要的是你恢复到100%的状态。

en: Are you sure taking two Mondays off will suffice?
cn: 你确定请两个星期一的假就够了吗？

en: It'll be enough.
cn: 够了。

en: I'm sure of it.
cn: 我很确定。

en: Okay, good.
cn: 好，很好。

en: So this is what we're going to do.
cn: 那我们就这么办。

en: You will take those days off and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self.
cn: 你休息的这几天，我希望你能逐渐恢复正常。

en: Then in two months' time, we will catch up again to see how you are faring.
cn: 然后两个月后，我们再谈一次，看看你的情况如何。

en: Sounds good.
cn: 听起来不错。

en: Thank you for your understanding.
cn: 谢谢您的理解。

en: There are many factors that impact our health.
cn: 影响我们健康的因素有很多。

en: These include our finances, our emotions and the way we work.
cn: 其中包括我们的财务状况、情绪和工作方式。

en: Education is one such factor.
cn: 教育也是其中一个因素。

en: Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity.
cn: 研究表明，教育水平越高，健康状况越好，甚至更长寿。

en: But what about the education of your partner?
cn: 但伴侣的教育水平对此影响如何呢？

en: New research seeks to answer this question.
cn: 一项新的研究试图回答这个问题。

en: Researchers use data from a longitudinal study.
cn: 研究人员使用了一项纵向研究的数据。

en: The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957.
cn: 这些数据来自1957年首次对高中生所进行的调查。

en: The surveys ended in 2011.
cn: 该调查于2011年结束。

en: The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health.
cn: 研究小组发现，配偶受教育程度较高的人往往健康状况较好。

en: This remained the case when adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background, and health status before and after marriage.
cn: 在对诸如参与者自身的教育程度、社会背景以及婚前婚后的健康状况等其他因素进行调整后，情况依然如此。

en: The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional, and financial resources.
cn: 作者认为，高教育水平提供了可共享的社会、智慧、情感和经济资源。

en: These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge or more money.
cn: 这些资源包括更高水平的情商、特殊技能或知识、或者更多的金钱。

en: The researchers concede that an individual's own level of education is clearly important for their health, but they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partners' education.
cn: 研究人员承认，个人自身的教育水平显然对其健康非常重要，但他们断言，个人也可以从伴侣的教育中获益。

en: It is noteworthy that the effects varied by gender.
cn: 值得注意的是，这种影响因素性别而异。

en: For women, health was more closely correlated to their spouses' education than for men.
cn: 与男性相比，女性的健康与其配偶的教育程度关系更为密切。

en: The team suggests this may be related to the time period of the study.
cn: 研究小组认为，这可能与研究的时间段有关。

en: Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men.
cn: 与男性相比，样本中的女性受教育程度较低，职业成就也较低。

en: The researchers' hypothesis is that this made the husbands' resources more likely to have a shared impact.
cn: 研究人员的假设是，这种情况使得丈夫的资源更有可能产生共同的影响。

en: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods.
cn: 气候科学家预测，世界许多地区将越来越容易发生洪灾。

en: This is a serious risk to human lives and property.
cn: 这对人类的生命和财产构成严重威胁。

en: So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe.
cn: 因此，了解并准确预测洪水风险是全球脆弱城市面临的关键挑战。

en: In 2017, Derek Loftis of the Virginia Institute of Marine Science started a project called Catch the King.
cn: 2017年，弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的Derek Loftis启动了一个名为'捕捉国王'（Catch the King）的项目。

en: It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides.
cn: 该项目使用智能手机应用程序，收集普通市民在洪灾期间的数据。

en: He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model called TideWatch.
cn: 他将利用这些数据来验证和改进其名为TideWatch的洪水数学模型。

en: Loftis' mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there.
cn: Loftis的任务是在水流到那里之前就知道水流的位置。

en: But collecting necessary data and then processing that information quickly enough to make usable forecasts is anything but easy.
cn: 但是，收集必要的数据，然后快速处理这些信息以做出可用的预报，这一切并不容易。

en: Accurate flood forecasts require an understanding of the situation on the ground.
cn: 准确的洪水预报需要了解实地情况。

en: By the early 2000s, supercomputing had advanced enough that scientists could integrate weather forecasting models with such measurements, but they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast- moving foods in real time.
cn: 到21世纪初，超级计算机已经发展到足够先进的程度，科学家们可以将天气预报模型与这些测量数据结合起来，但他们仍然不具备实时预报湍急洪水的重要能力。

en: So in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet- connected water- level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia.
cn: 因此，2017年，Loftis及其同事在弗吉尼亚州诺福克的洪水风险社区建立了一个由28个互联网连接的水位传感器组。

en: The new sensors relay rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia institute.
cn: 这些新传感器将有关水位高度和移动情况的粗略测量结果传送到弗吉尼亚研究所的一台计算机上。

en: Along with those sensors, hundreds of local citizens take photos of rising tides and transmit them real time to the institute.
cn: 除了这些传感器，数百名当地市民还拍摄了潮水上涨的照片，并实时传送给研究所。

en: Scientists hope that the data collected by these citizens can help sharpen the ability to forecast exactly when and where damaging floods will occur.
cn: 科学家们希望，这些市民收集的数据能够帮助提高准确预测破坏性洪水发生的时间和地点的能力。

en: Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree.
cn: 现在，讨论大学学位的价值已经成为一种惯例。

en: But as current population survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them.
cn: 但是，当前的人口调查数据显示，与拥有大学学位的男性相比，没有大学学位的男性就业率急剧下降。

en: This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time.
cn: 这种下降始于20世纪60年代，随着时间的推移变得越来越严重。

en: What has actually caused this decline?
cn: 究竟是什么导致了这种下降呢？

en: Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades, and have come up with several theories.
cn: 几十年来，经济学家们一直在研究这一下降的根源，并提出了几种理论。

en: One popular theory is that it's a case of too low wages for jobs that don't require a degree.
cn: 一种流行的理论认为，这是由于不需要学位的工作的工资太低。

en: An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.
cn: 另一种理论认为，过去不需要大学学位的工作比现在多。

en: A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem.
cn: 美国国家经济研究局最近的一份工作文件对这些理论进行了回顾，并就问题的原因提出了更多假设。

en: Let's look at that paper now.
cn: 现在让我们来看看这份文件。

en: First, the researchers considered the issue of wages.
cn: 首先，研究人员考虑了工资问题。

en: As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren't as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs.
cn: 随着拥有大学学位的人和没有大学学位的人之间的工资差距越来越大，经济学家们认为，男性对一些利润较低的工作不太感兴趣。

en: Well, the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation.
cn: 这份文件的作者认为这种解释是有道理的。

en: They assert that low wages can't be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven't changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.
cn: 他们断言，低工资不可能是唯一的因素，因为自20世纪60年代以来，没有大学文凭的男性的工资在扣除通货膨胀因素后并没有太大变化，这就很难解释为什么愿意接受这些工资的男性似乎越来越少了。

en: This leads to the second theory that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past.
cn: 这就引出了第二个理论，即与过去相比，现在有更多的工作需要大学学位。

en: Indeed, that theory seems valid because in America today, two thirds of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education.
cn: 事实上，这一理论似乎是成立的，因为在今天的美国，三分之二的工作都是由至少受过一些大学教育的工人来完成的。

en: However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem.
cn: 然而，该文件的作者认为，还有其他因素放大了这一问题。

en: They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage.
cn: 他们发现了两个新的潜在解释：第一个是自20世纪60年代以来，没有大学学历的男性结婚率大幅下降；第二个是在结婚率下降的同时，参加工作的女性人数增加。

en: These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work.
cn: 这两个变化意味着男性可能没有家庭需要养活，或者如果有家庭需要养活，他们的妻子可能会承担更多的养家糊口的工作，这两种情况都可能消除促使他们工作的经济动机。

en: The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn't complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.
cn: 该文件的作者承认，对这一问题的研究并不完整，但他们认为，他们的研究支持了大学教育的价值。

en: While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet.
cn: 越来越多的人开始尝试少吃肉，而一个市场研究小组在其最新的时尚与可持续发展报告中发现，这一趋势正从厨房蔓延到衣橱。

en: It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them.
cn: 报告发现，在人们购买服装前考虑的问题中，动物福祉排在首位，42%的人表示这对他们很重要。

en: The researchers of the team predicted that the next year would see a boom in animal- free shoe collections, since they heard shoppers of all ages say they would buy footwear designated as "vegan", meaning the goods were produced without using any animal or animal part.
cn: 研究小组的研究人员预测，明年不含动物成分的鞋类产品将大行其道，因为他们听到各个年龄段的购物者都说他们会购买'纯素'鞋类产品，这意味着这些产品在生产过程中不使用任何动物或动物的部位。

en: As well as being on trend - and with a much better ring to it than "synthetic leather"—the "vegan" label does convey an important extra distinction.
cn: '纯素'标签不仅符合潮流，而且比'合成革'好听得多，它还传达了一个重要的额外区别。

en: If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal- free.
cn: 如果你给某样东西贴上纯素标签，那么整个产品就必须不含动物成分。

en: That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together for example and the chemicals used for finishing them.
cn: 这意味着要检查诸如将鞋子粘在一起的胶水以及用于鞋面处理的化学品等。

en: At the top end, some of the world- renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time.
cn: 在高端市场，一些世界知名的时装设计师已经有一段时间没有使用皮革和皮草了。

en: In fact, some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms.
cn: 事实上，一些公司目前正在探索一种皮革替代品和一种用蘑菇制成的丝绸替代品。

en: The Animal Free Product Society says they've seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark.
cn: 无动物产品协会表示，他们看到了注册素食商标产品的蓬勃发展。

en: In 2018, there were 119.
cn: 2018年，共注册了119件该类产品。

en: So far this year, it says, an unprecedented 1956 have been registered.
cn: 而该协会说，今年到目前为止，已经注册了1956件这类产品，这是前所未有的。

en: New products are being added daily.
cn: 新产品每天都在增加。

en: There are fur coats that are "vegan", plastic "vegan" belts and shoes made from tree bark or natural rubber labeled "vegan".
cn: 有'纯素'的皮革大衣，有'纯素'的塑料腰带，还有用树皮或天然橡胶制成的标有'纯素'的鞋子。

en: These new products aren't coming at an extra cost to consumers, though.
cn: 不过，这些新产品并没有给消费者带来额外的成本。

en: Vegan boots cost the same as the leather originals.
cn: 纯素靴子的价格与皮革靴子相同。

en: New Look, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99, and a vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.
cn: New Look是最早使用'纯素'商标的知名连锁店之一，其芭蕾舞鞋售价为7.99英镑，纯素笔记本手提包售价为29.99英镑，与其他产品价格相当。

en: This signifies a change.
cn: 这标志着一种变化。

en: In the past, ethical products, whether they were fair trade or organic, came at a premium.
cn: 过去，道德产品，无论是公平贸易产品还是有机产品，价格都很高。

en: However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical.
cn: 然而，这些新产品能否被视为道德产品还不清楚。

en: The debate over durability, crop growing impacts, pollution and recyclability is a complicated one, not to mention the ethics around the working conditions for people making the products, whatever the component materials.
cn: 无论产品的组成材料是什么，关于耐用性、对作物生长的影响、污染和可回收性的争论十分复杂，更不用说与产品制造者的工作条件有关的道德问题了。

en: Environmental campaigners advise that the best approach is to buy less, never mind what the item is made of.
cn: 环保运动者建议，最好的办法是少买，而不要考虑产品是用什么材料制成的。

en: By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell.
cn: 到2016年年底，任何稍微关注新闻头条的人都有可能得出这样的结论：一切都糟透了，世界正在走向地狱。

en: It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses or terror attacks.
cn: 世界各地的战争、致命病毒的传播或恐怖袭击很容易让人感到沮丧。

en: Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity.
cn: 然而，2016年却是人类历史上最好的一年。

en: Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990.
cn: 儿童死亡率约为1990年的一半。

en: And 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day.
cn: 每天用上电的人数都会增加30万。

en: Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated.
cn: 在美洲、欧洲、亚洲、非洲乃至整个世界，物质和环境福利的每一项指标都在改善，而不是恶化。

en: We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline.
cn: 我们生活在历史上最和平的时代，各种暴力事件急剧减少。

en: Those are the facts.
cn: 这些都是事实。

en: So why aren't we all optimists?
cn: 那么，为什么我们不全是乐观主义者呢？

en: In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.
cn: 在2015年YouGov的一项调查中，65%的英国人和81%的法国人表示，他们认为世界正在变得更糟。

en: However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong.
cn: 然而，根据大量合理的统计数据，这些人根本就是错的。

en: Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century.
cn: 正常人都不会希望自己生活在上个世纪。

en: Yet people do.
cn: 然而，人们却这样做了。

en: Why?
cn: 为什么呢？

en: Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational.
cn: 我们普遍的绝望情绪是非理性的。

en: It says more about us than it does about how things really are.
cn: 它更多地反映了我们自己，而不是事情的真实情况。

en: It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors, but now, in a media- saturated era, constantly mislead us.
cn: 最好的解释是，我们的祖先在进化过程中产生了各种心理偏差，但现在，在媒体充斥的时代，这些心理偏差不断误导着我们。

en: Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong.
cn: 曾几何时，担心一切可能会出错的事情具有极大的生存价值。

en: This is what makes bad news especially compelling.
cn: 这就是坏消息特别引人注目的原因。

en: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival.
cn: 在我们进化的过去，负面信息很容易吸引我们的注意力，这是一件好事，因为它很可能预示着我们的生存面临危险。

en: The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite.
cn: 穴居人总是假设下一块石头后面有一头狮子，这种假设通常是错误的，但他比总是假设相反情况的人更有可能生存和繁衍后代。

en: But that was all before newspapers, television and the Internet.
cn: 但那都是在报纸、电视和互联网出现之前的事了。

en: In today's hyper- connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe.
cn: 在当今这个超级互联的时代，我们对坏消息的沉迷只会让我们从全球各地搜罗令人沮丧或愤怒的新闻。

en: Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are.
cn: 无论这些新闻是否威胁到我们，我们都会得出结论：事情比实际情况要糟糕得多。

en: Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events, by definition, aren't news.
cn: 另一方面，真正的好消息却很难在报纸上被发现，因为根据定义，可预测的日常事件并不是新闻。

en: I've just bought a new blender.
cn: 我刚买了一台新的搅拌机。

en: What's that?
cn: 那是什么？

en: A blender, you know, a machine that blends food.
cn: 搅拌机，你知道的，就是一种可以搅拌食物的机器。

en: Ah, yes.
cn: 啊，是的。

en: Of course.
cn: 当然了。

en: The electric kitchen appliance.
cn: 就是那种厨房里的电器。

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: This one is state of the art.
cn: 这台是最先进的。

en: I've been meaning to buy one for a while.
cn: 我一直想买一台搅拌机。

en: And I did thorough research on which specific model to get.
cn: 我还对具体买哪个型号做了详细的研究。

en: I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews.
cn: 可能看了上百条网上的用户评论。

en: Anyway, it's amazing!
cn: 不论如何，这台机器很棒！

en: Really?
cn: 真的？

en: What could be so special about it?
cn: 它有什么特别之处？

en: I mean it's just a blender.
cn: 我的意思是，它不就是一台搅拌机吗？

en: Well, basically, it's just a very good one.
cn: 说白了，它就是一台非常好的搅拌机。

en: It feels heavy and sturdy and well- made.
cn: 它很重，很结实，做工很好。

en: It also has lots of power and can easily cut and crush practically anything.
cn: 它的动力很强，可以轻松切碎几乎任何东西。

en: This way, the soups and juices I make come out really fine and smooth, with no lumpy bits.
cn: 这样，我做的汤和果汁更加细腻，没有结块。

en: Em, I see.
cn: 嗯，我明白了。

en: I've never thought of getting one myself.
cn: 我从没想过自己要买一台。

en: It sounds like the kind of thing that for me, personally, I would rarely use.
cn: 这对我来说，可能不常用得到。

en: I've never had one before.
cn: 我以前也没用过搅拌机。

en: And now that I do, I use it all the time.
cn: 现在有了它，我几乎天天都用。

en: I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning.
cn: 早上我会做新鲜的果汁。

en: Maybe not every morning, but 3 or 4 times a week, and it feels fantastic.
cn: 可能不是每天，但每周至少三四次，这样感觉很棒。

en: It's a really healthy habit.
cn: 这是一种非常健康的习惯。

en: I can imagine that must feel quite satisfying.
cn: 我可以想象那一定很满足。

en: I can picture you getting all creative in the kitchen and trying out a multitude of different ingredients.
cn: 我能想象你在厨房里创意满满，试各种不同的食材。

en: And it's obviously going to be healthier than buying packaged juice from a supermarket.
cn: 而且这样显然比去超市买包装果汁要健康多了。

en: It's so much healthier.
cn: 这健康多了。

en: It's not even close.
cn: 根本不能比。

en: Did you know that store- bought juice is like 10% sugar?
cn: 你知道吗，市售的果汁大约有10%是糖分。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: So then you bought it for the health benefits?
cn: 所以你买它是为了健康的好处？

en: Mostly yes.
cn: 主要是。

en: Basically, it allows me to have a more varied diet with a far wider assortment of nutrients, because it's not only fruit in my morning juices, you see?
cn: 基本上，它让我有更广泛的饮食和更多种类的营养，因为我早上的果汁不仅限于水果，你明白吗？

en: I can also throw in vegetables, nuts, yogurt, cereals, anything that tickles my fancy.
cn: 我还会加蔬菜、坚果、酸奶、麦片，任何我喜欢的东西。

en: Today we have a very interesting guest, Mr. Thomas Benjamin Grimm, the mayor of Berkton.
cn: 今天我们有一位非常有趣的客人，托马斯·本杰明·格林先生，他是伯克顿的市长。

en: He's here to talk about his job and responsibilities overseeing this charming village.
cn: 他是来谈谈他的工作，以及管理这个迷人村庄的职责的。

en: Mr. Grimm, thank you for being here.
cn: 格林先生，非常感谢您的到来。

en: Thank you for having me.
cn: 谢谢你邀请我。

en: I'd like to start by saying the obvious.
cn: 我想从显而易见的事情开始。

en: Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country.
cn: 伯克顿已经成为全国最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一。

en: And this has happened under your watch.
cn: 这是在您的领导下发生的变化。

en: Just how did you achieve this?
cn: 您是怎么做到的呢？

en: The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton.
cn: 这项成就属于所有伯克顿的居民。

en: It was a shared effort where everybody pitched in for the communal good.
cn: 这是大家为了公共利益共同努力的结果。

en: But how did this change happen?
cn: 但是这种变化是怎么发生的？

en: In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard- of sleepy village to a must- see destination.
cn: 在大约10年的时间里，伯克顿从一个相对不为人知的安静村庄变成了一个必看的旅游胜地。

en: Yes, the change has truly been remarkable.
cn: 是的，这种变化确实非常显著。

en: Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful, natural allure.
cn: 伯克顿一直很幸运，拥有如此美丽的自然风光。

en: The Agoura hills above the village remain untouched by human development.
cn: 村庄上方的阿古拉山丘至今未被人类开发。

en: And the Sonora valley just below it is equally stunning.
cn: 而其下方的索诺拉山谷也同样美丽。

en: The transformation commenced in a town hall meeting in spring 2008 over 10 years ago.
cn: 这种变革始于2008年春天的一次市政厅会议。

en: Now, when an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of Motion 836.
cn: 那时，绝大多数邻居投票赞成836号动议。

en: This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonise the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton.
cn: 这个立法提案的主要目的是协调伯克顿所有房屋的美学外观。

en: The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way we've shared design features, then the village as a whole would look more beautiful.
cn: 我们的想法是，如果所有的房产看起来有某种共同的设计特征，那么整个村庄看起来会更美。

en: And it worked.
cn: 而这一点确实奏效了。

en: It certainly did.
cn: 确实如此。

en: I'm looking now at a before- and- after photo, and the change is truly remarkable.
cn: 我现在看着一张前后的对比照片，变化真是非常显著。

en: It's hard to believe it's the same place.
cn: 很难相信这是同一个地方。

en: How do the neighbors feel now?
cn: 邻居们现在感觉怎么样？

en: Great pride.
cn: 我认为他们有很大的自豪感。

en: I would say.
cn: 我想说。

en: But what about the multitudes of visitors now crowding the streets?
cn: 但是现在街道上挤满了游客，大家对此都满意吗？

en: Is everyone happy about that?
cn: 大家对此都满意吗？

en: The tourists we receive are a blessing as they have completely revitalized our local economy.
cn: 我们接待的游客是我们的福气，因为他们完全振兴了我们当地的经济。

en: Every visitor is warmly welcome.
cn: 我们热烈欢迎每一位游客。

en: Researchers in the US have created a remote- controlled robot that is so small it can walk on the top of a US penny.
cn: 美国的研究人员发明了一种遥控机器人，体积小到可以在一美分硬币上行走。

en: In research published in the journal Science Robotics, a team at Northwestern University said the crab- like robot is 0.5 millimeters wide.
cn: 在《科学机器人》杂志上发表的一项研究中，西北大学的一个团队称这种类似螃蟹的机器人宽0.5毫米。

en: Researchers described it as the smallest- ever remote- controlled walking robot.
cn: 研究人员描述它是有史以来最小的遥控步行机器人。

en: The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn and even jump, without the use of complex hardware or special power.
cn: 这种微型机器人可以弯曲、扭转、爬行、步行、转弯甚至跳跃，而无需使用复杂的硬件或特殊电源。

en: The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body.
cn: 工程师们表示，这是因为该机器人由其身体的弹性特性提供动力。

en: To construct the robot, the researchers used a shape- memory alloy material that transforms to its remembered shape when heated.
cn: 为了构造机器人，研究人员使用了形状记忆合金材料，这种材料在加热时会变回忆的形状。

en: Using a laser, the team is able to heat the robot at specific parts of its body, causing it to change shape.
cn: 团队使用激光加热机器人身体的特定部位，使其改变形状。

en: As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another.
cn: 当机器人变形并恢复到原始形状时，它实现了从一个地方到另一个地方的移动。

en: "Because these structures are so tiny, the rate of cooling is very fast," project lead, professor John A Rogers said.
cn: 项目负责人John A. Rogers教授说：'由于这些结构非常小，冷却速度非常快。'

en: "In fact, reducing the sizes of these robots allows them to run faster."
cn: '实际上，减小这些机器人的尺寸使它们能跑得更快。'

en: While the research is still in the exploratory stage, the team believes that one day micro- robots could lead to miniaturized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces.
cn: 虽然研究仍处于探索阶段，但团队相信有一天微型机器人可以引领微型化机器人在狭小空间内执行实际任务。

en: "You might imagine micro- robots as agents to repair or assemble small structures or machines in industry or as a surgical assistance to clean clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding or to eliminate cancerous tumors - all in minimally invasive procedures," Rogers said.
cn: '你可以想象微型机器人作为修理或组装工业中小型结构或机器的代理人，或者作为手术助手清理堵塞的动脉，停止内出血或消除癌性肿瘤——所有这些都是微创手术，'Rogers说道。

en: I don't want to boast or anything, but I have always considered myself something of an elite sleeper.
cn: 我并不是想炫耀什么，但我一直认为自己是个出色的睡眠者。

en: Given the opportunity, I will sleep for marathon stretches and can doze through the most extreme situations.
cn: 如果有机会，我可以连续长时间睡觉，并且在最极端的情况下也能安然入睡。
