en: On one very rough ferry crossing on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my traveling companion spent the entire three- hour ride throwing up in the bathroom while I dozed happily on a plastic chair.
cn: 例如，在去锡利群岛的一次非常颠簸的渡轮航行中，我的旅行伴侣在三小时的航程中都在卫生间呕吐，而我却在一把塑料椅子上愉快地睡觉。

en: Unfortunately, it has come to my attention that I am not an elite sleeper after all.
cn: 然而，不幸的是，我发现自己其实并不是所谓的'精英睡眠者'。

en: It seems I am just lazy.
cn: 看来我只是懒而已。

en: Because elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3% of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us.
cn: 因为'精英睡眠者'是指大约3%的人口，他们的生理决定了他们比我们其他人需要更少的睡眠。

en: According to a study that came out in March, elite sleepers have rare genetic changes, which means they can sleep fewer hours than mere mortals without any risk of cognitive decline.
cn: 根据今年三月发表的一项研究，精英睡眠者拥有罕见的基因变化，这意味着他们可以比普通人睡得更少而不会有认知衰退的风险。

en: It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep?
cn: 虽然不可能改变你的基因，但你可以训练自己需要更少的睡眠吗？

en: Is there a non- biological way to reach elite sleeper status?
cn: 有没有一种非生物学的方法可以达到'精英睡眠者'的状态？

en: I have spent the past year trying to answer that question.
cn: 过去一年我一直在尝试回答这个问题。

en: Not for fun, I should add, but because having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep schedule, for which I still have a great passion.
cn: 我得补充一句，这并不是为了好玩，而是因为有了宝宝之后，我的睡眠时间表严重被扰乱了，而我对睡眠仍然充满热情。

en: For a while, I assumed I'd be forced to become one of those people who jumps out of bed at the crack of dawn.
cn: 有段时间，我以为自己会被迫成为那种在黎明时分一跃而起的人。

en: After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird.
cn: 然而，经过一年艰苦的科学研究，我发现被迫早起与成为一个早起的人是完全不同的。

en: If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you'd realise if it had changed your beliefs?
cn: 如果你阅读了一篇关于有争议问题的文章，你认为你会意识到它是否改变了你的信念吗？

en: No one knows your own mind like you do — it seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted.
cn: 没有人像你自己一样了解你的内心——你知道自己的信念是否发生了改变，这似乎显而易见。

en: And yet a new paper in The Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article.
cn: 然而，《实验心理学季刊》上的一项新调查表明，我们对自己信念改变的意识实际上非常差，这意味着我们往往会低估一篇有说服力的文章对我们影响的程度。

en: The researchers recruited over 200 undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline.
cn: 研究人员在两项研究中招募了200多名本科生，重点研究他们对体罚儿童是否是一种有效的训练手段的看法。

en: The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child on a scale from 1 (completely disbelieve) to 9 (completely believe).
cn: 学生们根据从1（完全不相信）到9（完全相信）的评分尺度，报告了他们对体罚是否是一种有效的儿童训练手段的初步看法。

en: Several weeks later they were given one of two researchbased texts to read: each was several pages long and either presented the arguments and data in favor of physical punishment or against it.
cn: 几周后，他们从两篇基于研究的文章中选择一篇来阅读：每篇都是几页长，并且要么呈现支持体罚的论据和数据，要么反对体罚。

en: After this, the students answered some questions to test their comprehension and memory of the text.
cn: 之后，学生们回答了一些问题，以测试他们对文本的理解和记忆。

en: Then the students again scored their belief in whether physical punishment is effective or not.
cn: 然后，学生们再次对体罚是否有效打分。

en: Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study.
cn: 最后，研究人员要求他们回忆在研究开始时的信念。

en: The students' belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position.
cn: 当学生们阅读了一篇与自己初步立场相反的文章时，他们对体罚的信念发生了变化。

en: Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief.
cn: 至关重要的是，他们对初始信念的记忆也向他们新信念的方向发生了偏移。

en: In fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief.
cn: 实际上，他们的记忆更接近他们当前的信念，而不是他们的原始信念。

en: The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce their initial belief.
cn: 信念改变得越多，这种记忆偏差就越大，这表明学生们依靠他们当前的信念来推断他们的初始信念。

en: The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they'd understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn't play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change.
cn: 记忆偏差与他们对文本的理解或记忆程度无关，这表明这些因素在初始信念记忆或信念改变意识中并不起作用。

en: The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs, it's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs.
cn: 研究人员承认，这项研究主要关于的是对温和信念的改变，在改变极端或根深蒂固信念的情况下，研究结果可能会有所不同。

en: However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position.
cn: 然而，我们对大多数话题的信念都处于中等范围内，在我们日常生活中阅读信息性材料时，这些有趣的发现表明，我们大多不知道我们刚刚读到的东西是如何更新和改变我们自己的立场的。

en: As the American population grows, so does the number of American moms.
cn: 随着美国人口的增长，美国母亲的数量也在增加。

en: But, more than a century after Mother's Day became an official holiday, even as that number increases, the share of the American population who are mothers is at the lowest point in a quarter century.
cn: 但是，在母亲节成为法定节日的一个多世纪后，虽然母亲的数量有所增加，但美国人口中母亲所占的比例却达到了25年以来的最低点。

en: It's frequently noted that fertility rates are falling sharply in richer countries, but the less observed consequence of this trend is that a decline in births can also mean a decline in motherhood in general.
cn: 经常有人提到，富裕国家的生育率在急剧下降，但这一趋势的一个不那么被注意到的后果是，出生率的下降也可能意味着母亲数量的总体减少。

en: According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau, the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly, and may continue for some time yet.
cn: 根据我对美国人口普查局数据的分析，美国母亲数量的下降是真实存在的，发生得非常快，并且可能会继续一段时间。

en: Not only are moms making up less of the population, but their characteristics are changing too, and in a way that might be linked to their proportional decline.
cn: 不仅母亲在总体人口中所占的比例在减少，她们的特征也在发生变化，这种变化可能与她们比例的下降有关。

en: Moms today tend to be older than in the past.
cn: 今天的母亲比过去往往年龄更大。

en: Just looking at recent years, the change in age- specific birth rates has been drastic.
cn: 仅看最近几年的数据，各年龄段人口出生率的变化是巨大的。

en: In just the past few years, the peak childbearing age range for American women has advanced from that of 25- to- 29 to that of 30 to 34.
cn: 在短短的几年里，美国女性的生育高峰年龄范围已经从25-29岁推迟到30-34岁。

en: Meanwhile, childbearing among women under 20 has fallen by half or more, while childbearing among women 35 and older is rising.
cn: 与此同时，20岁以下女性的生育率下降了一半或更多，而35岁及以上女性的生育率正在上升。

en: One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children.
cn: 这个年龄变化的一个积极后果是，更大比例的新母亲在经济上已做好养育儿童的准备。

en: Less positively, however, many women find that, as they age, they can't have as many kids as they would like.
cn: 然而，不那么积极的是，许多女性会发现，随着年龄增长，她们无法拥有期望的子女数量。

en: Plus, having children later in life can increase the risk of health complications.
cn: 此外，晚育还可能增加健康并发症的风险。

en: These finer points aside, one major consequence of the older- moms trend is that fewer years of a woman's life are spent as a mother.
cn: 撇开这些细节不谈，高龄妈妈趋势的一个主要后果是，女性作为母亲的时间更少了。

en: This means that, at any given time, a larger share of women, and thus of the whole population, will report not having children in government surveys.
cn: 这意味着，在任何时候，都有更大比例的女性（占总人口的比例）在政府调查中报告没有孩子。

en: In other words, later motherhood means less motherhood.
cn: 换句话说，晚育意味着母亲数量减少。

en: Even as motherhood rates decline, Mother's Day, of course, will endure.
cn: 即使母亲率在下降，母亲节当然仍将继续存在。

en: In fact, despite the demographic shift, retail spending on the holiday appears to be rising.
cn: 事实上，尽管人口结构有所变化，但节日期间的零售支出似乎在增加。

en: It is hard to say if Mother's Day spending is rising more than one would expect given that the American population keeps growing.
cn: 鉴于美国人口的持续增长，很难说母亲节消费的增长是否超出了人们的预期。

en: But one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising.
cn: 但其中一个因素可能是成年子女的母亲比例正在上升。

en: And those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with.
cn: 而这些成年子女为不再与自己同住的母亲庆祝时可能更加慷慨。

en: Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that house plants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air.
cn: 自从1989年美国宇航局（NASA）发表了一篇文章，声称室内植物可以吸收污染和有毒化学物质以来，企业和房主们越来越多地投资于绿色植物来帮助净化空气。

en: But a new analysis suggests it could actually take more than 1,000 plants per square meter to gain a benefit any greater than simply opening a couple of windows.
cn: 然而，一项新的分析表明，实际上每平方米可能需要超过1000株植物才能获得比简单地打开几扇窗户更大的好处。

en: The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their tests in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people's homes or offices.
cn: 问题在于，NASA的测试是在密封的容器中进行的，这并不能模拟大多数人居住或办公环境中的条件。

en: The space agency was primarily concerned about keeping the air fresh for astronauts cut off in biospheres or space stations, and helping to combat sick building syndrome which had become a problem due to the super insulated and energy efficient offices of the late 1970s.
cn: NASA主要关心的是保持宇航员在生物圈或空间站的空气新鲜，并帮助对抗病态建筑综合症，这是由于20世纪70年代末的超级隔热和节能办公室而形成的一个问题。

en: By the early 1980s, workers regularly complained of skin rashes, sleepiness, headaches and allergies, as they breathed in toxic chemicals from paints and plastics.
cn: 到80年代初，工作人员经常抱怨皮肤瘙痒、嗜睡、头痛和过敏，因为他们吸入了油漆和塑料中的有毒化学物质。

en: NASA found that certain plants could remove chemicals from the air, and even today garden centers recommend the plants for air- cleaning properties.
cn: NASA发现某些植物可以去除空气中的化学物质，甚至到今天，花园中心依然推荐这些植物以其空气净化特性。

en: However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that house plants in a normal environment have little impact.
cn: 然而，一项对30年来几十项研究的新评估发现，正常环境下的室内植物几乎没有影响。

en: In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air.
cn: 实际上，自然通风在净化空气方面要好得多。

en: The researchers also calculated the clean air delivery rate for plants in the studies they analysed and found that the rate at which plants dispersed the compounds was well below the usual rates of air exchange in a normal building, caused by the movements of people coming and going, opening doors and windows.
cn: 研究人员还计算了他们分析的研究中植物的清洁空气输送率，发现植物分散化合物的速率远低于正常建筑物内人们进出、开门和关门所造成的通常空气交换速率。

en: Many of the studies did show a reduction in the concentration of volatile organic compounds over time, which is likely why people have seized on them to praise the air purifying virtues of plants.
cn: 许多研究确实显示挥发性有机化合物的浓度随着时间而减少，这可能是为什么人们抓住它们不放，赞美植物的空气净化能力的原因。

en: But the researchers' calculations showed, it would take 10 to 1,000 plants per square meter of floor space to compete with the air- cleaning capacity of a building's air- handling system or even just a couple of open windows in a house.
cn: 然而，研究人员的计算显示，要达到与建筑的空气处理系统或甚至只是几扇打开窗户相媲美的空气净化效果，每平方米的地板空间需要10到1000株植物。

en: In contrast, NASA's sealed experiment recommended one pot plants per 100 square feet.
cn: 相比之下，NASA的密封实验推荐每100平方英尺使用一盆植物。

en: This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time.
cn: 这确实是科学发现如何随着时间推移而被误导或误解的一个典例。

en: But it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening.
cn: 但这也是科学研究应不断重新审视和质疑发现的一个很好的例子，以更接近于理解实际发生的事实。

en: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
cn: 谢谢您在这么短的时间内与我见面，Stephen。

en: Not a problem, Margaret.
cn: 没问题，Margaret。

en: Now, please give me some good news.
cn: 现在，请给我一些好消息。

en: Have you agreed to my last proposal?
cn: 您同意我的最后一个提案了吗？

en: I have indeed.
cn: 我确实同意了。

en: And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.
cn: 我希望在合同中进行一个小小修改后签署协议。

en: Margaret, we've been through this for almost a year now.
cn: Margaret，我们已经讨论了将近一年了。

en: Back and forth, making alterations.
cn: 不断往返修改。

en: Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients or not?
cn: 你确定你想为你的客户达成一项赞助协议吗？

en: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
cn: 我这样问，是因为，坦白说，我这边的一些人已经快没有耐心了。

en: I understand your concerns, but as I'm sure you understand, we hold our client's best interests to be of the utmost concern.
cn: 我理解你的担忧，但我相信你也明白，我们将客户的最佳利益视为首要考虑。

en: We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts.
cn: 因此，我们仔细检查所有合同的细节。

en: Rest assured, we all appreciate your firm's patience.
cn: 请放心，我们非常感激贵公司的耐心。

en: Okay, fine.
cn: 好的。

en: So what changes do you wish to make?
cn: 那么你希望做哪些修改？

en: Essentially, we would like the New Deal to exclude the Middle East.
cn: 基本上，我们希望这次协议不包括中东地区。

en: That's all the Middle East.
cn: 是整个中东地区。

en: Why?
cn: 为什么？

en: My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East.
cn: 我的客户还有一些来自中东公司的潜在营销协议。

en: Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client's image in the Middle East only.
cn: 如果那些提议成型的话，它们将只会在中东地区使用我客户的形象。

en: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
cn: 因此，为了避免任何冲突，我们需要确保两个营销活动在地域上不重叠。

en: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
cn: 我们在谈论中东的哪个业务领域？

en: Real estate.
cn: 房地产。

en: Well, that should be okay.
cn: 那么，这应该没问题。

en: So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest.
cn: 只要产品与我们的食品和饮料市场有很大的不同，就不会有利益冲突。

en: Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people.
cn: 尽管如此，我还是需要向我的团队进行确认。

en: I don't foresee any problem though.
cn: 不过，我不认为这会有任何问题。

en: The Middle East is a negligible market for us.
cn: 中东对我们来说是一个微不足道的市场。

en: But I still need to check this with a couple of departments.
cn: 但我仍需要与几个部门核实这个问题。

en: Next, we have a special science- related news story.
cn: 接下来，我们有一个与科学有关的特别新闻报道。

en: Paula Hancock is at the Denver Observatory.
cn: Paula Hancock现在在丹佛天文台。

en: Paula, what is the big story over there?
cn: 宝拉，那边有什么重大新闻吗？

en: Hi, John.
cn: 你好，约翰。

en: Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited.
cn: 是的，在场的所有天文学家都非常激动。

en: In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the northern hemisphere will be congregating on mountaintops tonight to watch the night sky.
cn: 事实上，今晚北美和北半球其他地方的太空爱好者们将聚集在山顶上观看夜空。

en: Why?
cn: 为什么？

en: What's the big event?
cn: 有什么大事发生吗？

en: Is there an eclipse happening soon?
cn: 是不是即将发生一次日食？

en: Tonight, the earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet.
cn: 今晚，地球将靠近奥本海默彗星。

en: It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.
cn: 这将是地球在超过100年里与这样一个天象最接近的一次。

en: For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
cn: 因此，预计今晚将有成千上万的人仰望天空来观看这个壮观的天体。

en: How far away is this common?
cn: 这颗彗星有多远？

en: Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
cn: 人们能用肉眼看到它吗？

en: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away on the edge of our galaxy.
cn: 奥本海默彗星仍将在我们银河系的边缘，距离地球数百万英里。

en: But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope.
cn: 但即便如此，这也是一个相对较近的距离，足够人们通过望远镜详细观察。

en: People will only see a blur without one.
cn: 没有望远镜，人们只能看到一个模糊的影子。

en: However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment.
cn: 不过，这并不意味着需要专业设备。

en: Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
cn: 即使是最普通的望远镜也足以让人们观察和惊叹于这个飞行物体。

en: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once in a lifetime event.
cn: 我们的许多观众会想知道他们如何才能参与到这个一生一次的活动中。

en: Where will this comet be in the sky?
cn: 彗星会出现在天空的哪个位置？

en: How can people find it?
cn: 人们如何才能找到它？

en: The comet will be almost exactly due north at 60 degrees above the equator.
cn: 这颗彗星将在正北方向，距离地平线60度。

en: However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky.
cn: 不过，找到这颗彗星确实非常困难。

en: And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
cn: 这里的科学家们告诉我，有很多手机应用程序可以帮助发现它。

en: How fantastic.
cn: 太棒了。

en: Thank you, Paula, for the information.
cn: 谢谢你，Paula，感谢你提供的信息。

en: Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition, advice and regulations around the world.
cn: 饮食指南是全球营养、建议和法规的基础。

en: While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate.
cn: 尽管大多数现有指南在科学上达成了强烈共识，但最近有一个问题引发了争议。

en: Should consumers be warned to avoid ultra- processed foods?
cn: 消费者是否应该被警告避免食用超加工食品？

en: Two papers published today in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra- processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems.
cn: 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文概述了支持和反对使用超加工食品概念来帮助制定超出传统食品分类系统的饮食指南的案例。

en: The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of Sao Paulo and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate August 14 during Nutrition 2024 Live Online.
cn: 文章的作者，圣保罗大学的卡洛斯·蒙泰罗和诺德基金会的阿恩·阿斯特鲁普，将在2024年8月14日的'在线营养2024直播'活动中进行一个现场虚拟辩论，讨论这一问题。

en: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra- processed.
cn: 争论的焦点是由蒙泰罗及其同事开发的一个系统，该系统根据食品的工业加工程度对其进行分类，从未加工到超加工。

en: The system defines ultra- processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product.
cn: 该系统对超加工食品的定义是，通过一系列工序从食品中提取物质，并用化学物质对其进行改变，以形成最终产品。

en: Ultra- processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient.
cn: 超加工食品的特点是廉价、简单和方便。

en: Examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready to heat products and reconstituted meat products.
cn: 例子包括软饮料和糖果、包装零食和糕点、加热即食产品和再制肉制品。

en: Studies have linked consumption of ultra- processed foods, which are often high in salt, sugar and fat with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases.
cn: 研究发现，摄入超加工食品（通常高盐、高糖和高脂肪）与体重增加和慢性疾病风险增加有关。

en: Even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar and fat in the diet.
cn: 即便在调整了饮食中的盐、糖和脂肪含量后也是如此。

en: While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra- processed foods and dietary recommendations and government policies.
cn: 尽管这些关联背后的机制尚未完全明了，蒙泰罗认为现有的证据足以证明在饮食建议和政府政策中不鼓励食用超加工食品是合理的。

en: Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints.
cn: 信不信由你，人类的创造力受益于约束。

en: According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently.
cn: 根据心理学家的观点，当你能使用的资源减少时，你实际上会开始以不同的方式看待世界。

en: With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully.
cn: 在有约束的情况下，你会将你的心理能量投入到更机智的行动上。

en: When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
cn: 当面临挑战时，你会想出新的方法来变得更好。

en: The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher.
cn: 最成功的有创意的人知道，约束会给他们的思想带来更高的动力。

en: People who invent new products are not limited by what they don't have or can't do.
cn: 发明新产品的人不受他们没有或不能做的东西的限制。

en: They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further.
cn: 他们利用自己的局限性来推动自己走得更远。

en: Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use.
cn: 许多产品和服务是因为创始人看到了他们所使用的东西中的限制而创造出来的。

en: They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
cn: 他们基于当前不适用的东西进行了创新。

en: Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation.
cn: 创新是有创意的人对限制的回应。

en: In a 2015 study, which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Chu at Johns Hopkins University, found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways.
cn: 2015年，伊利诺斯大学的拉维·梅塔（Ravi Mehta）和约翰·霍普金斯大学的朱萌（Meng Chu）进行了一项研究，该研究考察了对稀缺或丰富的思考如何影响人们创造性地使用资源的方式。他们发现，人们根本没有动力以新颖的方式使用现有资源。

en: When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to.
cn: 当人们面临稀缺时，他们会给自己自由，必须以不那么常规的方式使用资源。

en: Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes.
cn: 障碍可以拓宽你的视野，开启你的思维过程。

en: Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
cn: 持续的约束可以帮助你提高将不相关的想法和概念联系起来的能力。

en: Marissa Mayer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg, "Constraints shape and focus problems provide clear challenges to overcome.
cn: 谷歌负责搜索产品和用户体验的前副总裁玛丽莎·梅耶尔曾在彭博社发表的一篇文章中写道：'约束塑造和聚焦问题，提供了需要克服的明确挑战。

en: Creativity thrives best when constrained."
cn: 创造力在受到约束的情况下才能发挥得最好。'

en: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts.
cn: 不同的人使用不同的策略来管理冲突。

en: These strategies are learned in childhood.
cn: 这些策略是在儿童时期习得的。

en: Usually we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations.
cn: 通常我们不会意识到我们在冲突情况下的行为方式。

en: We just do whatever seems to come naturally.
cn: 我们只是顺其自然地做出反应。

en: But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.
cn: 但我们确实有自己的策略，而且因为它是后天习得的，所以我们总是可以通过学习新的、更有效的管理冲突的方法来改变它。

en: When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person.
cn: 当你卷入冲突时，有两个主要因素需要考虑：实现个人目标和保持与他人的良好关系。

en: How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict.
cn: 你的个人目标有多重要以及关系对你有多重要会影响你在冲突中的行为方式。

en: Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified:
cn: 鉴于这两个因素，可以确定五种管理冲突的风格：

en: 1. The turtle.
cn: 1. 乌龟。

en: Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.
cn: 乌龟会缩进壳里以避免冲突。

en: They give up their personal goals and relationships.
cn: 他们放弃个人目标和关系。

en: They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
cn: 他们认为撤退比面对冲突更容易。

en: 2. The shark.
cn: 2. 鲨鱼。

en: Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict.
cn: 鲨鱼试图通过强迫对手接受他们的解决方案来压倒对手。

en: They seek to achieve their goals at all costs.
cn: 他们不惜一切代价实现自己的目标。

en: Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing.
cn: 鲨鱼认为冲突是由一个人赢一个人输来解决的。

en: Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement.
cn: 赢得胜利给鲨鱼带来骄傲和成就感。

en: Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy and failure.
cn: 失败则让他们感到软弱、不足和失败。

en: 3. The Teddy bear.
cn: 3. 泰迪熊。

en: Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people.
cn: 泰迪熊希望被他人接受和喜欢。

en: They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships.
cn: 他们认为应避免冲突以维护和谐，并相信讨论冲突会破坏关系。

en: They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
cn: 他们放弃自己的目标以维护关系。

en: 4. The fox.
cn: 4. 狐狸。

en: Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people.
cn: 狐狸在他们的目标和与他人的关系上都持适度关注。

en: They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals.
cn: 狐狸放弃部分目标并说服冲突中的对方也放弃部分目标。

en: They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
cn: 他们寻求双方都能获得一些利益的解决方案。

en: 5. The owl.
cn: 5. 猫头鹰。

en: Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved.
cn: 猫头鹰将冲突视为需要解决的问题。

en: They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people.
cn: 他们认为冲突通过减少两人之间的紧张关系来改善关系。

en: They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem.
cn: 他们试图发起讨论，把冲突确定为问题。

en: By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship.
cn: 通过寻求能满足双方的解决方案，猫头鹰维持了这段关系。

en: Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals.
cn: 猫头鹰不满足于解决方案，直到找到一个既能实现他们自己的目标、又能实现对方目标的方案。

en: And they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.
cn: 直到紧张和负面情绪完全消除，他们才会满意。

en: The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on Earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health.
cn: 地球上已知的150万种动物和植物的基因代码将被绘制，以帮助拯救物种免于灭绝，并提升人类健康。

en: Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops and agriculture and create new biomaterials.
cn: 科学家们希望破解植物和动物的基因代码可以帮助发现治疗传染病的新方法、延缓衰老、改善农业作物并创造新的生物材料。

en: In Britain, organizations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens of Kew and the Wellcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants.
cn: 在英国，包括自然历史博物馆、邱园皇家植物园和威廉桑格研究所等组织已经联手对英国的66000种动物和植物进行测序。

en: Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take ten years and cost 100 million pounds.
cn: 这个被称为'达尔文生命之树计划'的项目预计将耗时十年，花费1亿英镑。

en: Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
cn: 一旦完成，所有信息将公开供研究者使用。

en: Many scientists believe that Earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500.
cn: 许多科学家认为地球现在已经进入了第六次大规模灭绝期，人类创造了一种有毒的混合因素，包括栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化，自1500年以来这些因素已经导致至少77种哺乳动物和140种鸟类的灭绝。

en: It is the biggest loss of species since dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago.
cn: 这是自6600万年前恐龙灭绝以来最大的物种丧失。

en: Scientists say that sequencing every species will revolutionize the understanding of biology and evolution, bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity.
cn: 科学家们表示，对每个物种的测序将彻底改变对生物学和进化的理解，加强保护、恢复生物多样性的努力。

en: Dr. Tim Littlewood, head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum, said whether you are interested in food or disease, the history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic makeup.
cn: 自然历史博物馆生命科学部主任蒂姆·利特尔伍德博士说：'无论您对食品还是疾病感兴趣，地球上每个生物对其环境的适应历史都记录在其基因构成中。'

en: How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it.
cn: 然后如何利用这些信息取决于您能否理解它。

en: We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past.
cn: 我们将采用现代方法来真正全面地了解现在和过去。

en: And of course, a window on the past gives you a perspective model on the future.
cn: 当然，从过去的视角来看未来也是如此。

en: Sir Jim Smith, director of science at Wellcome, said "Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project.
cn: 威康科学主任吉姆·史密斯爵士说：'尽管我尽力了，我仍然想不出一个更令人兴奋、更相关、更及时或更具国际灵感的项目。

en: Since 1970.
cn: 自1970年以来。

en: Humanity has wiped out 60% of animal populations.
cn: 人类已经消灭了60%的动物种群。

en: About 23,000 of 80,000 species surveyed are approaching extinction.
cn: 大约在调查的8万种中有23000种正在接近灭绝。

en: We are in the midst of the sixth great extinction event of life on our planet, which not only threatens wildlife species, but also imperils the global food supply.
cn: 我们正处于地球第六次重大生命灭绝事件之中，这不仅威胁到野生动物物种，还危及全球粮食供应。

en: As scientists, we all realize we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now.
cn: 作为科学家，我们都意识到我们急需现在记录我们脆弱星球上的生命种类。

en: I think we're making history."
cn: 我认为我们正在创造历史。'

en: John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century: "No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of a main."
cn: 约翰·多恩，这位17世纪的英国诗人曾写道：'没有任何一个人是一座孤岛，自成一体；每一个人都是大陆的一部分，是整体的一部分。'

en: Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical and cultural level than people realize.
cn: 现在，一位英国学者声称，人类的个体性实际上只是一个幻觉，因为社会在心理、身体和文化层面上的联系远比人们意识到的要紧密得多。

en: In his new book, The Self- delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as "self" and not even our bodies are truly "us".
cn: 在他的新书《自我幻觉》中，雷丁大学生态与进化研究小组的研究员汤姆·奥利弗教授提出，没有所谓的'自我'，甚至我们的身体也不完全是'我们自己'。

en: Just as Copernicus realized the earth is not the center of the universe, Professor Oliver said, Society urgently needs a Copernican like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity.
cn: 正如哥白尼意识到地球不是宇宙的中心一样，奥利弗教授说，社会迫切需要一次类似哥白尼革命的转变，理解人类不是独立的存在，而是一个互相关联的整体的一部分。

en: "A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the earth is not the center of the universe, the so- called Copernican revolution," he writes.
cn: 他说：'人类思想文化进化的一个重要里程碑是接受地球不是宇宙的中心，这就是所谓的哥白尼革命。'

en: "However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the center of a subjective universe.
cn: '然而，我们还有一个大迷思要摆脱：即我们作为独立个体存在于一个主观宇宙的中心。'

en: You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor point with the world changing around you.
cn: '你可能觉得自己是一个独立的个体，在世界上自主行动；你有一个在你的一生中不变的内在自我，作为一个中心锚点，而周围的世界则在变化。'

en: This is the illusion I seek to tackle.
cn: '这是我想要解决的幻觉。'

en: We are intimately connected to the world around us."
cn: '我们与周围的世界紧密相连。'

en: Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material "us" is constantly changing.
cn: 奥利弗教授指出，人体大约有37万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，因此物质上的'我们'是不断变化的。

en: In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than ten years.
cn: 实际上，你身体中没有任何部分存在超过十年。

en: "Since our bodies are essentially made a new every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity."
cn: '由于我们的身体每隔几周就基本上会重塑一次，仅仅靠物质无法解释身份的持续性。'

en: Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society and only by realizing we are part of a bigger entity, can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems.
cn: 奥利弗教授认为，个体主义实际上对社会有害，只有意识到我们是一个更大整体的一部分，我们才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题。

en: Through selfish overconsumption, we are destroying the natural world and using non- renewable resources at an accelerating rate.
cn: 通过自私的过度消费，我们正在以加速的速度破坏自然界并使用不可再生资源。

en: "We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behavior to act in less selfish ways," he said.
cn: '作为一个物种，我们正处于一个关键的十字路口，我们必须迅速改革我们的思维方式和行为，采取更少自私的方式行动，'他说。

en: "So let's open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us."
cn: '让我们睁开眼睛，看到我们周围隐藏的联系。'

en: OK then, this here is your yearly performance review.
cn: 好的，那么，这是你的年度绩效评估。

en: You've been with the company for three years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months.
cn: 你已经在公司工作了三年，并且在过去的12个月里在我的直接监督下工作。

en: Your report is mostly good, but there are a couple of issues we must discuss.
cn: 你的报告大部分是好的，但有几个问题我们必须讨论。

en: The report is yours to take with you.
cn: 这份报告你可以带走。

en: We'll go through the main points together now.
cn: 我们现在一起过一遍主要点。

en: And you can comb through it in greater detail later.
cn: 你可以稍后更详细地梳理它。

en: Do you have any questions before we start?
cn: 在我们开始之前，你有什么问题吗？

en: No, sir.
cn: 没有，先生。

en: I'll get straight to it then.
cn: 那我就直说了。

en: It is evident that you are a hard worker.
cn: 很明显，你是一个勤奋的员工。

en: You are punctual and industrious.
cn: 你准时且勤奋。

en: Furthermore, you have strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
cn: 此外，你有很强的分析能力和对细节的关注。

en: The company, myself included, are happy with your productivity and overall performance.
cn: 公司，包括我自己，对你的生产力和整体表现感到满意。

en: Thank you.
cn: 谢谢。

en: I appreciate the recognition.
cn: 我很感激这种认可。

en: Do you agree, then, with this depiction so far?
cn: 那么，你同意到目前为止的描述吗？

en: Yeah.
cn: 是的。

en: It's a little simplistic, perhaps, but that's to be expected from this kind of evaluation.
cn: 虽然这描述有点简单，但这在这种评估中是可以预料到的。

en: Sure.
cn: 当然。

en: Would you want to add anything?
cn: 你想补充什么呢？

en: Your comments can be added to the report if you wish.
cn: 如果你愿意，你的评论可以添加到报告中。

en: Oh, there's no need.
cn: 哦，没有必要。

en: It's a flattering portrayal, really.
cn: 这真的是一种恭维的描述。

en: Thank you, though.
cn: 谢谢。

en: Okay.
cn: 好的。

en: This leads me to the not so good part.
cn: 这把我带到了不那么好的部分。

en: This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect—your ability to work with others.
cn: 这主要集中在一个行为方面——你与他人合作的能力。

en: I see.
cn: 我明白了。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: As you already know, over the last several months, there have been some complaints raised about your communication style.
cn: 正如你已经知道的，在过去的几个月里，有一些关于你沟通风格的投诉。

en: Of course.
cn: 当然。

en: We already had, like, three meetings about this.
cn: 我们已经为此开了三次会。

en: Look, all I'm going to say is that it was never my intention to offend anyone.
cn: 听着，我只想说，我从来没有打算冒犯任何人。

en: Simply put, I don't like to write long emails because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time.
cn: 简单地说，我不喜欢写长邮件，因为坦率地说，我认为这是一种浪费时间。

en: Conciseness is efficiency.
cn: 简洁就是效率。

en: I feel that writing long emails hurts that same productivity you praised me for just a minute ago.
cn: 我觉得写长邮件会损害你刚才称赞我的生产力。

en: And I already apologized if anyone was offended.
cn: 而且我已经为冒犯任何人道歉了。

en: But to be perfectly honest, I think anyone who was offended was being a little too sensitive.
cn: 但老实说，我认为任何被冒犯的人都太敏感了。

en: So tell me, why do you wish to study medicine?
cn: 那么告诉我，你为什么想学医？

en: I've always wanted to be a doctor.
cn: 我一直想成为一名医生。

en: I come from a small town where health care was never the best, and I think that had a profound effect on me.
cn: 我来自一个小镇，那里的医疗服务从来都不是最好的，我认为这对我产生了深远的影响。

en: As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people!
cn: 小时候，我记得当时想着，能为社区服务和治病救人该有多好啊！

en: What other people or events in your life have shaped your interest in becoming a doctor?
cn: 在你生活中还有哪些人或事件让你对成为一名医生产生了兴趣？

en: Well, that's hard to say.
cn: 嗯，这很难说。

en: I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor.
cn: 我肯定会说我的父母是一个关键因素。

en: They always pushed me to study hard, and I certainly wouldn't be here without their support.
cn: 他们总是鼓励我努力学习，没有他们的支持，我当然不会在这里。

en: I guess I was also immensely fortunate to have good teachers and friends around me.
cn: 我想我也非常幸运，身边有好的老师和朋友。

en: At the end of the day, I've always been surrounded by a positive environment, conducive to my working hard and pursuing my dreams.
cn: 归根结底，我一直处在一个积极的环境中，有利于我努力工作和追求梦想。

en: Is there any medical branch that you would like to specialize in?
cn: 有没有你想专攻的医学分支？

en: I haven't decided yet.
cn: 我还没有决定。

en: It's still early days.
cn: 现在还早。

en: However, if I had to say, internal medicine.
cn: 不过，如果非要说的话，内科。

en: Why internal medicine?
cn: 为什么是内科？

en: I know it's no picnic, but I find it the most intriguing because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties.
cn: 我知道这并不轻松，但我发现它最有趣，因为它涵盖了很多内容，并将许多其他专业联系在一起。

en: Thank you.
cn: 谢谢。

en: Now I'd like to address your academic history and projected grades.
cn: 现在我想谈谈你的学术历史和预期成绩。

en: We like to think of ourselves as a prestigious institution with a highly competitive and promising student body.
cn: 我们喜欢把自己看作是一个有声望的机构，拥有高度竞争力和有前途的学生群体。

en: As you know, to get into our programs, you need at least an 85 percent score in the entrance exam.
cn: 如你所知，要进入我们的课程，你需要在入学考试中至少获得85分。

en: Do you think you can attain this?
cn: 你认为你能达到这个目标吗？

en: I think so, yes.
cn: 我想是的。

en: I'm looking at your school grades now, and I'll be honest.
cn: 我现在在看你的学校成绩，说实话。

en: It's a bit of a mixed bag.
cn: 有点参差不齐。

en: You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very, shall we say, consistent?
cn: 你确实在一些科目上取得了高分，但你的成绩不是很稳定，对吗？

en: I see no problem in making you a conditional offer, but consider yourself warned.
cn: 我认为给你提供一个有条件的录取通知书没有问题，但请注意。

en: Our entrance exam is, to use your own words, no picnic.
cn: 我们的入学考试，正如你所说，并不轻松。

en: Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon.
cn: 登录你的电子邮件账户有时感觉就像试图入侵五角大楼。

en: If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts, use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols, sign up for two- step verification, and change every password every time one of them is compromised.
cn: 如果你遵循所有的指导方针，你需要为每个账户使用不同的密码，使用难以理解的字母、数字和符号组合，注册两步验证，并在每次密码被泄露时更改每个密码。

en: More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.
cn: 更多的时候，你还需要选择包含街道标志的照片，因为这显然为你的电脑提供了坚实的证据，证明你实际上是一个人。

en: It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys.
cn: 难怪我们大多数人忘记密码的频率比忘记钥匙的频率更高。

en: Now, a new peer- reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon.
cn: 现在，芬兰阿尔托大学的研究人员进行的一项新的同行评审研究试图找出我们忘记密码的原因，以帮助结束这一令人沮丧的现象。

en: Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the intricacy of the password itself and more to do with how often you anticipate using it.
cn: 他们的研究结果表明，你记住密码的可能性与密码本身的复杂性关系不大，而与你预期使用它的频率关系更大。

en: Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often.
cn: 也就是说：如果你知道你会经常使用一个复杂的密码登录账户，那么你记住它的可能性要比记住一个你不经常登录的账户的简单密码大得多。

en: The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.
cn: 研究人员建议网站提供更多的激励措施，让用户更频繁地登录，以帮助他们记住他们的秘密代码。

en: Four years ago, Jenny Wainer was in a fitness slump.
cn: 四年前，珍妮·韦纳陷入了健身的低谷。

en: She wanted to improve her physical and mental health.
cn: 她想要改善她的身体和心理健康。

en: However, her workouts lacked intensity without a proper training program to follow.
cn: 然而，她的锻炼缺乏强度，因为没有适当的训练计划可以遵循。

en: When she went to the gym, her daily ritual predominantly involved easy exercise options like jogging.
cn: 当她去健身房时，她的日常习惯主要是像慢跑这样的轻松锻炼选项。

en: She avoided more formidable exercises like lifting weights.
cn: 她避免了像举重这样更具挑战性的锻炼。

en: A personal trainer who might push her was out of the question.
cn: 请私人教练来激励她是不可能的。

en: The extravagant cost was just unaffordable.
cn: 高昂的费用是她无法负担的。

en: She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimeretics.
cn: 然后她发现了名为Slimeretics的健身手机应用程序。

en: To use the app, you first input your profile about your previous training experiences and preferences, as well as your desired goals.
cn: 要使用这个应用，你首先输入你的个人资料，包括你以前的训练经验和偏好，以及你期望的目标。

en: A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalized training regime.
cn: 然后，一个虚拟教练会使用这些信息来建议一个个性化的训练计划。

en: After the workout, the app's artificial intelligence software system uses feedback from Ms. Wehner and its other 53 million users around the world to adjust future training sessions.
cn: 锻炼后，应用的人工智能软件系统使用来自韦纳女士和全球其他5300万用户的反馈来调整未来的训练课程。

en: Now Ms. Wehner finds the workouts exciting.
cn: 现在，韦纳女士发现锻炼变得令人兴奋。

en: This is because no two are ever the same.
cn: 这是因为没有两次锻炼是完全相同的。

en: As a result, the app has helped her to lose more than 25 kilograms.
cn: 结果，这个应用帮助她减掉了超过25公斤。

en: The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule.
cn: 应用的数学方法可以安排更细致的锻炼计划。

en: This has led to optimal results.
cn: 这导致了最佳的结果。

en: However, some experts think that apps can't replace human personal trainers and apps can't understand human behavior.
cn: 然而，一些专家认为应用不能取代人类私人教练，应用无法理解人类行为。

en: It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside the health and fitness.
cn: 它无法理解健康和健身之外还有竞争的利益。

en: Additionally, a human trainer can add compassion to the workout.
cn: 此外，人类教练可以为锻炼增加同情心。

en: He can also make exercise fun and sustainable.
cn: 他还可以使锻炼变得有趣和可持续。

en: Trainers can monitor whether a person is doing exercises correctly.
cn: 教练可以监控一个人是否正确地进行锻炼。

en: This can safeguard against injuries.
cn: 这可以防止受伤。

en: An app cannot perceive such subtleties.
cn: 应用无法感知这些细微差别。

en: All societies are held together by 7 universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
cn: 所有社会都是由七条普遍的道德规则支撑的，这些规则包括顺从上级和尊重他人财产，牛津大学得出这样的结论。

en: Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
cn: 虽然许多文化正朝着更加自由、等级制度较弱的组织迈进，但新的研究表明，传统的权力结构以及慈善和兄弟情谊的基本价值观是成功社会的基石。

en: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes.
cn: 这项对全球60种不同文化的大型研究发现，所有社区都在七种基本道德准则下运作。

en: Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favours, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly and respect the property of others.
cn: 这些普遍规则是：帮助你的家人，帮助你的群体，回报恩惠，勇敢，服从上级，公平分配资源，尊重他人财产。

en: The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found.
cn: 研究人员发现，这些性格特征适用于各种社区，无论是传统的狩猎采集者还是先进文明，都有助于维护文明社会和促进社会合作。

en: "Everyone, everywhere, shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford.
cn: '每个人，无论在哪里，都共享一个共同的道德准则，'牛津大学的首席作者和高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·库里博士说。

en: "These 7 moral rules appear to be universal across cultures because people face the same social problems.
cn: '这7个道德规则似乎在不同文化中普遍存在，因为人们面临相同的社会问题。

en: Even if some of these traits look right wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something.
cn: 即使其中一些特征看起来是右翼或保守的，例如服从权威，左翼人士仍然会有群体忠诚和对某人或某事的尊重。

en: This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."
cn: 这表明我们之间的共同点确实比分歧更多。'

en: The study, published in Current Anthropology, is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
cn: 这项发表在《当代人类学》上的研究是有史以来规模最大、最全面和最广泛的道德调查，旨在找出不同社会是否有不同版本的道德。

en: The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world.
cn: 该团队访问了世界上最好的档案，分析了来自全球60个社会的600多个来源的描述。

en: They found that the 7 rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions, and politics.
cn: 他们发现，这7个规则在所有社会中被认为是道德良好的，并且在所有大陆、宗教和政治中都被观察到。

en: However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others.
cn: 然而，一些社区比其他社区更重视某些规则。

en: Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ.
cn: 库里博士希望这项研究有助于促进不同文化之间的相互理解，并欣赏我们的共同点以及我们如何和为什么不同。

en: Co- author, Professor Harvey Loinbo, said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field rather than relying on old data.
cn: 合著者哈维·洛因博教授说，社会科学家现在应该开始在实地测试这一理论，而不是依赖旧数据。

en: "This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world," he said.
cn: '这项研究基于对世界各地文化的历史描述，'他说。

en: "These descriptions were made independent of, and prior to, the theory we're testing.
cn: '这些描述是在我们测试的理论之前独立进行的。

en: In the future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data more systematically out in the field."
cn: 未来，如果社会科学家认真对待道德理论的测试，他们将需要更系统地在实地收集新数据。'

en: When it comes to food, color is money.
cn: 当谈到食物时，颜色就是金钱。

en: Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings.
cn: 食品公司知道更好的颜色会带来更好的价格，因此他们确保他们的产品在颜色上具有吸引力以增加收入。

en: Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards, and oranges are just the beginning.
cn: 例如，橙子必须符合特定的颜色标准，而橙子只是开始。

en: There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey, and milk.
cn: 包括炸薯条、西红柿、南瓜、橄榄、蜂蜜和牛奶在内的食物都有颜色标准。

en: The attention to color is for good reason.
cn: 对颜色的关注是有充分理由的。

en: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience.
cn: 尽管我们谈论舌头，但我们的眼睛可能真的是饮食体验中最重要的部分。

en: A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
cn: 我们大脑的许多功能都致力于处理视觉，而只有百分之一二的功能用于味觉，结果是颜色实际上改变了我们对食物的味觉。

en: Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste.
cn: 科学家们多次证明了颜色对味觉的重要性。

en: In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage.
cn: 例如，在1980年代的一项研究中，测试参与者被要求在不看到饮料的情况下说出他们正在喝的饮料的味道。

en: Only one in five was able to identify it as orange.
cn: 只有五分之一的人能够识别出它是橙子味。

en: But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking, which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor.
cn: 但当他们被允许看到他们正在喝的饮料，它是橙色的，每个人都识别出了橙子味。

en: And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange.
cn: 而当一种酸橙味的饮料被染成橙色时，近一半的受访者将饮料的味道识别为橙子味。

en: None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color.
cn: 当饮料是绿色时，没有人犯这个错误。

en: What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see, or that has an abnormal color?
cn: 当有人无法识别他们看不到的饮料的味道，或者饮料颜色异常时，发生了什么？

en: Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is and so rely on visual cues?
cn: 是参与者无法辨别味道，因此依赖视觉线索吗？

en: Or does color actually change the experience of taste?
cn: 还是颜色实际上改变了味觉体验？

en: The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation.
cn: 这些问题的关键在于颜色对期望的影响。

en: The brain makes predictions using color.
cn: 大脑使用颜色进行预测。

en: These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience.
cn: 这些预测依赖于来自经验的期望。

en: Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them.
cn: 研究表明，我们天生喜欢甜食并渴望吃它们。

en: But we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like, so we need to learn this over time.
cn: 但我们并不是天生就知道我们渴望的甜食是什么样子的，所以我们需要随着时间的推移学习这一点。

en: The brain gets information from the environment, and we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet.
cn: 大脑从环境中获取信息，我们学习到，例如，水果从绿色和酸味变为红色和成熟和甜味。

en: Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste.
cn: 因此，如果我们看到一个绿色的浆果，我们会将其颜色与酸味联系起来。

en: And just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.
cn: 仅仅看到一个红色的水果就会激活我们的期望，认为它会尝起来甜美可口。

en: Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives.
cn: 寻找意义是我们许多人在一生中都会经历的事情。

en: For some, this meaning is religious, some political, and some interpersonal.
cn: 对一些人来说，这种意义是宗教的，一些是政治的，一些是人际关系的。

en: And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.
cn: 拥有意义感可以带给我们幸福。

en: A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources.
cn: 一项新的研究探讨了在财务资源背景下意义与幸福之间的关系。

en: Rhea Katapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning.
cn: 多伦多大学的Rhea Katapano和同事们发现，对富人来说，意义对幸福的预测作用远弱于贫穷的人，这表明经济资源会影响我们感受意义的方式。

en: The team analyzed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries.
cn: 该团队分析了来自123个国家的超过50万人的数据。

en: The first study used data from a daily poll of U.S. residents collected between 2013 and 2015.
cn: 第一项研究使用了2013年至2015年间收集的美国居民的每日民意调查数据。

en: Well- being was tracked using measures of positive effect—whether during the day, before they were surveyed, participants have smiled or laughed a lot, or experienced a lot of happiness.
cn: 幸福感的衡量标准是积极情绪指标——即在受访前的日常生活中，参与者是否经常开怀大笑或频繁体验到快乐。

en: Meaning was measured through a daily 'purpose index', which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals.
cn: 意义通过每日'目的指数'测量，探索了参与者对他们每天做的事情的喜好程度以及实现目标的动机程度。

en: Finally, income levels were assessed.
cn: 最后，评估了收入水平。

en: The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets.
cn: 结果显示，意义与幸福之间的相关性在低收入群体中最为强烈。

en: But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker.
cn: 但随着收入水平的提高，相关性变弱。

en: The second study looked at worldwide data.
cn: 第二项研究查看了全球数据。

en: Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question: 'Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?'
cn: 幸福感使用与第一项研究相同的问题来衡量，而意义则使用单一问题来衡量：'你觉得你的生活有重要的目的或意义吗？'

en: Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants' income: meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets.
cn: 再次，意义与幸福之间关系的强度取决于参与者的收入：与高收入群体相比，意义对低收入群体的幸福感有更大的影响。

en: In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life and how much they considered themselves a happy person.
cn: 在最后一项研究中，法国参与者表示他们认为自己过着有目的和有意义的生活的程度，以及他们认为自己是一个幸福的人的程度。

en: Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a social ladder, representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career.
cn: 与其使用特定的收入区间，研究让他们在一个社会阶梯上自我定位，表示他们在财富、教育和职业方面的位置。

en: The results from this study duplicated those of the first two.
cn: 这项研究的结果与前两项研究的结果相同。

en: So overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship in those with fewer resources than those with more.
cn: 因此，总体来说，意义和幸福在资源较少的人群中相关性较强，而在资源较多的群体中则较弱。

en: This might be the case because richer individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community.
cn: 这可能是由于较富裕的个体有更多获得其他幸福来源的途径，其中许多是外部的，如缺乏压力或社区。

en: Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose, or meaning is less important.
cn: 因此，对内部满足感、目的或意义的关注就不那么重要了。

en: Hi, Alan.
cn: 嗨，艾伦。

en: Sorry for not calling you back sooner.
cn: 抱歉没有早点给你回电话。

en: You said on the phone you had something you needed to discuss with me?
cn: 你在电话里说有事要和我讨论？

en: Well, to get right down to it, I'm having second thoughts about my major.
cn: 嗯，直说吧，我对我的专业有些犹豫了。

en: With my family situation getting more complicated and the end of my university education nearing, persisting with Art History just doesn't seem the right choice.
cn: 随着我的家庭情况变得越来越复杂，加上大学教育接近尾声，继续坚持艺术史似乎不是一个正确的选择。

en: Alan, in the last 3 years, I have heard nothing but how passionate you are about the Art History programme.
cn: 艾伦，在过去三年里，我听到的都是你对艺术史项目的热情。

en: You often told fellow classmates how fabulous the instructors were and that you finally felt accepted.
cn: 你经常告诉同学们那些讲师有多棒，而且你终于感到被接纳了。

en: What would cause you to abandon it?
cn: 是什么让你想放弃呢？

en: My father's current financial situation has helped me realize that a more financially viable employment opportunity is not necessarily a bad thing.
cn: 我父亲目前的经济状况让我意识到，选择一个更有经济前景的就业机会未必是件坏事。

en: Art History nourishes my soul, but does nothing to put food on my plate.
cn: 艺术史滋养了我的灵魂，但却不能为我提供生计。

en: What about all the work opportunities I discussed with you last month?
cn: 那我上个月和你讨论的那些工作机会呢？

en: Have you gone to those places of business to investigate whether any legitimate positions might be available for someone with your background?
cn: 你有没有去那些公司调查一下，看看是否有适合你背景的合法职位？

en: Um, well...
cn: 嗯，这个……

en: Look, Alan, if your heart is set on working in the art industry, you need to be more assertive and start talking with people.
cn: 听着，艾伦，如果你一心想要在艺术行业工作，你需要更加积极主动，开始与人交流。

en: Networking is key if you want to become a celebrity in the world of museums and galleries.
cn: 如果你想在博物馆和画廊的世界里成名，人脉是关键。

en: Time is a very precious commodity right now.
cn: 现在时间非常宝贵。

en: My social life does not exist.
cn: 我的社交生活几乎不存在。

en: I can barely keep up with my studies and thesis is due by the end of this year.
cn: 我几乎跟不上我的学习进度，而且论文今年年底就要交了。

en: When can I find time to research jobs when I have so much to do as it is?
cn: 在这么多事情要做的情况下，我哪有时间去研究工作？

en: What you do now will determine your future options.
cn: 你现在所做的将决定你未来的选择。

en: Now is the optimum time to put forth your best effort.
cn: 现在是全力以赴的最佳时机。

en: I will take what you said into consideration.
cn: 我会考虑你说的话。

en: The advice is much appreciated.
cn: 非常感谢你的建议。

en: Have you decided yet what your end- of- semester business project will be on?
cn: 你决定好期末的商业项目要做什么了吗？

en: Yes, how about you?
cn: 是的，你呢？

en: Yes, go on.
cn: 我也决定了，你先说吧。

en: You go first.
cn: 你先说吧。

en: I'm going to do it about beef.
cn: 我打算做关于牛肉的项目。

en: Beef?
cn: 牛肉？

en: Yeah, beef.
cn: 对，牛肉。

en: I'm going to design a business case study for a cow farm that supplies beef for the domestic market.
cn: 我打算为一家供应国内市场的养牛场设计一个商业案例研究。

en: Wow, that sounds very interesting and original.
cn: 哇，这听起来非常有趣且有创意。

en: Where ever did you get that idea?
cn: 你是怎么想到这个主意的？

en: I don't know, it just came to me I guess.
cn: 我也不知道，可能就是灵光一现吧。

en: But think about it.
cn: 但想想看。

en: Beef consumption has been rising strongly over the past 20 years.
cn: 过去20年里，牛肉消费量一直在强劲增长。

en: As the economy continues to grow, consumer demand is expected to continue to increase, for the foreseeable future.
cn: 随着经济的持续发展，预计在可预见的未来，消费者需求还会继续增加。

en: And currently, most of the beef is imported, which brings with it added fees.
cn: 而目前，大部分牛肉都是进口的，这带来了额外的费用。

en: So why not raise cattle here?
cn: 所以为什么不在本地养牛呢？

en: Of course.
cn: 当然。

en: Makes perfect sense.
cn: 这完全说得通。

en: There's plenty of land out west, so if done right, it should be very profitable to raise our own cattle.
cn: 西部有大量的土地，如果操作得当，养牛应该会非常有利可图。

en: Exactly.
cn: 没错。

en: Seriously, that sounds like a great idea.
cn: 说真的，这听起来是个很棒的主意。

en: You should genuinely look into it once we get our degrees.
cn: 等我们拿到学位后，你真的应该好好考虑一下。

en: Thanks.
cn: 谢谢。

en: So, your turn now.
cn: 那么，轮到你了。

en: What are you doing your case study on?
cn: 你的案例研究是关于什么的？

en: I was thinking about a car wash, but it now seems like such a boring notion after hearing your brilliant idea.
cn: 我本来想做一个洗车场的项目，但听完你的好主意后，现在觉得这个想法有点无聊了。

en: That's cool.
cn: 那也不错啊。

en: I could see that working.
cn: 我觉得这个项目可行。

en: After all, there's plenty of cars about, and those aren't going away anytime soon.
cn: 毕竟，街上有很多车，而且短期内也不会减少。

en: While many people don't care how their car looks, many other people do.
cn: 虽然很多人不在乎车的外观，但也有很多人很在意。

en: You've got yourself a vast and continual market.
cn: 你有一个庞大且持续的市场。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: So the idea is a large, self- cleaning car wash.
cn: 所以我的想法是做一个大型的自助洗车场。

en: But I mean really big and well outfitted, like they have in America.
cn: 但我说的是那种非常大且设备齐全的，就像美国的那种。

en: I was thinking of having it cater to high- end consumers in large cities.
cn: 我考虑把它定位为服务大城市的高端消费者。

en: It could charge a profitable mark up by offering just a bit more technical equipment and professional service than competitors.
cn: 通过提供比竞争对手更先进的技术设备和更专业的服务，可以收取更高的费用，从而获得可观的利润。

en: Increased television time for young children has long been linked with poorer progress in some areas of development.
cn: 长期以来，幼儿看电视时间的增加一直与某些发展领域的进展较差有关。

en: One possible way to counter those negative effects is talking while watching the screen.
cn: 抵消这些负面影响的一种可能方法是在看电视时进行对话。

en: As a new study suggests, the more parents engaged in conversation with preschoolers during TV time, the more likely those children were to have higher curiosity levels when they reached kindergarten.
cn: 一项新研究表明，父母在幼儿看电视时与他们交谈得越多，这些孩子在进入幼儿园时就越有可能表现出更高的好奇心水平。

en: This was particularly true for children with socioeconomic disadvantages.
cn: 这对于社会经济条件较差的儿童尤其明显。

en: "Our findings reinforce the importance of parent conversation to promote early childhood development and curiosity," said lead author Prachi Shah at University of Michigan Health C. S. Mott Children's Hospital.
cn: 密歇根大学健康中心C.S.莫特儿童医院的首席作者Prachi Shah表示：'我们的研究结果强调了父母对话对促进幼儿发展和好奇心的重要性。'

en: Researchers assessed hours of daily television exposure and frequency of parent screen time conversation among 1, 500 preschoolers.
cn: 研究人员评估了1500名学龄前儿童的每日电视观看时间以及父母在屏幕时间内的对话频率。

en: And then measured early childhood curiosity in kindergarten.
cn: 然后在幼儿园阶段测量了他们的好奇心水平。

en: The study specifically focused on curiosity levels, which are associated with enhanced learning and higher academic achievement in reading and math at kindergarten.
cn: 该研究特别关注好奇心水平，好奇心与幼儿园阶段阅读和数学的学习能力增强以及更高的学业成绩相关。

en: And behavioral developmental benefits, especially for children from families with lower socioeconomic status.
cn: 并且对来自社会经济地位较低家庭的儿童有行为发展的益处。

en: While many young children are now growing up with digital media exposure through mobile devices like tablets and phones.
cn: 尽管现在许多幼儿通过平板电脑和手机等移动设备接触数字媒体。

en: Television remains a dominant screen activity, accounting for 72% of all screen time.
cn: 电视仍然是主要的屏幕活动，占所有屏幕时间的72%。

en: TVs are in 98% of all homes, keeping television exposure a relevant developmental context in young children.
cn: 98%的家庭拥有电视，这使得电视观看仍然是幼儿发展的一个重要背景。

en: Excessive media exposure, including television, can displace exploratory activities such as play and parent- child interactions, which are believed to be key to cultivating curiosity in kids.
cn: 过度的媒体接触，包括电视，可能会取代探索性活动，如玩耍和亲子互动，而这些活动被认为是培养孩子好奇心的关键。

en: "Our findings suggest the importance of parents finding opportunities to foster conversational exchanges in daily routines with their young children—including while watching television," Shah said.
cn: Shah表示：'我们的研究结果表明，父母在日常生活中，包括看电视时，找到机会与幼儿进行对话交流的重要性。'

en: Humans are aspirational, goal- seeking beings.
cn: 人类是有抱负、追求目标的生物。

en: Each of us, according to research, has an inborn drive to acquire.
cn: 根据研究，我们每个人都有一种与生俱来的获取欲望。

en: The dark side of this drive to acquire is being mindlessly driven to possess more and more things and to socially compare our stuff with all the stuff other people have in their lives.
cn: 这种获取欲望的阴暗面是盲目地追求拥有越来越多的东西，并在社会上将自己拥有的东西与他人生活中的东西进行比较。

en: So the question is, how do we ensure we tap into our drive to acquire in positive ways that will benefit our well- being?
cn: 那么问题来了，我们如何确保以积极的方式利用这种获取欲望，从而有益于我们的幸福感？

en: One way is to become more intentionally aspirational.
cn: 一种方法是变得更加有意识地追求抱负。

en: To be intentionally aspirational includes consciously aspiring to be the person you need to be to succeed in your professional and personal life.
cn: 有意识地追求抱负包括有意识地渴望成为在职业和个人生活中取得成功所需的人。

en: It also includes consciously aspiring to acquire things in your life that will positively impact your sense of well- being.
cn: 它还包括有意识地渴望获得生活中那些能积极影响你幸福感的东西。

en: If you're not consciously, mindfully, and intentionally harnessing this innate, inborn drive to acquire.
cn: 如果你没有有意识、有目的地利用这种与生俱来的获取欲望。

en: You might be mindlessly pursuing all the wrong things.
cn: 你可能会盲目地追求所有错误的东西。

en: While your intentional, aspirational goals will include the pursuit of inquiring things that will increase your sense of well- being, they ought to also include goals to help other people in your various life roles.
cn: 虽然你有意识的、有抱负的目标将包括追求那些能增加你幸福感的东西，但它们也应该包括在你各种生活角色中帮助他人的目标。

en: Your intentional, aspirational goals will also include striving to be your personal best—a person of good character, integrity, and trustworthiness.
cn: 你有意识的、有抱负的目标还将包括努力做到个人最佳——成为一个具有良好品格、正直和值得信赖的人。

en: Think about this from a practical rather than theoretical viewpoint.
cn: 从实际而非理论的角度来思考这个问题。

en: If you're not pursuing intentional aspirational goals, you have nothing to strive for.
cn: 如果你不追求有意识的有抱负的目标，你就没有奋斗的方向。

en: If you have nothing to strive for, you're putting yourself in the dangerous position of simply drifting through life, and you'll not be able to experience, live, and enjoy all that life has to offer.
cn: 如果你没有奋斗的方向，你就会陷入一种危险的状态，即只是随波逐流地生活，你将无法体验、生活和享受生活所提供的一切。

en: It's revision time for exams and dissertations.
cn: 现在是考试和论文的复习时间。

en: The pressure is on, so you'll want all the help you can get to age your memory and raise your grades.
cn: 压力很大，所以你希望尽一切可能提高记忆力和成绩。

en: As a nutrition expert, I want to say that eating well can make a real difference to your revision regime.
cn: 作为一名营养专家，我想说，良好的饮食真的可以对你的复习计划产生重大影响。

en: So, what brain- boosting food and drink would I recommend?
cn: 那么，我会推荐哪些有助于提升大脑功能的食物和饮料呢？

en: Coffee can have numerous benefits.
cn: 咖啡有很多好处。

en: However, while coffee may make you more alert, individuals can build up a tolerance, meaning this is short- lived.
cn: 然而，虽然咖啡可能会让你更加警觉，但个人可能会对其产生耐受性，这意味着这种效果是短暂的。

en: Coffee can also increase blood sugar and eventually cause lack of focus and energy.
cn: 咖啡还可能会升高血糖，最终导致注意力不集中和能量不足。

en: It's also worth noting that people react differently to coffee.
cn: 值得注意的是，人们对咖啡的反应不同。

en: Some people can drink it at midnight and go straight to sleep, whereas others get feelings of anxiety after a small amount.
cn: 有些人可以在午夜喝咖啡后直接入睡，而另一些人则在少量饮用后感到焦虑。

en: Also remember that coffee from a coffee shop may be stronger than coffee made at home.
cn: 还要记住，咖啡店的咖啡可能比家里煮的咖啡更浓。

en: So stop drinking coffee by 2 p.m. and have a maximum of two cups of coffee a day.
cn: 所以请在下午2点之前停止饮用咖啡，并且每天最多喝两杯。

en: But be aware of your own reaction to it.
cn: 但要留意自己对咖啡的反应。

en: Whole grain foods will ward off hunger.
cn: 全谷物食品可以抵御饥饿感。

en: Examples include porridge and whole wheat bread.
cn: 例子包括燕麦粥和全麦面包。

en: Combining whole grain foods with protein will help keep your blood sugar levels balanced, which is essential for mood and concentration.
cn: 将全谷物食品与蛋白质结合可以帮助平衡血糖水平，这对情绪和注意力至关重要。

en: Berries and nuts are a convenient and nutritious snack.
cn: 浆果和坚果是一种方便且营养丰富的零食。

en: Blueberries, like many dark colored fruits and vegetables, can slow down brain damage and age- related decline.
cn: 蓝莓，像许多深色水果和蔬菜一样，可以减缓大脑损伤和与年龄相关的衰退。

en: Frozen berries are also a good choice.
cn: 冷冻浆果也是一个不错的选择。

en: They are usually cheap, last longer, and don't lose their nutrients when frozen.
cn: 它们通常价格便宜，保存时间更长，并且在冷冻时不会失去营养。

en: But flavored and coated nuts are less healthy, as they contain added oil, salt, and sugar.
cn: 但调味和涂层的坚果不太健康，因为它们含有额外的油、盐和糖。

en: Doctors often recommend taking vitamin supplements to top up on the nutrients you need.
cn: 医生经常建议服用维生素补充剂来补充所需的营养。

en: But I would say food should always come before supplements, and the key to getting as many nutrients as possible is to eat a varied diet, with lots of different colors, such as frozen berries and dark green vegetables.
cn: 但我想说，食物应该始终优先于补充剂，而获取尽可能多营养的关键是饮食多样化，包括多种颜色的食物，如冷冻浆果和深绿色蔬菜。

en: It's better to get everything you need from food and drink.
cn: 最好从食物和饮料中获取所需的一切。

en: For example, oranges contain not only vitamin C, which boosts the immune system, but also fiber and other components that you can't get packaged together in a tablet.
cn: 例如，橙子不仅含有增强免疫系统的维生素C，还含有纤维和其他成分，这些成分无法在药片中一起获得。

en: Don't forget to drink a proper amount of water, which can boost attention by almost 25%, and can elevate your mood as well.
cn: 不要忘记喝适量的水，这可以将注意力提高近25%，并提升你的情绪。

en: Finally, don't skip meals.
cn: 最后，不要不吃饭。

en: Eating regularly will help keep blood sugar balanced, and feed the brain with the fuel it needs.
cn: 规律饮食有助于保持血糖平衡，并为大脑提供所需的能量。

en: The late Swedish academic Hans Rosling has identified a worrying trend: not only do many people across advanced economies have no idea that the world is becoming a much better place, but they actually even think the opposite.
cn: 已故的瑞典学者汉斯·罗斯林发现了一个令人担忧的趋势：不仅许多发达经济体的人不知道世界正在变得更好，他们甚至认为情况相反。

en: This is no wonder, when the news focuses on reporting catastrophes, terrorist attacks, wars, and famines.
cn: 这并不奇怪，因为新闻专注于报道灾难、恐怖袭击、战争和饥荒。

en: Who wants to hear about the fact that every day some 200,000 people around the world are lifted above the two dollar a day poverty line?
cn: 谁愿意听到每天约有20万人摆脱每天2美元的贫困线？

en: Or that more than 300,000 people get access to electricity and clean water for the first time every day?
cn: 或者每天有超过30万人首次获得电力和清洁用水？

en: These stories of people in low- income countries simply don't make for exciting news coverage.
cn: 这些关于低收入国家人民的故事并不能成为激动人心的新闻报道。

en: But as Rosling pointed out in his book Factfulness.
cn: 但正如罗斯林在他的书《事实》中指出的那样。

en: It's important to put all the bad news in perspective.
cn: 重要的是要全面看待所有坏消息。

en: While it is true that globalization has put some downward pressure on middle class wages in advanced economies in recent decades, it has also helped lift hundreds of millions of people above the global poverty line.
cn: 虽然全球化确实在近几十年来对发达经济体的中产阶级工资施加了下行压力，但它也帮助数亿人摆脱了全球贫困线。

en: If we really care about global welfare, globalization is the only way forward to ensure that economic prosperity is shared among all countries and not only a select few advanced economies.
cn: 如果我们真正关心全球福祉，全球化是确保经济繁荣在所有国家之间共享的唯一途径，而不仅仅是少数发达经济体。

en: While some people glorify the past, one of the big facts of economic history is that until quite recently, a significant part of the world's population has lived under quite miserable conditions—and this has been true throughout most of human history.
cn: 尽管有些人总爱美化过去，但经济史上一个不争的事实是：直到不久之前，全球仍有大量人口生活在极度贫困之中——而这在人类历史长河中才是常态。

en: While there were many long- lasting ups and downs, like the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession, the constancy of the long- run growth rate is actually quite miraculous.
cn: 尽管有许多长期的起伏，如大萧条或最近的大衰退，但长期增长率的稳定性实际上是一个奇迹。

en: Low- income countries, including China and India, have been growing at a significantly faster pace in recent decades, and are quickly catching up to the West.
cn: 包括中国和印度在内的低收入国家在近年来增长速度显著加快，并迅速赶上西方。

en: A 10 percent growth rate over a prolonged period means that income levels double roughly every seven years.
cn: 长期保持10%的增长率意味着收入水平大约每七年翻一番。

en: It is obviously good news if prosperity is more shared across the globe.
cn: 如果全球范围内的繁荣更加共享，这显然是个好消息。

en: While inequality within countries has gone up as a result of globalization, global inequality has been on a steady downward trend for several decades.
cn: 尽管全球化导致国家内部的不平等加剧，但全球不平等已经持续了几十年的下降趋势。

en: This is mostly a result of the improvement of hundreds of millions of people's living standards.
cn: 这主要是数亿人生活水平提高的结果。

en: In fact, for the first time ever since the Industrial Revolution, about half of the global population can be considered middle class.
cn: 事实上，自工业革命以来，全球人口中约有一半可以被视为中产阶级，这是有史以来的第一次。

en: We all know that the sense of smell is powerful.
cn: 我们都知道嗅觉是非常强大的。

en: The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine.
cn: 例如，面包的香味可以像一台时光机。

en: One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago.
cn: 一嗅就能唤起多年前的记忆。

en: Indeed, scent particles, in general, can revive memories that have been long forgotten.
cn: 事实上，气味分子通常可以唤醒早已被遗忘的记忆。

en: But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones?
cn: 但为什么气味有时会触发强烈的记忆，尤其是情感记忆呢？

en: The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories, and emotions are linked.
cn: 简短的答案是，处理气味、记忆和情感的大脑区域是相互关联的。

en: A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read.
cn: 气味是一种化学粒子，通过鼻子进入大脑中负责嗅觉的区域，在那里感觉首先被处理成大脑可以读取的形式。

en: Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place.
cn: 然后，脑细胞将这些信息传递到处理情感的大脑区域，再传递到相邻的学习和记忆形成区域。

en: Scents are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain.
cn: 气味是唯一一种通过如此直接的路径到达大脑情感和记忆中心的感觉。

en: That results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories, and sense.
cn: 这导致了情感、记忆和气味之间的紧密联系。

en: Which is why memories triggered by sense are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound.
cn: 这就是为什么由气味触发的记忆比由视觉或听觉触发的记忆更具情感性。

en: Let's take a closer look at how those memories are activated.
cn: 让我们更仔细地看看这些记忆是如何被激活的。

en: Usually, when a person smells something that's connected to a meaningful event in their past, they'll first have an emotional response to the sensation, and then a memory might follow.
cn: 通常，当一个人闻到与过去有意义的事件相关的气味时，他们首先会对这种感觉产生情感反应，然后可能会回忆起相关的记忆。

en: But sometimes, the memory doesn't come to the surface.
cn: 但有时，记忆并不会浮现。

en: The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past, but won't remember what they experienced.
cn: 这个人可能会感受到过去发生的事情的情感，但不会记得他们经历了什么。

en: What causes this baffling phenomenon?
cn: 是什么导致了这种令人困惑的现象？

en: The explanation is context.
cn: 答案是情境。

en: Imagine this scenario: a person is walking down the street, smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response.
cn: 想象一下这个场景：一个人走在街上，闻到几十年前第一次遇到的气味，这会激活情感反应。

en: If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory, because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory.
cn: 如果这个人第一次闻到这种气味时的情境非常不同，那么回忆起相关记忆就会更加困难，因为大脑使用情境来赋予信息意义并找到那个记忆。

en: The special nature of memories brought back by scents notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories.
cn: 尽管由气味唤起的记忆具有特殊性，但它们与其他记忆有相同的缺点。

en: They aren't always accurate, and they can change over time.
cn: 它们并不总是准确的，而且会随着时间的推移而改变。

en: In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted.
cn: 事实上，每当我们回忆起某件事时，那个记忆可能会变得扭曲。

en: But, because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren't.
cn: 但是，由于这些记忆唤起了强烈的情感联想，人们往往会坚信由气味唤起的记忆是准确的，即使它们并不准确。

en: Good morning.
cn: 早上好。

en: My name is Bob Fetterman.
cn: 我叫鲍勃·费特曼。

en: I'm the computer technician.
cn: 我是电脑技术员。

en: Didn't I call for you last week?
cn: 我上周是不是给你打过电话？

en: Maybe.
cn: 可能吧。

en: I work for Alpha Maintenance.
cn: 我在阿尔法维修公司工作。

en: I imagine someone from your office called our central office, and I'm the engineer designated to your case.
cn: 我想是你们办公室有人打了我们的中心办公室电话，而我是被指派来处理你这个情况的工程师。

en: Yeah, I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago.
cn: 是的，我上周二和那里的一位女士通过话，到现在已经10天了。

en: I made it clear it was an urgent matter and 'please send someone as soon as possible'.
cn: 我当时说得很清楚，事情很紧急，'请尽快派人过来'。

en: Couldn't you or someone else have come sooner?
cn: 你们就不能早点派人来吗？

en: I'm sorry, but I'm not in charge of scheduling or logistics.
cn: 抱歉，排期和后勤安排不归我管。

en: I simply do not know.
cn: 我确实不清楚。

en: All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could.
cn: 我只能告诉你，我这周接到通知后就尽快赶过来了。

en: I see.
cn: 我知道了。

en: Well, I'll have you know my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come.
cn: 跟你说吧，我经理对你们这么久才来非常生气。

en: I understand it might not be your fault, but nevertheless, you should know what the feeling is around here.
cn: 我明白这可能不是你的错，但不管怎样，你应该知道我们这边的感受。

en: I understand.
cn: 我理解。

en: And I'm sorry for any inconvenience.
cn: 对于造成的任何不便，我很抱歉。

en: I will try to resolve your computer problem as swiftly and optimally as I can.
cn: 我会尽力尽快且妥善地解决你的电脑问题。

en: What and where is the issue?
cn: 问题出在哪里，是什么情况？

en: It's this machine right here.
cn: 就是这台机器。

en: It was running slow for a while, I guess, and gradually got worse and worse.
cn: 我觉得它之前慢了好一阵子，然后越来越慢。

en: Last Tuesday, it just stopped working altogether.
cn: 上周二，它干脆完全不能用了。

en: If you switch it on, you will see what I mean.
cn: 你开机看看就知道我意思了。

en: OK.
cn: 好的。

en: Do you know if it's backed up?
cn: 你知道它有没有备份吗？

en: Backed up?
cn: 备份？

en: I mean do you know if its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else?
cn: 我是说，你知道它里面的内容有没有复制保存到别的地方吗？

en: I don't know.
cn: 我不知道。

en: Well, depending on the ensuing operative scenario, if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols, then my first intervention should be to intricately retrieve all inventories that I can.
cn: 嗯，根据接下来的操作情况，如果我需要清空系统目录来重新配置默认协议，那我的首要操作就是尽可能详细地找回所有文件。

en: Otherwise, all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost.
cn: 否则，硬盘里存储的所有数据就会永远丢失了。

en: My manager would know.
cn: 我经理应该知道。

en: Let me go get him.
cn: 我去叫他过来。

en: Have you given more thoughts to studying law?
cn: 你有没有再深入考虑过学习法律这件事？

en: I've been thinking about it a lot.
cn: 我确实一直在认真思考。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: In fact, this is why I wished to speak to you.
cn: 其实，这就是我想和你聊聊的原因。

en: I wanted to hear more about what it's like.
cn: 我想多了解一下学法律是什么样子的。

en: A career in law is a beautiful thing, in my opinion.
cn: 在我看来，从事法律行业是很棒的。

en: Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree.
cn: 很多人会说这是个枯燥的领域，但我不这么认为。

en: The thing is there are many different branches of law and many different jobs.
cn: 关键是法律有很多不同的分支，也有很多不同的工作岗位。

en: You are involved with buildings and construction, right?
cn: 你是从事与建筑相关的法律工作，对吗？

en: Correct.
cn: 没错。

en: I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate.
cn: 我是一名律师，专门处理房地产方面的事务。

en: Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.
cn: 我的大部分工作都涉及调解土地纠纷。

en: Do you mind giving me an example?
cn: 你能举个例子吗？

en: Sure.
cn: 当然可以。

en: So in many cases, I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties.
cn: 在很多情况下，我受雇于当事人，在意见相左的双方之间进行仲裁。

en: Let's say, for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something, like the borders of their adjacent plots.
cn: 比如说，假设有两位土地所有者，他们在某件事上陷入了棘手的分歧，比如相邻地块的边界问题。

en: Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute.
cn: 这时可能就会有人聘请我来打破僵局，解决争端。

en: Often my work involves negotiating agreements, plain and simple.
cn: 通常来说，我的工作就是进行协议谈判，就这么简单明了。

en: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people's legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating.
cn: 所以你的意思是，你做的很多工作都是解决人们的法律问题，比如努力找到一个对每个人都有利的解决方案，防止问题升级。

en: Exactly.
cn: 完全正确。

en: Well put.
cn: 说得很到位。

en: You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating and expensive.
cn: 你要知道，法院和所有的官僚机构一样，事情往往很繁琐、令人沮丧，而且花费高昂。

en: For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.
cn: 正因为如此，只要有可能，最好在法庭之外解决问题。

en: I see.
cn: 我明白了。

en: So besides knowing the law inside out, you need good people skills, right?
cn: 所以除了要精通法律，还需要具备良好的人际交往能力，对吗？

en: Of course.
cn: 当然。

en: Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating their arguments.
cn: 任何涉及与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际交往能力，而且任何法律专业人士都需要能言善辩，清晰地阐述自己的论点。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: So I've been thinking about studying criminal law.
cn: 我一直在考虑学习刑法。

en: I think it sounds very interesting.
cn: 我觉得它听起来很有意思。

en: Mm, yes.
cn: 嗯，是的。

en: I'd say there's more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law.
cn: 我得说，财产法领域的收入更高一些，但刑法领域的风险更大。

en: I can see how you would find it more interesting.
cn: 我能理解你为什么会觉得刑法更有意思。

en: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information.
cn: 当一个人试图唤起一段记忆时，他们的大脑会迅速检查其中存储的所有信息，以找到相关内容。

en: But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
cn: 但随着年龄的增长，我们很多人在回忆往事时会遇到困难。

en: In a review published in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.
cn: 在2月11日发表于《认知科学趋势》杂志的一篇综述中，研究人员对这一现象的原因提出了一种解释：老年人的大脑会为积累的知识分配更多空间，因此在试图唤起记忆时，需要处理的信息更多。

en: While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides—this life experience can aid with creativity and decision- making.
cn: 研究人员表示，虽然丰富的已有知识会给记忆提取带来挑战，但也有其积极的一面——这些生活经验有助于提升创造力和决策能力。

en: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it.
cn: 研究人员塔里克·阿米尔、乔丹娜·韦恩和林恩·哈舍查看了多项行为学和脑成像研究，这些研究表明，老年人难以抑制不再相关的信息，而且在搜寻特定记忆时，他们往往会同时回忆起其他不相关的记忆。

en: The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
cn: 研究还显示，在执行认知任务时，老年人比年轻人更依赖过往知识。

en: While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful.
cn: 尽管研究人员主要关注这些杂乱繁多的记忆可能带来的困难，但他们也强调，在某些情况下，这种记忆模式可能是有用的。

en: "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write.
cn: 研究人员写道：'有证据表明，由于记忆更加丰富，老年人的创造力得以保持，有时甚至会增强。'

en: They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision- making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.
cn: 他们进一步推测，在决策方面，老年人可能会得益于自己的已有知识，因为他们可以运用积累的智慧。

en: There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
cn: 如今，美国的工作存在至少四个主要问题。

en: First, work can be alienating.
cn: 首先，工作可能会让人感到疏离。

en: Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
cn: 员工往往无法掌控自己的工作方式、工作时间、他们所生产的商品和服务的去向，以及他们的劳动所产生的利润的用途。

en: Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor.
cn: 其次，劳动者没有获得其劳动的全部价值。

en: Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.
cn: 实际工资未能跟上生产率的增长步伐，这加剧了经济不平等，并导致劳动收入占比下降。

en: Third, people are time- poor.
cn: 第三，人们时间匮乏。

en: In the US, full- time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases.
cn: 在美国，尽管生产率有所提高，但全职员工平均每天仍工作8.72小时。

en: Long working hours contribute to the feeling of time poverty, which has an adverse effect on psychological well- being.
cn: 长时间的工作导致了时间贫困感，这对心理健康产生了不利影响。

en: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk.
cn: 第四，自动化使工作岗位和工资面临风险。

en: Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40- hour workweek, but unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
cn: 从理论上讲，技术创新可以将人们从每周40小时的工作中解放出来，但除非对工作结构进行改革，否则自动化只会给工资带来下行压力，并进一步减少就业机会。

en: So, what can be done to alleviate these problems?
cn: 那么，我们能做些什么来缓解这些问题呢？

en: There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution.
cn: 对于找到最佳解决方案，存在着不同的观点。

en: One vision is what's known as the 'post- work' position.
cn: 其中一种观点被称为'后工作'立场。

en: The post- work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time.
cn: 后工作理论家认为，工作不应在我们的生活中占据核心地位，也不应占用我们如此多的时间。

en: They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace.
cn: 他们主张，尽管做一些工作可能是必要的，但意义、目标和社会价值存在于工作场所之外建立和维系的社区与人际关系中。

en: Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.
cn: 因此，生活本身就应该被视为目的。

en: Recent studies show that self- control and persistence increase academic outcomes independent of IQ.
