cn: 近期研究表明，自控力和毅力能提高学业成绩，且这种提升与智商无关。

en: Even our personal beliefs about effort can affect academic outcomes.
cn: 甚至我们个人对努力的信念也会影响学业成绩。

en: Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait.
cn: 认为努力能带来成就的孩子，比那些认为能力是固定特质的孩子表现更好。

en: Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about effort are particularly important in childhood.
cn: 鉴于毅力与学业成功之间存在关联，在童年时期，关于付出努力的决定就显得尤为重要。

en: Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort.
cn: 然而，相对而言，很少有研究探讨幼儿是如何了解哪些事情值得付出努力的。

en: We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world.
cn: 我们都知道，婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者。

en: But they're not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines.
cn: 但他们并非只是漫无目的地看着，他们是小小的学习机器。

en: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples.
cn: 他们能从几个例子中归纳出因果关系、社会角色等抽象概念。

en: Even a 15- month- old infant can outperform a high- level computer in such tasks.
cn: 即便是15个月大的婴儿，在这类任务中也能胜过高级计算机。

en: Could infants also make broad, generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?
cn: 那么，当涉及到努力时，婴儿是否也能从几个例子中做出广泛且可推广的推断呢？

en: If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait.
cn: 如果可以，那么毅力或许不只是一种性格特质。

en: Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.
cn: 它可能会根据社会环境灵活调整。

en: To explore this question, we showed 15- month- old babies one of two things: an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal.
cn: 为了探究这个问题，我们向15个月大的婴儿展示了两种情况中的一种：要么是一位实验者努力完成两个不同的目标，要么是这位实验者毫不费力地达成了每个目标。

en: Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top.
cn: 之后，我们给婴儿介绍了一个新奇的音乐玩具，看起来似乎按下顶部的大按钮就能启动它。

en: The button could be pressed down but didn't actually activate anything.
cn: 这个按钮可以按下去，但实际上并不能启动任何东西。

en: Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music.
cn: 在婴儿看不到的地方，我们用一个隐藏的按钮打开了音乐玩具，让他们听到玩具发出的音乐。

en: We gave the babies the music toy and left the room.
cn: 我们把音乐玩具给了婴儿，然后离开了房间。

en: Then analysts, who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched videotapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
cn: 之后，那些不知道每个婴儿处于哪种情况的分析师们观看了实验录像，并统计了婴儿通过按按钮试图启动玩具的次数。

en: Across one study and a preregistered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed pushed the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed.
cn: 在一项研究及其预先注册的重复实验中，看到成人坚持不懈并取得成功的婴儿，按按钮的次数大约是看到成人毫不费力就成功的婴儿的两倍。

en: In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding.
cn: 换句话说，婴儿在仅观看了两个成人努力并成功的例子后，就明白了努力是有价值的。

en: Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions; instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task.
cn: 这一发现的令人兴奋之处在于，婴儿不仅仅是模仿成人的动作，而是将努力的价值推广到了一项新任务中。

en: The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music.
cn: 实验者从未演示过按按钮或试图播放音乐。

en: Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.
cn: 相反，婴儿从不同的努力行动例子中得知，这个新玩具可能也需要坚持不懈才能启动。

en: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more.
cn: 如果习惯性迟到已经占据了你的生活，并变成了你的一个标志性特征，那么你很可能正在错失工作机会、娱乐良机、友谊等诸多东西。

en: If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality and address any underlying causes.
cn: 如果你在自己的生活中总是迟到，那就做好规划、把守时放在优先位置，并解决任何潜在的原因。

en: When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to.
cn: 当你必须去某个地方时，尽量提前15到30分钟到达。

en: If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do.
cn: 如果你总是迟到，那意味着你肯定没有把自己总会做的某件事考虑进去。

en: Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive.
cn: 通过给自己留出额外的到达时间来提前应对这种情况。

en: Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early.
cn: 记录下自己是否真的提前到了。

en: You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time.
cn: 你可能会发现，早点出发能让你准时到达目的地。

en: Set two alarms.
cn: 设置两个闹钟。

en: Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing, and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door.
cn: 第一个闹钟提醒你该放下手头的事情了，第二个闹钟则意味着你需要出门了。

en: Obey the alarms.
cn: 要遵守闹钟的提示。

en: As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing.
cn: 第一个闹钟一响，就停下正在做的事。

en: If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off.
cn: 如果是你之后还要回来做的事情，比如一项工作任务，那就做个笔记，提醒自己做到哪儿了。

en: Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going.
cn: 带上所有需要的东西，确保自己知道怎么去目的地。

en: Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings.
cn: 争取在第二个闹钟响之前出门上路。

en: This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
cn: 只有当你认真对待这些闹钟时，这个方法才会奏效，所以一定要一听到闹钟响就行动起来。

en: Prepare for the day ahead.
cn: 为第二天做好准备。

en: Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it's the actual day.
cn: 在每个活动开始前，提前把所有的笔记和材料整理好，这样到了当天，你所要做的就是拿起它们就走。

en: If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before.
cn: 如果你早上总是手忙脚乱，那就在前一晚尽可能多地做好准备。

en: Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
cn: 睡觉前，把第二天要穿的衣服摆好，把包收拾好。

en: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings.
cn: 学会在各项任务和会议之间留出时间。

en: It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without space in between.
cn: 一个会议紧接着另一个会议，中间没有间隙，很快就会让人难以忍受。

en: If you over schedule yourself, however, you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump.
cn: 然而，如果你把日程安排得太满，一旦遇到一点小麻烦，你就会迟到。

en: As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events which can be 'borrowed' from should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.
cn: 除了给你留出缓冲空间外，这段时间在不同活动之间还能起到'备用时间'的作用——如果你在前一个会议中被耽搁了，就可以借用这段时间，这样你仍然能准时参加下一个会议。

en: Calculate transit time between activities, and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.
cn: 计算好各项活动之间的交通时间，然后再加上10到30分钟，以应对意外延误。

en: Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat?
cn: 你觉得波士顿人会热情好客吗？

en: Do you find other cities to be more or less polite?
cn: 你认为其他城市的人更有礼貌还是更没礼貌？

en: Different cities have different feels for visitors.
cn: 不同的城市给游客的感觉各不相同。

en: Some are friendly and open; some are formal and distant.
cn: 有些城市友好开放，有些则拘谨疏离。

en: Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude.
cn: 波士顿往往给人一种行色匆匆、有时甚至有点粗鲁的感觉。

en: That's what some tourists have said.
cn: 这是一些游客的评价。

en: One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other US cities.
cn: 一项研究发现，与美国其他城市的居民相比，这里的人不太愿意主动帮助陌生人。

en: Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn and occasionally cursing at each other; drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park, but instead, simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.
cn: 下次你去波士顿的时候仔细观察一下，可能会看到这样一些情景：人们无视频繁的提醒，在地铁站内吸烟；行人不顾红绿灯，在人行横道灯显示禁止通行时过马路，对车辆视而不见；汽车司机超速行驶，按喇叭制造噪音，偶尔还会互相咒骂；司机们懒得找地方停车，只是打开转向灯，就把车停在马路中间。

en: Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite.
cn: 有时候，波士顿人似乎太忙了，没空讲究礼貌。

en: Why is their city like that?
cn: 为什么这座城市会是这样呢？

en: Former US representative Chester Atkins says it's because the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad- tempered, and had little time for courtesy.
cn: 美国前众议员切斯特·阿特金斯表示，这是因为清教徒开国元勋们自己就性子急躁、脾气不好，没什么时间讲完礼节。

en: That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes.
cn: 他认为这种文化一直延续到了今天。

en: Boston College professor Thomas O'Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion.
cn: 波士顿学院的托马斯·奥康纳教授则认为，一个促成因素是波士顿的历史——在这座城市里，每一批新来的移民都曾遭到怀疑和排斥。

en: That's given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks.
cn: 他认为，这让波士顿有了一种小圈子意识和保守心态。

en: "The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture," he says.
cn: '陌生人之间互相打招呼的做法根本就不是当地文化的一部分，'他说。

en: "People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger."
cn: '人们会和认识的人交谈，但不会和陌生人说话。'

en: Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts, at Amherst, thinks it's because Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions.
cn: 马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的新闻学教授拉尔夫·怀特黑德认为，这是因为波士顿的上层阶级用礼仪来区分社会阶层。

en: "By being snobbish about manners, Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy," he says.
cn: '正宗的波士顿人对礼仪嗤之以鼻，这使得其他人也看不起礼节，'他说。

en: Some say that's just the way Boston is, and that the city will never change.
cn: 有人说波士顿就是这个样子，而且永远不会改变。

en: Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images.
cn: 尽管如此，其他一些以更粗鲁著称的城市却在努力改变自己的形象。

en: Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly.
cn: 巴黎就是一个例子，那里的人们正努力变得友好起来。

en: New York City is another—there the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate.
cn: 纽约市是另一个例子——该市正试图劝说地铁乘客多为他人着想。

en: If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.
cn: 如果那些城市都能付出努力，或许波士顿也应该这样做。

en: We are down to two candidates for one position, and we need to decide by the end of the day in order to finalize this whole procedure.
cn: 我们只剩下两个候选人竞争一个职位了，我们需要在今天结束前做出决定，以便完成整个流程。

en: Yes, but it isn't an easy choice to make.
cn: 是的，但这不是一个容易的选择。

en: Both applicants are quite strong.
cn: 两位申请人都很优秀。

en: Let's get to it then.
cn: 那我们开始讨论吧。

en: Both of them went to good universities, and both of them studied business- related subjects.
cn: 他们俩都毕业于好大学，而且都学的是和商业相关的专业。

en: So, academically, I'd say they're pretty much the same.
cn: 所以，在学术方面，我觉得他们几乎不相上下。

en: What do you think?
cn: 你怎么看？

en: I would agree.
cn: 我同意你的看法。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university.
cn: 或许唯一值得注意的区别是，雷切尔在高中和大学期间的成绩似乎略好一些。

en: But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter.
cn: 但就像我说的，只比彼得高一点点。

en: That's true and worth noting.
cn: 确实如此，这一点值得关注。

en: Thank you.
cn: 谢谢。

en: In addition, Rachel interviewed very well.
cn: 另外，雷切尔的面试表现非常好。

en: I thought she came across as bright and alert.
cn: 我觉得她给人的印象是聪明又机敏。

en: Yes.
cn: 是的。

en: She asked some very good questions about the position and the company, which made me think she is very keen about the job.
cn: 她问了一些关于这个职位和公司的很好的问题，这让我觉得她对这份工作非常热衷。

en: I thought so too.
cn: 我也这么觉得。

en: Now let's look at Peter's interview performance.
cn: 现在我们来看看彼得的面试表现。

en: I thought he also did very well.
cn: 我觉得他也做得很好。

en: He came across as respectful and professional.
cn: 他给人的印象是恭敬且专业。

en: Wouldn't you say?
cn: 你不这么认为吗？

en: Calm and poised; very mature for his age.
cn: 沉着冷静，泰然自若，以他的年龄来说非常成熟。

en: Exactly.
cn: 完全正确。

en: In my notes, I wrote that he seemed composed and in control of his emotions.
cn: 我在笔记里写了，他看起来沉着冷静，能控制自己的情绪。

en: I think he definitely looked more mature than Rachel.
cn: 我觉得他显然比雷切尔看起来更成熟。

en: Interesting.
cn: 有意思。

en: So we agree that Rachel appeared inexperienced and less mature than Peter, even though both candidates are the same age and have practically no work experience.
cn: 所以我们都认为，尽管两位候选人年龄相同，而且实际上都没有工作经验，但雷切尔显得缺乏经验，也不如彼得成熟。

en: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self- assured, somehow.
cn: 把他们放在一起比较的话，是的，不知怎么的，彼得看起来更自信。

en: Maybe it was something about their body language.
cn: 也许和他们的肢体语言有关。

en: Sure.
cn: 当然。

en: Maybe he was simply less nervous.
cn: 也许他只是没那么紧张。

en: Maybe.
cn: 也许吧。

en: Who knows?
cn: 谁知道呢？

en: To be honest, I think I like Rachel better.
cn: 说实话，我更喜欢雷切尔。

en: Hmm, really?
cn: 嗯，真的吗？

en: I think I like Peter.
cn: 我更喜欢彼得。

en: Ah, well, if there's a tie and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote.
cn: 啊，好吧，如果意见相持不下，我们无法达成一致，那我们就把这件事交给约翰，让他投决定性的一票。

en: We're here with Clémentine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection.
cn: 今天我们邀请到了私人时尚品牌'橙'的首席设计师克莱门汀·奥特加，来聊聊她的最新系列。

en: Ms Ortega, how would you describe this season's look?
cn: 奥特加女士，您会如何描述本季的风格呢？

en: To be honest, my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side, and I think this collection is even more so.
cn: 说实话，我偏爱的风格一直带有几分模糊感，而我觉得这个系列更是如此。

en: I try not to adhere to social norms and expectations.
cn: 我努力不遵循社会规范和期望。

en: Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.
cn: 相反，我总是尝试在自己的美学风格中融入一些略带荒诞的元素。

en: The assortment of accessories in this collection has had quite an impact on critics.
cn: 这个系列中的配饰组合给评论家们留下了相当深刻的印象。

en: The dazzling cape deployed at the end of the show, for example, bewildered many in the audience.
cn: 比如，秀场结尾展示的那件耀眼的披风，让很多观众都感到困惑。

en: What was your inspiration for this piece?
cn: 这件作品的灵感来自哪里呢？

en: Over the summer, I travelled through rural mountain villages throughout Asia in search of handicrafts to decorate my new studio with.
cn: 今年夏天，我游历了亚洲各地的山区乡村，想寻找一些手工艺品来装饰我的新工作室。

en: The embroidery done by the women in a particular village was so exquisite.
cn: 某个村子里的妇女们做的刺绣非常精美。

en: I couldn't stop thinking about it.
cn: 我一直念念不忘。

en: Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile.
cn: 要重现她们的设计是徒劳的。

en: So instead, I applied my own eccentric approach.
cn: 所以，我采用了自己独特古怪的方式。

en: Using glitter, I drew similar, intricate patterns onto the velvet cape.
cn: 我用闪光材料在天鹅绒披风上绘制了类似的复杂图案。

en: This ended up in the glamorous, luminous look that concluded the show.
cn: 最终呈现出的就是那种华丽又亮眼的样子，作为秀的结尾。

en: It was indeed majestic, and yet, dare I say masculine at the same time.
cn: 它确实很华丽，但恕我直言，同时也带有几分阳刚之气。

en: Well, yes.
cn: 嗯，是的。

en: That was intentional.
cn: 这是有意为之。

en: I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.
cn: 我喜欢融合那些通常处于时尚光谱两端的风格。

en: Hence the sparkling cape was paired with a traditional power suit you would typically see in a business setting.
cn: 所以，这件闪闪发光的披风搭配了一套传统的权力套装，就是那种你在商务场合常见的款式。

en: It was sensational if I do say so myself.
cn: 我得说，效果非常惊艳。

en: Spectacular for sure.
cn: 绝对是精彩绝伦。

en: A stunning show all around.
cn: 整场秀都令人赞叹。

en: Going against stereotypes, the incorporation of indigenous aspects along with your underlying signature touch made this collection a statement of the season.
cn: 打破刻板印象，将本土元素与您标志性的内在风格相结合，使得这个系列成为本季的一个标志性作品。

en: You have proven yourself a formidable young designer, and we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next.
cn: 您已经证明了自己是一位出色的年轻设计师，而且我们迫不及待地想看到您接下来的创作。

en: Pet dogs can often readily understand a wide range of their owners' commands and gestures.
cn: 宠物狗通常能轻松理解主人的各种指令和手势。

en: But are these abilities inborn or are they exclusively learned through training?
cn: 但这些能力是天生的，还是完全通过训练习得的呢？

en: To find out, a new study examined whether stray dogs could understand human gestures.
cn: 为了找到答案，一项新研究调查了流浪狗是否能理解人类的手势。

en: The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training.
cn: 研究显示，80%参与实验的狗尽管从未接受过训练，却能成功跟随指向手势找到特定位置。

en: The results suggest that dogs can understand complex gestures by simply watching humans.
cn: 结果表明，狗只需观察人类就能理解复杂的手势。

en: This could have implications in reducing conflict between stray dogs and humans.
cn: 这可能对减少流浪狗与人类之间的冲突具有重要意义。

en: Dogs were domesticated 10,000 to 15,000 years ago.
cn: 狗在1万到1.5万年前被驯化。

en: This means they are probably the oldest domesticated animals on the planet.
cn: 这意味着它们可能是地球上最早被驯化的动物。

en: Humans then bred dogs with the most desirable and useful traits so that they could function as companions and workers.
cn: 之后，人类培育出具有最理想、最有用特质的狗，使它们能充当伙伴和工作助手。

en: This resulted in domesticated dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures.
cn: 这使得驯化后的狗对人类的指令和手势反应极为灵敏。

en: However, it was not clear whether dogs understand us through training alone, or whether this was an inherent ability.
cn: 然而，目前尚不清楚狗理解我们是完全通过训练，还是这是一种与生俱来的能力。

en: Why does this matter?
cn: 这为什么重要呢？

en: Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world.
cn: 流浪狗是世界各地城市中常见的景象。

en: They may observe and occasionally interact with people, but such dogs have never been trained and are behaviorally 'wild'.
cn: 它们可能会观察人类，偶尔也会与人类互动，但这类狗从未受过训练，行为上处于'野生'状态。

en: Conflicts between stray dogs and humans are a problem.
cn: 流浪狗与人类之间的冲突是一个问题。

en: Understanding how humans shape stray dogs' behavior may help alleviate this problem.
cn: 了解人类如何影响流浪狗的行为可能有助于缓解这一问题。

en: According to the researchers of the new study, stray dogs are intelligent creatures.
cn: 新研究的研究人员表示，流浪狗是聪明的生物。

en: They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us to make a decision.
cn: 它们会密切观察人类，并利用对人类的理解来做决定。

en: "Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect and giving them space," the researchers assert, "can reduce much conflict."
cn: 研究人员断言：'带着善意和尊重对待流浪狗，并给它们空间，能大大减少冲突。'

en: Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air?
cn: 你是不是觉得冰箱里就是一大箱子温度均匀的冷空气？

en: Not so!
cn: 并非如此！

en: The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between.
cn: 普通冰箱内部的温度实际上从前往后、从下到上以及各个角落都有所不同。

en: Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.
cn: 正因为如此，食物在冰箱内的摆放位置比你可能意识到的要重要得多。

en: The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 °C.
cn: 现代冰箱的整个用途就是减缓细菌的生长，而细菌在4.4到60摄氏度的温度下会大量繁殖。

en: As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria.
cn: 因此，冰箱通常会设置在这个温度范围的下限或更低，以保护食物免受细菌侵害。

en: Although it might seem like time spent organizing the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user- friendly, easier to clean and food safety- conscious.
cn: 虽然整理冰箱的时间可能会让你这一天变得不愉快，但这样做实际上会让冰箱更易用、更容易清洁，并且更注重食品安全。

en: Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don't maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there.
cn: 冰箱门内侧的那些小储物格很方便，但它们不能保持稳定的温度，所以绝对不要把易腐食品放在那里。

en: The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don't need extra- chilly temperatures.
cn: 冰箱上层不像下层那么冷，所以把它留给那些不需要特别低温的食物。

en: Store foods that are ready- to- eat or already cooked on the top shelf.
cn: 将即食食品或已经做熟的食物存放在上层货架。

en: The middle shelf is the most temperature- controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here.
cn: 中层货架是冰箱里温度最稳定的部分，所以把鸡蛋放在这里。

en: Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you run out of room up top.
cn: 如果上层没地方了，饮料和预制食品也可以放在中层货架。

en: The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible, longer.
cn: 下层货架的后部是冰箱里最冷的地方，所以把易腐乳制品存放在这里，可以让它们保存更长时间。

en: Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.
cn: 千万不要把水分含量高的食物放在这里，因为其中的水分会结冰，从而彻底毁掉这些食物。

en: My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how would it affect our immune system.
cn: 我目前的研究主要关注压力等因素以及它们会如何影响我们的免疫系统。

en: So the current projects that I am quite excited about are looking at older people and factors that are important to them.
cn: 所以，我现在特别感兴趣的项目是研究老年人以及对他们而言重要的各种因素。

en: In one project, we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event, and we are trying to understand the impact of depression.
cn: 在一个项目中，我们正在研究老年人的髋部骨折问题，这是一种常见情况，同时我们也在努力弄清楚抑郁症带来的影响。

en: Often people in hospital with a hip fracture develop depression, and these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly than others.
cn: 髋部骨折住院的患者往往会患上抑郁症，而这些人随后会比其他人更快地变得虚弱。

en: They get infections; often, these infections lead to death.
cn: 他们会受到感染，这些感染往往会导致死亡。

en: So we're trying to slow down that progression to feebleness.
cn: 因此，我们正试图减缓他们走向虚弱的进程。

en: So if we can better understand how these factors interact, then we can actually start doing something about it.
cn: 要是我们能更好地理解这些因素之间的相互作用，那我们就能真正着手采取一些措施了。

en: The impact that my research will have in Birmingham, first of all, is obviously for older people, because these are the people that are having hip fractures and developing depression.
cn: 我的研究对伯明翰产生的影响，首先当然是针对老年人的，因为正是这些人会遭遇髋部骨折并患上抑郁症。

en: And we're trying to improve their health and their quality of life.
cn: 我们在努力改善他们的健康状况和生活质量。

en: But this isn't just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK.
cn: 但这不仅仅是伯明翰甚至英国存在的问题。

en: This is a problem globally.
cn: 这是一个全球性的问题。

en: People are aging.
cn: 人口正在老龄化。

en: There're a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer, but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives.
cn: 老年群体中寿命更长的人越来越多，但他们在人生的大部分时间里未必能保持健康。

en: So the last part of their life can often be full of ill health and we're trying to understand factors that can contribute to the quality of life later on.
cn: 所以，他们人生的最后阶段往往充满了病痛，我们正努力弄清哪些因素能影响晚年的生活质量。

en: I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant.
cn: 我认为我的研究最让我感到兴奋的一点是，它感觉真实且具有现实意义。

en: Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them.
cn: 很多学者或许对自己的研究感到非常兴奋，但他们的研究可能与身边人的生活关联不大。

en: Whereas I feel that the work I do is relevant to everyone, because everyone is aging.
cn: 而我觉得自己所做的工作与每个人都息息相关，因为每个人都会衰老。

en: Health is an issue for everyone, regardless of their age.
cn: 无论年龄大小，健康对每个人来说都是一个问题。

en: And what I'm trying to do is understand the factors that affect health and how we can improve the quality of life and people.
cn: 我所努力做的就是弄清楚影响健康的因素，以及我们如何能提高人们的生活质量。

en: So that's one of the things that really excites me about it.
cn: 这正是让我对这项研究充满热情的原因之一。

en: One of the other things is rather than just taking one perspective—so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist—we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.
cn: 另一点是，我们并非只从单一角度出发—不只是从心理学家的角度去研究衰老和健康—我们现在正汇集多种不同的技术和众多不同的观点，来切实研究影响健康的各类不同因素。

en: Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs.
cn: 美国人痴迷于明星厨师。

en: We talk about them and try to eat like them.
cn: 我们谈论他们，还努力像他们那样饮食。

en: But could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques?
cn: 但除了食谱和烹饪技巧，我们能从他们身上学到更多东西吗？

en: According to Marketdata Enterprises, Americans spend nearly $10 billion a year on selfhelp and personal organization products.
cn: 根据市场数据和企业公司的统计，美国人每年在自助类和个人整理类产品上的花费近100亿美元。

en: The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don't teach basic organization.
cn: 这个市场规模巨大，部分原因是大多数学院和研究生院并不教授基础的整理能力。

en: But cooking schools and professional kitchens do.
cn: 但烹饪学校和专业厨房却会教授。

en: Perhaps the principles of cooking organization can be extended to help even those of us who aren't top chefs.
cn: 或许，烹饪整理的原则可以推广开来，甚至能帮助我们这些并非顶级厨师的人。

en: The system that makes kitchens function is called mise- en- place, or, literally, 'put in place'.
cn: 让厨房有序运转的体系被称为'mise- en- place'，字面意思是'各就各位'。

en: It's a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking.
cn: 这是一个法语短语，指的是收集并整理好烹饪所需的食材和工具。

en: But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper.
cn: 但对许多专业厨师而言，这个短语有着更深层的含义。

en: Some cooks call it their religion.
cn: 有些厨师将其视为自己的信仰。

en: It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labor and material, and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self- discipline.
cn: 它帮助他们协调大量的人力和物力，并通过专注和自律改变从业者的生活。

en: Students at the Culinary Institute of America view it as a way of life.
cn: 美国烹饪学院的学生将其视为一种生活方式。

en: It's a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment, to kind of rid themselves of distractions.
cn: 这是一种让他们集中精神，只专注于当下需要处理的事情、摆脱各种干扰的方式。

en: And it's a habit that some students carry with them even when they're not in the kitchen.
cn: 而且，有些学生即便不在厨房，也会保持这种习惯。

en: They mise- en- place their life.
cn: 他们会把生活安排得'各就各位'。

en: They set up their books for class, they set up their chef whites, they shine their shoes, they know everything that they need every step of the day.
cn: 整理好上课要用的书本，准备好厨师白大褂，擦亮鞋子，清楚一天中每一步需要做的所有事情。

en: Then how does one attain this level of organization?
cn: 那么，一个人如何才能达到这种条理程度呢？

en: The key to high level organization is the mindset.
cn: 高水平条理的关键在于心态。

en: Cooks can easily do 6 hours of preparation for a 3- hour dinner shift.
cn: 厨师们为一场3小时的晚餐服务，很容易就要做6小时的准备工作。

en: Mise- en- place forces cooks to account for every minute of their time and every movement.
cn: '各就各位'的原则迫使厨师们计算好每一分钟的时间和每一个动作。

en: "Every component of one single dish is in one single corner so their hand literally moves inches," explains Dwayne Lipuma, an instructor at the Culinary Institute of America.
cn: '一道菜的每一个组成部分都放在一个固定的角落，所以他们的手实际上只需要移动几英寸，'美国烹饪学院的讲师德韦恩·利普解释道。

en: "Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes.
cn: '一旦学生们布置好自己的工作台，我就算蒙上他们的眼睛。

en: And they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here."
cn: 他们也应该知道刀总是在这里，油总是就在这里，盐和胡椒也总是就在这里。'

en: But practiced at its highest level, mise- en- place says that time is precious.
cn: 但如果以最高水平践行'各就各位'原则，它传递的是：时间宝贵。

en: Resources are precious.
cn: 资源宝贵。

en: Space is precious.
cn: 空间宝贵。

en: Your self- respect and the respect of others are precious.
cn: 自尊以及他人的尊重也宝贵。

en: Use them wisely.
cn: 要明智地利用它们。

en: Isn't that a philosophy for our time?
cn: 这不正是我们这个时代的一种人生哲学吗？

en: Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life?
cn: 我们为什么会停止为自己设定目标，停止在生活中进步呢？

en: One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves.
cn: 一个原因是我们认为应该接受自己本来的样子，而不是不断努力去提升自己。

en: The mistake we make with this is that whilst self- acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.
cn: 我们在这方面犯的错误是，虽然自我接纳至关重要，但它实际上应该被用作成长的基础。

en: When we are not growing, learning and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what it is and stop believing we can be better.
cn: 当我们不在生活中成长、学习和寻求进步时，我们往往会停滞不前，接受现状，不再相信自己能变得更好。

en: A key tool for creating goals and progressing is using our imagination.
cn: 设定目标和取得进步的一个关键工具是运用我们的想象力。

en: Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal- setting.
cn: 然而，通常情况下，到了中年，我们就不再梦想自己想要实现什么，并且对设定目标持有相当消极的态度。

en: Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short.
cn: 达成目标时，我们感受到的不是自信、快乐和满足，而是总觉得自己做得不够好。

en: That leads to disappointment and we stop dreaming.
cn: 这会导致失望，于是我们停止了梦想。

en: We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be, quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality.
cn: 我们不再想象自己想要的生活或想要成为的人，很快就被现实的痛苦击垮。

en: Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we've found the idea of using 'play' a bit childish.
cn: 到目前为止，除非我们在创意行业工作，否则我们会觉得'玩耍'这个概念有点幼稚。

en: In the West, we are mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind, but it's beginning to be better understood, because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do.
cn: 在西方，我们大多依靠大脑，依靠理性思维，但人们开始逐渐理解，运用想象力其实是我们能做的最有力量的事情之一。

en: The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not.
cn: 因为没有实现目标而感到烦躁，问题在于目标总是在变化，而我们也总是在适应，不管我们有没有意识到这一点。

en: What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we are never going to reach our goals.
cn: 因此，结果就是我们最终觉得自己永远无法实现目标。

en: And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction, and unhappiness.
cn: 这其中就存在着导致失败、不满和不快乐的最大误解之一以及原因之一。

en: We measure against the goal rather than where we've come from.
cn: 我们总是对照目标来衡量，而不是对照自己的起点。

en: Dan Sullivan calls this 'the gap and the gain'.
cn: 丹·沙利文称之为'差距与收获'。

en: We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we're reaching, rather than the gain.
cn: 我们总是对照那个似乎永远也达不到的目标来衡量，而不是看收获。

en: That is where we've come from.
cn: 也就是我们从哪里起步。

en: In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results.
cn: 当我们衡量自己的起点，而不是衡量我们试图到达的地方时，我们就能看到成果。

en: We see things we've taken for granted or not noticed.
cn: 我们会看到那些我们习以为常或未曾注意到的东西。

en: It's a simple, yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear.
cn: 这是一种简单却意义深远的观念转变，我喜欢它的地方在于，它有能力立即让我们更上一层楼。

en: It's so, so simple, yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.
cn: 这非常、非常简单，却能对我们的思维产生立竿见影的积极影响。

en: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats.
cn: 今天的特邀嘉宾是布莱克韦尔勋爵，他是我国经验最丰富、最杰出的职业外交官之一。

en: Welcome!
cn: 欢迎您！

en: It's my pleasure.
cn: 很荣幸能来。

en: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service.
cn: 我们的观众会对如何在外交部门发展职业非常感兴趣。

en: However, before we talk about that, I'd like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today, regarding the Republic of Winopia.
cn: 不过，在谈论这个之前，我想问问您今天新闻中有关威诺皮亚共和国的最新动态。

en: What can you tell us?
cn: 您能给我们讲讲吗？

en: I'm afraid I don't know much beyond what we've all seen on the news.
cn: 恐怕除了我们在新闻上看到的内容，我知道的并不多。

en: It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy.
cn: 看起来威诺皮亚政府似乎正经历某种合法性危机。

en: And an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on.
cn: 在国家元首人选确定之前，已经临时成立了一个过渡政府。

en: But my career work has mostly focused around the continental spheres of Europe and the Americas.
cn: 但我的职业生涯主要集中在欧洲和美洲大陆地区。

en: And thus I've never been involved with Winopian relations.
cn: 因此从未参与过与威诺皮亚的外交关系事务。

en: It's for this reason that I don't know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
cn: 正因为如此，关于这件事，我所知道的和大家从报纸上读到的没什么两样。

en: Oh, I see.
cn: 哦，我明白了。

en: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our export envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation.
cn: 尽管如此，请放心，我们驻当地领事馆的出口特使会密切关注局势。

en: And I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
cn: 而且我预计我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。

en: So how does one get a career in foreign relations?
cn: 那么，怎样才能从事外交相关的职业呢？

en: There are many different paths one can take.
cn: 有很多不同的途径。

en: All diplomats have their own story.
cn: 每个外交官都有自己的故事。

en: But in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering, followed by 6 years' service in the Air Force.
cn: 就我而言，我先获得了电气工程学位，之后在空军服役了6年。

en: Then I went to law school and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic corps where I've been for 22 years.
cn: 然后我去了法学院，获得国际法学位后，就加入了外交使团，至今已有22年了。

en: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
cn: 您认为这份工作需要哪些关键技能呢？

en: There are so many.
cn: 有很多。

en: Being a hard worker and good student is important.
cn: 勤奋工作和善于学习很重要。

en: You never stop learning.
cn: 因为你永远不能停止学习。

en: In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric.
cn: 此外，外交官在言谈和修辞方面需要非常善于表达。

en: Whether it is diffusing tension or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
cn: 无论是缓解紧张局势还是制定政策，人际交往和沟通技能都至关重要。

en: It's getting late and we're both displaying signs of weariness.
cn: 天色不早了，我们俩都露出了疲倦的神色。

en: I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning.
cn: 我觉得我们今天就到这儿吧，明天早上再碰面。

en: Oh, come on, Jeff.
cn: 哦，别这样，杰夫。

en: We are so close.
cn: 我们就快完成了。

en: Don't you think we are almost done?
cn: 你不觉得我们差不多要做完了吗？

en: Let's do two more hours, please.
cn: 求你了，再干两个小时吧。

en: One hour, then I'm going home.
cn: 一个小时，然后我就回家。

en: Okay, fine!
cn: 好吧，行！

en: I think we are making good progress, and that with a few more amendments we will be all done.
cn: 我觉得我们进展得很顺利，再做几处修改就能全部完成了。

en: I'm sure looking forward to it.
cn: 我确实很期待完成的那一刻。

en: I'm so tired of this project.
cn: 我对这个项目已经感到很厌倦了。

en: Don't get me wrong.
cn: 别误会我的意思。

en: It's a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company.
cn: 这对我来说是个很棒的职业机会，对公司来说也是一个里程碑。

en: But it's just been so long.
cn: 但这个项目实在拖太久了。

en: Yeah, two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough.
cn: 是啊，整整两个月就只围着这份合同转，确实有点难熬。

en: Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck, we'll be done by next week.
cn: 不过，我觉得只要运气好点，我们下周就能完成。

en: Ha! You must be delusional.
cn: 哈！你肯定是痴心妄想。

en: You don't think so?
cn: 你不这么认为吗？

en: No chance.
cn: 根本不可能。

en: Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework.
cn: 第4、5、8和9部分还得根据新框架进行调整。

en: Then we need to proofread the whole thing, and make sure all selling points are watertight.
cn: 然后我们还需要校对整个文件，确保所有卖点都无懈可击。

en: But that will all take no more than a couple of days.
cn: 但这些活儿最多也就花两三天时间。

en: I wasn't finished.
cn: 我还没说完呢。

en: When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen?
cn: 等我们做完这些，把文件交上去，你觉得会发生什么？

en: What?
cn: 会发生什么？

en: They'll argue about it for like a month.
cn: 他们会为此争论一个月左右。

en: There's always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made.
cn: 总会有某个董事跳出来干预，要求进行修改。

en: They might think they're being helpful, but in reality, they're being obstructive and hampering progress.
cn: 他们可能觉得自己是在帮忙，但实际上，他们是在阻碍项目进展。

en: Oh, Jeff.
cn: 哦，杰夫。

en: You're too preoccupied and cynical.
cn: 你太忧心忡忡，也太愤世嫉俗了。

en: It won't be anywhere as bad as that.
cn: 事情不会有那么糟的。

en: You'll see.
cn: 你等着瞧吧。

en: The entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible.
cn: 整个管理层都希望这个项目能尽快实施。

en: And the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support.
cn: 而且董事会也几乎一致支持。

en: Go on then.
cn: 那行吧。

en: Let's stop there and meet up again same time tomorrow.
cn: 我们就到这儿，明天同一时间再碰面。

en: One thing I've learned in a quarter- century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior and that there may not always be clear right- or- wrong solutions to employee disputes.
cn: 在二十几年的管理生涯中，我学到的一点是，人类行为存在大量模糊地带，对于员工之间的纠纷，并非总能找到明确的对错解决方案。

en: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
cn: 当两个人对同一件事各执一词时，很难判断该相信谁。

en: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
cn: 有这样一种情况总让我回想起来。

en: It happened years ago and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
cn: 那是多年前发生的事，这场冲突的性质实在不值一提，我甚至已经不记得纠纷的缘由了，但我清楚地记得解决方式。

en: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth.
cn: 两位才华横溢的年轻高管——其中一位由我管理——对同一件事的描述大相径庭，我们似乎永远也无法得知真相。

en: We reached a deadlock.
cn: 我们陷入了僵局。

en: And the manager of the other individual said, "Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for."
cn: 另一位高管的经理说：“我曾经从一位非常出色的经理那里学到了一点。”

en: He used to say, 'When in doubt, assume positive intent.'
cn: 他常说：‘有疑问时，要假定对方的意图是好的。’

en: And just like that, we had a path forward.
cn: 就这么一句话，我们找到了前进的方向。

en: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
cn: 我和那位经理都认为，我们可能永远无法查明事情的全部真相。

en: Quite likely, there were elements of truth in both employees' stories.
cn: 很可能，两位员工的说法都有一定的真实性。

en: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
cn: 我们一致同意，会关注他们今后的行为和关系，但不会再进一步干预。

en: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
cn: 我们往好的方面看待他们两人，然后继续处理其他事情。

en: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
cn: 结果是，我们成功地把这场冲突抛在了脑后。

en: In fact, their problems didn't recur.
cn: 事实上，他们的问题也没有再出现。

en: Over the years, this general approach has proved useful.
cn: 多年来，这种通用方法被证明是有效的。

en: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
cn: 每当真相模糊不清时，假定对方心怀善意并同意继续前行，可能是一个富有建设性的决定。

en: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for.
cn: 对一些美国人来说，出去吃晚餐是一种享受，是经过计划和预算的。

en: For others, it's just a daily occurrence.
cn: 对另一些人来说，这只是日常发生的事。

en: And that second group of people is becoming the majority, as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
cn: 而且随着喜欢做饭的美国人数量不断减少，第二类人正逐渐成为多数。

en: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking.
cn: 21世纪初，研究员埃迪·尹开展了一项调查，以了解美国人对做饭的态度。

en: The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings.
cn: 调查发现，15%的美国人热爱做饭，50%的人表示讨厌做饭，35%的人则感觉复杂。

en: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it, and 45% had mixed feelings.
cn: 15年后，尹进行了同样的调查，结果只有10%的受访者表示热爱做饭，45%的人说讨厌做饭，45%的人态度混杂。

en: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
cn: 尹声称，做饭和缝纫类似。

en: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
cn: 就在20世纪初，许多美国人还自己缝制衣服。

en: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing.
cn: 如今，绝大多数美国人都是购买衣服。

en: Only a tiny minority still sew and they do it mainly as a hobby.
cn: 只有极少数人还在缝纫，而且他们主要是把缝纫当作一种爱好。

en: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
cn: 尹认为，家庭厨师的数量也会以类似的方式减少。

en: Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out.
cn: 目前，美国家庭平均每年在外出就餐上的花费超过3000美元。

en: However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash.
cn: 然而，人们在便利性上节省的时间，却在金钱上有所损失。

en: Take buying lunch on workdays, for example.
cn: 以工作日买午餐为例。

en: People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
cn: 人们买午餐平均每餐要花10美元。

en: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
cn: 与此同时，自己做午餐花费会更少。

en: One survey found people only spend, on average, $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
cn: 一项调查发现，人们带家里准备的午餐时，平均只花6.30美元。

en: Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
cn: 美国人越来越不愿意花时间在厨房，这对杂货行业来说意味着诸多挑战。

en: It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
cn: 这也可能会对家庭财务造成不利影响。

en: Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing.
cn: 每年，在全球超过25亿件托运到航班上的行李中，有2600万件会丢失。

en: And of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
cn: 而在这2600万件中，有100万件再也无法回到原主人手中。

en: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
cn: 恶劣天气、航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，以及一些人只是忘了去取自己的其中一件行李，这些都是部分原因。

en: But the number- one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
cn: 但行李最终丢失的首要原因是它没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它属于谁。

en: Transferring baggage from check- in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
cn: 将行李从值机处转运到出发登机口、再到到达登机口，最后到行李提取处，这是一个对时间把控要求很高的过程。

en: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights.
cn: 如果系统运转太慢，行李就赶不上转机航班。

en: If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection, but the passengers might miss the flight.
cn: 如果太快，行李可能赶上转机，但乘客可能会错过航班。

en: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
cn: 每个机场都有自己的方式来分配行李在转运过程中所需的时间。

en: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination- coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
cn: 一些机场拥有先进的自动化系统，包括能读取行李标签的扫描仪、无需停下就能装卸行李的目的地编码车辆，以及将行李分拣到相应登机口的分拣机。

en: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
cn: 即便如此，所有这些技术也可能无法避免你的行李标签在传送带上被撕掉，让你成为一个没有名字的行李的主人。

en: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared "mishandled" by the carrier.
cn: 一旦行李丢失，乘客提出索赔，航空公司就会将该行李定为“处理不当”。

en: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged.
cn: “处理不当”指的是那些被延误、丢失、被盗或损坏的行李。

en: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
cn: 大多数延误的行李只比主人晚到一个航班，能在24小时内送达。

en: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination.
cn: 其他行李会由航空公司工作人员检查，以寻找其主人和目的地的线索。

en: If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within 4 or 5 days.
cn: 如果谜团解开，这些行李会在4到5天内归还给主人。

en: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
cn: 没有目的地编码或身份标签的行李会被运到一个中央仓库，并在接下来的90天内进行全面的行李追踪流程。

en: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions.
cn: 航空公司会对其处理不当的行李进行清点，许多公司会使用数据库，将行李内的物品与主人的描述进行匹配。

en: It takes about 3 months to go from "missing in action" to "irretrievably lost".
cn: 从“下落不明”到“无法找回”大约需要3个月时间。

en: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
cn: 一旦出现这种情况，这些行李会被捐赠给慈善机构、在拍卖会上出售，或者被一家公司买下后再卖给公众。

en: So, never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage.
cn: 所以，千万不要在托运行李中放置任何真正有价值的东西。

en: And make sure your name is on the bag, along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.
cn: 而且要确保行李上有你的名字和电话号码，这样工作人员就能联系到你。

en: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone.
cn: 你可能遇到过这样的人：他们一边和你相处，一边却只顾着玩智能手机，对你置之不理。

en: And you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
cn: 你自己或许也有过这种行为。

en: In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
cn: 在最近的一项调查中，十分之九的受访者表示，他们在最近一次社交活动中使用过智能手机。

en: There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
cn: 还有证据表明，这种行为对社交有害。

en: It can leave people less satisfied with their face- to- face interactions, and it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
cn: 它会降低人们对面对面交流的满意度，还可能引发怨恨和嫉妒情绪。

en: Now the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
cn: 如今，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探究了这些影响产生的原因。

en: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
cn: 该研究有128名参与者，其中大部分是女学生。

en: The participants watched a 3- minute animation, in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
cn: 参与者观看了一段3分钟的动画，动画中有两个卡通人物在互动交谈。

en: The conversation couldn't be heard, but could be detected through mouth movements.
cn: 虽然听不到对话内容，但能从嘴部动作看出他们在交流。

en: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video, and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
cn: 参与者要想象自己是视频中离得较近的那个角色，然后对对话以及自己对交谈伙伴的感受做出判断。

en: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participants' conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
cn: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者的交谈伙伴的手机全程放在桌子上，没有被使用。

en: In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
cn: 在另一个版本中，交谈伙伴的注意力很快被手机上的内容吸引，剩下的时间都在玩手机。

en: A third version involved the participants' partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
cn: 第三个版本中，交谈伙伴在玩手机和不玩手机这两种状态之间交替。

en: If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
cn: 如果你有过类似的经历，可能不会对实验结果感到惊讶。

en: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
cn: 参与者对社交互动中使用手机的行为持负面看法。

en: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
cn: 手机使用得越多，他们认为互动质量和人际关系质量就越差。

en: The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion.
cn: 研究人员认为，专注于手机而不是身边的人会产生这样的效果，是因为这种行为被视为一种社会排斥。

en: They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
cn: 他们声称，这种行为类似于人们别无选择，只能独自在学校食堂吃饭的情况。

en: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
cn: 不同的是，这种排斥发生在共享物理空间并进行交谈的过程中。

en: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self- esteem.
cn: 研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊产生了负面影响。

en: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
cn: 这些负面影响与传统形式的社会排斥所造成的影响相似。

en: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience.
cn: 这项新发现很重要，因为它加深了我们对日常经历中一个微妙但常见的方面的理解。

en: This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
cn: 这种常见的行为可能会在我们试图与他人建立联系时，形成疏离的恶性循环。

en: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons.
cn: 越来越多的人出于各种各样的原因出行。

en: Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business.
cn: 其中许多是游客，但也有很多人是因私人事务或公务外出。

en: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
cn: 无论出行的原因是什么，旅行者们一个常见的抱怨是他们所找到的住宿缺乏人情味。

en: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited.
cn: 商务旅行者在五家相似的酒店连续住了五个晚上后，可能会发现很难记住每天发生了什么，甚至不记得去过哪些城镇。

en: And the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
cn: 而游客可能会产生一种错误的印象，觉得所有城市都大同小异，至少在装修、食物和服务方面是这样。

en: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in- home hospitality or bed- and- breakfast arrangements.
cn: 为了对抗这种缺乏个性的雷同感，旅行者们开始利用家庭寄宿或提供住宿加早餐的服务。

en: B&Bs, I mean bed- and- breakfast arrangements, are private homes, which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting.
cn: 我所说的B&B，也就是提供住宿加早餐的地方，指的是私人住宅，它们在极具个性化且友好的环境中提供住宿和早餐。

en: For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles.
cn: 几十年来，B&B一直是游览欧洲的经典方式，尤其是在不列颠群岛。

en: And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
cn: 事实上，在美国，这也并非真正意义上的新事物。

en: The tradition dates back to colonial times, when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
cn: 这一传统可以追溯到殖民时期，当时旅馆数量稀少且分布零散，疲惫的旅行者不得不依靠陌生人的善意来获取一餐一宿。

en: But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
cn: 但B&B作为理想住宿选择的复兴却是一个相当近期的现象。

en: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
cn: 如果经营一家B&B的想法引起了你的兴趣，那么在投身这一行业之前，有几个因素需要考虑。

en: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location.
cn: 首要考虑的是你的房产，不仅包括建筑本身，还包括其位置。

en: If you live near a famous historical site, or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington D.C., your home can be fairly simple yet still do well as a B&B.
cn: 如果你住在著名的历史景点附近，或者像纽约市、华盛顿特区这样的热门目的地，你的房子即使相当简单，作为B&B也能经营得不错。

en: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique, or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
cn: 另一方面，如果你的房子在建筑风格上独具特色，或者拥有能为旅行者提供便利的设施，比如私人入口、私人浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意长途跋涉前来入住。

en: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
cn: 另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。

en: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved.
cn: 你必须考虑到，家庭成员是否都真正喜欢接待访客，是否愿意反复谈论当地的景点和活动，以及是否有时间和精力来处理额外的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和记账工作。

en: The final consideration is a financial one.
cn: 最后一个需要考虑的是财务方面。

en: Potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
cn: 潜在的B&B主人必须对收入机会持现实态度。

en: While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
cn: 虽然B&B通常初始成本较低，但专家估计，主人至少需要有五个房间能定期租出去，才能依靠B&B谋生。

en: I must say, I love our canteen.
cn: 我得说，我喜欢我们的食堂。

en: It's such a great meeting point.
cn: 这里真是个很棒的碰面地点。

en: Yeah, it really is.
cn: 是啊，确实是这样。

en: Both for students and teachers.
cn: 对学生和老师来说都是如此。

en: Shame about the food.
cn: 就是食物有点可惜了。

en: What do you mean?
cn: 你什么意思？

en: I think the food is fine.
cn: 我觉得食物还不错啊。

en: I would say the food is just okay, but the prices are absurd.
cn: 我觉得也就一般吧，但价格太离谱了。

en: Don't you agree?
cn: 你不觉得吗？

en: I don't, actually.
cn: 其实我不这么认为。

en: I personally think they're perfectly appropriate.
cn: 我个人觉得价格非常合理。

en: If it's overpriced, why does it get so frantically busy at lunchtimes?
cn: 如果定价过高，那为什么午餐时间这里还会忙得不可开交呢？

en: Hmm, you make a good point.
cn: 嗯，你说得有道理。

en: I guess a lot of it is good value, maybe even most of it.
cn: 我想很多食物性价比都挺高的，或许大部分都是。

en: However, don't you think six bucks for a slice of apple crumble is beyond most students' budgets?
cn: 不过，你不觉得一块苹果酥要6美元，超出了大多数学生的预算吗？

en: Um, yes, desserts are overpriced.
cn: 嗯，甜点确实定价过高。

en: I'll give you that.
cn: 这一点我同意你。

en: To be honest, I've forgotten about those as I never eat them.
cn: 说实话，我都忘了甜点这回事了，因为我从来不吃。

en: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies.
cn: 我其实不怎么想吃甜食或者任何精致的佳肴。

en: What I always go for is their scrambled eggs.
cn: 我每次去都点他们的炒鸡蛋。

en: They have such a great variety.
cn: 他们的炒鸡蛋种类特别多。

en: Yeah, those are good.
cn: 是啊，炒鸡蛋确实不错。

en: They also come out really fast.
cn: 而且上得也很快。

en: Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen—the speed.
cn: 其实，食堂最棒的一点就是速度快。

en: If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don't have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option.
cn: 如果我想吃点比三明治更管饱的东西，但午餐时间又不多，大学食堂总是个不错的选择。

en: The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace.
cn: 厨房工作人员的工作节奏非常快。

en: They really deserve to be complimented for it.
cn: 他们确实值得为此受到赞扬。

en: Totally.
cn: 完全同意。

en: And it's such a great environment too.
cn: 而且这里的环境也特别好。

en: Like the entire building is beautiful.
cn: 整个建筑都很漂亮。

en: It is very nice.
cn: 确实非常不错。

en: The massive glass windows make all the difference.
cn: 巨大的玻璃窗起到了关键作用。

en: I think they're so cool.
cn: 我觉得它们太酷了。

en: Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago.
cn: 显然，几年前这里进行了大规模翻新。

en: It cost them a pretty penny.
cn: 花了一大笔钱呢。

en: Yeah, I'm not surprised.
cn: 是啊，这我并不意外。

en: It's a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing.
cn: 这里是个多功能空间，既适合用餐也适合放松。

en: And for working.
cn: 还适合工作。

en: You're right, working too.
cn: 你说得对，也适合工作。

en: I've used my laptop there once or twice and there's always a group project or meeting going on at the far end.
cn: 我在那儿用笔记本电脑工作过一两次，而且最里面总是有小组项目讨论或者会议在进行。

en: Hi, Tony.
cn: 嗨，托尼。

en: Today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work.
cn: 今天我们来聊聊管理者如何能更好地与职场中的年轻人相处。

en: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic.
cn: 我们经常听说现在的年轻人职业道德差。

en: That's not really justified, though, is it?
cn: 不过，这其实是没有道理的，对吧？

en: Not really.
cn: 确实没道理。

en: In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
cn: 实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代一样，都是形形色色、多才多艺的。

en: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
cn: 是啊，但如果你在工作中很难和年轻人共事，该怎么办呢？

en: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values.
cn: 嗯，重要的是要和他们建立联系，了解他们的价值观。

en: It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
cn: 同样非常重要的是，要认识到年轻人希望平衡工作与个人生活的方式。

en: So they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
cn: 所以他们通常不想为了职业发展而推迟享受快乐？

en: Absolutely.
cn: 完全是这样。

en: They're not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives.
cn: 他们不愿意为了工作而牺牲个人生活。

en: And this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
cn: 而这就让人们把这等同于不愿意努力工作。

en: Right.
cn: 对。

en: But that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
cn: 但事实远非如此，对吧？

en: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have that time off, like weekends and nights free from work.
cn: 年轻人会在规定的工作时间内非常努力地工作，但他们希望有休息时间，比如周末和晚上不被工作占用。

en: So how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
cn: 那么管理者应该如何评估年轻人的工作效率呢？

en: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work.
cn: 一般来说，年轻人认为他们的工作效率不应该用工作时长来衡量。

en: Since someone can work for 8 hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company.
cn: 因为有些人可能工作8小时，却几乎没为公司完成什么有意义的事情。

en: Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
cn: 相反，年轻人是通过自己工作的质量来衡量工作效率的。

en: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine.
cn: 但我们经常听说，年轻人不想仅仅感觉自己是一台大机器上的一个零件。

en: Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
cn: 这种观点很难反驳，对吧？

en: It's important to legitimize their work.
cn: 认可他们的工作很重要。

en: Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large.
cn: 年轻员工希望从事那些对自己、对公司或者对整个世界都有意义的项目。

en: They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
cn: 他们必须觉得有必要留在一家价值观与自己一致的公司工作。

en: Thanks for your advice.
cn: 谢谢你的建议。

en: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.
cn: 许多餐厅正努力劝说顾客更可持续地饮食，从对环境不友好的肉类转向更绿色的菜肴。

en: Although it sounds counterintuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
cn: 一项新的研究表明，尽管听起来违背直觉，但在菜单上设置特定素食区域的餐厅，可能在无意中鼓励顾客食用肉类。

en: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, "Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant- based food and less meat.
cn: 该研究的作者之一、行为科学家琳达·培根表示：“餐厅可以通过鼓励顾客选择更多植物性食物、更少肉类，对环境产生积极影响。”

en: However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro- environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others."
cn: 然而，我们的研究结果表明，虽然某些餐厅的菜单设计能鼓励部分消费者做出有利于环境的食物选择，但对另一些消费者可能会产生相反的效果。”

en: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it.
cn: 这项研究涉及750人，其中一半经常吃素食，另一半则很少吃素食。

en: No vegetarians were included.
cn: 研究中没有纳入严格的素食者。

en: They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.
cn: 研究人员给他们提供了不同的菜单，让他们模拟和朋友外出就餐时选择一餐。

en: Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters, but it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%.
cn: 将素食菜肴放在单独的区域，对很少吃素食的人的选择没有显著影响，但对经常吃素食的人却有明显影响，使他们选择素食的几率降低了65%。

en: The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation or including a more appealing description of a non- meat meal leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option.
cn: 研究人员还发现，将某道素食菜肴列为厨师推荐，或者对非肉类菜肴进行更具吸引力的描述，会让更多很少吃素食的人选择素食。

en: But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
cn: 但同样，这些经过修改的菜单设计对那些更常吃素食的人却产生了反效果，导致他们选择素食的可能性降低。

en: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors.
cn: 诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在努力寻找防止致命的室外空气污染潜入室内的方法。

en: They found that if pollution is frozen to around -18°C in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through.
cn: 他们发现，如果在冷凝管中将污染物冷冻至约零下18摄氏度，这些颗粒物就会聚集并落到管底，从而让新鲜、洁净的空气通过。

en: Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants.
cn: 他们的这种方法能够去除99%的污染物。

en: It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
cn: 人们希望这项研究成果能为空调设备的简单改造铺平道路，使其也能净化受污染的室内空气。

en: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem—whether it be haze plaguing Calcutta or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools.
cn: 城市中的室外空气污染是一个全球性问题——无论是困扰加尔各答的雾霾，还是影响伦敦学校儿童健康的劣质空气，都是如此。

en: While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive, or produce harmful by- products.
cn: 虽然目前已有一些净化室内空气的技术，但它们可能效率低下、成本高昂，或者会产生有害的副产品。

en: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors.
cn: 当室外空气质量不佳时，人们往往会在室内待更长时间。

en: But outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer.
cn: 但室外污染也会导致室内污染，人们仍然会受到影响。

en: It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year.
cn: 据估计，在英国，污染每年与超过4万例过早死亡相关。

en: Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, "We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.
cn: 中国科学院的潘刚教授表示：“我们在实验中已经证明，只需让受污染的空气通过一个小型冷冻室循环，就能去除大部分细颗粒物和气体污染物。”

en: Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.
cn: 我们的研究使得在可能遭遇极端恶劣空气状况的地区，为家用电器增加空气净化功能成为可能。

en: By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health."
cn: 通过这种方式控制室内空气污染、改善空气质量，这项研究工作可能会对公众健康大有益处。”

en: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self- aware.
cn: 我的团队最近开展的研究表明，鱼类可能具有自我意识。

en: A certain species of fish recently passed the well- known mirror test.
cn: 某一物种的鱼最近通过了著名的镜子测试。

en: This is a test that demonstrates self- recognition in animals.
cn: 这是一项用于证明动物自我识别能力的测试。

en: Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins, and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror and only these animals capable of self- recognition will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection.
cn: 只有少数动物，如人类、类人猿、海豚和一些鸟类，能够在镜子中认出自己——而且只有这些具备自我识别能力的动物，在从镜中注意到自己皮肤上被放置的标记后，才会试图将其移除。

en: This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness.
cn: 这种能力体现了一定程度的更高智力和意识水平。

en: This is not shown by children until around 18 months.
cn: 儿童大约要到18个月大时才会展现出这种能力。

en: Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability.
cn: 在此之前，从未有鱼类表现出这种能力。

en: But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror.
cn: 但我们的实验显示，这种鱼在镜子中看到自己后，会在坚硬的表面上摩擦，以去除研究人员放置在其身体上的标记。

en: The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out.
cn: 我们观察到的这些行为无疑表明，这种鱼在行为上满足了最初设定的镜子测试的所有标准。

en: The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present, or when the marks were just placed on the mirror.
cn: 在我们的研究中，当没有镜子存在，或者标记只是被放在镜子上时，这种鱼从未试图去除标记。

en: Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window.
cn: 当未被标记的鱼与窗户另一侧被标记的鱼互动时，它们也没有试图从自己身上去除标记。

en: These results show either that fish are self- aware, or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
cn: 这些结果表明，要么鱼类具有自我意识，要么被视为衡量高智力黄金标准的镜子测试可能存在缺陷。

en: What is less clear is whether these behaviors should be considered as evidence that fish are self- aware, even though in the past, these same behaviors have been interpreted as self- awareness in so many other animals.
cn: 目前尚不清楚的是，尽管过去在许多其他动物身上，这些相同的行为被解读为自我意识的证据，但在鱼类身上，这些行为是否也应被视为它们具有自我意识的证据。

en: Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviors in a fish satisfy passing the test at all.
cn: 根据你的立场，你可能会反对将鱼类的这些行为解读为通过了测试。

en: But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviors they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
cn: 但当它们所表现出的行为在功能上与其他通过测试的物种的行为如此相似时，你又能基于什么客观依据来这样做呢？

en: Results from our research raise more questions than answers.
cn: 我们的研究结果引发的问题多于答案。

en: What if self- awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer, rather than appearing all at once?
cn: 倘若自我意识的发展像洋葱一样，是一层一层累积起来的，而非一蹴而就的，那会怎样呢？

en: Perhaps, in order to explore self- awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test.
cn: 或许，为了进一步探索自我意识，我们应该不再将对镜子的反应视为决定性的测试。

en: Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self- awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
cn: 只有凭借更完善的自我理论和更丰富的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的各种不同水平，包括鱼类在其中的确切定位。

en: Reading with a young child is important.
cn: 和幼儿一起阅读很重要。

en: But does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print?
cn: 但用电子书读还是用传统纸质书读，这有区别吗？

en: As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens.
cn: 任何家长都知道，小孩子通常很喜欢屏幕。

en: So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise—but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behave differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books, and the children who read the electronic books learned more.
cn: 因此，一项新研究发现幼儿更喜欢电子书而非纸质图画书，这或许不足为奇——但接下来的其他发现可能会让人惊讶：家长和孩子在阅读电子书与纸质图画书时的表现不同，而且阅读电子书的孩子学到的东西更多。

en: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print.
cn: 以往针对幼儿的研究表明，电子书包含了词典、描绘故事情节的图片等额外功能，可能比纸质书更有优势。

en: In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books.
cn: 事实上，多项研究发现，相比纸质书，电子书更有助于孩子理解故事和增加词汇量。

en: But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
cn: 但也有研究表明，孩子们有时在通过电子书学习时投入的脑力较少，而且家长在和孩子一起看这类书时，对内容的讨论也更少。

en: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children.
cn: 我们今天要关注的这项研究旨在让我们更好地了解电子书对幼儿有多有益。

en: For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents.
cn: 在这项研究中，研究人员对17至26个月大的孩子和他们的一位家长一起阅读的场景进行了录像。

en: Each parent- and- child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content.
cn: 每对亲子被随机分配阅读两本教育类电子书或两本内容相同的纸质书。

en: While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
cn: 家长大声朗读纸质书中的文字，而电子书则有配音演员朗读文本的音频。

en: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books.
cn: 研究人员发现，阅读纸质书的家长比阅读电子书的家长更频繁地指着书页。

en: But the opposite was true for the children.
cn: 但孩子们的情况则相反。

en: Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
cn: 阅读电子书的孩子对内容的评论也更多，学到的新单词也比阅读纸质书的孩子多。

en: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books.
cn: 这种更强的学习效果被归因于孩子们与电子书有更强的互动。

en: It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple.
cn: 值得注意的是，这项研究中使用的电子书很简单。

en: While they included background music, animation, and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
cn: 虽然它们包含背景音乐、动画和音效，但没有其他额外功能。

en: It's also important to note that there's research on older children finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning.
cn: 还有一点很重要，有针对年龄较大孩子的研究发现，电子书并不总能促进学习。

en: Parents and educators need to beware.
cn: 家长和教育工作者需要注意。

en: Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
cn: 电子书的额外功能可能会增加孩子们对它们的参与度；然而，如果这些功能不能将注意力吸引到教育内容上，它们可能就无法起到辅助作用。

en: Let me be honest with you.
cn: 让我跟你坦诚地说。

en: If you're living your life full of regret, you're wasting your time.
cn: 如果你过着充满遗憾的生活，那你就是在浪费时间。

en: Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today?
cn: 你为何要在人生中一直后悔那些造就了今天的你的决定呢？

en: There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them?
cn: 我们都做过很多不恰当的决定，但这就意味着我们应该后悔吗？

en: No!
cn: 不！

en: I've had many moments when I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently.
cn: 我有很多次坐在那里，想着所有我希望当初能换种做法的事情。

en: However, just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better.
cn: 然而，事情本可以不一样，并不一定意味着它们会变得更好。

en: You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one.
cn: 你不必一直纠结于自己过去的所有决定，纠结于自己是否做了正确的选择。

en: You can't go back and change anything, so what's the point in worrying about it?
cn: 你无法回到过去改变任何事情，所以为此担忧又有什么意义呢？

en: Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today.
cn: 你做过的每一个决定，无论积极还是消极，都造就了今天的你。

en: We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that?
cn: 我们想回到过去，改变过去的某些部分，但那样做有什么好处呢？

en: We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
cn: 我们会失去从吸取的教训中获得的宝贵知识。

en: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are.
cn: 你做出某些选择是有原因的，这些原因能让我们了解你是怎样的人。

en: So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself.
cn: 所以，在人生的任何决策中，都要毫无歉意地做自己。

en: Because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
cn: 因为归根结底，是你自己做的那个决定。

en: With less time spent focused on regrets, you'll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life.
cn: 花在遗憾上的时间少了，你最终就会有时间去关注生活中更重要的事情。

en: In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make.
cn: 在任何情况下，你都会随着每一个决定而成长为更好的人。

en: Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward.
cn: 生活中充满了要学习的教训，所以我们不能让遗憾阻止我们前进。

en: We don't know if we've made the right or wrong choice until after it's already been made.
cn: 在做出选择之后，我们才知道自己的选择是对是错。

en: So it can be easy to start regretting your decision.
cn: 所以，人们很容易开始后悔自己的决定。

en: But if the decision has already been made, what's the purpose of dwelling on it?
cn: 但如果决定已经做出，一直纠结于此又有什么意义呢？

en: There isn't one.
cn: 没有任何意义。

en: All you can do is move forward.
cn: 你所能做的就是继续前进。

en: You can't let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice.
cn: 你不能让自己坐在那里，为过去的每一个选择而担忧。

en: We aren't all perfect.
cn: 我们并非都是完美的。

en: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later.
cn: 无论何时做决定，日后都总有可能会后悔。

en: But that's how life is supposed to be.
cn: 但生活本就该是这样。

en: You will make poor decisions in life—we all do—but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
cn: 你在生活中会做出糟糕的决定——我们都会——但重要的是你如何利用从中学到的教训。

en: Think about every decision you've ever made.
cn: 想想你做过的每一个决定。

en: Were they always the best?
cn: 它们总是最好的吗？

en: Of course not.
cn: 当然不是。

en: But look at how far you've come since then.
cn: 但看看从那以后你已经取得了多大的进步。
